text.text:
Came here for my birthday dinner and had an amazing experience! We decided to arrive early and sit in the main dining room rather than at the chef’s counter or garden area, and I’m so glad that we did. The restaurant itself is clean, modern, and fresh. The website says that they try to create an experience that feels like you’re walking right into Beirut, and they hit the nail on the head. The decor, music, and lighting give you that effect. I was extremely impressed by the food. We decided to do the Taste of Suraya option, and it was perfect. Great value as well. I highly recommend the Kawarma dish and all of their dessert options. If you are looking for a romantic experience, I recommend Suraya.

Our reservation was at 5pm, right when they opened, so it felt like more of a private experience.

text.text:
Incredible Lebanese restaurant in Fishtown. I was blown away by the fatteh (eggplant) dish. They packed a ton of flavor into every bite.

The pita is made fresh in a wood fire oven, and packaged in paper bags to keep them warm, a nice touch.

Muhamurra was delicious, red peppery, very nutty, and a little sweet.

The layered dessert was also really good and had a lot of texture. Was expecting it to have more cake in it but it's more like an ice cream sundae.

Service was great. Quick, friendly, and let me charge my phone at the host desk.

The restaurant is huge with a massive outdoor patio. But the best spot in the house is the chef's counter so you can watch the action in the kitchen.

Would go back to try more next time I'm in Philly!

We went to Suraya in Fishtown, Philadelphia with a group of ten friends and had an amazing time! The Lebanese food was absolutely delicious — fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The cocktails were fantastic and paired perfectly with the meal.
The service was excellent, and the staff handled our large group with warmth and efficiency. The ambiance is stunning — vibrant yet cozy, with a great energy that makes you immediately feel at home.
I highly recommend Suraya for anyone looking for great food, drinks, and atmosphere in Philly. It’s truly one of the best dining experiences in the city!

We wanted some drinks it’s great that they have a pitcher options for big parties . Our server Violet was awesome ! We ordered multiple different things for everyone to try . Nachos (shrimp and birria) , aguachile, potatoes , a burger , fish tacos , steak tacos, all so delicious!   So good all of it ! I have to say those were some of the best fish tacos I’ve had in a while. When in doubt on what or where to go to eat in Philly come here ! Always a pleasure dining here ! Keep up the good work!

We sat outside since it was so hot out. The space isn’t huge, but it has enough room to enjoy both the outdoor seating and the bar area, and the inside is really cute too. The atmosphere felt relaxed and inviting, making it a nice spot for a laid-back meal
We started with the margarita pitcher mango, which was good but a little syrupy for my taste. For food, we had the shrimp and tuna ceviche, and it was delicious, super fresh, and one of the highlights of the meal. For entrees, we ordered the red snapper and the lobster dish, and both were absolutely a 10 out of 10 . I would go back just for those

Service was also really good: quick, friendly, and attentive without feeling rushed. We didn’t try dessert, but overall it was a great experience and a cute spot for a good meal in Philly.

text.text:
El emm enn-oh (and the P is for Philly.)

We throughly enjoyed our time celebrating life at this spot. So much to see, taste, hear, such little time. I wasn’t prepared for what I was getting ready to experience but I was completely delighted and will be returning for more. This restaurant concept feels like school for adults. I don’t know if that was the idea, but I want to be sent to the principal’s office.

Da’Mya was our wonderful, knowledgeable waitress. Even though she just started recently and was training with Alex, she knew her way around the menu and even suggested drinks and menu items to set the night off right. Conversationally open to our time travel banter and unsolicited advice, we’ll becoming back to continue exploring the LMNO menu, cocktails, and each atmosphere that the restaurant has to offer. The menu is always better when wait staff makes suggestions for palette and experience combined. We love a helpful & playful participant! Thanks Da’Mya & Alex, we can tell that you love what you do.

There’s a reading room, a listening room, bar area, outdoor area, and other different types of dining experiences. We gotta try them all, one by one. Can’t lie, we were most impressed with the listening room that we stumbled upon while going to the restroom. The portal to get there was an amazing happening, great touch. We love a speakeasy but especially love a speakeasy with a record collection. Bartender Ashley is beyond cutesy, adorbs really! We want her making our drinks and adding all of the sparkles. We couldn’t stay too long this time but we’ll be going straight to the speakeasy next time, put a password on it to keep it available when I return.

The food was great. We went for the drinks but couldn’t resist getting nachos. Definitely wanted to be greedy and get everything on the menu. Pace yourself young grasshopper, pace yourself.

The owners tug at my stomach and heart strings in the best way. They are clearly masters of vibes. LMNO for the win.

text.text:
We walked in on a Friday night for dinner and were lucky enough to be able to choose between spots at the main bar and the lounge room. The lounge was a bit quieter and the vibes were cooler so we chose there. Penthouse magazine covers lined the ceiling and in a dimly lit room with a disco ball. There was a huge vinyl collection and dj set up but nobody was spinning.

Bartenders were attentive and got us set up with a blended frozen mango margarita and a prickly pear margarita - both delicious. We split aguachile and spare rib enchiladas - both delicious as well and came with a side of rice and beans.

Atmosphere in the room was fun, with a mix of younger people drinking and/or eating. We sparked some random conversations as we ate, enjoying the atmosphere. Would recommend this spot, we only really checked out the lunge but the actual restaurant space looked liked it had a ton of seating and cool vibe as well.

text.text:
I thought I ordered the shrimp and tuna tostadas, but I believe what I received was the ceviche. Either way, fair warning: if you don’t like lime, do not get this. It’s very lime forward. That said, if you enjoy citrus, it’s good. The seasoned chips, cilantro, and avocado help balance the acidity and make it enjoyable.

The rice and beans were honestly the highlight. The rice doesn’t look heavily seasoned, but it’s incredibly flavorful buttery, savory, and perfectly cooked, not mushy at all. The beans have a noticeable kick, so if you prefer very mild food, keep that in mind. The spice pairs well with the richness of the rice.

I got the short rib enchiladas. The meat was the best part well cooked and flavorful but the enchiladas themselves were a bit on the drier side and slightly underwhelming compared to expectations.

Takeout was quick; I ordered in the restaurant and waited about 10 minutes. Overall, it’s a great option for a restaurant quality meal at home.

The ambiance inside is also beautiful, dark, calm, and luxurious with colorful yet monochromatic tones, textured furniture, and subtle industrial details around the bar. Very cute and well designed.

text.text:
Visited with reservation on a Friday night. Reservations via OpenTable. We were quickly greeted and seated and the team was very courteous. The manager also greeted us at our table to let us know she was available during our dining experience. We ordered the pictured dishes as well as their non alcoholic mocktail options which were very refreshing takes on standard cocktails like an Aperol spritz. The portion sizes were perfect for sharing and trying several different dishes. The flavors were robust and my favorite dish were the swordfish brochettes. Enjoyed the citrus fruit at the end of dinner which was a very sweet nightcap. Tables in the interior dining area are a little close together and it is very dim which made it a little challenging to read the menu.

$$
There is valet and very limited street parking (the rest isn't is in a residential area)

text.text:
Great hidden gem in Fishtown✨

Everything was fantastic to the apps, the ambiance, and even our server!

🍝 Food: We loved all the apps, and honestly for us we’d just get all apps if we could. The winter special monkfish was ok. And it was cool to try a new pasta “shape” for us: storzapretti e.g. look like meatballs, but are herby delicious ricotta balls with a snap. We loved the orata fish dish. WOW, perfectly cooked fish! For about $100 pp, we essentially got an XL 8-course tasting menu which is pretty worth it!

what we got:
⭐️ scallop focaccia toast 5/5 WOW! impressed, the flavor, the texture. more than just a fish-on-toast
⭐️ shaved artichoke 5/5 acidic goodness
⭐️ skate cheeks 4/5 great texture! flavor combo was amazing with the calabrian chili and polenta
⭐️ grilled orata 4/5 perfectly cooked with the buttery meat and crispy skin, tapenade was fire!
- tagliolini monkfish 3/5 not a fan gritty pieces in the pasta, monkfish felt a bit overcooked and tough
- storzapretti ricotta dumplings 3/5 glad to try something new!! not our thing

🍴 service: amazing! our server was attentive, helpful and sassy — we liked her. overall staff was great too, they brought the dishes and explained them and between courses they took plates and cleaned the table. very pleasurable :)

🕯️ atmosphere: the ambiance was intimate and sexy! there was not a bad angle of the interior — it was a classy date night spot

text.text:
I’ve very relieved to say my opinion has changed about Bastia! I recently visited this restaurant on Valentine’s Day and left an appropriate but sour review of this restaurant. After expressing my disappointment and concerns here on Google I was quickly emailed by the GM, Kim. She let me know how much herself and her staff valued my review and were very apologetic.
I was encouraged to come back and give it another shot. Kim let me know how much they would value the opportunity to redeem themselves and provide my partner and I with the proper Bastia experience free of charge. I could tell how much they cared, and I accepted this kind invitation back. Last night was the reservation on March 1st.
We were treated as VIP guests the minute we walked in the door. I could tell all staff was on notice, the host, our server, food runners… Everyone was very attentive and telling us how glad they were that we decided to give them another chance. I appreciated that very much!
We were greeted with a presentation of the history of Bastia, what regions inspire the cuisine, menu recommendations, details about specials, and right away we were asked about potential food allergies and our personal preferences.
To say the least, the service IMMEDIATELY stood out and was a vast improvement from our previous visit. Our food came out promptly, hot, beautifully plated and tasted exquisite.  We were gifted an additional appetizer from the chef during our first course and an extra scoop of gelati with our desert! The food was exceptional, our interactions with staff were pleasant, and we felt more than welcomed at Bastia!
I’m happy to say they out did themselves and changed my mind entirely. Night and day, truly.
Little did Bastia know they were catering to a surprise celebration for my girlfriend and I, as earlier in the day we found out we’re pregnant!
Aside from the great food and great staff, Bastia will forever hold a special place in my heart for being the place my partner and I shared a decadent meal together the first night finding out we are going to have a baby.
They again comped our entire ticket but I still left a substantial tip for our server who did an incredible job! Thank you Bastia, I will be back!!

text.text:
Probably my new favorite bakery in all of Philly, and I love bakeries

Food:
+ plain cornetti 100/10 my new fave pastry. flakey, layered, and egg-based? AMAZING, no notes!
+ gnudi 8/10 the sesame based sauce was incredible. I loved the texture and it was oh so creamy!
+ Dolce latte - was ok! they split it and made it in two separate glasses for us to try. I thought it was ok!

Service: amazing! the woman at the counter was fun, funny and helpful!

Atmosphere: I’m sure everyone is pleasant since they’re eating amazing food. BUT it is actually so sweet in there too!

note: it is first come first served seats. if you can, I recommend snagging a table and then waiting in line, which was through the whole store to the door when we went.

text.text: On the first floor is the bar and restaurant that has a pool table, second and third with the bar. This is by far my favorite small music venue in all of Philly. It really is the best vibe ever in there. For shows you can get pretty close to the performance, it’s pretty intimate and tight on the stage level but it can fit a lot of people, everyone’s standing having a great time. I absolutely love the balcony level and that standing room area. There’s a bar on every level! I usually get the tickets directly from their website, usually in the $20-30 range. I recommend being on the email list as well.

For shows you can get pretty close to the performance, it’s pretty intimate and tight on the stage level but it can fit a lot of people, everyone’s standing having a great time. I absolutely love the balcony level and that standing room area. There’s a bar on every level! I usually get the tickets directly from their website, usually in the $20-30 range. I recommend being on the email list as well.

text.text: It was my first time there on a Monday night. I was there for a DJ event and it was a nice vibe. I had a hibiscus margarita, which was lovely. The food smelled good so I tried a smash burger. It was juicy and came with crispy delicious fries. I was pleasantly surprised. Danced for a while on the second floor, my only complaint was too much 'smoke effect'. Other than that, definitely an enjoyable spot.

text.text: Went there when visiting, everything was mostly good. There wasn't a band playing that night, but atmosphere was bumpin and the food was decent. Their kitchen is open later than some of the other bars in the area. However, the host was a bit unwelcoming and had a rude attitude when we wanted to be seated which caught us off guard. He was berating us about whether we would be eating which was confusing because isn't that why you ask to be seated? One person in our group had allergies and didn't know if they would be able to eat. He said if we weren't all eating we had to go to the bar. We ended up getting seated but it felt we had to insist. I don't know if we will go back to dine because it seemed like they didn't want anyone actually dining? The server was super nice and helpful, so maybe the host just doesn't like having to walk 3 feet to sit patrons at a table? Might go back to check out a show, but I don't really like going places where employees make you feel like a burden for showing up.

text.text:
If you are not locals, you’re not cool enough to be served at this bar. Was there yesterday 6/23, popped in before the Spoon concert (visiting from Florida). The bartender was not great. WE greeted HIM at the bar. Before taking our drink order he disappeared for 10 mins. Then we were finally able to put in our order for a few beers. I got up and helped myself to menus since they were not offered. By the time he came back around to check on us our beers had been empty for a while and we were just feeling the unwelcoming service so we never got food. Although the food on the menu did look great.

We decided to come back after the concert to get food and give the staff another chance. We are arrived 15 mins before the advertised time of the kitchen being closed, we were told that they were no longer serving food. Although we did notice other customers placing orders. Again, it took about 15 mins to get a few beers.

Again, the staff projects the attitude that if you are not local, you are not welcome.

Cool atmosphere, menu looks delicious, fun crowd, snobby bartender.

Stopped in to grab some food. Ordered Diet Coke, got some weird off brand cola but was assured it was diet something. Ordered a cheeseburger which is described as a single beef patty, was asked how I wanted it and said I wanted it medium rare and added on lettuce, tomato and mayo which is listed as free.

And then waited for a very long time. There weren't many people there, maybe half a dozen others. When I got my burger it was a smash patty and no add ons. I'm not sure why it took so long to be so wrong. The pickle was also a lacto-fermented one or rotten, I'm not sure which but it was the sourest stomach bile tasting pickle I had ever had.

Staff was nice when they weren't awol. I overtipped because I didn't want to wait for my change after fifteen minutes of trying to get my check because staff just disappeared at one point.

My wife and I went and had a great time.  It was everything we were hoping for - good drinks, great vibe, and great live entertainment.

We had a couple rounds of drinks, and shared an appetizer.  All very good.  Absolutely nothing to complain about.

Ahead of the night, I spent a while trying to read reviews and it seemed like a mixed bag - not fair.

Here's the deal - it is a lively and fun atmosphere.  Servers are covering allot of ground while the performances are going on.  Sure, a drink took a few minutes to get, but it was a good drink!  And the food - you won't be disappointed so long as don't go expecting a Michelin star level of quality.

The earlier you arrive, the better seat you will have.  If you show at the time the show start, expect to have a limited view.  We showed up at 7 and the seats were were fine.  Next time, we'll target 6:30.

text.text:
Get ready to have a wonderful time. Fabrika hosts drag brunches, burlesque shows, wrestling events, and dance parties. The party seemingly never stops here. The décor is unique and a lot of fun. The use of lights and smoke sets the tone of the show and isn’t used excessively.

The staff is superb. They are all very attentive and friendly. Everyone from the greeters to the waitstaff to security are professional and top-notch. The venue uses a digital menu (QR code at the table) that also serves as the payment portal. The food is made well and the drinks are great. Definitely get your order in ASAP, especially at brunches.

Every show is fantastic. The entertainment you get is always at the highest level. The crowd is always cheering or singing along or just having a great time in general. I’ve seen bridal showers, anniversaries, birthdays, and everything in between being celebrated.

There are two floors with different seating options, such as tables, couches, or standing. Depending on the event, you may want to arrive early for the best seating (or secure a VIP spot, if available).

Fabrika has its own paid parking lot, as well as street parking. It’s not terribly difficult to find parking around the venue, although you may end up parking further than you thought you would. The paid lot uses a web portal that is super quick and easy to navigate.

Keep your eyes on Fabrika for a fun, delightful time.

Wm. Mulherin’s Sons is an absolute must-visit for brunch! The food was fantastic from start to finish.
We started with the Yellowtail Crudo, which was incredibly light and flavorful. The Ricotta Bomboloni were a total standout—they honestly could have been dessert! They had an amazing texture and a lovely hint of orange.
For our mains, both the Spaghetti Pomodoro and the Mezze Maniche Carbonara were executed to perfection. If you're looking for high-quality pasta and a great atmosphere, this is the spot.

The outdoor seating is pet-friendly which makes the whole vibe even better — good food, good drinks, and your furry mate by your side. What more do you need?
Pro tip: book a table if you're going on a weekend — it's popular for a reason and walk-in waits can be real.

text.text: Great experience here! Beautiful dark mahogany wood serves up a classy vibe! This modern Italian joint serves up some delicious thin style pizzas and a great range of cocktails. We started with the grilled charred octopus and man was this a flagship dish! Huge tender and juicy octopus perfectly charred with a crunchy exterior yet soft interior! Paired with a delicious pesto arugula, this could have and should have been my meal! We got the Downtown abbey pizza and the Spicy Jawn pizza! The spicy jawn was way better, the sauce was tangy yet had a kick to it and was loaded with spicy meats! The downtown abbey was tasty yet, not standout. The focaccia itself was tasty but the ricotta whip could have used a bit more salt or seasoning!

text.text:
Food was mediocre and made without love. Atmosphere is amazing.

Ordered:
Radicchio Salad
Tagliatelle Lamb Ragu
Sweet Jawn Pizza

Radicchio salad was pretty good and tasteful, but the presentation of the dish was dreadful. The radicchio was too large of chunks, our garnish was all on one side of the plate and on one radicchio leaf. Salad had appropriate amount of dressing, but wasn't tossed in the dressing or it was sitting out for too long because it pooled at the bottom.

Tagliatelle was quite disappointing. There’s too much thyme on that plate. Too much thyme. So much herb on there it completely overpowers the rest of the plate. Also it says it’s a "ragu," but it really seems like a few chunks of sausage with a vodka sauce.

Pizza was decent and made well, no complaints.

None of our food came out hot which seemed off, like it wasn’t even sitting under a heat lamp.
Seems like presentation from the kitchen needs an overhaul. Expo or head chef isn't looking at the dishes before they're sent out. The clumps of gremolata on the Tagliatelle is pathetic.

Portion sizes are okay, on the smaller size. 1 app, 2 entrees is barely enough for 2 people. The prices for the plates are about good. Came to ~$140 for 2 people, yikes.

Drinks were pretty good.

Atmosphere is amazing. We were on the patio, so we didn’t get to see too much inside but everywhere you look is eye candy.

I don’t recommend going here for food, but it is an amazing place to enjoy with friends.

Mamajuana Cafe Philly has a lively atmosphere with a vibrant interior and a good energy, especially during busier hours. The space feels more like a mix between a restaurant and lounge, which makes it a fun spot for groups or a night out.

The food overall was solid. The skirt steak was very good—well-cooked, flavorful, and one of the highlights of the meal. Some of the appetizers and smaller dishes were decent, though not particularly standout.

Drinks were a strong point—the cocktail I had was good, refreshing and well-balanced.

Service was fine, though it can get a bit busy, which may impact timing. Overall, it’s a good place if you’re looking for a lively dining experience with solid food and drinks.

Brunch at Cedar Point Bar & Kitchen was outstanding! The drinks were delicious — especially the Manhattan, which was top notch.

Every dish we tried was full of flavor. The wings paired with crispy Brussels sprouts were fantastic, and the chicken thigh was perfectly seasoned. The hummus spring salad with pickled onions added a fresh, bright touch to the meal. And my personal favorite — the sausage gravy over biscuits — was rich, comforting, and done just right.

The home fries really impressed me too. I always judge a breakfast by the potatoes, and these were cooked and seasoned perfectly — they definitely passed the test!

Overall, a great brunch spot with excellent food and drinks. We’ll definitely be back.

The hummus spring salad with pickled onions added a fresh, bright touch to the meal. And my personal favorite — the sausage gravy over biscuits — was rich, comforting, and done just right.

The home fries really impressed me too. I always judge a breakfast by the potatoes, and these were cooked and seasoned perfectly — they definitely passed the test!

Overall, a great brunch spot with excellent food and drinks. We’ll definitely be back.

text.text:
The food itself was five stars. The only reason reason there is one star left out, and this just goes for being vegan. There was a little bit of uncertainty about some of the sauces and after having our server find out what was in them there was no problem. I didn’t want to be too critical.
This was a Google search to find a place with vegan options and wow, I have to say this was an amazing find it’s nestled in the heart of Fishtown just off of Frankford Avenue. What a really cool place. Aside from my pet sauce peeve.
This place has the best vegan wings out of the 10 places we have tried that serve vegan wings, so far. For us most places over fry the seitan and it turns out a little bit like jerky so when we go into a restaurant and order seitan wings, we ask to lightly fry them which they did and in this case, they were done perfectly crispy on the outside, tender on the inside With a great buffalo sauce, and this order is served with Brussels that are also deep-fried and they were done just as well.
Second dish we ordered was something I’ve never had before Bahn mi lettuce cups,
Consisted of house mushroom walnut, pate, baked tofu, pickled veggies, seaweed and herbs, and a vegan aïoli on the side. Theses were simply food at its best perfectly done tofu the pickle veggies were a great balance of sweet with a tiny bit of salt. The leaves are handpicked to make it easy to wrap the ingredients, whoever is in the kitchen knows exactly what they’re doing.
The final dish we shared was the red curry cheesesteak made with pulled oats cooked in a red curry sauce with vegan cheese, green peppers and caramelized onions. Just look at the picture. It tasted better than the picture looks. We have had many cheesesteak wraps and vegan cheesesteaks served on Italian rolls, and this is the best Served on a fresh Italian roll, tough call to make there are so many great vegan cheesesteaks out there, best vegan cheesesteak wrap being the joy Café.
The rest of the menu is a great mix of sandwiches seafood burgers that anybody would find enticing. They put a lot of love into this menu and what a great atmosphere the outdoor seating is on the corner as you’ll see what a great way to wind down the summer hope to get back here within the next few weeks .

text.text:
Great little find. Just down the street from Hotel Anna & Bel, where we were staying. This local bar & kitchen fit the bill when we wanted a filling meal after a long day of sightseeing.

We ordered a Cedar Point Cobb Salad (it was delicious & big) and a specialty grilled cheese sandwich. The fries were delicious and plentiful. Service was great, and we ended the evening with a specialty cocktail—wish I could remember the name, but it was tasty.

We were here in January, but I'm sure during warmer weather, the patio would be fun to enjoy and people-watch. Great little spot in Fishtown!

Definitely recommend. Note: 20% gratuity is added to the bill automatically. Not a problem for us, as we always appreciate good service.

text.text:
Picnic is a Philly Staple for a Reason

Picnic is the real deal. Put together by some of the best in the restaurant world, this place has earned its spot as a Philly favorite and you feel that the moment you walk in.

The flavors are bold and unapologetic, and everything pairs with the proteins in a way that just makes sense. It’s the kind of food that makes you stop mid-bite and contemplate life. The service matches the energy perfectly — upscale without being stuffy, relaxed without being sloppy. Honestly, I was impressed before the food even hit the table.

Whether you’re celebrating something special or just want to show someone why Philly’s food scene is one of the best in the world, this is the move. Bring your people — they’ll thank you.

Highly recommend, no hesitation.

FYI, reservations are pretty hard to come by.

We live nearby and have always wanted to try this place. It's been a minute since I left a restaurant so disappointed.

Let's start with the good: the food was okay. The Lebanon Bologna and Melon was refreshing.

The rest was… meh…

We were three, and we shared everything; the waiter didn't seem to care that we were sharing everything and could have suggested more food, or at least shown some knowledge of the menu and asked us how hungry we were. We could have spent more money had we been offered more food. The food we ordered was not enough. I left hungry, and we went to OG Pizzeria right across from Post Haste to get a slice of pizza.

Mind you, we spent almost $100 per person including tips.

Don't expect the bar to make simple cocktails like an espresso martini or a dirty one; apparently, it's beneath them to make regular cocktails, and the amount of time we heard “we actually don't do…” was a bit too much.

The staff in general seems like they don't enjoy working there, and the only one who was nice to us was the host.

It took us 3 years to get there, and we will probably not be going back.

text.text:
This place is such a vibe.

A solid staple for whenever you're craving good food, good coffee and a no frills environment that makes you feel like you're dining in a time capsule from the 1960's and beyond.

When you walk you're greeted by  mirror paned walls speckled with random pieces of Philly nostalgia. Booths line one side while a counter lines the other and while the initial interpretation might leave you worried about having to wait, the place is quite spacious albeit narrow.

Before even being seated, the waitress turned her head while walking us to the table and said, I'll get cha's wooder and coffee, k?

Absolutely. Love it already.

The menu is a mix blend of classics and imaginative spins. For our brunch we opted for "The Fishtown Scrapettizer" which is not your typical pork-centric scrapple. No, this scrapple is freaking delicious. Made with white fish and fried in a thick square, placed a top of thick sliced tomato with a zesty mayo-based sauce then topped with a fried egg and sliced pepperoncini.

Definitely order this.

Next we opted for the "Shopsins Scramble" which came with eggs scrambled with blue cheese, bacon, baby spinach and avocado + choice of toast and potatoes or hash browns. I opted for rye and hash and both were delicious. All in all a good option and the blue cheese was an interesting addition to eggs I've never had before.

Next was the classic #2 (2 eggs + 2 pancakes.+ choice of meat. Option for cheddar, American or Cooper Sharp for the cheese).

Love the option for Cooper sharp and the bacon was perfectly crispy. Overall a good dish. Have heard fantastic things about their buttermilk pancakes and while solid, not completely blown away (there's a clubhouse near by that still can't be beat when it comes to breakfast cakes).

Note that prices fluctuate bc of eggs so what's listed on the menu isn't what you'll likely see reflected on your check. And speaking of, this place is a classic CASH ONLY (but they do have an ATM in the back).

Sullimays. A sweet soulful spot that is a great place to grab breakfast or brunch with a group of good people.

text.text:
Fishtown Diner Review

Google Maps leads you right to the front door. Street parking is available (when you can find it), or you can use a nearby shopping plaza a few blocks away and then walk a short distance to the diner. Upon entering, we were greeted by smiling faces, a warm dose of Philadelphia nostalgia, and murals gracing nearly every wall. We were seated in front of a mural featuring the Liberty Bell, a subway train car, a Fishtown bus, the Love Statue, and of course my favorite, the Rocky statue with the art museum in the background. Behind the register, another mural pays homage to local sports legends: the Philadelphia Eagles, Flyers, 76ers, and Phillies, celebrating the city's rich heritage. The diner offers a mix of tables, booths, and counter seating, while the menu boasts plenty of choices at reasonable prices. We arrived at 11:30 AM, and the atmosphere really picks up around noon, so I recommend getting there before 12 if you can.

Now, let’s talk about the food. I enjoyed this experience with my wife and kiddo. My kiddo ordered the cookies and cream milkshake, which was rich and creamy, and he also tried the boston crème short stack pancakes. Although the portion was so large he couldn’t finish them, so come hungry! My wife, who has a gluten allergy, opted for the salmon and grits served with a fruit cup instead of bread. The salmon was cooked to perfection without tasting frozen or dried out, and its flavor was spot on. As for me, I went with the Fishtown omelet, accompanied by home fries and rye toast. When the server asked if I wanted peppers and onions with the home fries, I couldn’t resist when in Rome, right? Overall, the food was fantastic and the dining experience was truly memorable. Shout out to our server, Kat, you were awesome!

text.text: Food was excellent. It tasted like I was back in Southern Thailand. We went on a Friday, they only had the tasting menu. You pick one appetizer, one curry, one entree, two sides, and one dessert from the menu for the table. You also get two dumpling dishes for the table. The food was served family style and portioned based on the number of people. We've been to Southern Thailand many times and loved spicy food. So, we chose dishes that reminded us of our trips. It definitely didn't disappoint. The flavor profiles were spot on. For us, the spice level was more like a 7 of 10. It was hot but still enjoyable. A lot of places we ate in Southern Thailand, the spicy dishes tend to be a 10 or 11 out of 10. I would come back. However, we would come back Sunday-Thursday. The amount of food in the tasting menu was too much for us and we were staying in a hotel, not ideal for a doggy bag.

text.text:
What an absolutely amazing experience. Knowing how popular this restaurant is, I made reservations a few weeks in advance. We arrived early and were quickly shown to our seats. We both saw the 'Taste of Kalaya' which goes for $85 per person. It comes with a few sharable appetizers, an entree and dessert served family style.

Starting off with their Shaw Muang which are flower shaped dumplings with ground chicken, cucumber and a Thai chili, these were phenomenal. Simple, but beautifully presented. The fact these bite-sized dumplings were packed full of flavor and texture were extraordinary. Next were the Gui Chai which are crispy garlic chive rice cakes with a spicy sweet soy sauce. These were also tasty, but I would have preferred a thicker accompanying sauce that coats the rice cake after each dip, rather running right off it. We were also able to choose an extra appetizer, which we opted in for Plah Hoy Namg Rom which are grilled oysters with a chili jam, crispy shallot, lemongrass and herbs. These looked beautiful, but I felt the flavours overpowered the natural taste of the oyster.

For mains, we opted in for the Goong Thod Kluae which is their wok-fried river prawn in brown butter w. shrimp paste and seafood nam jim, Gaeng Pae which is a goat and lamb curry with their own spice blend and toasted coconut, and Gai Yaang Naa Por (add-on, extra charge) which is charcoal grilled chicken glazed with coconut cream, turmeric, dark soy and fish sauce.

The river prawn was phenomenal. The fact this was the size of a lobster was a huge wow-factor. It's served tableside where the head butter is first removed, then the succulent meat, and finally topped with the head butter. Presentation-wise, not that prettiest thing, but the flavours were incredible. Perhaps as the server is dissecting the river prawn, they could move it onto a clean plate with garnishes to make it look more presentable. Nevertheless, this is one of the best dishes I've had anywhere.

The goat and lamb curry was slightly disappointing. We found it to be overly spicy where we couldn't taste the goat and/or lamb in the dish. We're not shy when it comes to spicy food, but this set our mouths ablaze and it was difficult to take 2nd and 3rd bites from this particular dish.

For the charcoal grilled chicken was decent. I found parts of the dish to be on the dry side and other parts to be tender and juicy. I didn't necessarily taste the coconut cream or turmeric, but it was a decent dish.

For sides, we opted in for the Yum Makhua Yao which is marinated eggplant w. mint, galangal, fried shallots and prik nam pla, and the Moo Tod Nam Pla which is crispy pork belly w. fish sauce.

The eggplant was a nice side dish to take a break from the main courses and the crispy pork belly was nice as well. Crispy, not overly fatty or oily, and would have preferred that as a main over the goat and lamb curry.

For dessert, we saw a couple of our favourites but with a twist. We opted in for their Durian Sticky Rice (Great spin on a traditional mango sticky rice) and their Thai tea tiramisu (a spin on your traditional tiramisu which comes with coffee-soaked ladyfingers).

The durian sticky rice was out of this world. Durian in place of mango was brilliant. Perfectly ripe, soft and was a breathtaking dessert. As for the tiramisu, this was fantastic as well. The Thai tea flavour didn't shine through as much as I would have liked, but overall, excellent.

It's worth noting, the service at this restaurant is impeccable. Probably one of the best hospitalities I've received anywhere. The servers reset your table in between courses by wiping it off and everyone was professional, knowledgeable and kind.

Overall, I can see why this is listed on the top 50 restaurants in the U.S. coming in at #11 according to 'theworlds50best'. The quality of food, the service, atmosphere is top notch.

Today (July 24), I drove over an hour after watching a halal food reel on Instagram, and it was one of the most disappointing restaurant experiences I’ve had.

The first impression wasn’t great. There was no visible halal sign and it was just a pickup window.

Then came the service. The girl wearing glasses was unbelievably rude. She stayed on her phone and acted as if taking my order was a burden. I genuinely felt like I was bothering her just by ordering food. A simple greeting, smile, or basic customer service seemed too much to ask. I’m honestly shocked that people describe the staff here as friendly. The other girl was polite, but the girl with glasses completely ruined the experience.

Food ratings:

* Vegetable Dumplings: 1/5
* Tiger Fried Rice: 4/5
* Honey Garlic Shrimp Lo Mein: 3/5
* Hibiscus Lemon Iced Tea: 0/5 — it tasted like plain water with red coloring.

The food wasn’t entirely bad, but customer service matters just as much. I would never hire someone with that attitude to interact with customers. Because of the rude service alone, I would not return to this location, even though some of the food was decent.

Absolutely Delicious! A Must-Try Spot!
Today was our first time visiting Amy’s Pastellios, and to say we enjoyed it would be an understatement. We originally discovered it through a post on Instagram, and since my brother lives in PA, we decided to give it a try—and we’re so glad we did!
The flavors were on point! I’m a pretty picky eater, but every flavor combination we tried absolutely hit the spot. My personal favorites were the yuca and gandules pastellitos (which are vegan!), the fried cheese with guava, the arroz con gandules, and the yuca en escabeche—all full of flavor and beautifully balanced.
My family also loved the chicken, beef, margarita, and mushrooms with cheese options. Each one had its own distinct taste and was clearly made with care and quality ingredients.
I wish I had taken better pictures (I snapped them mid-meal because we couldn’t wait to dig in!), but trust me—the food speaks for itself.
We’ll definitely be back!

text.text:
I grew up with and around Boricuas my whole life, so when I saw a highly rated rican spot, I happily made my way over.

I absolutely loved the interior design, the music, and the friendly service. I wish that reflected in the food :(

I was in disbelief from the mediocre food, even worse when I got food poisoning from their pollito (chicken) bowl.

The tostones were pleasant! I loved crunchiness and saltiness paired with the avocado which made me look forward to eating the rest of the bowl. When I took the first bite of chicken, it was barely warm and shockingly seasonless.

The arroz con gandules was nothing like I've had before. It had this cheesy like (or something similar) after taste. Maybe it was the ancho or cumin they used. I couldn't taste the sofrito at all. That's the holy grail for this type of rice!!

I kept eating it because I wanted to it a fair chance. Perhaps it's a different style or an off day. As I kept forking my food, I noticed there was a pool of grease and water on the bottom of my bowl. I hate food waste, but I had to regrettably trash the rest.

I was willing to come back, honestly. Until I had food poisoning, that was enough to discourage me from coming back.

1st and last time here! I thought that I'd swing by and get an order of fries on my way home. The kiosks for ordering are convenient, and that part was painless. I know that the young lady there that greeted me and handed me my food was trying her best to be nice to everyone, but the whole interaction felt surrealistic and robotic. They really charged me almost $6.00 for barely a handful of cold fries that were dry and stale and tasted like soft pencils in rancid oil. She handed those fries not even a minute after I ordered, so there's no way that the order was actually freshly made. They literally grabbed whatever was lying at the bottom of the basket, tossed it in 2 containers and a paper bag, and called it a day. I asked the lady if it was really a full order of fries. She looked at it and said yes. I told her that it doesn't seem right, and she checked the ticket simply to confirm that I ordered what I ordered. I thanked her for robbing me, and she continued with her robotic toxic-positivity as I left vowing to never go there again. If you're going to rip folks off on your burgers, then the least you could do is come correct with the fries like 5 Guys. If this is just a location thing then that sucks, but if that small handful of fries is their corporate policy, then I hope the company goes under. Maybe try giving out two small handfuls of fries per order and make due with one less yacht or something. Gross, overpriced food served by fake robotic people just going through the motions.

Editing to add that perhaps they redeemed themselves or maybe they just give you more when ordering cheese fries, but I gave them another chance yesterday and I was satisfied with the, not exactly generous amount but at a least reasonable, amount of cheese fries. 1st and last time here! I thought that I'd swing by and get an order of fries on my way home. The kiosks for ordering are convenient, and that part was painless. I know that the young lady there that greeted me and handed me my food was trying her best to be nice to everyone, but the whole interaction felt surrealistic and robotic. They really charged me almost $6.00 for barely a handful of cold fries that were dry and stale and tasted like soft pencils in rancid oil. She handed those fries not even a minute after I ordered, so there's no way that the order was actually freshly made. They literally grabbed whatever was lying at the bottom of the basket, tossed it in 2 containers and a paper bag, and called it a day. I asked the lady if it was really a full order of fries. She looked at it and said yes. I told her that it doesn't seem right, and she checked the ticket simply to confirm that I ordered what I ordered. I thanked her for robbing me, and she continued with her robotic toxic-positivity as I left vowing to never go there again. If you're going to rip folks off on your burgers, then the least you could do is come correct with the fries like 5 Guys. If this is just a location thing then that sucks, but if that small handful of fries is their corporate policy, then I hope the company goes under. Maybe try giving out two small handfuls of fries per order and make due with one less yacht or something. Gross, overpriced food served by fake robotic people just going through the motions.

Editing to add that perhaps they redeemed themselves or maybe they just give you more when ordering cheese fries, but I gave them another chance yesterday and I was satisfied with the, not exactly generous amount but at a least reasonable, amount of cheese fries. They were salted well and everyone there was kind and helpful. Thanks.

My Thoughts on US vs. Japan vs. Thailand
Having tried Shake Shack in the US, Japan, and Thailand, I've developed some strong opinions on where each excels.
For me, the burgers in the US are the clear winner. They just hit different – the flavor balance is absolutely perfect, and everything comes together so harmoniously.
However, when it comes to milkshakes, the US version is far too sweet for my liking. The milkshakes in Japan, on the other hand, are the best!

text.text:
Philadelphia boasts an abundance of fantastic Asian dining spots, and this restaurant stands out among them. After passing by numerous times, I finally seized the opportunity to step inside. Although it’s somewhat petite, the place exudes a warm coziness, and I truly admire the effort they've invested in the restaurant's decor.

The layout is quite straightforward, featuring a delightful mix of seating options, including cozy four-tops, one impressive six-top table, and some window seats. I couldn’t help but appreciate the tables within; they appear hand-crafted, boasting extremely sturdy wooden designs with eye beams for legs. Sitting at these tables is a pleasure, as there's absolutely no tilt or wobble—a refreshing change from the usual restaurant experience where tables can be uneven and tend to rock.

Each table is thoughtfully equipped with a condiment tray, which features a delightful Asian spice shaker filled with white sesame seeds and one of my personal favorites: hot chili oil. For our entrées, I opted for the vegan pho, while one friend selected the Tonkatsu ramen, and the other went for tempura shrimp ramen. All three dishes were authentically delicious—the photos tell the story, so be sure to check them out. Our server was exceptional and made for a wonderful host. Without a doubt, we will be returning!

text.text:
Nice little ramen shop. Interestingly I was thinking of getting sushi, searched on Google and this place popped up. No sushi to be found on the menu when I arrived though.

Arrived on a quiet Sunday night, and ordered the signature Ramen, the chashu Don, and chicken karrage.

The chicken karrage was fresh and delicious, but it was $10 so I certainly wonder if it was worth the price.

The ramen, as warned by some other reviewers, was quite bland, despite having two chilli peppers on the menu, it was not spicy at all, though I’m not complaining about that given my low spice tolerance. The broth was simply lacking in depth and I had to add salt to enhance it, though it ended up being too salty afterwards. It also doesn’t help that I had Ichiran in Manhattan the day before so it was clearly a deviation in quality. Though Ichiran was double the price of this.

The pork and eggs in the ramen were wonderful however, tender, sweet, and full of flavor. This applies for the chashu don as well, because of the tenderness and flavor of the meat, it is top notch and I certainly would return/order again for the don but not the ramen.

The ramen here is good, not great. Very solid for hitting that craving, though, and looks great if you're trying to show off to your friends!

We ordered a bunch of different items, takoyaki, karage chicken bowl, signature ramen, curry mini rice bowl and tan tan ramen.

Takoyaki was solid, hit the spot and exactly what I want in a takoyaki. The karage chicken was crunchy and we enjoyed the sauce that came with it. The chashu in signature ramen is to die for, sooo tender (maybe just lacking a bit of flavor?) and the soft boiled eggs were perfect. I would say the biggest thing missing in the ramen is that I felt it was missing the usual richness that you get with a good ramen bowl. The broth felt a bit thin for ramen. The mini curry rice bowl was also good, but I think the curry was also a tiny bit lacking flavor - maybe I should have added more salt.

Overall would still dine here for a ramen craving but don't expect the best ramen you've ever had here.

text.text:
How do they manage to achieve this? What is the secret to crafting an ambiance that seamlessly blends coziness, warmth, trendiness, and a touch of romance? Although I may not possess the precise answer, I can say that every time I step foot into a Loco Pez restaurant, it immediately feels like they have set the benchmark for all of these qualities. It’s as if they’ve uncovered the hidden formula—unveiled the secret or devised the ultimate guide, whichever phrase you prefer. All three of the locations I have visited have been absolutely remarkable in every conceivable aspect. I’ve patronized their other establishments on numerous occasions and have consistently enjoyed nothing short of exceptional experiences. I genuinely cannot believe I delayed my visit to this particular location for so long.

It’s challenging to articulate, but I believe this one might just be my favorite—though I express this with a tinge of mixed feelings, as every location provides an excellent experience while also being distinct in its own right. Consistently, Loco Pez never disappoints when it comes to delivering the finest food, outstanding service, and an inviting atmosphere, time after time. While I have yet to meet the owners, I wholeheartedly tip my hat to them—whoever they may be—and express my sincere gratitude for offering what I regard as a place I can confidently call home.

Today, I opted for the vegan nachos which include freshly prepared tortilla chips, perfectly refried beans, vegan cheese, vegan sour cream, pico de gallo, jalapeños, seitan, and guacamole. Just take a moment to admire the picture; it truly conveys everything about this dish. Surprisingly, it tastes even better than it appears, if such a thing is conceivable. It’s simply extraordinary how effortlessly they execute this, although I’m certain a significant amount of hard work goes into it. They consistently excel.

My friend chose to order what I typically opt for, which are the vegan tacos that feature three different types of vegan treats. Meanwhile, our other friend decided to go for the shrimp and pez, carne asada, and pollo tinga tacos. Again, take a glance at the photos—phenomenal is an understatement that we often use every time we visit. To cap it all off, we cannot forget about the drinks—the drinks, oh the drinks! Yes, I mentioned them three times, as they are invariably delightful. I enjoyed the Coupe Deville, which included nonalcoholic tequila, blood orange purée, lime juice, and a spicy cinnamon rim. I fondly refer to this as a “baby sipper,” as you definitely don’t want to rush through it; it’s too delicious to finish quickly, so take your time and savor every drop.

One of my friends opted for the Ventura Boulevard cocktail, made with mango habanero-infused tequila, lime, mango, and a delightful Chamoy and Tajin rim. It was simply delightful. We couldn’t resist sharing sips of each other's drinks, while our third friend stuck to her usual choice of a straightforward margarita, which always brings a smile to her face. Our server, Jessica, was truly exceptional—just an all-around lovely person. She was remarkably knowledgeable about both the menu and the drink offerings and was always attentive, hitting the mark with everything she offered us. I find this level of service at every location. I’m not quite sure what their hiring process entails, but they’ve certainly nailed it.

I wholeheartedly recommend this venue to anyone interested in enjoying a fantastic time with loved ones or seeking an intimate dining experience. The music playlists at each location, while varied, are always outstanding. I can’t rave enough about this establishment. If it were possible to rate beyond five stars, I would gladly award it two additional stars. Just thinking about what they’ve managed to create brings a smile to my face.

text.text:
We finally decided to try Tulip after hearing so many wonderful things, and the atmosphere was just as charming as expected. Our table by the front was lovely, and both the food and service were pleasant overall.

The only disappointment came with the prix fixe policy. We had mentioned to our server that we didn’t want the prix fixe menu and instead chose to share a couple of appetizers and three pasta dishes among the four of us. After the meal arrived, the manager kindly stopped by but explained that our order technically counted as prix fixe, so we’d be charged $55 per person. It was a surprise and took a bit away from an otherwise nice evening.

The pasta was tasty — fresh and nicely prepared — but felt a bit pricey given the final total (around $400 for four people, including drinks).

Tulip has a lot of potential, and I can see why people enjoy it. My suggestion would be to simplify or remove the prix fixe option and perhaps make the wine pricing a bit more approachable, especially since the wines come from the same owned winery. A few small tweaks could make the experience feel much more inviting.

Overall, a pleasant dinner with great company, but I hope to see some refinements before returning.

text.text:
Interstate Drafthouse has the feel of a true neighborhood bar. There’s a great outdoor seating area right next to a park, and the place was full of families. It made me wonder—is Fishtown just packed with families, or does the park send everyone here?
Their cheesesteak menu offers several different proteins, and after chatting with the very friendly bartender, I took the recommendation and ordered the Kielbasa Cheesesteak with tots.
First, let’s talk about the tots. Outstanding. Crispy, golden, and exactly what tots should be.
The kielbasa itself was excellent. Am I completely sold on kielbasa cheesesteaks? Not yet. That might just be my old-school thinking. I still believe kielbasa belongs on a soft pretzel roll with spicy mustard.
That said, if you’re going to order a kielbasa cheesesteak, this is a very good version. The beer selection is excellent, the staff is welcoming, and the atmosphere makes Interstate Drafthouse the kind of neighborhood spot you’ll want to come back to—even if you’re not there for the cheesesteak..

I really had high hopes for this restaurant, considering I drove all the way from Cobbs Creek area. The external was beautiful. Narrow-like entrance, side lined with cute tables. Then you walk into a huge bar which actually felt welcoming. It was close to 7pm so the overcast from the clouds made it feel medieval for some reason. Anyways, the banter between the the gentleman and I was reassuring I would return to try their other meats!

Unfortunately, the mac and cheese, which is what I was feein for, taste like box Kraft mac and it was dry. It was Shiney like cheese but dry when you bite it.

Pulled pork sandwich had so much meat on there I could have made another sandwich! Lol. Demolished . Flavor amazing and sauce!

My mom ordered the ribs but from what I nibbled, they were really good and so was the reg BBQ sauce. Can't do spicy so idk what that one taste like.

Lastly, the spicy slaw I asked for on the side, I just didn't like it.

Hubby and I wanted to try something new and we LOVE BBQ, we’re from out of town and was in the area so we ended up here.

Shredded beef was good, better with the sweet bbq sauce
Wings ( if cooked a little longer) good flavor
Mac and cheese was ok
Brisket VERY fatty no flavor
Baked Beans was still hard, ok flavor
Collard Greens, meh, strong vinegar taste
The slaw, potato salad and broccoli salad were THE WORSE SIDES EVER! All of them taste like vinegar, bitter and bland!

So out of everything we only liked 3 items….very disappointed and not worth the money. Won’t consider coming back or recommending this place. Wish we could get our money back honestly.

Happy Hour Chicken Legs $4 for 2 legs!

I hurt my own chicken leg this weekend skiing on some icy spring slopes up north, but Adam and I couldn't pass up this Happy Hour deal when we heard about it. So, I sucked it up and hobbled on over for some chickie legs - totally worth it. Great bang for your buck, and the extra protein will go towards my speedy recovery! Deviled eggs were devilishly eggs!

Adam: Chicken Chicken read all about it! And we dids and then ordered 4 orders! These 8 chicken legs didn't last 5 minutes between my sweet Jamie and I. The meat was moist, practically falling off the bone. There was a residual smokeyness engrained in the meat that filled your mouth with each bite. The chicken was plenty flavorful by itself but of course imma sauce boss and couldn't resist a dip into their wide variety of homemade sauces; vinegar, sweet, and spicy!! Ooooooweeeee I think we owe those chicken dinner after we were done with em'

OG Pizza: This pizza truly exceeded my expectations. From the first bite, it’s clear that only top-quality ingredients are used — everything tastes remarkably fresh and well-balanced. The dough deserves special mention: perfectly textured, with just the right balance of chewiness and crispness. It’s clear a lot of care and craft go into the preparation.

While the price point is a touch higher than average, the quality more than justifies it. In fact, I found it so good that I ordered four pizzas in just two days — and I’d do it again without hesitation. This is pizza done right: simple, skillful, and absolutely satisfying.

text.text:
There’s a newish Pizza Spot in Fishtown and baby it’s the place to be!
So first off the vibe - it’s casual yet bougie, I love the green tiles, open concept, patio area. It’s inviting and for the awkward penguins who don’t like direct interaction, there’s a kiosk you can pick your slices or pies from.
The food- So this is not just another pizzeria, the owner a “youngin” has Pizza in his soul, he comes from a family who specialized in pies, so you are getting that NY style pie, but with a philly flare. I tried a few slices and each one was amazing.
For the wow factor- try the caviar slice, because you deserve it! It’s based on a creamy garlicky slice, limited edition!
It’s the kind of place you go to enjoy a slice of pizza without feeling guilty. It’s delicious, it’s crisp, it’s fresh.

text.text:
This was one of our most memorable dinners of 2025 so far — everything we ordered was delicious.

We started with the marinated tomatoes with stracciatella and the focaccia, then had the Thai basil tagliatelle with crab and the breaded pork chop as mains, and finished with the corn brûlée and blueberry pâte à choux for dessert.

The marinated tomatoes with the focaccia were an excellent pairing, and the tagliatelle was a surprisingly delightful fusion — spicy, flavorful, and very well balanced. The pork chop was excellent too: juicy and flavorful, though slightly undercooked near the bone. The corn brûlée was fantastic, while the pâte à choux was the only dish that didn’t quite hit the mark.

Overall, the food was outstanding and the space was very cozy. Our only wish was for slightly better ventilation in the restaurant, but otherwise, it was an amazing dining experience.

text.text:
Cook and Shaker is a cozy corner bar that just reopened after renovations!

The bar was huge with nice ambient lighting. There were also lots of high tops around the restaurant, plenty of seating in an open space.

One of the bartenders, Tori, gave us samples of their espresso martini which was SO delicious. One of the best I’ve had in Philly. Highly recommend.

For food, we got the cook and shaker salad, popcorn chicken and their special of the night which was a pizza steak sandwich with vodka sauce. The salad was fresh and delicious, the croutons seemed homemade (the best). The popcorn chicken was heavily breaded which I personally like, but my friend wasn’t a fan. If you like crispy small pieces of chicken, you’ll enjoy these.

We were unfortunately not a fan of the pizza steak sandwich. We got it because of the vodka sauce, but we couldn’t taste that at all. We swapped it for a grilled cheese, which was just okay.

Overall, we loved the atmosphere, espresso martini and some of the food. I will definitely come back in the future to try more things!

text.text:
I decided to check out this place based on the glowing reviews, but others are severely overselling it unless this is just the standard in Philly. As a transplant, I can’t understand the hype.

Staff was really nice and helpful. They great everyone who walks in, which does not seem to be the going rate in Philly.

I ordered the meatloaf special because it was recommended and I assumed I’d be coming back and could check out the menu then. It looked fantastic, so I was excited to try it. But it had a one-dimensional onion flavor to it, but at least it wasn’t dry. The potatoes that came with it were unseasoned and under salted.

As for drinks, the Smoke Show was phenomenal - interesting, well balanced flavors of mezcal, green chartreuse, and jalapeño with a maraschino cherry garnish. It was so good that I was convinced to try another drink. I was stuck between two choices, then the bartender said the Olde Richmond Punch was his favorite. I can’t imagine why. It simply tastes of whiskey and lemon - none of the honey nor rosemary came through. And I can see why if the rosemary incorporation was simply a few floating rosemary leaves. It didn’t taste bad, but it was nowhere near the caliber of drink as the Smoke Show.

Overall ⭐️⭐️⭐️/5

text.text:
Cook & Shaker is back after renovations! This was my favorite local spot after recently moving here and I'm so happy to see it back open and better than ever! They still have the same amazing food, craft beer, and cocktails and the new space is huge and beautiful. There is 3 times the amount of dining space and the bar is twice the size now with 30 seats. There is also a huge new window letting in tons of natural light and sunset views, that's opened during good weather. Now with many huge tvs it is the perfect place to watch any sports game!

You'll come for the game and stay for the food and drinks:) I got the weekly Sunday 16$ dinner special that comes with 1 draft beer and 1 sandwhich. I got the cod filet sandwich and the dragonfruit mango sour draft beer. Both were phenomenal! The hours and menu is currently updated only on Instagram, as well as daily dinner specials posted @Cookandshaker. This is the new place to be in Fishtown so don't miss out! Reservations required for parties of 5 or more!!

To say shocked, is to say the least. No exaggeration, I actually laughed and asked myself, "Wait... where's the rest of it?" I genuinely couldn't find the cheese or the meat! The roll was doing almost all the heavy lifting and everything was super dry. I mean heavy duty dry.

The servers were friendly, so no complaints there, but the cheesesteak itself was incredibly skimpy. If you're really hungry and expecting a hearty, filling cheesesteak that sticks to your ribs, you may leave wondering where the rest of it went.

Hopefully this was just an off day, but based on my experience, I'd have a hard time recommending it if you're looking for a hearty satisfying meal. For a name like one pound cheeseteaks, I reallyyy expected better. Huge disappointment.

You also get what you pay for! Our food was delicious—I got the burger and my partner got the schnitzel. Both were served hot and very quickly, and tasted extremely fresh. The fries were very good as well, and the Bavarian pretzel we shared was so tasty with a nice cheese sauce on the side.

Overall, I had a wonderful time here! Will definitely be visiting again!

The pineapple lemonade was very delicious but it's criminal not to give ice! 😳😳😳 My lemonade was luke warm so I am sipping on it until I can get home and get some ice. 😢

Overall I'll give them another try but I'd have to order something different. Glad it's an option downtown though. We need more food spots.

text.text:
I had an amazing breakfast at Green Eggs Café. Everything was delicious from start to finish. My French toast was perfectly cooked and had just the right amount of sweetness—not overpowering at all. The eggs with cheddar were cooked just right, with a generous amount of cheese that made every bite satisfying.

One of the highlights for me, as a Muslim woman, was that they offer beef bacon, which honestly made me so excited and instantly elevated the experience. My friend ordered the surf and turf, and when I tell you that crab cake was top-tier—I mean one of the best crab cakes I’ve had, topped with a delicious, flavorful sauce.

The only thing I didn’t love was the home fries. I wish they were cut into more traditional potato-sized pieces instead of the tiny diced style, but that’s a small preference and didn’t take away from the overall experience.

The service was excellent, the environment was cozy and cute, and to top it all off, I ordered an Irish coffee that was chef’s kiss. The balance of Jameson and Baileys was perfect, and the whipped cream was the ideal finishing touch.

Overall, a great breakfast spot with great food, great service, and a welcoming vibe. Definitely worth the visit. ☕🍳✨

text.text:
Philly Brewing Company is a great sweet spot bar in East Kensington. The beer selection isn't the biggest and food isn't served but it really makes up for it by having a amazing ambiance for individual or group outings. With spacious options for both indoor and outside seating if you're out and about and want a quick drink or if you're looking to chill with people you'll find plenty of space to relax.

Another notable thing about the bar, the frequently serve for local functions in the area. If you follow them in social media, if there's a event in East be it a thrift event, pride, or anything else, Philly Brew will be serving the function.

They're also very pet friendly! Dog treats are available at the bar so it's definitely worth stopping by if you dog needs a snack break!

TLDR: Beer selection is to be desired but the variance of seating space, frequency of events, pet friendlyness and general vibe makes it up in spades!

To be honest, I prefer to eat food prepared by hand. I LOVE GOOD FOOD. This is the third time I have visited this establishment . Today, I intended to have breakfast and lunch, as I reside in the Holmesburg area. FAR AWAY.
I anticipated that my Saturday would commence with exceptional food, as I am preparing for the events of the weekend. However, I was denied the lunch portion, despite the establishment closing at 3:00 PM.
While waiting, I noticed that the chef and I exchanged glances as I observed him eating food. I am uncertain whether it was from his plate, a customer’s plate, or one of my shrimp that should have been included in my burrito. Regardless, I am certain that you are aware of my presence.
As I waited, I was offered a complimentary drink with each breakfast sandwich I ordered. I was expecting two drinks, but I only received one. Cause it is stated on MENU
Finally, I received my food, as I had ordered two shrimp fajita burritos. I typically order the same item, but on my second and third visits, I noticed that the quantity of shrimp did not match the description. I believe that if you charge nearly $18 for a burrito, you should provide the customer with their money’s worth. Therefore, I must express my dissatisfaction with the quantity of the food. The quality was good

text.text:
Forgot how good La Colombe’s oat draft lattes were. This flagship store had flavors I’d never seen (Blueberry, S’mores), so we grabbed one of each. Not too sweet, and the blueberry cold foam absolutely slapped. Might be my all-time favorite oat latte.

Most cafes do oat latte with just coffee and oat milk in a cup. La Colombe builds theirs with a lot of details. Nitrogen infusion instead of CO2, so you get that dense microfoam and a silky texture. And because it’s pushed into a tight, uniform emulsion, the nutty aldehydes and pyrazines release slow and even instead of spiking, which is why it tastes so integrated. The blueberry and s’mores notes mostly creep in retronasally, so they can pull the actual sugar down.

Also the chocolate croissant was great. Baked in-house with crisp laminated layers, just the right amount of butteriness.

We originally saw this place on Instagram and decided to take a
2 hour scenic drive just to check it out. My wife and I really enjoy taking relaxing drives together, and this was absolutely worth the trip! Even though they were a little busy, the atmosphere remained calm and laid back. We enjoyed an iced coffee, a refreshing ginger ale, and some absolutely delicious pastries while taking in the cozy ambiance. The exposed brick walls decorated with unique painted murals gave the cafe so much character. Afterward, it was the perfect place to start a leisurely walk and explore the charming town. If you enjoy a peaceful weekend drive, great coffee, and a relaxing cafe with plenty of character, I highly recommend this place!

—
update:

Emily is the best!! Super sweet and helpful, she gave us recommendations. And she came over to give us our order ❤️❤️

we got 3 strawberry matchas and did a mix of oat and almond milk in them! very milky — the strawberry puree is great! we also tried the matcha muffin with raspberry jelly. yummy combo and much better warm!

—

My partner and I were starstruck by the strawberry matcha we got from their new center city location — and apparently that barista has been working at the fishtown location for 3 years so we thought we'd be given a real treat!

It might be a hit or miss depending on the day.

🍵 Food: We were unfortunately a little disappointed. The flavor was pretty mild — I thought my taro drink was alright, it was more taro forward than anything. The matcha flavor was just too light the color was very light green. Suggestion to the team to also store the matcha in amber/aluminium containers since it degrades in UV.

The croissants were apparently made in-house every morning, even though it had the honeycomb inside, the texture felt stale and not flaky or buttery - more like when you leave a piece of bread out.

What we got:
- Strawberry matcha latte with oat milk ($6)
- Taro coconut matcha latte ($6.5)
- Croissant ($5)

⭐️ Service: 1000/5 Emily our cashier was great she was so sweet and helpful! She even said if we didn’t like the food she’d get us another one.

🕯️ Atmosphere: Beautiful interior. Tables were a little light so as people walked by and brushed the tables, the whole table would move. It was VERY quiet you could hear a pin drop. It felt almost a little awkward trying to have a 1-1 convo since everyone else was so quiet.

This coffee shop is so cute, and the pastries are absolutely beautiful. I tried the mango cheesecake and another dessert (I think it was hazelnut or coffee flavored), and the mango cheesecake was the standout. The mango flavor was rich, fresh, and perfectly balanced. You could really taste it in every bite.

I also ordered the pork rice bowl, which was delicious and felt like true comfort food it was warm, satisfying, and well seasoned.

Lastly, I had a strawberry matcha latte, and it was honestly one of the best matchas I’ve had. The only downside is that the serving size is a bit small.

Overall, it’s a great place to work or grab lunch. Seating is somewhat limited, but customers rotate, so you can usually find a spot without waiting too long.

text.text:
Il Ghiottone in Philadelphia is a hidden culinary gem that offers an unforgettable dining experience. Tucked away in a charming neighborhood, this restaurant specializes in authentic Italian cuisine, and it does not disappoint! From the moment you enter, the warm and inviting atmosphere sets the stage for a fantastic meal.

The menu features a delightful array of classic Italian dishes, with a focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients. I highly recommend trying the homemade pasta, which is cooked to perfection and pairs beautifully with their rich sauces. The Osso Buco was tender and flavorful, showcasing the chef’s attention to detail and passion for Italian cooking.

The service at Il Ghiottone is exceptional; the staff is friendly, knowledgeable, and always ready to provide recommendations or accommodate special requests. Their wine selection is impressive, featuring a variety of Italian vintages that complement the menu perfectly.

Whether you’re celebrating a special occasion or simply looking for a cozy spot for dinner, Il Ghiottone delivers an authentic Italian dining experience that will leave you wanting more. I can’t wait to return and explore more of their delicious offerings!

text.text:
I had heard incredible things about Pizzeria Beddia, and let me tell you, it absolutely lives up to the hype. Growing up in New York, I’ve had my fair share of good pizza. But wow. The pizza here was SO delicious. What truly sets a pizza apart is the the crust, and pizzeria beddia has mastered it. We ordered the pie with roasted potato, smoked paprika cream and charred scallions, and it may have just become my all time favorite. The combination was so flavorful, perfectly paired with the light and crispy crust.

We lucked out and were able to walk in and get 2 seats at the bar at 5pm on a Friday. But definitely recommend making reservations in advance or coming even earlier. It’s popular for a reason!

text.text:
Everyone knows that Pizzeria Beddia has great pizza. Delicious, lots of varieties, excellent service. Chill ambience and staff. Quiet  too - no excessively loud music to top over. Easy to have a relaxed quiet conversation. Located on a tiny street parallel to and between Front Street and Frankford Avenue, in the heart of Fishtown.
What you may not know though is that they also have two varieties of soft serv ice cream - sweet cream and espresso. Their own (of course). They are spectacular - creamy, rich and smooth. Flavors that are subtle and satisfying. Small batch at its best. Philadelphia local ice cream purveyors are the best you'll find in the country. Of these, Pizzeria Beddia soft serve is among the best in the city. You can order it at the bar as well. So, come for the pizza and do yourself a favor and don't leave without this dessert. Or, skip the pizza and just come for the ice cream.

text.text:
** Drag Show Brunch Event **

Parking: There’s street parking but I wouldn’t count on it being available. There’s a nearby parking lot within walking distance (1320 N Front St)

Food: Limited food options & the quality isn’t the best. Flatbread reminded me of an Ellio’s frozen pizza. Small & thin, so not very filling!

I got the Meat Lovers (marinara, mozzarella, pepperoni, salami, & bacon).

Staff brought it out to my friend and we were confused because she got a different flatbread and mine wasn’t supposed to come with chicken.

Might’ve been a mistake or used in place of Salami? When I asked about it - they said it’s part of the meat lovers.

It sounds like they need to update their menus in general. The reason I came to this event was for a drag show BRUNCH. There is a drag brunch menu online. When we came in, we were instructed to scan the QR code which didn’t include brunch at all….

No one came over to take your order (appears it’s all done digitally). When I came across a staff member, I asked if they were doing brunch and she said no - that the website hasn’t been updated. Later I saw someone with waffles! So that was kind of annoying because you’re being told one thing, and then seeing others doing another.

Lavender Lemon drop was tasty! If it was bigger, I would’ve ordered more of those!

Environment:  Variable seating options, outdoor section could be a pro with nicer weather. Bathrooms tight.

Drag Show: I didn’t like how they were playing Schitts Creek scenes in the background. It was distracting and didn’t relate to the scenes being performed. One or two performers lip synced very badly. That’s always the most cringiest part of a drag show. Stevie & Moira’s attire was the best! Otherwise - not very clear of Schitts Creek cast.  (Alexis was okay). The performers did a good job interacting with the crowd and their ending was Simply The Best!

The event itself went by fast, almost think these events could be 3 hrs instead.

I don’t know that I would be interested in attending another show, but they pick good themes! (ex. Taylor Swift, Brittney Spears)

text.text:
I visited Evil Genius for their once-a-year Hot Ones–style wing challenge, based on the popular YouTube show where celebrities take on insanely hot wings while answering questions. They used the same sauces and ran their own version of the Q&A — and it was an absolute blast.

Somewhere in the middle I’m pretty sure I burned my entire mouth off, but the energy, the crowd, and the questions made it worth every second. The staff was great, the beer was cold, and the whole place had a fun, relaxed vibe that makes you want to come back even when you’re not chasing the heat.

I’d definitely return on a normal night and highly recommend checking this place out.

I think a better bet for me next time will be something fruity. I will be back to try a burrito!

My companion had to sit with his back to the bathroom, but he didn’t mind. He had the bun Bo Hue without the blood cube. For two bowls of noodles soup and one dessert, our bill was $46 and we gave $9 tip. We avoided the 3% up charge by paying cash. The one unisex bathroom was clean.

text.text:
While visiting South Philly, we originally planned to try another restaurant, but it was closed. We decided to give D'jakarta Cafe a try since it had great reviews, and we were genuinely surprised by both how nice the space is and how amazing the food turned out to be.

Overall Ratings
Atmosphere - 5/5
Service - 5/5
Food - 5/5
Parking - Street Parking

Atmosphere -
The restaurant is on the smaller side with limited seating, but it feels modern and thoughtfully designed. I especially enjoyed the artwork throughout the space.

Service -
We had the chance to chat with one of the owners and learned they have only been open for a couple of years. Everyone was very friendly and welcoming, and I truly hope they continue to see the success they deserve.

What We Ordered -
-Chicken satay (Very good, with a peanut sauce that isn’t overly heavy or overpowering like at some places)
-Beef rendang (An incredible dish. We were both impressed by how rich and flavorful it was)

Final Thoughts -
I would definitely recommend visiting this restaurant if you are ever in the area.

The restaurant is small but the service is reasonably quick so there's a good turnaround.
Very friendly staff.
Parking is tough, of course because of the location and there's not a lot of parking facilities around. Tight Philly street parking as usual.

They prefer cash payment but also accept credit card with a 4% transaction charge
