Hủ tiếu khô is okay, it is very saucy and on the sweeter side. The meat in bún chả is tender and well seasoned, but the noodle is not that good, a bit overcooked. Also the bowl is really small so it is hard to eat. Although it is called phở cyclo, but phở here is meh. Bột chiên is decent, a bit too crispy imo. The wait time can sometimes be long and it's a pretty small place.

text.text: Five adults went here on a Thuraday evening before a hockey game. We had a reservation and we're seated early too. The space is small, so the sound was loud from neighboring tables. We ordered the flatbread pizza appetizer and aranchini balls which were good. Then we ordered our main entrees. We waited a little longer than expected for our entrees but they were packed and it seemed like they were cooking to order as they should. The steak was phenomenal. The chicken marsala looked good and so did the chicken parm. I had the eggplant rolled up with ricotta and spinach with the Vodka sauce on top. Honestly my meal had 1 flavor to it and that was the sauce, which is good. But I could have gotten a pasta with the sauce and got the same flavor. So even though the waitress loved that dish, I wouldn't get it again. I ordered the holiday chocolate espresso martini and it was just okay...I've definitely had better. The waitress did amazing even though she was the only one for the whole room. (I'm guessing they were busier than expected due to the hockey game). There was a food runner who was constantly up and down the stairs. There was a girl at the front entrance that was just sitting there (as no one was coming in constantly). I feel as though she should have helped clean dishes off the tables or get drink refills. They have Pepsi products even though the menu and reciept said coke. They have a full bar, tvs, open garage door for warm days.

text.text: If you're not from the area, you will probably not notice this gem of a pizzeria located in same shopping area of Chickie and Petes and Termini Brothers Bakery. However, you must enter this unassuming South Philly staple. Upon entering, there are several tables placed closely together to really make it feel like an old style family restaurant. There is nothing fancy inside, but the food is quality and the customer service is great. You can go with a traditional pie or try one of the specialty ones like the Pizzaz or Round Robin. You will not be disappointed, but if you order the Pizzaz, you must get it with hot peppers and sausage. Truly fantastic and it will become your go to place before attending a sporting event at the stadiums off Pattison Avenue.

Made a phone call to order my food for pickup. The lady made me repeat my order 3 times before finally finding my item. I had to describe what was in it so she could find it. The food was ready on time. Quantity, yes, but unfortunately, no quality. The lump crab was very limited, and as you can see in the picture, TONS of sun-dried tomatoes. I love them, but it was way too much! A lot of peas 🫛 as well. Good amount of shrimps 🍤
The side salad was good and fresh, but the minuscule piece of tiramisu looked like it was some leftover. Very small for the price, too much mascarpone cheese, barely any coffee flavor, and no liquor flavor as well.
I don't recommend that place, I'm not surprised based on the reviews and ratings.

Food was delicious and service was amazing!!!
If you dine in, you get tortilla chips that are dusted with a spot on seasoning. Comes with a great salsa verde.
We ordered corn fritters, a vegetarian tamale, and quesabirria tacos. The corn fritters had a yummy sweet corn filling. The tamale was interesting plantain, roasted red pepper, and bean filling that was different but very good. And finally, the quesabirria tacos were amazing!!! They were everything you could ask for! Crispy outside, stuffed with a ton of meat, perfect cheese, and a delicious consomé! I can’t wait to come back and try a couple more things including the birria ramen! The owner actually served us and she was super sweet. She gave us free dessert that we can’t wait to try. I recommend giving her a follow bc she truly cares about her community. It’s so amazing to have restaurant owners/chefs that care about the community they serve.

text.text:
This lovely spot situated in the heart of South Philly is a fantastic find! We are craving some tasty tacos and hoping to find a spot that caters to vegans. Luckily, we stumbled upon this gem that serves up delicious vegan Barrio style tacos. I decided to order the slow-roasted yam, hominy, and black bean tacos with housemade vegan cheese, served with a side of lime salsa. They were absolutely delicious! The portion size was generous and really hit the spot. The tomatillo sauce on the side was a nice touch.

We also tried the SEITAN wings with Thai chili sauce and vegan ranch. They were cooked perfectly - crispy on the outside, tender on the inside. The homemade vegan ranch and chili sauce complemented them well. We were pleasantly surprised when a complimentary order of tortilla chips and tomatillo sauce arrived. The food here is top-notch, and the service was excellent. Our meals were served promptly in a relaxing atmosphere with tasteful decor and a great selection of background music. The server was very friendly and helpful.

Both dishes were good—solid Italian comfort food—though not overwhelmingly great. We also tried a few cocktails(recommend the espresso martini), which were very well made and definitely a highlight of the meal.

Another big plus is the ample parking, which is especially convenient if you’re heading to the stadiums for an event.

Our food came out surprisingly fast, but the overall service throughout the meal was a bit slow. That said, the staff was very friendly and welcoming.

Our family's experience with Popi's was average. The food was decent and the pacing of the food coming out was good, but minor things during this experience made me not want to come back. It was exactly what you'd expect. Good enough.

The service was okay, although service staff seemed slightly irritated when we hit their threshold for requests, and there were times we felt they would slide by rather than check up on our party. Just to mention, the restaurant wasn't busy at the time we went.

My biggest disappointment: no one mentioned the fountain (not can) soda refills weren't free. It would've been nice to know upfront instead of finding out when the bill arrived. That kind of thing should be communicated clearly. Seems minor, but it was 6 people that ordered drinks and each got charged 2 or 3 times, which adds up to the price of an extra dish.

Overall, I'd give it a solid B- or C. It's a perfectly fine option if you're in the area.

text.text: I recently had a couple of great lunches here. I found parking along Wolf Street with no problem.  The inside was clean and the staff was friendly. They serve you fresh waster (Drinks to order include Hanks, Boylan's, Harney and Sons, Teas etc.) and will serve you at the table or you can walk up and order at the counter. Their menu has a great mix of deli, steak, "chicken" steak, meatball, sausage and cutlet sandwiches with interesting flavor combos. You can also get breakfast (till 11AM) or a salad. They also have sides that include - tots, fried pickle chips, onion rings, fries, fried mozzarella and Zayda's pickle spears, chips and cherry pepper shooters. They have a couple of vegan options and GF rolls for extra $$.  The staff was more than happy to give recommendations and their favs. My first lunch was The Eye - $15 Ribeye steak, Cooper Sharp American, fried onions came on a seeded Liscio's roll. If you enjoy the somewhat newer Cooper sharp style that's out there you'll like theirs. The Cooper sharp was gooey, mixed in well with the meat and on the heavier side. The ribeye was thin cut, delicious and the portion was pretty hefty.  Second visit I went with - The Nad - $15 Chicken cutlet, fresh mozzarella, prosciutto, arugula, Mike's Hot Honey that came on an unseeded Liscio's roll. The portion size was good, chicken was fresh with good breading, the hot honey was a tad on the heavy side, but the flavors all came together pretty good on this one. Sweet, salty, light bitterness from the arugula and some heat from the hot honey. I added Thin Cut Idaho fries to make it a combo for $3 extra and I have to say they were delicious. They smelled like McD's and tasted similar.   They are cash only, but have an ATM on site. You can use a card if you order online. The one bathroom they have was pretty clean and organized.   I will certainly stop back for a visit if I'm in the area to try out more of their menu.  Thanks guys!

text.text:
The Gatehouse ended up being a pretty average experience for me overall, which is why I’d put it at about a 3-star visit. It was not terrible by any means, but it also did not feel like a place I would go out of my way to visit for a night out.

The food was basically typical bar food, nothing special or memorable about any of the dishes we tried. Everything was edible and came out hot enough, but there was not much in the way of seasoning or distinctive flavors that would make anything stand out. If you are looking for something quick and familiar, it gets the job done, but it does not feel like a spot for anyone seeking a more interesting meal.

The drinks were a letdown and probably the biggest disappointment of the night. Cocktails tasted watered down and a bit flat, like they were missing both punch and balance. For a place you might consider for happy hour or a casual night drink, it just did not deliver the kind of quality you would hope for.

Overall, the whole vibe felt much more like a daytime lunch spot for people working in the Navy Yard than a destination for a night out. As a convenient place to grab a bite with coworkers or a quick drink after work, it makes sense, but it does not have the energy or food quality you would expect for an evening out.

In the end, I would say Gatehouse is fine for what it is: a serviceable lunch place with standard bar food and basic drinks. But if you are looking for a special dinner, a date night, or a place to really enjoy great food and drinks, there are plenty of better options, and I probably would not choose this one again for that kind of outing.

We had the crispy Brussel sprouts for an appetizer and they were awesome.  I had the cheeses teak and my husband had a burger and they were both great.
The only issue is that they were out of a lot on the menu. There was no fish, or cheese for the flatbreads and mozzarella sticks and they were substituting mixed greens for the salad items. We were there at 6 pm and they aren't supposed to close until 10 pm.
However. what we did have was great. I would definitely come here again if we were in the area.
It was also nice to get a 20% discount since we went to the game and showed our ticket.

text.text: This restaurant is a must go in South Philly. From the moment we stepped in, we felt very welcomed. The place was impeccable, clean, bright, tidy and decorated with paintings of Indonesian landscapes. The food came quickly and did not disappoint. I'm only sharing a photo of the dessert because when our food arrived, it looked so good and we were so hungry that we dug right in. I didn't anticipate liking it so much that I'd be inclined to write a review, but here we are. This place is an amazing find. Prices were also very reasonable given the quality and quantity. We had two entrees, shared an appetizer and a dessert, and had two drinks (also delicious), and the total, including tip, came to about $60. We'll definitely be back, as it ticks all the boxes: amazing food, superb service, great ambiance, reasonable prices/value, plenty of parking (free on weekends), and in a safe area. I highly recommend this restaurant!

I came here as an out of towner craving good indo food and was very happy.

I ordered Sate Babi, Nasi Goreng Merah, Dadar Jagung, and Ketoprak.

The sate was very good and well cooked (perfect texture; not dry at all), but could use a bit more of that classic charcoal flavor. (9/10)

Nasi goreng merah was perfect and tasted just like what you can get in Surabaya. (10/10)

Dadar jagung was super yummy. Perfectly crispy and they used sweet corn. (10/10)

Ketoprak was just okay— there was a puddle of water on the plate and the peanut sauce was somewhat bland. (6/10)

All in all I would highly recommend for people craving good authentic Chindo food.

text.text:
I love this place! It’s a living example of the best of Philadelphia: our people and food, and does South Philly-Packer Park-proud. It’s welcoming to neighbors and newbies alike, down to earth, and takes care of both like family.
And… The food, and service are amazing, and the dining room clean, bright and comfortable.

I had a sausage and broccoli rabe pizza. All the ingredients were fresh. The dough, fired in a wood pizza oven, was thin, with a little crunch on the bottom and a perfect little amount of chewiness under the toppings.

If you don’t get a pizza, the fresh baked bread will give you a good sense of a thicker version of the pizza dough.

I also had a bowl of chicken and orzo soup which was delicious.
One diner, exclaimed “Wait! Hold my order!!” When she found out they had pasta and peas soup; her favorite. I suspect it’s soup Italian grandmothers make and is thus a family specialty. Well, I’ll have to hope it’s on the menu when I return.

Speaking of which I had no trouble getting seated the night I went. But you may want to call ahead to confirm availability because I suspect during the soccer World Cup, it’ll get booked.

And that’ll be a good thing for at least one venue in Philly during the World Cup to hit capacity; and a well earned and deserved victory for a great team.
Thanks Joe & Emily. Look forward to returning with some family.

Also note it’s cash only, and priced very fair.

My waiter had quite a conversation with the table next to mine about growing up in the area and the business his grandparents owned which the couple at the table were familiar with.... Anyway totally a neighborhood joint. I think most everyone there was a local from the surrounding neighborhood but even though I wasn't everyone was very friendly.   Upon entry there is a big bakery case which had a ton of delicious looking pastries. I was seated right away, I went with the chicken parm alla vodka sauce. It came with penne and garlic bread. Also you get a bowl of soup with it (I had beef barley) and a bowl of pudding for dessert (I went with chocolate).   Good cake really quickly and was nice and hot. Very tasty as well. Entree was a really big portion - I initially was going to halve it all and bring some as takeaway however it was tasty so I finished it all. Would definitely return. Several good looking items in the menu.

text.text:
Had a great breakfast at Penrose Diner! I ordered the Penrose Deluxe Breakfast, which comes with your choice of pancakes or French toast, eggs any style, bacon, and sausage. I went with the French toast, scrambled eggs, bacon, and sausage, plus a coffee and a side of home fries. My brother went with the pancakes, eggs over easy, bacon, and sausage.

What really impressed me was how fast everything came out. We waited maybe 10 minutes, and everything arrived fresh and hot. The food was delicious all around.the French toast, eggs, bacon, sausage, pancakes, and home fries were all on point.

For two Penrose Deluxe breakfasts, two coffees, an orange juice, and a side of home fries, the bill was only about $55, which I thought was a great deal, especially considering the quality and portions.

The service was great and fast, the bathrooms were clean, there was plenty of parking, and we didn’t have to wait at all to be seated. Good food, good prices, and an easy experience from start to finish.

Definitely a 5-star diner for me. I would recommend Penrose Diner and absolutely come back again!

text.text:
My aunt is visiting me from out of state and we decided this was the place to try for a nice dinner out. It had good reviews for the most part and looked promising. The two waiter and waitress that were working were very kind from the get go and so was the woman that brought out our bread and to go containers. So the service was very good from start to finish. We really enjoyed the complimentary warm bread with the garlic infused oil. That was very good.

My aunt decided to order their Chicken Italiano with broccoli rabe. I ordered the Chicken Siciliana. We both had high hopes for our entrees.

When they came out, mine was not what I was expecting but my aunts looked good. I didn't like how mine was small pieces of very thin and chewy chicken breast. The quality of the chicken was just not great at all. The sauce itself was pretty good but not amazing. They advertise it on the menu as spicy but it wasn't spicy to me at all so that was disappointing. It said it had cherry peppers, mushrooms, and olives but there were a ton of bell peppers so that was kind of weird and unexpected. I liked my linguine with red sauce on the side but it didn't really feel like it matched the entree with the white wine sauce. I wish they would do linguine with the sauce, chicken, and veggies rather than separately with a red sauce.

My aunt felt like her chicken cutlet didn't have much flavor at all so she was disappointed with that. She liked the broccoli rabe but that was about it. The linguine and red sauce side was really disappointing to her and again she felt lacked flavor. She ended up not eating her pasta anymore after the first bite and barely ate half of her chicken because she just wasn't into it.

We ordered the tiramisu for dessert and that was delicious. It had the perfect amount of each component so it was very balanced. We really loved it. That was the highlight of the meal.

I honestly regret coming here for our special night out. It wasn't the worst food I've had but I expected a lot better. Like I said earlier, the waitstaff was very nice, the bread was good, and the dessert was good but the entrees are supposed to be the star of the show and really fell short for us.

Old Original Nick’s Roast Beef is an institution that feels like walking into a warm, meaty time capsule – and I mean that in the best way possible. It’s got all the character you’d expect from a place with “Old Original” in the name: wood paneling, regulars who probably have assigned stools, and staff who don’t mess around but also secretly care. The whole place smells like a roast beef baptism, and I left spiritually full.

The roast beef sandwich? Gone before I even thought to take a picture. That should tell you enough. Juicy, tender, perfectly “wet” – like a sandwich with street smarts. Grab a drink at the bar, soak in the no-nonsense Philly vibes, and accept that you’ll be haunted by this sandwich during moments when it’s very much not available to you – like when you’re out of state, stuck in traffic, or it’s 3AM and Nick’s is closed.

text.text:
In Philadelphia for work trip, I wanted to try a good Italian Roast Pork sandwich after having previously been to John’s (which was phenomenal by the way) and DiNics (which was highly disappointing). I was told by those I’ve worked with originally from Philadelphia the kind of places to find good Italian Roast Porks, this place was that exactly for reasons I’ll describe below.

After researching various restaurants and getting tips from locals who worked at the hotel I stayed at, I figured Nick’s would be worth visiting. As I was told by others from Philadelphia, the best Cheesesteaks and Italian Roast Porks will come from places with a non-touristy hole in the wall feel, Nicks was exactly this.

Nicks appears on the outside like a blue collar bar in a working class neighborhood. On the inside it is exactly that as there was affordable Alcohol and a not so large dining area. Several of the customers worked construction and utility jobs, something I have learned in my experience indicates good food is being served.

For takeout we ordered some roast pork and roast beef sandwiches. Both of them were mouthwatering with nicely seasoned wet meat with melty Provelone cheese that was accompanied nicely by broccoli rabe, peppers and horseradish. The French fries they sold also went well with the gravy option. Compared to other Italian Roast Porks I’ve had this easily ties with John’s for the best one I’ve tasted.

Overall, it was good food at a place that is as South Philadelphia as it gets. It’s located in the kind of place you’d expect to see a modern day Rocky Balboa hail from. Its menu was simple short sweet and perfectly done. If you are looking for fine dining, I wouldn’t advise coming here but if you want a no frills salt of the earth sandwich shop, you will not go wrong coming here.

This place is easily one of the most disappointing restaurants I’ve tried in Philly. I ordered online because of all the hype and positive reviews, but the food wasn’t even close to what I expected. It was overpriced, flavorless, and so unappetizing that I couldn’t even finish my meal.

What I don’t understand is how a restaurant can constantly brag about having great food when the quality is this bad. The food lacked seasoning, had no real flavor, and felt like a complete waste of money. For the prices they’re charging, customers should be getting something memorable—not food that makes you regret ordering it after a few bites.

The hype surrounding this place makes absolutely no sense to me. Between the disappointing food and underwhelming experience, I honestly can’t recommend it to anyone.

text.text:
I was highly disappointed with my experience when I came here for Valentine’s Day. My partner and I are asian, and the rest of the customers in the hall were white. It was very clear that other customers were being serviced and attended to more often than we were, which was very saddening. We were not offered an explanation of their set menu for the night, nor an introduction from our waiter himself. We were barely offered water refills or checked in on compared to the other customers our waiter was managing.

The osso bucco was very bland and greasy at the same time, contrary to many of the positive reviews of this dish. The smoked mozzarella was also underwhelming, given the raving reviews for this dish as well. The mussels were so fishy, almost like they weren’t fresh or cooked off long enough. Thankfully, our meal was saved by the seafood parpadelle, which we thought was exceptional.

We had to flag down a separate waitress to get our check, and we were not informed of their 3% credit card surcharge, so when we questioned why the bill was higher than what we saw on the check, the waitress stared at us strangely and spoke to us like we were children. Obviously we didn’t have a problem with paying their CC surcharge; it is just common courtesy to inform customers that that is your policy and that the bill will be higher than initially quoted on the check.

This restaurant was well spoken about on Reddit, so it was very disappointing that we had an experience like this. Our meal was not worth $60 per person. I could’ve had a better time at Cheesecake Factory for the food and service we were given. Will not be returning.

text.text:
Reservations essential with both locals and visitors coming from NYC to eat here.
Excellent service. BYO. There is a lot of culinary knowledge with some of our dishes to a high standard of Italian cuisine. On this occasion, the Osso Buco was excellent. Also the mushroom starter was wonderfully put together and plated. The penne was delightful but oddly, the optional shrimp had half their number burned, one solid, black and inedible. Another conflicted surprise (because clearly the chef is an expert and can put out very good food) was the chicken with mushroom. Looked, smelled and tasted very good but the chicken breast flesh was tough; half was eaten, the rest thrown.
Cheesecake and tiramisu were both expertly created and plated too. So the two shortcomings were very unexpected. There are two very nice washrooms, kept nicely clean.

text.text: This place surprised me in all wonderful ways! Food is delicious and made out of farm fresh ingredients! Cocktail menu has all the staples and unexpected choices. I had a pomegranate and blood orange gimlet that was lip smacking good. We shared buffalo wings that were perfectly spicy and chicken was densely meaty. My friend had the fish sandwich which may seem overloaded with layers, however all are essential to build a juicy, briny and crunchy texture and flavor. The cod was perfectly flaky. I ordered the lamb chops with fingerling potatoes and peas, taking a bet as I thought. I certainly felt like I won a prize! The chops were perfectly pink and server with a pairing of a capers spread, the potatoes were lovely but the star of the dish were peas. I never expect much from peas but these were farm fresh and somehow toasty. The staff is very attentive and friendly, the ambience is perfect for a date or dinner with friends. The place has a lot of space inside and a terrace outside. While food is superb the place feels very relaxed. The music was great and not too loud to have a good conversation. We will be back! Thank you very much.

First... I write this review with the utmost bias, thank you very much
Breakfast is my absolute favorite meal of the day and Brunics is my favorite place to get it. I just never get the chance to write a review because I always eat the food and fall asleep and then... Forget Lol. But this place is amazing and more people need to know it. They've got some slamming breakfast(though they do offer non breakfast alternatives but... Breakfast is my jam lol) i always order from GrubHub and my food is always quick and hot even when it says its busy. I've tried quite a few different things from them since I order a lot but for this sake of this review I'll stick to mainly what's pictured here.(I plated this myself after ordering online) Pictured  below is the

Sourdough French Toast: 7/10
Does leave a bit of a taste simple because it is sourdough but I personally think it adds to the flavor but if you aren't a french toast fan, I would stay away but if you're willing to try something new this is delicious they arent as wonderfully thick as normal french toast would be, which is the reason for the score but very much still worth every bite.

Eggs: 8/10

I mean its eggs. You cant really mess up eggs Lol. But they always make sure to make them nice and fluffy and delicious

Scrapple: 10/10
I grew up on scrapple, I've had all kinds of scrapple, I've cooked scrapple and I've even had scrapple from places that have been called the best by magazines but this was hands doen my favorite. It was huge, cut perfectly and tasted delicious. It's definitely worth trying

Links: 8/10
I mean... Its sausage links... Nothing more needs to be said

(Half Eaten) Grits with cheese: 8/10
🤤🤤🤤🤤 not many people can make a good bowl of grits... Brunics you've definitely got it down. Good job.

(New additions pictured below, flounder with eggs and potatoes and a large coffee/16oz)

I had a truly awful experience here picking up a Doordash order (two orders, for two different customers) last night. I arrived, and two young workers up front said the food was "still cooking."

They both then stood around and did nothing, for the next 20 minutes, while I waited on the food. They talked about what music they both listened to, how one had lost their airpods recently, and complained about another customer that was angry it had been an hour since they placed had their order and it was still not delivered, which they blamed on the customer, for living a distance away.

Eventually, I had to cancel pickup for both orders, and spent 20 minutes sitting there, unpaid, as Doordash does not pay you for waiting time.

For the owner of this restaurant, this was last night, 11/23/2025 at 9:30pm. The workers were both young, likely late 20's. Both light skinned latino, one with curly shorter hair, one with longer hair, both black hair.

They were the definition of lazy and unprofessional and both should be fired, that is unless you are paying them to do nothing but chat on your dime, while customers wait, and eventually don't even get their food.

This restaurant is unable to dine food, not fine food. Avoid at all costs.

text.text:
I’ll honestly call this a strong 4.5-star experience because this spot definitely has a lot of potential to become one of my favorite breakfast places.

I was in the area and saw Scramble Cafe from across the street, and the first thing that caught my attention was how clean and welcoming it looked from the outside. I love when a breakfast spot gives “reliable neighborhood diner” energy before you even walk in. It made me immediately want to try it.

The space itself is very small, but in a cute, cozy way. It reminds me of a little breakfast diner where you can still comfortably sit down and enjoy your food indoors. The atmosphere was calm, simple, and inviting.

Since it was my first time, I wanted to order something that would really let me get a feel for the place. What stood out to me immediately were the veggie home fries. I had NEVER seen home fries with broccoli, spinach, mushrooms, and tomatoes before, and since I’ve been trying to eat more vegetarian meals lately, I knew I had to try them. I paired that with scrambled eggs with no cheese.

I also tried the pineapple smoothie. The flavor was REALLY good and tasted very pineapple-forward, but it was extremely thick. Like… almost spoon-thick. I personally wish it had been blended a little longer or made a little smoother because it was hard to drink through the straw, but the actual flavor itself was still good.

Now the reason I didn’t go full 5 stars was because my order did come out wrong at first. My veggie home fries were missing the tomatoes, and my eggs came with cheese when I asked for no cheese. BUT and this is important they fixed everything immediately with no attitude, no problem, and no hesitation. That matters a lot to me.

Once everything came back corrected, the food was honestly REALLY good. The veggie home fries were flavorful on their own. I didn’t need ketchup, hot sauce, or anything extra. And the scrambled eggs? Some of the best diner-style scrambled eggs I’ve had in a long time. Soft, flavorful, and cooked perfectly.

What also stood out to me was the menu variety. There are SO many things I still want to come back and try breakfast sandwiches, pancakes, other smoothies, coffees… this definitely feels like one of those places you slowly work your way through the menu.

Overall, I really enjoyed this spot. Even with the small mistakes, the customer service and willingness to correct things quickly made the experience positive. I can definitely see this becoming one of my top breakfast spots.

I don’t know who’s managing this place but this was a Sunday afternoon during a Phillies game and these are just the most basic of expectations.

text.text: Kasumi Sushi is located in a newer strip mall with ample, but tight parking. The inside was bright and nicely decorated. The floors were a little sticky and didn't look mopped.   There are split booth's along the wall and quad tables throughout the inside. I sat at the long wooden sushi counter which was a little low for my liking, but I could still see the sushi chef in action.   The staff was very attentive and nice. I was the only patron in there for a little while before it began to fill up around noon.  Their menu contains apps, classic rolls/signature rolls/sushi/sashimi, soups, salads, yaki soba/udon, Japanese ramen and teriyaki. They seem to be a QSR Japanese offering (no big bloated menu) with simple, but plenty of well thought out choices.  I ordered miso soup - $2.50 - was salty and had an off flavor. I would skip it next time.   For sushi I went with the Angel Roll - $13.95 shrimp tempura, avocado topped with spicy crab meat with mayo, old bay powder - sizable pieces of eight that had a nice mix of flavors. I would have liked more spice, but a good choice and I also chose the Cowboy - $15.95 eight pieces, pepper tuna, avocado topped with seared beef with spicy mayo, hot chili, scallion, fried onion - big portion, tender beef, would have liked more spice, but overall the flavors went well together. The ingredients were fresh and the rolls were tight and held together.  I left absolutely stuffed. For this area of the city and for the parking, I think this spot is great. The roll varieties were creative, presentation was good and wait time was minimal (sushi chef was quick on the draw!) with fair prices.   The bathroom was ok, but needed a good cleaning.   I would repeat.  Thanks guys!

I would have liked more spice, but a good choice and I also chose the Cowboy - $15.95 eight pieces, pepper tuna, avocado topped with seared beef with spicy mayo, hot chili, scallion, fried onion - big portion, tender beef, would have liked more spice, but overall the flavors went well together. The ingredients were fresh and the rolls were tight and held together.  I left absolutely stuffed. For this area of the city and for the parking, I think this spot is great. The roll varieties were creative, presentation was good and wait time was minimal (sushi chef was quick on the draw!) with fair prices.   The bathroom was ok, but needed a good cleaning.   I would repeat.  Thanks guys!

Kasumi Sushi was our go-to lunch spot when I worked at an office near the Philadelphia Airport. My coworkers and I ate here regularly, both dining in and ordering takeout, and it never let us down.
The bento box lunch special with soup was our usual order, and it was consistently satisfying — generous portions, fresh ingredients, and good variety in each box. It's the kind of reliable, well-priced lunch that makes it easy to become a regular.
What stood out most was the consistency. Whether we called ahead for takeout or sat down for a quick meal, the quality and service were dependable every time. Our whole office group kept coming back, which says a lot.
Docking one star only because I'd love to see a bit more variety rotated into the lunch specials, but that's a minor note. Overall, a solid neighborhood sushi spot that's perfect for a work lunch routine.

text.text:
Decided to try out their dim sum, since they offered the discount. The service was alright; they did try to ensure we had everything we needed but when they took our order, it was all by memory. They didn't write it down or had any device to record the order. This did result us not getting some items.

Unfortunately, the dim sum dishes were very disappointing. We tried the shrimp balls, siu mai, shrimp rolls, rice rolls, and a few other dishes. For some reason, most of the dishes, especially the rice rolls, had a tangy/sour aftertaste. The shrimp balls were small and WAY overcooked to the point where it was almost too hard to bite into. The shrimp rolls had a lot of veggies in it, so it was more like a typical Chinese takeout spring roll. Overall, I don't think there was a dish I could recommend from their dim sum menu.

Also, note that the dim sum dishes are made-to-order and NOT a push cart experience like some other places. This was an issue since some plates can come out pretty quickly while others can take much longer. Like we ordered shrimp siu mai towards the end, and after 15 mins, we asked the waiter and he said it was coming. After more time passed, still nothing. We paid for our bills and only then did he packed it in a to go container for us. Unfortunately, it was the wrong order since we ordered siu mai but got hacao in the container. We went at a time when there were maybe one or two other parties in the place, so I can't imagine what the wait time would be like if they were more busy.

We've dined here before and their other dishes were decent. They'll need to go back to the drawing board for their dim sum plates and experience (protip: write down the orders because your staff is struggling to remember when we order 8 small plates).

I've also came to learn that they might have had a turnover in owneship and kitchen staff.. which might explain the disappointing food experience now.

text.text:
The service experience was very disappointing. The servers were loud, rushed us while taking our order, and made the payment process uncomfortable. During our visit, one of the servers was yelling loudly at someone in the kitchen and dragging a trash can through the dining area, which created an unpleasant atmosphere.

Additionally, both servers insisted that we pay separately for the food and the sodas and requested that the soda payment be made in cash. They charged us $2 per soda in cash, despite stating that the menu price was $3 each, and refused to provide a receipt for the cash payment.

The servers also repeatedly stated that customers would be charged an additional 3% fee for paying by credit card, which added to the confusion and discomfort during the payment process.

To make matters worse, we felt pressured to leave a higher tip despite the poor service and the inconveniences we experienced throughout our visit.

Overall, the experience was unprofessional and left us very dissatisfied. The combination of the disruptive behavior in the dining area, the unusual payment practices, the refusal to provide a receipt for cash transactions, and the pressure regarding tipping created a very negative customer experience. I hope management will review these concerns and take appropriate steps to improve customer service, professionalism, and payment practices.

text.text: Very disappointing experience from start to finish. When we arrived for dinner, the restaurant was completely empty. We ordered two entrées to start, and the waitress immediately questioned whether it would be enough. When we later tried to order additional items, we were told they were unavailable. Instead of giving us time to choose alternatives, the waitress seemed impatient and pushed us toward the dishes she recommended. The service throughout the meal was rushed and careless. Utensils were dropped while serving, and even our leftovers were handled carelessly during packing. The most concerning issue was the bill. We discovered that we had been charged at least $5 more per item than the prices listed on the menu. When we questioned it, we were told the menu had not been updated in six years. If the listed prices are inaccurate, customers should be informed before ordering, not after receiving the check. Despite our frustration, we still left a tip. However, the situation became even more uncomfortable when the waitress confronted us and demanded a larger tip. Poor service, inaccurate pricing, and unprofessional behavior made this an experience we will not be repeating.

If I can give zero stars I would, please stay away from this place. Management is very unprofessional.

My family have been waiting to try this place for a while. We finally decided to try this place and my mom was super exited because she wanted this fish po’ boy (made with cod). Now mistakes happen, however, this was not a simple mistake. Thankfully my mom didn’t have to get rushed to the hospital.

I called the restaurant to speak with the manager. Mike came on the phone and didn’t believe they made a mistake. He was very condescending with his responses and even made jokes about the refund saying “I can give for a refund for just the sandwich and a piece of key lime pieee” in a funny tone.  I have never felt so disrespected in my life. This is mother and if anything were for happen to her, it would have been very devastating. I asked for a full refund and was told that wasn’t going to happened, but I can bring the sandwich and receipt back.

When I went back Mike left, leaving his associates to deal with this issue that is still not resolved. Mangers are suppose to be leaders for their staff and the fact that he left just shows he is not ready for a leadership position. I’m just very disappointed and will not support this business or the other locations.

The food at El Mezcal Cantina was good, but nothing that really stood out or blew me away. The service, however, was excellent — attentive, friendly, and easily the best part of the experience. The spicy margarita was also outstanding and definitely one of the highlights of the meal.
That said, the pricing was honestly hard to justify. Spending around $80 for six tacos, chips, and salsa felt pretty outrageous for what was served. I’ve had the same quality — and often even better — in Mexico for about a third of the price. Overall, it’s a decent spot with great service and excellent drinks, but the value just didn’t match the cost for me.

text.text: Let me preface by saying, we attempted to visit on Cinco De Mayo, so results may vary on a different day. Where do I even begin….we made a reservation for 7:15pm and arrived promptly at that time for our table. After waiting 20 minutes for someone to even acknowledge our existence, we were told they were getting a table ready for us. 10 additional minutes later, much to our surprise, someone else is sitting at the table that was committed to us.  After another 10 minutes of waiting, we’re now 40 minutes past our confirmed reservation, we have been committed to another table at their upstairs room. This required the party already sitting there to depart, which we waited for. After sensing no bussing would be happening to the table, we decided to sit with the previous party’s leftovers still on the table. Thinking we’ve weathered the worst of the storm, we were excited to sit, order, and enjoy our meal….that thought was misguided. Service was dreadfully slow, a glass of water took an hour, incorrect drinks were served, and appetizers were provided in tin foil containers, with small quantities as we likened the appetizer experience to military food rations. I completely understand that instances like this can happen at high volume times, however, what irked me the most was that during the time that we were seated, we got the impression from the minimal service interaction we did have, that we were the inconvenience - for simply wanting our reservation honored.  After nearly two hours, we threw in the towel and left. To be honest, I have been on a slower evening and the food is great, however, this experience is making me question whether I would come back.

text.text:
i rarely leave reviews but last night was THE WORST experience i’ve ever had at a restaurant.

we arrived at 6:30 (remember this)
me and my partner were seated at the bar to wait for a table we reserved but we never got a table. there was practically no communication throughout the entire night aside from our order being taken.

after 45 minutes we finally had our order taken. chips, a salad, a molcajete, and steak tacos. we waited 2 entire hours to get our food (now 9:00) i get it’s cinco de mayo, but a 2 hour wait on CHIPS and SALAD is insane…they were supposed to be our starters but came out with our entrees?

but to make things worse the ceasar salad had little to no dressing and came grilled and unchopped? just 2 romaine hearts with minuscule amounts of cheese and croutons. we couldn’t even care anymore though so some romain hearts with our entrees it was👍🏼

[i hate being all negative and doing this so i will say the molcajete was good, chips were average but not worth a 2 hour wait. tacos were eh.]

as we finished our food i jokingly told my partner we would probably have to wait an hour for the check now…unfortunately that became a reality😀 for once in my dining experience it hurt me to leave a tip but i couldn’t find it in me to leave a well deserved 0%.
we finally ended up leaving around 10:00.

i’m not sure what went wrong and why they handled this day so poorly. i’ve never ever had an experience like this in my life, but i hope they’re prepared for next years cinco de mayo. (and change up the salad i still can’t believe what they served us😭)

moral of the story, probably never come here on cinco de mayo🫩

text.text:
My first time here yesterday, and wanted to grab some hoagies before heading down AC with the wife. Grabbing sandwiches is our go to move before departing and wanted to switch things up by trying a new place this go-round. Had always seen Pastificio in passing when heading down the stadiums for games but never had the chance. Did this time, and honestly didn't have a huge issue with them.

The place is IMMACULATE, the service from the friendly ladies up front is top tier, and ordering was a breeze through the touch screen system. I imagine they have non-seeded rolls but the two Italians my wife and I grabbed were seeded. I usually don't go for seeded but these were pillow soft and had a very good taste. They for sure have mastered the seasoning which a lot of places haven't. The taste was just what you should expect from an expertly crafted Italian. (The ONLY kind to get when trying a place for the first time) My one complaint is that they are a little light with the meat. I always gauge the side view to see how well the sandwich is put together and although nicely done, they only give a few layers. Now I've had hoagies where it's nothing BUT meat but no taste, and that's a fail if I'm being honest but I do like a little heft to go with the flavor I cherish. Not sure if you can request extra meat, but for $15 plus, you shouldn't have to. Regardless, a very good hoagie it was, and I could see myself going back if I'm by there. Hasn't surpassed the one and only Gooey Louies which IMO is the best in the city, but these guys are pretty good.

text.text:
From Los Angeles, in Philly for work all week, I hadn’t left my hotel until Friday night when my wife and I decided to treat ourselves to a special dinner before flying home. We searched high and low online for the perfect spot and came across OLEA—the photos looked beautiful and inviting, and it turned out to be even more magical in person.

From the moment we arrived, we were greeted by the owner, Louie, whose warmth and charm set the tone for the evening. The restaurant itself is cozy, elegant, and homey all at once—like stepping into someone’s welcoming living room but with the refinement of a thoughtfully curated dining space.

I ordered the salmon with leek and mushroom purée, while my wife had the swordfish, both accompanied by perfectly creamy mashed potatoes. Every bite was outstanding—beautifully balanced flavors, fresh ingredients, and executed with care.

What made the night truly unforgettable, though, was Louie himself. He personally waited on us, bringing so much humor, kindness, and hospitality that we felt like cherished guests in his own home. At one point, I watched him water the window box plants above the restaurant’s hand-painted picture window, a simple but telling gesture of the love and detail he pours into his place.

OLEA is BYOB, and when we mentioned we hadn’t brought wine, Louie suggested we pop next door. Instead, he surprised us by getting a chilled sparkling bottle for $12—absolutely delicious and the perfect pairing.

The entire experience felt personal, warm, and special—the kind of dinner you remember long after. OLEA is truly a diamond in the rough in Philly, the best find of our trip, and we can’t recommend it highly enough. From Los Angeles, in Philly for work all week, I hadn’t left my hotel until Friday night when my wife and I decided to treat ourselves to a special dinner before flying home. We searched high and low online for the perfect spot and came across OLEA—the photos looked beautiful and inviting, and it turned out to be even more magical in person.

From the moment we arrived, we were greeted by the owner, Louie, whose warmth and charm set the tone for the evening. The restaurant itself is cozy, elegant, and homey all at once—like stepping into someone’s welcoming living room but with the refinement of a thoughtfully curated dining space.

I ordered the salmon with leek and mushroom purée, while my wife had the swordfish, both accompanied by perfectly creamy mashed potatoes. Every bite was outstanding—beautifully balanced flavors, fresh ingredients, and executed with care.

What made the night truly unforgettable, though, was Louie himself. He personally waited on us, bringing so much humor, kindness, and hospitality that we felt like cherished guests in his own home. At one point, I watched him water the window box plants above the restaurant’s hand-painted picture window, a simple but telling gesture of the love and detail he pours into his place.

OLEA is BYOB, and when we mentioned we hadn’t brought wine, Louie suggested we pop next door. Instead, he surprised us by getting a chilled sparkling bottle for $12—absolutely delicious and the perfect pairing.

The entire experience felt personal, warm, and special—the kind of dinner you remember long after. OLEA is truly a diamond in the rough in Philly, the best find of our trip, and we can’t recommend it highly enough. We will definitely be back next time we’re in Philadelphia—and I’ll be telling everyone I know that OLEA is the place to dine.

The starters showed real promise — the mussels toast and spaghetti were genuinely good. But the mains were a letdown that’s hard to overlook at these prices. The half chicken ($42) and scallops ($46) were both underwhelming — no interesting flavors, nothing memorable, portions that don’t justify the cost. The scallops especially felt like a safe, uninspired execution of a dish that should be a showstopper at that price point. Wine by the glass starts at $17, which is steep even by Philly fine dining standards.

Fork has a strong reputation and the space is lovely, but this felt like a restaurant coasting on its name. Stick to the pasta and starters and you’ll have a better time — just don’t expect the mains to deliver.

Went here for lunch after a half conference event at the National Constitution Center (it's just a few blocks away). It was lunch time, but we were able to be seated as soon as we walked in. Staff were all so friendly and attentive, smiling and checking in throughout our meal to see how we ere doing. The menu was smaller than what I expected, but had some good options and I'm thinking it's scaled down since it's the lunch menu.

The food itself was pretty good. I'm not a person that really likes/chooses to eat fries - I know, I know but I would choose sweet potato fries instead of regular fries, but I digress. But the fries are fried in beef tallow which really gives it such a great flavor and taste! Was really happy with the portion size of my plate - the sandwich has hefty but not too overwhelming and the side salad was the perfect size. My boss said she enjoyed her meal also.

Nice spot for American fare in Old City. Would eat from here again.

Stopped in for a quick dinner before a concert while staying at the Kimpton. Service was good, no complaints at all about our waitress. (possibly Daria?).

The fries were really good and honestly reminded me of McDonald’s fries as a kid. The burger was solid, and while my husband wasn’t fully sold on the jalapeño jam, he ordered it on the side and agreed it complimented the burger well.

My biggest disappointment was the “Gnocchi not Gnocchi” dish. I’m a huge gnocchi fan, so this was an easy choice—but it definitely wasn’t gnocchi. It wasn’t solid and had more of a shell-like texture, which missed the mark for me.

We also had the carrot cake, which to me was too sweet, and the cake-to-icing ratio felt off.

Drinks were good. Overall, I just wish I liked the food more, as the service was solid, but it’s not somewhere I’m rushing back to.

text.text:
Amada (Old City) — Solid Tapas, but Mixed Results for Brunch
I’ve visited Amada in Old City about three times and have also been to their Atlantic City location, but this was my first time trying their brunch. While the atmosphere and decor remain beautiful and rustic, our recent visit for a party of eight was a bit of a mixed bag.
The Food
Overall, the group enjoyed their selections. We tried a wide variety:
• The Classics: The Crab Benedict, Shakshuka (with tomato piperade), and the Mahon Cheese Toast were all hits.
• The Sides: The Espelette Glazed Bacon and Patatas Rösti were solid additions to the table.
• The Paella: I ordered the Paella Valencia. While the menu warns of a 30-minute wait, it took quite a bit longer than that despite the restaurant not being crowded. It was good, but definitely something you have to plan your afternoon around.
The Disappointments
I was really looking forward to the family-style menu and the Sangria Pancakes, but I was told they are no longer offered. It was disappointing to see them still advertised on their website during our meal, and the service regarding that specific letdown felt a bit indifferent.
Service & Vibe
The rest of the staff was friendly, and they provided some complimentary starters for the table (it seemed like Frittada and Prosciutto), which was a nice touch even if it wasn't officially announced. Most of us enjoyed the mimosas, which added a nice touch to the brunch vibe.
Final Verdict: I still love the decor and the quality of the tapas, but I’d likely stick to dinner or maybe try happy hour here in the future. It's a great spot for a group, but the brunch menu changes and service timing were a bit of a letdown this time around.

The service was friendly and attentive, and the entire experience made my birthday feel special. Everything we tried was delicious, and I can't wait to come back and enjoy another brunch. Highly recommend!

During our recent visit to Pennsylvania, my partner and I had the pleasure of dining at a fantastic spot that truly exceeded expectations. For a very reasonable price of $59, we enjoyed a delicious spread, including tacos with a side of chili, two burgers with fries, tea, and two waters. One of the standout features was that everything on the menu could be made gluten-free, which was a huge plus for us. A nice touch is the digital payment option on the receipt, where you can easily pay and leave a tip with a code.

Overall, the experience was fantastic, and we are definitely looking forward to coming back the next time we’re in the area. If you’re in PA and craving some great food in a comfortable setting, this place is highly recommended! Thank you for such a wonderful experience!

The food was inconsistent. The Meatball Parmigiano sandwich was excellent, and the shrimp appetizer was also very well prepared. The shrimp were flavorful and perfectly cooked. One surprise, though, was that the shrimp came with four slices of bread. Combined with the fries that came with the sandwich, we ended up with far more carbs than we expected.

The Truffle Fries were the biggest disappointment. They were basically regular fries with a pile of truffle topping added on top instead of being evenly tossed together. Better restaurants usually distribute the truffle flavor more evenly and finish the dish with touches like chopped parsley or other garnishes. This version felt unfinished.

The service was decent but missed an opportunity. The Meatball Parmigiano already comes with a generous serving of regular fries, and since we also ordered the Truffle Fries, we ended up with two large baskets of fries. It would have been nice if our server had pointed that out before we ordered. When I mentioned it afterward, the response was simply, “Sorry, but I can give you a box.” It solved the leftover problem, but it didn’t really address the issue.

The atmosphere was just as contradictory. The restaurant is beautifully designed and clearly invested a lot in the décor. At the same time, the leather seat at my table was badly cracked, with the foam exposed. On the other hand, they provided very high-quality cloth napkins. Small details like these made the restaurant feel strangely inconsistent.

And the price, we spend 80+ for two people, not expensive but still quiet a lot.

Overall, there are definitely some dishes worth coming back for, but the overall experience lacked the attention to detail that separates a good restaurant from a great one.

text.text:
Extremely disappointing - would not recommend to anyone. I booked a Baby Shower at Independence Beer Garden for Saturday, July 11, 2026, reserving the full Adirondack space at the Ranstead and 6th entrance of the venue for 60 guests. We paid a significant amount for what was supposed to be a professionally managed event, and IBG failed to deliver even the most basic contracted services. This was one of the most stressful experiences I’ve ever had, and I cannot recommend this venue for any event.

Despite booking two months in advance, the sales manager/coordinator, Lauren Andrews, never provided a point of contact, event rundown, or even show up on the day of the event. My husband and I called her multiple times the week prior with important questions, and none of our calls were returned. On the day of the shower, no one answered when we called ahead, and when we arrived, our reserved space was completely filled with regular (non-Baby Shower) guests.

Staff at the Main Bar had no idea an event was scheduled, requiring me to repeat multiple times the details of my confirmed reservation. I am 8 months pregnant and had to walk around the venue in 90 degree heat to track down a staff member only to find the on‑duty manager, Jacob, who was confused, unprepared, and whom seemed to be scared to do his job as a manager, leaving me for extended times waiting by a wall while he tried to "figure things out". He found my sister instead of going back to me to provide an update, leading to confusion on my end as I was still waiting to hear from him, and he offered 3 small tables instead of the full space we paid for, which would not accommodate my 60 guests, many of whom flew and drove in from out of state. He was also unwilling/seemingly scared to ask non‑event guests to relocate, leaving my family to notify them of the reserved event since there were no signs from the venue indicating an event was scheduled. My family and friends also had to clear dirty tables just to begin setup because of all the disorganization. My guests began arriving during all of this with nowhere to sit, and I had to triage them myself.

The event started nearly an hour late. Guests weren’t seated until 3:50 PM, first round of drinks arrived around 4:00 PM, and food didn’t come out until 4:15 PM—served all at once on a single table in the back by the bathroom area instead of family‑style (starters, then apps, followed mains & sides on each table) as promised. Drink service was so slow despite being told we would have a dedicated server for our paid event and guests would not have to worry about getting up to get drinks. Many guests were confused and ended up buying their own drinks at the main bar because it was faster.

The only helpful staff member was Lee, who stepped in at 3:15/3:30 to assist once he realized how disorganized things were.

Management insisted on immediate payment despite not fully acknowledging the issues that happened and promised a follow‑up regarding compensation from a director/corporate that never came. Overall, coordination was severely lacking, staff were unprepared, and the first half of my shower was chaotic. My Baby Shower felt entirely mismanaged, and their management failed to provide any accountability afterward. For the price we paid and the significance of the occasion, this level of service was unacceptable. I cannot recommend IBG for any event.

If you are looking for a Middle Eastern restaurant in the city, you have to go to Malooga - Old City (Philadelphia) on Chestnut St.  Perfect cozy atmosphere to relax and enjoy a meal in Old City.

The food of course, is the star of the show, which is why Malooga is a go to.  We ordered the Lamb Haneeth which is a super, ultra-tender, and I mean ultra-tender roasted lamb. So tender, melt off the bone tender, that I had to ask Chef Mohammed what the secret was. He did tell us, but I figured we should let him share it if he wants once you try it. He said it came from Grandmother.  The dish comes on a bed of aromatic rice and can be shared by at least 2 persons, in this case my wife and myself. In fact, many of the dishes are shareable, which is one of the reasons I love Middle Eastern food.  It’s the experience of sharing a meal that draws you together. I digress.

Our server, McKenzie, was very helpful with his recommendations, which is why we chose the Lamb Haneeth.

Definitely going back again when we’re near Old City. We saw 1 dish that is on our radar for the next time - the Adventure Platter.  You will also want to go back for more after your first time at Malooga - Old City.

Walked in with a group of 6 to get a few rounds of drinks before we went our separate ways. A few other bars we went to were packed so we ended up passing this place and stopping in because there were a ton of tables open. When we walked in, there were a total of 5 customers. We asked if he could sit for 6 for some drinks, and they refused to let us sit and has us all huddle around a tiny standing table that barely fit 6 drinks. We left about 40 minutes later, and in that time, 2 additional customers came in. I understand keeping the tables open if you are busy, but that place was a ghost town the entire night. I watched one pizza and one burger get made in the 40 minutes we were there. Frankly, we were likely going to share 2 apps, but chose not to when we weren’t allowed to sit.

Mixed drinks were okay. Dive bar quality, priced like normal Philly prices.

Overall, way too many places in the areas with better drinks and hospitality to go to. I won’t go back, and judging by the fact they were the only dead bar in Philly on Friday night (730pm) during restaurant week tells me I’m not the only one that has this feeling…

text.text:
My honest review of Plough in Philadelphia is a 7/10 if you’re looking for a calm, relaxed sit-down meal, but I’d give it closer to a 9/10 if you’re looking for a lively atmosphere with music, a DJ (I’m not sure if that’s every night), live entertainment, and a late-night menu.

We arrived fairly late and were looking for some good food that wasn’t going to be overly greasy or fried, and I was pleasantly surprised by the food.

The spice bag was delicious, the grilled chicken sandwich was spot-on (although I would have loved a little more potatoes on the side), and the calamari was cooked perfectly.

My only real criticism was the volume of the atmosphere. I enjoy a restaurant with music and energy, but the music was loud enough that we literally had to yell at each other to have a conversation. 😂 In my opinion, there’s a difference between having a fun, lively atmosphere and having the music overpower every other sound in the restaurant. If you’re looking for a place where you can focus on the music, drinks, and overall nightlife atmosphere, though, this could be exactly what you’re looking for.

That said, I definitely don’t dislike Plough and I would absolutely go back. There were chicken tenders and wings coming out that looked fantastic, and there are several other things on the menu I’d like to try next time.

Overall, I’d recommend it depending on what kind of experience you’re looking for. If you want a quiet dinner and lots of conversation, I’d probably choose somewhere else. If you want good food, music, energy, and a fun late-night atmosphere, Plough is worth checking out.

text.text:
I dined at La Famiglia last week and had an outstanding experience from start to finish. I began with the special appetizer, Tuna Crudo con Peperoni Rossi, which was incredibly fresh, bright, and beautifully balanced—a perfect way to start the meal.

For my entrée, I was fortunate enough to order one of the evening specials, Costata di Maiale con Fontina e Funghi. The pork chop was thick, juicy, and stuffed with rich fontina cheese and earthy morels. It was so tender it practically melted like butter. Actually, now that I think about it, this wasn’t my first buttery pork chop at La Famiglia—I had a similarly memorable one during a visit earlier this year. Consistency like that deserves applause.

The dish was elevated even further by a beautifully executed wine reduction sauce. To complement the meal, I paired it with a young Barolo Marcenasco from Renato Ratti, which was an excellent match.

My guests thoroughly enjoyed their meals as well. My niece had the Caesar Salad and Penne alla Famiglia, while my friend ordered the Vitello alla Milanese. Both were very satisfied with their dishes and left equally impressed.

I passed on dessert while keeping an eye on my sugar intake, but left already looking forward to my next visit.

Very highly acclaimed restaurant for a reason! Beautiful decor, incredible food, and the evening tasting menu was incredible! Indescribably delicious, flavors that melt in your mouth. And so many great stand outs!

We recommend doing the wine pairing with the tasting menu available Tuesday- Saturdays! Pomegranate lamb shoulder was definitely the star! I would just recommend indoors over outdoors (if you have the option on reservations).

text.text:
Zahav — A World-Class Experience in Old City
I can honestly say that Zahav is one of the best restaurants I have ever experienced—not just in Philadelphia, but likely in the entire country. It is absolutely worth every bit of the hype.
The Food & "Taste of Zahav" Menu
When you dine here, you don't just order a single dish; you experience a multi-course "chef’s menu" that takes you through an incredible range of flavors.
• The Hummus: It is legendary for a reason. It tastes so fresh, it’s as if they prepared it just moments before it hit the table.
• The Experience: Every course, from the variety of small plates to the main dishes, is high-quality and packed with flavor. The drinks were also excellent and well-crafted.
Service & Atmosphere
The atmosphere is lively and sophisticated. Regarding the service, the staff is very attentive and professional, ensuring everything runs smoothly. While the service was efficient, it felt a bit formal and lacked a personal or warm touch. It wasn't rude by any means, just very "by the book," which is good to know if you're expecting a more conversational experience.
Reservations & Tips
This is one of the hardest tables to get in the city, so plan ahead—reservations often book out a month or more in advance.
• Pro-Tip: If you can’t snag a reservation, try walking in right when they open to see if you can grab a seat at the bar or catch a last-minute cancellation.
Final Verdict: It is pricey, but for a meal that many consider to be among the best in the world, it is well worth the investment. I would go back in a heartbeat!

If you're looking for one of the best dining experiences of your life, Zahav is the place to be! Unbelievably unique, creative, and high-quality Israeli/Middle Eastern dishes with dazzling attention to detail and service (especially from Chef Daniel who was so kind and welcoming!).

Some of our favorite dishes included the pomegranate lamb shoulder, roasted figs, piping hot fresh laffa bread with multiple delicious dips, and the fried cauliflower with herbed labneh. The signature cocktails were delightful and complemented each course perfectly. For dessert, the chocolate malabi and pear cardamom sorbet were a refreshingly sweet ending to a phenomenal meal. Overall, can't recommend this restaurant highly enough and I still think about this dining experience all the time.

Be sure to make reservations far in advance to guarantee yourself a table. I will be visiting every time I visit Philadelphia, as this was a truly a special restaurant! Shout out again to Chef Daniel who made every moment of this meal special for me and my friend.

text.text:
Five stars, no hesitation.

Stumbled into Sassafras on a Sunday afternoon and somehow walked into the exact vibe you hope for but rarely find. Live jazz drifting through the room, including a beautiful rendition of Sunday Girl from Impademada that just set the tone. Relaxed, soulful, and effortlessly cool.

The cocktails are where this place really shines. Thoughtful twists on classics, each one balanced and beautifully made. You can tell there’s real craft behind the bar, not just show.

Speaking of the bar, Shay, the bartender from Louisiana, is a standout. Warm, engaging, and clearly knows her stuff. She made the whole experience feel personal, like you were a regular even if it’s your first visit.

Small touches matter too. The bowl of assorted olives was perfect alongside the drinks, simple but elevated.

Only note, and it’s minor, give us 2–3 pretzels instead of just one. That’s it.

Otherwise, a perfect Sunday afternoon. This is the kind of place you come back to, and then bring friends to show them you’ve found something special.

text.text:
I wish Jen and I had shown up in matching flapper dresses because Sassafras feels like stepping straight into the 1920s. Huge bar, giant wall of liquor bottles, dim lighting, and a cool old-school vibe.
I told the bartender that ordering a beer in a place like this felt like I was insulting him. He laughed and told me not to worry about it. The drink special was called “Naked and Famous,” which honestly sounded like the perfect cocktail to order in honor of Jen. But then I spotted a dark beer on the menu that sounded too good to pass up.
If you follow me, you know I’m slowly becoming a dark beer guy. I liked it a lot.
The sandwich special was a cheesesteak. Sorry, I should’ve taken a picture of the menu. But I really enjoyed it, and for $18 it came with a mountain of seasoned fries, which feels like a bargain these days.
Bomb Shell: the two people working absolutely crushed it. I don’t know if they were understaffed or if Monday night got busier than expected, but they were working their tails off the entire time. Even with that, they stayed polite, friendly, helpful, and incredibly accommodating to the guy carrying around a mannequin.
Great visit to Sassafras!

text.text:
I rarely leave negative reviews, but this was one of the worst dining experiences I've had in a long time.

Oh Brother Philly served the worst cheesesteak I've ever had.

Summary:
1. Dry, bland steak with almost no flavor
2. Hot dining area and dirty restroom
3. Long wait times and disorganized service

We chose this restaurant because of its excellent Google ratings. However, I had a bad feeling the moment I walked in. The line was long, and we waited quite a while for our food. I assumed it must be worth the wait because it seemed so popular. Unfortunately, I was completely disappointed after the first bite.

The cheesesteak was incredibly dry and bland. The meat had almost no seasoning, not even enough salt and very little flavor overall. I tried adding the sweet peppers and pickles, but nothing could save it. It was, without question, the worst cheesesteak I've ever eaten.

The service didn't make the experience any better. The staff was polite enough, but they were not welcoming or attentive, and there was little sense of hospitality.

The dining area was also very uncomfortable. There was no air conditioning, only a few ceiling fans spinning slowly, making the restaurant uncomfortably hot. There was only one restroom, which resulted in a long line, and it was not clean.

What surprised me most was the number of positive reviews. The restaurant encourages customers to leave Google reviews in exchange for free fried Oreos. I decided to participate, but after waiting for quite some time, I asked about my dessert. I was told that my order had never made it to the kitchen and that I would need to wait another 5–10 minutes. More than 10 minutes later, my two fried Oreos finally arrived and they were just average.

This was the most disappointing restaurant I visited in Philadelphia.

If you're a tourist looking for an authentic Philly cheesesteak, I'd recommend going to Reading Terminal Market instead. In my experience, the cheesesteaks there are far better than the one I had at Oh Brother Philly.

There were a selection of free side toppings near the fountain drinks: sweet peppers, spicy pickles, hot peppers. Adding them into our cheesesteak brought the taste profile up to a whole other level.

My boyfriend and I were so happy with the 10/10 meal that we had to return the next day before we had to head back home. If and when we come back to Philly, this will for sure be in the itinerary!

Our dinner started with a platter containing two bruschetta as well as additional freshly made warm Italian bread. Our salads, hers Gorgonzola, pear and nuts, mine goat cheese atop spring mix, were fresh and imaginative. Given that every table appeared to be in use, we did end up waiting another 25 minutes after the salad for our entrees. text.text:
Went here and was excited to try their Dan Dan noodles. Ended up getting that and the fried green beans. The atmosphere was great, there were just two things I wasn't a fan of.

The food was cooked very well, but it had little spice. This was a disappointment, particularly because this restaurant says it is a Sichuan restaurant and I had no Sichuan peppercorns in either my my dishes. Both were listed as spicy, with at least one up to 7/10. To me it was a 2/10 but again that's subjective. Really, the dishes should have had Sichuan peppercorns no matter the slice level.

What also happened was that I found there was happy hour (food and drinks) when there, but only if I was sitting at the bar. I wasn't offered the seating option when I entered, only to the dining area. One, it's odd that happy hour is only based on seating, but two to not be offered that when walking in was confusing and unhelpful. In the future, I hope that is made clear during happy hour or the seating dependence is removed.

Overall food is great, it just needs more spice. And please either remove the seating policy for happy hour or make it clear to customers when they come in.

Stopped by here for a late lunch with the family. It was close to our hotel (walking distance). We went during a time when it wasn't busy. We were welcomed by a staff member who seated us right away. Those who took our order and brought out the food were friendly and efficient. Overall, the food was good. The scallion pancakes were a little on the smaller size. The shrimp for the honey walnut dish was not what we had initially expected -- it was breaded, similar to that of Chinese chicken fingers -- but still good. The shrimp lo mein had an added taste which I was trying to identify. It reminded me of pork or some kind of meat -- but again, still good.

The place was nice, spacious with high ceilings, and has a huge bar. It reminded me of a bar/lounge back in NYC, but it was a little dim.

Overall, it was a decent place to get some Chinese food in the area. Also, I believe they will be moving locations soon.

text.text: I've been wanting to have a meal at Morimoto for many years.  I was a big fan of the original Iron Chef many years ago so that may have influenced me a bit. We all ordered several courses and passed bites around the table so that everyone got to try everything that they cared to.  The atmosphere was relaxed with low light, and sparse decorations so you weren't distracted from the meal or the fellowship.  The cocktail menu was extensive, the sake selection even more so.  As many others have noted, the light fixtures on the table are a little weird, but not enough take anything away from the experience.  LOL  From seating until we were out the door was around 3 hours and that was just right for our group.  We took our time over each course and never felt rushed by the staff.  Truly a memorable meal!!

text.text:
Why is it so hard to find an excellent hotel restaurant in the U.S?  My boys and I had a long day.  We drove down from the NYC, had great food in Philly, visited the Please Touch Museum and wanted to relax at the hotel.  We decided to have dinner at Keating’s Rope & Anchor and were very disappointed.  Is it really difficult to have an intimate, authentic, good quality meal?  I don’t think so.   It is sad when a Hilton knows that they have a captive audience and provides a mediocre experience.

The one highlight is how friendly the staff is.  Christina was assigned our table and she was excellent.

text.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Fresh sushi, flavorful ramen, and a hidden gem in Philly!

I visited Oishii Sushi & Ramen and it quickly became one of my favorite spots for sushi and Japanese comfort food in the city. Everything tasted fresh, looked absolutely beautiful, and was full of flavor.

The only small downside is the seating area is a bit limited, so it can feel tight when it gets busy — but honestly the food is absolutely worth the visit at any time.

💁🏻‍♀️ Here’s what I tried:

🥗 Oishii Poke Bowl
Fresh, colorful, and packed with flavor. The fish tasted incredibly fresh and the mix of toppings added great texture and balance.

🍣 Inari
Light, slightly sweet tofu pockets filled with seasoned rice. Simple but delicious and very satisfying.

🥟 Gyoza
Perfectly pan-fried dumplings — crispy on the outside and juicy inside with a flavorful pork filling.

🍜 Spicy Tonkotsu Ramen
Rich, creamy broth with a nice spicy kick. The noodles were perfectly cooked and the toppings made it a very comforting bowl.

🍜 Shrimp Yakisoba
Savory stir-fried noodles with tender shrimp and vegetables. Super flavorful and cooked just right.

🍣 Salmon Lobster Roll
Fresh salmon sashimi paired with rich lobster for a really indulgent sushi roll. Great texture and flavor combination.

🍣 Las Vegas Signature Roll
One of the most flavorful rolls I tried. Crispy, savory, and topped with delicious sauces that make every bite exciting.

🍣 Tokyo Signature Roll
Beautifully presented with fresh fish and balanced flavors. Very smooth and satisfying.

🐙 Takoyaki
Soft, savory octopus balls topped with sauce and bonito flakes. Warm, fluffy, and full of umami flavor.

Overall:
Great sushi, comforting ramen, and flavorful Japanese dishes all in one place. Even though the seating area is a little small, the quality of the food makes this spot completely worth visiting.

If you’re looking for fresh sushi and ramen in Philadelphia, I definitely recommend checking this place out. I love this place and will definitely be coming back! 🍣🍜
