text.text:
I was excited to go to a New Mexican restarant near washington square. We arrived around 6:20pm. We ordered off Birria burrito and steak enchiladas with a blue Hawaiian and a mango margaritas.

The Birria burrito was good but lacked any sides. It had a tasty dipping sauce. The steak enchilada dish was disappointing. The rice and beans were cold and bland. My steak enchiladas was actually a cheese enchiladas with steak and green sauce spread on top. Nothing else was inside my tortilla. The green sauce was a little too acidic.

Our drinks were very contrasting The blue Hawaiian was strong with two shots of rum. While my margaritas which ended up being a happy hour special tasted flavorful but lacked a kick of tequila.

Our service was great at the start but went downhill as the dinner progressed. We waited 10-15 minutes trying to get our bill with only a few tables with customers. We also did not get the happy hour menu 4-7pm so would could have ordered off of that menu but wasn’t told or provided any HH menus. See my picture for HH menu.

The decor was nice with some Mexican themed murals with some music in the background. The entire restaurant was very clean and well kept. There was a steady stream of to go orders being picked up and even 2-3 police officers picking up take away dinners.

I was extremely disappointed with dinner but I would give DBB&B another chance.  Try it out and let me know how yours turned out.

If you've been searching for an authentic Philly cheesesteak, stop looking and head to Lamberti Pizza & Market! I had been wanting to try a real Philly cheesesteak for the longest time, and this place absolutely delivered. The steak was tender, flavorful, and piled high, the bread was fresh, and every bite tasted like the real deal.
The pizza and market sandwichs are just as impressive, and the staff made the experience even better with their friendly service. It's one of those places that feels like a hidden gem. You walk in for one meal and walk out with more food immediately start planning your next visit. Whether you're craving a cheesesteak, pizza, or just quality Italian food, Lamberti is definitely worth the trip. Highly recommend!

text.text: I spent over $30 here for two cheesesteaks with paid extras, and the entire experience was a disaster from start to finish. This restaurant is exactly four stars in my book. Only because my family and I agreed the pizza was pretty good, but it wasn’t great. Neither were the garlic knots. We’re not super picky about them either, they just didn’t hit. I really wanted to like their garlic knots cuz they do them very cool like a cinnamon roll. The sausage is that really crumbly, ground sausage. Again, not their fault, it’s just our least favorite. We prefer larger crumbles or sliced sausage.

The employees that helped us were nice. They gave us plates for our to-go order and made sure we were set up.

It’s definitely laid out like a pizza joint in the city with a smaller footprint, but they make it work. Several tables and chairs available for seating.

I would definitely recommend giving this place a try if you’re in the area. Hopefully it’ll be a five star experience for you and/or your family.

Came here for a birthday celebration and overall had a good experience. The ambiance and decor were beautiful and definitely a great spot for a date night or special occasion.

Our server Briana was very friendly, attentive, and helpful throughout the meal. Since it was our first time here, she took the time to explain the menu and even asked if we were celebrating anything which I appreciated. The host however, could’ve been a little more welcoming.

We started with the Wagyu egg rolls which were decent but a bit dry. For entrees, we ordered the Braised Oxtail Lo Mein and the lamb chops. The oxtail lo mein was delicious and full of flavor. The lamb chops were flavorful but we ordered them medium well and they came out more well done than expected.

We ended with the chocolate cake for dessert. It tasted a little store bought but it was still a nice touch that they brought it out with a candle for the birthday celebration. Overall, good food, great service from Briana, and a really nice atmosphere.

text.text:
I recently visited Mei Mei in Philadelphia and had one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in a long time. The food was outstanding, the cocktails were creative and balanced, and the entire atmosphere made it easy to settle in and enjoy the evening.

The highlight of the experience was CK behind the bar. It’s immediately obvious that he genuinely loves bartending and has a real passion for pairing food and cocktails. He didn’t just take drink orders—he asked questions, made thoughtful recommendations, and explained how certain cocktails would complement different dishes. His knowledge and enthusiasm elevated the entire meal.

What impressed me most was his level of hospitality. Even during the busiest moments, when he seemed to be making drinks nonstop, he still found time to check in with guests, make sure everyone was enjoying themselves, and answer questions. Somehow he managed to make every person at the bar feel seen and taken care of.

Great food and drinks will bring people in, but exceptional service is what makes them come back. CK provided exactly that. If you visit Mei Mei, I highly recommend sitting at the bar and letting him guide your experience. It turned a great meal into a memorable night.

text.text:
We chose this beautiful restaurant for our Father's Day celebration and were incredibly impressed by the stunning decor and fantastic music playlist. We arrived shortly after opening, which meant there weren't many other customers present. While our server was very friendly, service was a bit slow at times, starting with a 10-minute wait just to be greeted at our table.  Instead of individual entrees, we shared several plates. The Short Rib Lo Mein was delicious, and while the Mei Mei Fried Rice was okay on its own, the addition of the thick sweet soy sauce we requested took it to a "10"! The Ribeye Egg Rolls tasted like the typical cheese steak egg roll but featured great meat quality.  The Taiwanese Chicken Wings tasted like classic buffalo wings, and the Spare Ribs had fantastic flavor (though some bites were slightly tough). The deviled eggs were simply average.  We also had a few alcoholic beverages that were tasty,  including one that was on the house in honor of our Father's day celebration.  I would definitely go back again.  It is also worth noting that gratuity was already included, a fact that I almost missed upon receiving the bill.

Parking tip: On-street paid parking takes some patience to find but it is possible, there is also a paid garage at the end of the street.

I visited for the first time to celebrate my mother’s birthday, and overall we had a great experience. The staff was incredibly friendly, we were seated quickly, and both our food and drinks came out in a timely manner. The drinks were good, though the food portions and menu selection were a bit smaller than I expected.

The restaurant is absolutely beautiful, with a gorgeous aesthetic and a lovely ambiance. I do think the music could have been turned up just a bit to enhance the overall vibe. They also make birthdays and special occasions feel festive with sparklers, which was a nice touch. I was a little surprised there wasn’t a complimentary birthday dessert, and it’s worth noting that a service charge of about 20% was automatically added to our final bill.

Overall, it’s a beautiful establishment with great service and a nice atmosphere. With a few small adjustments, it could easily be an even better experience.

text.text:
I discovered The Angelo Pizza by chance while out with a friend, and it turned out to be an exceptional find.

As someone who enjoys exploring different pizza spots across the city, I pay close attention to styles, flavors, textures, and the quality of ingredients used. From the very first bite, it was clear that The Angelo Pizza stands out for its commitment to fresh, high-quality ingredients and pizzas made entirely from scratch. That dedication creates a truly remarkable taste. One of my favorites on the menu is St. Antney’s, it’s so delicious that I could enjoy it every day.

The restaurant itself has a warm and cozy atmosphere. While the indoor space is modest in size, it’s comfortable for dining in, and during the summer, outdoor seating is available. A particularly important feature is its wheelchair accessibility, including a private restroom—an amenity that isn’t common in many restaurants in the area and one I truly appreciate.

The service is equally impressive. Angelo, the owner, is welcoming, friendly, and a passionate baseball fan. From the moment you walk in, you’re greeted with genuine hospitality and a positive atmosphere that makes you want to return.

Whether you’re a Philadelphia local, a tourist, or simply passing through, if you’re craving excellent pizza, The Angelo Pizza is a must-visit.

Rosario’s has become my go-to for pizza delivery in Philly. This is the best pizza I’ve had in Philly, and I’ve tried a lot. Mexican style pizza is a unique and genius concept! Their American style pizzas are also delicious.
The crust is absolutely perfect every time - so flavorful you wouldn’t dare toss it! Great quality, fresh ingredients and loads of toppings. Order the La Chicana pizza - you will be forever changed.
Fries are also delicious, esp with cheese whiz + add bacon. They absolutely do not skimp on toppings here! Thank you for doing what you do - please don’t change!! There’s a lot of love here.

EDIT: I tried the burritos today and they are out of this WORLD. We got the pastor burrito and steak burrito. They are HUGE, the size of your head. So much meat inside!! I am so so happy to know of Rosario’s and the clear effort and pure love they put into this incredible hidden gem in Philly.

Another Edit: Tried the cheesesteak today - it’s good!

text.text:
Tucked away on lively South Street, this unassuming Indian restaurant turned out to be a pleasant surprise. We visited on Independence Day, and the place was packed with diners—always a good sign.

We ordered chicken tandoori, lamb biryani, butter naan, matar paneer, and both salted and mango lassi. The chicken tandoori came out hot and smoky, with that perfect char you hope for. The lamb biryani was rich, fragrant, and generously portioned, with tender pieces of lamb throughout. The butter naan was soft and pillowy, great for scooping up the creamy matar paneer, which had a lovely balance of spice and comfort. The salted lassi was a refreshing break from the heat, while the mango lassi was thick, sweet, and satisfying.

Overall, the food was genuinely delicious, the portions generous, and the atmosphere lively. A solid spot for anyone craving classic Indian flavors in the heart of Philly.

text.text:
I rarely give five-star reviews that wholeheartedly encourage people to go out of their way to visit somewhere — but Old Towne and Sanna’s is one of those places.

How we found it:
We’d been hearing about this spot for a while from our Lebanese friends. On a Saturday afternoon walk with our dog, we finally decided to stop in and see for ourselves. We’re glad we did.

The hospitality:
Sam welcomed us the moment we sat down and treated us like family. My girlfriend is Lebanese, so we know our way around the menu, but Sam’s warmth stood out on its own. In the short time we were there, at least five people walked by and greeted him like an old friend. That kind of community presence is rare and says everything about how he runs this place — as an experience, not a transaction.

The food:
Authentic, rich, inspired, and clearly made with care. The muhammara, hummus, tabbouleh, warak enab, and chicken platter were all standouts — every plate had depth and balance, and nothing felt phoned in.
Honestly, between the flavor, the range of the menu, and the way we were treated, this was a better meal than any I’ve had at Suraya or Li Beirut in the city.

For dog owners:
Even our pup got the royal treatment — one of the most ornate water bowls she’s ever been served. She was treated like a princess.

Bottom line:
Whether you’re headed to Igloo for ice cream, out for a walk in the neighborhood, or specifically planning a meal, go out of your way to stop in here. You won’t be disappointed — and like us, you may have just found a new regular spot.

We had our wedding dinner here and the whole experience from beginning to end was absolutely top-tier. The owner Mike was able to work with our family-style long table style dinner, many event requests, and our guests not-so-easy allergy restrictions. The day of their team helped with setting up place settings and some light decor before which helped us out tremendously and also alleviated the stress of outsourcing someone.

Mike also made the experience totally customizable to my liking when it came to the event layout to the menu options - he was flexible with just about anything from suggestions and if he wasn’t available his assistant Alysia answered my questions right away via email and he also gave me his number as well for any day of questions.

We can’t also say enough about Dom who was one of the servers during the night of our dinner. He was so personable and proactive in ensuring everyone’s glass was full and making sure everyone had what they wanted! He even helped my handicap father down the stairs at the end of the night - truly a saint who deserves all the flowers!

Thank you so much Miles Table team and thanking for making our day so incredibly special - you truly bring the meaning of family into everything you guys do!

Don’t sleep on this gem for your event needs! If I could give a thousand stars I would.

text.text:
Reliable, Kid-Approved Comfort Delivered Fast

Randazzo’s isn’t my personal favorite, but when it comes to pleasing my boys, it’s the ultimate go-to. When I need a quick, guaranteed hit of a meal for them, this is the spot I count on every time.

Their cheesesteak, always ordered with Cheese Whiz, fried onions, and a squirt of ketchup is a staple. Add to that a piping hot pizza loaded with pepperoni and bacon, and I’ve got two very happy kids. One thing I really appreciate is the flexibility with toppings. It’s one of the few places where you can customize different sections of the pizza, perfect for picky eaters or families with mixed tastes.

I usually order via DoorDash and the delivery is consistently fast, accurate, and still hot when it arrives. It’s not fancy, but it’s reliable, satisfying, and hits the mark when you need an easy win with the kiddos.

A nice night out in Philly!  Was visiting friends in Philly and we went out for a nice dinner.   The plan was we had a reservation,but   a technical snafu on our end never processed the reservation, clearly a simple mistake.  When we arrived, our non existent reservation was not there.  Luckily we arrived before it was to busy and they managed to find a table. Original:
I only got a bagel sandwich here (sausage egg and cheese) and it was only okay. In all fairness, I usually get them on blueberry or everything bagels and they had run out of those and only had plain (I can just before close). Eating a bagel sandwich with a plane bagel is probably the best way to judge one for flavor but I’ve only done it like twice. What I found here is little to no balance in the ingredients: The cheese was all texture and no taste, it added nothing to the sandwich (a good sharp tasting cheddar would have gone a long way). The eggs were bland enough that I forgot they were there. The sausage was alright, maybe a bit too peppery but I bet it would have been much better if it wasn’t the only source of flavor. And I don’t think I can complain about the plain bagel, had good texture.

I might come back to try the bacon on an everything or blueberry if they have it, but I might pass. Not sure!

text.text:
Great family dinner spot with options for everyone!

This was our first time at The Side Car and we were really pleased. It can be tough for me to find classic bar food that still works with being gluten free and mostly plant based, so I was thrilled to see both an appetizer and an entrée that fit my needs.

The brussel sprout appetizer was fabulous, though be warned, it’s spicy. I love heat, so it was perfect for me. My entrée, the new vegan enchiladas, was also great. They were flavorful without being overly heavy, which made the whole meal feel satisfying but not too filling.

The rest of my family raved about the Detroit style pizza and the wings. We will definitely be back. The service was spot on, the food was enjoyable, and while the atmosphere was loud, it was still manageable for a fun family night out. Best of all, the prices felt reasonable, especially compared to many places that feel a bit overpriced for a family dinner.

Highly recommend!

text.text:
Fortune Chinese on South Street has become our preferred neighborhood spot for Chinese American takeout, and it consistently delivers exactly what you want from a place like this. The food is reliable and flavorful, without being overly greasy or salty, and the portions are generous and filling.

We usually order a combination of Mongolian beef, shrimp egg rolls, kung pao chicken, General Tso’s chicken, shrimp fried rice, and white rice, and everything is consistently good. It hits that classic takeout balance: satisfying, well-prepared, and easy to return to regularly.

The service stands out as well. The man who runs the counter is kind and welcoming, always smiling when you come in, which we really appreciate. He’s also generous with the mustard packets and soy sauce at the front, a small touch that doesn’t go unnoticed. The space is very clean, and while there are tables for dining in, most people seem to opt for takeout.

Fortune Chinese is a convenient and dependable local option for us, and one we return to often. Highly recommend if you’re looking for a quick, consistent, and genuinely enjoyable Chinese American takeout meal.

One minor suggestion: the menu on the online ordering portal might need a slight adjustment. General Tso’s chicken, which is excellent, is listed in the combo and meal sections but not under the main chicken category, which has been a bit perplexing for me in the past. A small tweak would make ordering even smoother.

Highly recommended. Thank you!

A good place to go for southern food and drinks.

When the family needed a new Christmas tradition we looked for a intimate, quant, family owned restaurant that felt like just like Nonna's. La Sera is it. We started with sharing the Mussels, Arugula Beet Salad, and the Calamari. Your gonna need a pairing but since this is BYOB you bring what makes sense but we brought a Vermintino for the White Sauces and a DOCG Chianti reserve to compliment the red sauces. Pick your battle.

The staff was attentive, helpful, personable and fast. Waters never lowered beyond a halffull. Nonna would be proud.

After trying everything you really can't go wrong, if your curious I suggest the Spaghetti Carbonara, Chicken Parmesan, or the Alfredo Linguine they were impressive. If you still have room and you should make sure you do...I suggest the Tiramisu or the Canolis they were fresh and delicious. We'll definitely be at La Sera next Christmas.

text.text:
Sabrina’s Café on South Street is one of those places that immediately comes to mind whenever friends are visiting town and want a great brunch spot. It’s been a Philadelphia favorite for years, and after multiple visits, it’s easy to understand why. Sabrina’s started as a small neighborhood café and has built a loyal following thanks to its creative menu, massive portions, and consistently good food.
You can almost always expect a bit of a wait, but that's usually a good sign. We stopped by on a Saturday morning and waited about 15–20 minutes, which honestly wasn't bad at all considering how popular the place is. The South Street location has a fun energy to it and is in a great area to walk around before or after your meal.
One nice bonus at this location is that they serve alcohol, making it a great spot for a true brunch experience. The portions here are no joke either. I ordered the triple-stack chocolate chip pancakes and had to take some home because there was no way I was finishing them in one sitting. We also ordered the Ultimate Mexy Scramble, which was just as filling and packed with flavor.
The space is a little tight inside, but that's part of the charm. The music was great, the atmosphere was lively, and there was a steady flow of people coming through the door all morning. It felt like a true neighborhood staple rather than a trendy brunch spot trying too hard.
Overall, Sabrina’s continues to be one of the most reliable brunch spots in Philadelphia. Great portions, creative menu options, and a fun atmosphere make it a place I keep coming back to. If you're looking for brunch in Philly, this should absolutely be on your list. I'll definitely be back, and it's usually one of the first places I recommend when friends come to town.

text.text:
This was our second time dining at Illata, and it definitely won’t be our last.

From the moment you walk in, the service is exceptional. Down to earth, welcoming, genuinely friendly, and a huge part of what makes the whole experience so special. A huge shout-out to Mary and Maggie. You two are absolutely fantastic.

Then there’s the food. We can confidently say we’ve tried every dish on the menu, and every single one came with a genuine “wow” at first bite. The standout dishes for us were the carrot and crab, the pasta, the tuna and the lamb, but honestly, there isn’t a weak link on the menu. 10/10. No notes.

This is the kind of place you go when you want a memorable meal, but it’s also exactly the kind of restaurant you wish was your regular spot. Somehow it manages to be both. We already can’t wait to come back.

text.text:
Exquisite! I lived in Point Breeze for a while and decided to try Insatiable just a little before I moved out. Well, let me tell you how disappointed I was to not have tried this place sooner! From the cocktails to the food, this establishment deserves more praises. Go-to cocktail: Drunk Text ($15), a great choice if you like Mezcal.
For food, I don’t know how to put this more plainly, you have to get the Tuna Wontons and the Shrimp Tostadas. The Tuna Wontons is what made me go back to Insatiable a second time… and then a third time… and I am on my way for my fourth time. The tuna is cooked perfectly, but you have to like tuna that is tataki style. If you do like it like that, then you will be the happiest when you have a bite of that Tuna Wonton, especially since the wonton taste so fresh and the wasabi sauce gives it the perfect quick. If you want to continue riding the asian flavor profile of the menu, the cucumber salad is divine. I drank the leftover sesame dressing, that’s how good it is.
The great discovery during the third time I went there was the Shrimp Tostadas, what a delicious, fresh, home-made (I assume) tostada with a perfectly cooked shrimp. There was so much flavor. I am going back a fourth time for these.
Main course-wise, they were out of lobster roll so I went for the burger. I typically don’t go for burgers but given how good the food had already been the previous times, I knew my burger was going to come out delicious. And, to no one’s surprise, it did. There was also a steak frites order at my table, but that wasn’t as good as the burger. The dessert was not interesting, it was an apple crisp with a square of flaky dough but the dough didn’t taste good (it had a freezer taste) and the apples were too sugary.

Basically, don’t go there for desserts, in fact you won’t need to get desserts because if you order their small plates and some main dishes, you will already be the happiest full stomach. And, even better if you get a cocktail because that really ties it together.

Enjoy!

P.S.: Service was great, 10/10.

text.text:
I typically prefer local, family owned and operated restaurants. Maybe we just came on an off day but, they fell short on several areas.

First off, we got two of the “craft cocktails”. Weirdly, both of them, with vastly different ingredients, looked and tasted strikingly similar yet at the same time quite bland.

Second, the menu promises rich, flavorful gastropub fare. It fails to deliver. Everything we got tasted overly salty except for one, the “Salted Caramel Brownie” dessert.

Another pet peeve of mine if filtered water. Look tap water is fine but, in major cities, it heavily treated and it tastes like it. If you run a restaurant you HAVE to filter your water. Otherwise, every glass of water, every cup of coffee, every cup of tea and every cocktail that has soda in it is gonna taste like bleach. You shouldn’t own a restaurant if you don’t know that.

Here’s hoping they get it together.

text.text:
I would have a hard time coming anywhere near this part of town without stopping back in; pastries are bold and unique, so delicious. The porchetta sandwich comes in many renditions; there's the tried and true OG, with other sandwich varieties and names building off that. I got the Truffle Pig, which I'd get a hundred times over; the subtle truffle mushroom flavor becomes one with that goat cheese spread and sneaks into every bite, but doesn't smother or overpower.

The crackling (a crisp but more meaty and dense pork rind plank) included on most of their sandwiches is such a clutch addition and I'll be looking for it in more places now; it doesn't break down or burst into dust and holds up much better than a chip for that extra crunch to a sandwich. Along with the seeded roll, you can tell there has been heavy consideration given to the way texture and crunch can elevate any sandwich.

We tried a variety of sweets, too many to name, but the tahini halva blondie stood out to me, and on our way back with the sandwiches I had to chug a very refreshing corpse reviver spritz (juniper berry, citrus peel, elderflower, star anise, lemon seltzer).

The food here is simply phenomenal. I come here very often and it’s consistently great. The Omelettes and sandwiches are amazing. They know how to cook an egg!

You’re in for a treat if they still have pastries or bread pudding (the bread pudding is out of this world - they use their own croissants).

Every Saturday they typically have a special sandwich or something like that - often very good.

Jordan the host / waitress /  part of family team and her parents are amazing hosts. It’s always so warm and friendly.

The cafe is well lit. The prices are reasonable. It’s a neighborhood staple that has been around for a long time and gets a lot of regulars. You’ll feel like you’re in a small town in southern France but in the heart of Philadelphia.

They play relaxed level music that doesn’t distract and allows you to talk.

A good place to bring a dog if sitting outside.

Can’t say enough great things!

text.text:
We imagined this place will be good, but we did not imagine it’s gonna be this good.

My husband and I celebrated our anniversary here. Their staff reminded us this is BYOB and recommended us to grab a bottle of wine from the nearby liquor store. We highly appreciate this suggestion and would like to suggest everyone bring your favorite wine and enjoy it at this place, because their food is feast level enjoyable.

Admittedly, we went over the top in ordering and tried very many dishes. We are absolutely happy about each and everything we got and super impressed by the gnocchi and the stufato. The texture of the gnocchi was so great. It was soft like a pillow, holding together very well, easy to squish, but not mushy. And their calamari is at the perfect spot of tenderness and chewy-ness. The sauce came with the stufato was so delicious. I think I can just take shots of this sauce and not get tired of it.

We definitely see ourselves come back here frequently, and would highly recommend this place to anybody who wants to celebrate a special occasion, treat themselves with the best homestyle Italian food there can be, but also keep a budget.

text.text:
Honest review:

Staff was very pleasant! Very nice kind people, talked to us with great enthusiasm and kindness. We were a table of 4 people and I would say the table was very very small. We were fighting to have enough space for our plates and drinks.

I also would say the food is unfortunately overpriced. I paid $26 for a bolognese and was finished eating just as my friend was starting. We also paid $16 for a Caesar salad appetizer which was not a lot and very expensive for an appetizer with no protein on a small plate.

It was generally nice and a great BYOB but wouldn’t come back. I do want to reemphasize every staff member was so kind to us. The food was also very good.

Edit: I appreciate the feedback from the owner but it seems he comes on to these reviews to berate people in a very childish manner when they give any sort of criticism. I find it to be very unprofessional - but wishing you the best.

I ordered online through ubereats. My build your own chicken souvklaki sandwich was fine…. missing some flavor but somewhat fine. i ordered the spanakopita as an app and i think whoever prepared it severely missed the mark in every way possible. it tasted resembling of wet cardboard, paper bag, construction paper and was close to burnt? this was probably one of most unsettling foods i’ve ever ingested. i’m the last person to review a restaurant badly but this slice of spanakopita set me over the edge. i will be looking forward to a supervisor/owner explaining why i spent nearly $10 of crunchy burnt paper, soggy, greasy in the middle, concoction with slimy spinach that they call “spanakopita.” I warn customers to not order this item online unless you see you can see it in the restaurant before it’s served.
i added an extra star because i’ve ordered here a handful of times and the food usually is solid.

First time customer, stumbled upon this on Google maps. Odd location, it's a walk up window but you're definitely in the way of trucks and other cars in the space when you pull in. Besides that, Menu looks amazing and the person taking my order was great!

I ordered an egg sandwich and brisket hashbrowns (pictured) with a juice, which came to $14. The sandwich was a little messy and the eggs weren't completely cooked but it still tastes good. I would definitely like to try the other sandwiches.

The hashbrowns confused me.  I mistakenly assumed the brisket would be on top.  After eating one and not finding brisket inside, I thought I received the wrong order. I called to ask and the young lady explained the brisket is mixed into the hash browns. No problem, didn't hurt to ask.  However,  out of the 5 or 6 pieces I had, only 2 contained brisket.  The taste is unmistakable and easy to tell between the ones that had none.

This place has mice.

Went to get drinks with friends on 5/14 and there were at least 3-5 mice running around under the bar. We tried to tell the bartender and they were downright rude. Man and a woman told us to "call the police" and ignored us. We weren't trying to make a big deal but their response was ridiculous. I will be calling the health department and sending along photos/videos.

Also, I let it slide at the time but the last time I went here I paid the check, they brought back the copy to be signed and it was $50 more than the previous copy. I pointed it out and they waved me off and again, ignored the complaint without so much as an apology.

The staff at this place is rude if not downright scamming people. Don't go here and if you do, check what they're charging you.

A “hidden gem” on its way to being the main attraction! I saw this place on social media and the fish kept calling me; this is one time where Instagram vs. reality are the same! The fish was delicious, tender, and a great portion (2 of us shared one and we were beyond full!). We also had the suya wings, again flavorful and filling; the mango hot sauce on the side is chef’s kiss. The sides are on the smaller side for the price point, but the entree is so huge you actually won’t be hungry when leaving. The caramelized pineapple for dessert was the first of its kind for us and we were not disappointed with our choice.

We also adored outdoor back garden/patio set up, and the inside decor was on theme for the cuisine. The customer service can be improved to be more seamless but not a dealbreaker, rather something to fine tune. All in all, a good experience and we would go back.

This place was a 10/10!!
I ordered on the run, a quick lunch platter.
Called in an order for a medium jerk chicken, mac and cheese, and yams.
My food was ready in about 15 minutes, which was exactly what I was hoping for.
The store was pretty small, but it was clean and welcoming! The guy behind the counter was nice, and he was quick with grabbing my order.
They do accept credit cards. The platter was surprisingly heavy!! For $13, I was already happy with what I got!
I had to stop at a few places before making it home to eat, so when I did get home, I had to reheat the food.
I have to say, EVERYTHING WAS still DELICIOUS!!
The chicken was flavored perfectly! It was so spicy that sweat was dripping down my back, and that's how I like my jerk chicken! Mac was cheesy and flavorful! And the YAMS! OMG, THE YAMS!
I got full after eating about half the platter, but it was so good that I couldn't stop eating. However, I couldn't finish it all, so I saved some for my husband to try!
We both have decided that when we go to PA, this will be the new spot for Jamaican food!

Mr. Jerk PUT IN THAT WORK!
🌟 🌟 🌟 🌟 🌟

text.text:
Their food is really good!
I am picky about Jamaican food and have been trying to find a new place since my old favorite closed last year. I'm glad to finally have gotten around to trying Mr. Jerk and I wish I would have done it sooner.

I ordered the curry chicken, jerk chicken, yams, and mac and cheese, and was really happy with everything.

The curry chicken was well-seasoned and the jerk chicken had the perfect amount of spice. The meat on both was tender and moist, cooked perfectly, with flavor all the way down to the bone.
Rice and peas and cabbage were seasoned in their own right, not bland,
and the texture was just right, not too soft or too hard.
Mac and cheese was tasty, pretty textbook macaroni pie.
But the secret ingredient to the plate had to be the yams lol. By themselves, they were just this side of too sweet for me, but when I mixed them with the other savory dishes, that hit of sweetness just amplified the whole plate and brought it together.
Especially with the jerk chicken, because it had the heat to play against. And I also really liked it with the macaroni pie.
Those yams have been living rent free in my head lol. I'll just be eating something and I'm like dang, you know what would really set this off? Mr. Jerk's yams lmao.
I got everything in large and was happy with the portions and the pricing.
I ordered through UberEats, and my order was completed perfectly, including the notes I left.
I really appreciated the attention to detail and service provided, because those things make a big difference.

Oh I almost forgot! I tried the cake too, the pound cake. Yall gotta get you some of that, it was good as hell. Very dense, but not heavy and not too sweet. I could have done with a bit of lemon to it, but it was a really good cake. Very satisfying end to the meal.

Overall, I had a really positive experience with Mr. Jerk and will definitely keep them as my go-to spot when I'm feeling for Jamaican.

Give them a try, I'm sure you won't be disappointed!

text.text:
We live in the neighborhood and have walked past Banshee countless times. Every time, we’d stop to look at the menu and ultimately decide against it—mostly because we couldn’t get past the idea of paying $16 for a carrot.

This was our second visit, though, because our first experience completely won us over. This time, we finally tried the famous $16 carrot. It was good, but not our favorite dish.

What keeps bringing us back are the oysters, prawns, sourdough, patatas bravas, olives, salami, and outstanding cocktails. The service has been excellent on both visits, and the overall experience is consistently impressive.

Banshee definitely isn’t cheap, but for us, it’s absolutely worth it. We’re lucky to have it in the neighborhood and look forward to coming back.

I took the first bite of the Patatas Bravas and immediately found a black curly hair in it. Absolutely disgusting.

The restaurant looks nice and the interior is well designed, but every single dish we ordered was bad.

The Chicory Salad was overly bitter. The oysters were just average. The Wagyu Beef Tartare had no natural beef flavor at all because it was drowned in too much sauce, making it overwhelmingly salty. It honestly tasted like raw dumpling filling. Terrible.

The Roast Half Chicken was extremely gamey and tasted completely unfresh. I could only manage two bites. It tasted like chicken that had been repeatedly frozen and thawed, with a clearly spoiled, rotten taste. Costco’s rotisserie chicken is $5 — just go eat that instead.

Strongly do not recommend.

text.text:
GO HERE!

This location used to be Tio Flores, and we were amazed at how different the inside felt. The lighting and set up is quite nice - good atmosphere.

The bartender/waitress we had was phenomenal - very nice and the ideal level of attentiveness. She really knew the menu well and could speak to different options fluently.

We loved the hamachi crudo, chicory salad, and baked Alaska. The other dishes were also amazing - these three stood out though.

Shoutout to the tart flambé for a very unique taste, and more broadly, it was refreshing to have genuinely unique flavors / dishes at this restaurant. The food was not only delicious, but unique!

We’d be very excited to go back. They take reservations and also have a bar seating area which was quite comfortable for dinner - I usually don’t love doing bar seats but this was different and felt more private.

I went to Almyra for happy hour for the first time and absolutely loved it! It’s definitely one of the best happy hours in the city. Small plates range from $7–8 and cocktails are $7 each, which in this day and age is GREAT pricing for happy hour.

The food and cocktails were incredible, the ambiance was both beautiful and lively, and the service was impeccable. Our server consistently checked in on us throughout the evening. The happy hour menu allowed us to try so many dishes at a great price without sacrificing quality — it doesn’t get much better than that.

I highly recommend the Pyra and Synephos, along with the drink of the day. Our favorite bites were the Saganaki (which comes out in flames — such a cool photo op), all of the dips, the lamb rib, crispy rice, and the salmon skewers.

I can’t wait to come back for another happy hour!

text.text:
Philadelphia honestly doesn’t get enough credit for how incredible its food scene is, and Butcher & Singer completely proved that to me. From the moment we walked in, the whole experience felt special, classic atmosphere, beautiful space, attentive service without ever feeling overwhelming.

I have to start with the biscuits because I’m still thinking about them. I used to live in Nashville, Tennessee, a city famous for amazing biscuits, and somehow these were the best biscuits I’ve ever had in my life. Perfectly warm, buttery, soft, and unforgettable.

Everything we ordered was outstanding. The baked oysters were fantastic, the lobster tail was cooked perfectly, and the steak was exactly what you hope for when you go to a great steakhouse, rich, flavorful, and executed flawlessly.

It was also my first time trying Baked Alaska, something I’d always been curious about, and it completely lived up to the anticipation. It was spectacular and instantly became one of my favorite desserts I’ve ever had.

The entire evening felt elevated yet comfortable, the kind of restaurant that stays in your memory long after you leave. Butcher & Singer is easily one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in Philadelphia, and I already can’t wait to come back.

text.text:
We had a wonderful Saturday evening dinner at Butcher and Singer while celebrating the day before Father’s Day. It was myself, my husband, and our two boys, ages 10 and 13, and all four of us thoroughly enjoyed the experience.

What stood out most to me was how attentive and accommodating the staff was with my dietary needs. I am gluten and dairy free, and I only eat seafood occasionally, so dining out can sometimes feel limiting. Here, it felt easy. The staff was very knowledgeable and ready to modify sides as needed. They even adjusted the mushrooms and onions, which originally had a sauce containing gluten, and the modified version was absolutely delicious.

I started with the lobster cocktail, which was incredibly fresh. For my entree, I had the salmon, which was one of the more reasonably priced dishes on the menu and cooked perfectly. I also added three scallops, a lovely upgrade that made the dish feel extra special.

The service throughout the evening was excellent. The restaurant was very crowded, but we never felt rushed. When our original seating in the deep bucket seats didn’t work well for our 10-year-old, the staff accommodated us right away and moved us to a table in the middle, which made the evening much more comfortable.

My husband and one of our boys also split the Baked Alaska, one of the desserts Butcher and Singer is known for, and they said it was the perfect end to their meal. It was definitely shareable and made for a fun finale.

One thing to know before going: it is a loud, lively atmosphere, so be prepared to speak up. The good news is, everyone else is doing the same, so it fits the energy of the room.

Overall, this was a memorable meal with thoughtful service, excellent food, and real care taken around dietary restrictions. We would happily return.

text.text:
We (party of two) stopped in for a quick dinner on a Tuesday night before heading to play pickleball. We were quickly seated and given menus. They had a good number of draft craft beers, a Belgium, some IPAs, and one cider.  We ordered the short rib steak sandwich and a jerk chicken sandwich with fries. Don’t forgot to check out the daily specials on a board near the entrance. Their sandwiches were very large! My rib sandwich had a pile of rib meat with melted cheese. Even though my bun was a pretzel bun, the bottom bread bun was a little soggy and soft from the weight and heat. It was kind of a good problem to have but it might be a problem for the unadventurous eater. They also gave lettuce, tomato, and several pickle slices for toppings. The jerk sandwich tasted more like a bbq sauce. My friend was not a fan of it but it didn’t stop him from eating the whole sandwich. The fries were cooked just right, being crispy on the outside and a soft on the inside.

There were two wait staff. They bounced around their duties. Both were friendly enough and provided quick service. No complaints here.

It was around 8pm on a Tuesday but they still had about 5-6 groups at tables and a few at the bar. They even had a family dining with two children so bring you kids. The atmosphere it’s more of a sports restaurant. There are TVs playing sports games with retro music playing and a jukebox if you want to pay to play your favorite hits.

They have billards table with ample room to play around it and a dart board. There was additional seating in the back behind the bar.

Please check this place out. It has everything from good food, lots of draft beers, some wine, billards table, a dart board, jukebox, televisions playing sports games, and a friendly staff.

We were warmly welcomed by one of the owners, Sri, upon entering. We ordered mango lassis, a benne dosa, a kofta bowl, and a bucket of samosas (who doesn’t want a bucket of samosas?) For two, this amount of food was perfect. Everything was flavored beautifully and prepared with love. Before leaving, we rounded out the meal with two chais, which brought smiles to both of our faces. The food was all delicious, but Sri’s friendly demeanor made the whole dining experience exemplary. We can’t wait to go back!

text.text:
Spice Finch was a very enjoyable Mediterranean dining experience with a creative menu, beautiful presentation, and plenty of bold flavours. We ordered several dishes to share, including the whole fish, lamb shank, roasted beets, peppers, hummus, dips, and fresh breads. The lamb was incredibly tender and rich, while the fish was fresh, well-seasoned, and served with a bright herb sauce that worked perfectly with it. The smaller plates were also excellent, especially the roasted vegetables and dips, which made it easy to try a wide variety of flavours.

The restaurant has a warm, modern atmosphere and feels upscale without being overly formal. The service was friendly and helpful, although it was a little slow and inattentive at certain points, which is the main reason I would give it four stars instead of five. Overall, the food quality was very strong, the portions were good for sharing, and the experience felt worth the price. I would definitely return and recommend Spice Finch for a date night, family dinner, or group meal.

Food allergies can be very serious and I’m deeply disappointed that my allergy to tree nuts was mishandled. They were informed of my allergy at all levels and I still had an allergic reaction following my visit to spice finch. At some point our server said something to the effect of “oh did you like the roasted beets with the pistachios” and my eyes lit up because…. There shouldn’t have even been any pistachios at my table. I’d like to believe he just misspoke. But hearing that as the person with an allergy is at the very least, concerning. I would love to make an addendum to my review. I will be contacting management and would love to make an edit to this review. Outside of a potential life threatening mishap 😵‍💫 I have many great things to say about Spice Finch.

Firstly, you can tell that though some items may seem simple, there is a lot of care in the layering of flavors/textures and overall care in the food that is put out. Very warm and pleasant interior design. The staff are nice enough, especially the manager that was on duty. Andres was patient and kind. The chef’s tasting menu was amazing for me and my family. We enjoyed so many items - notably the lamb shank, broccoli tabbouleh, and the fried chickpea fritters (not sure what they’re actually called). It was so much food and well worth it.

Spice Finch delivers exceptional Mediterranean-inspired cuisine.

Seated at the chef's table with 7 college friends, we experienced standout starters: garlic yogurt, green hummus, and melitzanosalata (first time trying… excellent).
Chef's beet recommendation hit the mark…smoky &  sweet. Shanti fries and roasted cauliflower were astounding.
Highlights: pri-pri shrimp with pita, steak frites, swordfish, eggplant kebab. All top-notch. The tahini brownie is essential.
Chef sent complimentary chickpea wedges which melted in your mouth.

Service note: staff clearly stretched thin. Drink orders lagged. With better timing, our group could've easily doubled the bill.

Our college friend is the exec chef here, and we couldn't have been more impressed or thankful for an incredible night. Watching someone you've known for decades command a kitchen at this level is a genuine treat.

We'll be back. 100%.

text.text:
I recently celebrated my 40th birthday at Silk City, and once again, it reminded me why I've been coming here since the early 2000s. Silk City never fails me.

One thing to know if it's your first time visiting: the diner, outdoor garden, and lounge are connected but operate a little differently. Even if you're dining in the outdoor garden area, you'll still need to pay separate admission to enter the lounge later, so keep that in mind.

Because my party was pretty large, Silk City accommodated us with a back section that felt almost like a private event space for my family and friends. It was perfect for our celebration. Service was fast, attentive, and efficient, and the space was large enough to comfortably fit everyone in our group.

I brought my own birthday cake and learned that they charge $3 per slice if you'd like the staff to cut and serve it. No complaints—just something worth knowing ahead of time. I chose to skip that service.

As for the food, I ordered the fried chicken with mashed potatoes and spinach (it normally comes with collard greens, but that's not my thing). This has been one of my favorite meals here since around 2011, and I'm happy to say it tastes exactly as good as I remember. The fried chicken was seasoned to perfection with a crispy, flavorful crust. The mashed potatoes were smooth, creamy, and absolutely delicious. Even the spinach was well-seasoned and surprisingly flavorful. Everyone else in my party seemed happy with their meals as well.

After dinner, we wandered into the diner area, which is one of my favorite parts of Silk City. It's got a cute retro vibe with vintage-style seating and a classic diner feel. It's tucked right between the outdoor dining area and the lounge, making it a great place to grab a drink, hang out, or enjoy a meal. We stopped at the bar for drinks and had a great time there before heading into the lounge.

A quick tip: if you're planning to go into the lounge, buy your entry sooner rather than later. The admission price tends to increase throughout the night. Once we got onto the dance floor, though, it was completely worth it. The DJ kept the music going all night, the crowd was fun, and the energy was amazing. Several of my friends said they hadn't partied like that since college. The dance floor stayed packed, everyone was dancing, and the DJ was playing hit after hit. The drinks were flowing, the vibes were right, and everyone was having an amazing time.

Whether you're looking for good food, a nostalgic diner experience, or a fun night out dancing, Silk City continues to be one of Philadelphia's most reliable spots. After more than 20 years of visiting, I can honestly say: Silk City still delivers.

text.text: New joint that just opened in Northern Liberties and located within the Piazza. As always, parking might be tough to find in this area, but there is Valet service. Reservations are available via Resy. The ambiance is very trendy inside, whereas the outside is definitely brighter. The menu wasn't overwhelming, and prices were a bit higher than typical so expect to pay a bit more, which is expected as they market the restaurant is owned by Chef Laurent Tourondel. We ended up ordering several appetizers, including the rolls, calamari, and octopus. No lie, these were amazing! The octopus was one of the best I've ever had, and it would've been better if it was warmer when it got to our table. I had the spicy Asian salad with tuna and it was also amazing. The service was the main reason I did not rate this restaurant a 5. We sat outside and it wasn't that full, but yet our server(s) were hard to find at times. In addition, when we ordered drinks, it took a very long long time to arrive. It happened during the first round and the server apologized and said there was a large order ahead of us. And then it happened again on our 2nd round, and this time it was even longer and we had to catch the manager's attention. Not entirely sure what was going on. However, I would come back again because the food and vibes were pretty good.

We ended up ordering several appetizers, including the rolls, calamari, and octopus. No lie, these were amazing! The octopus was one of the best I've ever had, and it would've been better if it was warmer when it got to our table. I had the spicy Asian salad with tuna and it was also amazing. The service was the main reason I did not rate this restaurant a 5. We sat outside and it wasn't that full, but yet our server(s) were hard to find at times. In addition, when we ordered drinks, it took a very long long time to arrive. It happened during the first round and the server apologized and said there was a large order ahead of us. And then it happened again on our 2nd round, and this time it was even longer and we had to catch the manager's attention. Not entirely sure what was going on. However, I would come back again because the food and vibes were pretty good.

My family I truly enjoyed our dining  experience and no doubt will return.

From the moment our food arrived, it was clear something was wrong — the chicken and waffles were both cold, as if they had been sitting out for quite some time. Not lukewarm… actually cold. Customers should not be forced to pay extra for service that was clearly not provided.

On top of that, the music was so loud that it was nearly impossible to hold a conversation. This made what should have been a pleasant meal feel chaotic and uncomfortable.

Overall, the experience fell far below what any customer should reasonably expect, especially at these prices. I rarely leave negative reviews, but this visit was unacceptable from start to finish. I would appreciate a response from management regarding how situations like this are addressed, because as it stands, I have no intention of returning.

My bill for 2 people was 160 dollars! Imagine that and my experience was terrible!

text.text:
More than anything, I desire the success of a restaurant as the dedication, time, and passion required to achieve success is not simple. Good food and good service are essential, but having good parking is also crucial. The extra effort of finding parking is worth it, as great food and consistency are key to success.

In this review, starting with the parking situation, it is quite challenging to find a parking spot at this location. Although there are side streets and a second street available, we had to park three blocks away, which was not an issue for me. Personally, I enjoy the exercise but for a higher-end restaurant, valet parking may be necessary. Partnering with a local lot would greatly benefit this location, especially for those who may have physical challenges.

This was my first visit to this restaurant, and I must say it is quite beautiful. The decor is tastefully chosen, accompanied by wonderful music. The bar area is very nice with comfortable seating, and there are high back booth seating along the walls. The seats are incredibly comfortable, something that some people may overlook. The table setting is luxurious with bone china or porcelain plates, linen napkin service, and classic stemmed water goblets.

We ordered mimosas, and a carafe along with flutes was brought to the table. Classic large four-tined table forks and knives were also provided. For the entrees, my two friends decided to order the stone-ground blue grits with petite greens, and Mississippi Fried catfish, which they both enjoyed. The portion size was quite generous. My companion ordered the king salmon served on top of warm fingerling potato salad, sautéed spinach, and mustard marmalade, which she found delightful. She also ordered a side of smoked turkey collard greens, which were perfect.

As a vegan, I opted for the avocado toast without the poached egg. It was beautifully made with a perfect avocado fan sprinkled with red pepper flakes, Black Eyed Peas caviar underneath, served atop seven grain toast, and garnished with cherry tomato halves. Two things that were missing were the microgreens and breakfast radish, which I only noticed the following morning when reviewing the meal. Attention to detail is crucial, especially with the accessibility of local markets.

The dish was delicious, and when we requested lemons on the side to squeeze over the dish, it enhanced the flavors even more. This meal deserves four stars but could easily be a five-star dish if it were complete. For drinks, we shared mimosas and I also ordered a Savannah glow mocktail with peach, lavender, and lemon topped with a dried lemon wheel, which was delicious. The dessert menu was not available online, but we shared a peach cobbler with a cinnamon sugar crust topped with vanilla ice cream, which was perfectly executed and left us wanting more.

The service was excellent, with Rachel providing exceptional service and Chef Issac showcasing his culinary talent. We look forward to returning for dinner in the future.

text.text:
Amina is definitely a place Philadelphia needed. My friend suggested it knowing I love some really good food and this menu absolutely did not disappoint.

The food was honestly a 10 out of 10. The collard greens were so good and full of flavor, and I got the smothered turkey wings which were amazing. Definitely ask for extra gravy because that gravy is too good not to. My friend got the shrimp and cheesecake pop and the portion size was actually really solid.

I also cannot forget the cheesesteak beignets because wow… such a creative idea and they were amazing. I asked for the sauce on the side and it initially came out wrong, so I had to flag someone down to fix it, but once they corrected it everything was perfect.

Now the only downside for me was definitely the service. We really were not checked on much outside of taking our order and bringing drinks. Anytime we needed something like boxes, extra help, or corrections to food, we kinda had to wave down bus boys or random staff members passing by. A few more table check ins would’ve made the experience so much better because the food itself truly deserves top tier service.

Parking can also be a little annoying, but I did notice there’s a garage across the street which helps. Overall though, I absolutely loved this place and I’m so happy my friend brought me here. Even with the service issues, I would 100% come back because the food alone is worth it.

I love the drawings on the wall and the place has a cute and cozy feel which we love!

Also there’s a Photo Booth! You have to pay but cute touch

text.text:
This place felt like a nostalgic American breakfast diner made for hipsters, in a good way.

I was honestly surprised to see it so packed on a Wednesday morning. The atmosphere had a fun, lively energy that made the place feel popular with both locals and visitors.

We ordered a pancake, a Midgriddle, and a hashbrown. I really enjoyed my Midgriddle - it had a thick, square egg custard between the buns that made it feel richer and more satisfying than a typical breakfast sandwich. The sausage was a bit hard and dry.

My friend’s hashbrown looked delicious, crispy, and well cooked. Her pancake was huge and looked more like a cake than the usual thin pancake. The butter portion was also very generous and even had a cute little face stamped onto it, which was a fun touch. The pancake did come out a bit later after we had already finished most of the other food, though.

I liked my iced latte, but the clemonade was strong and needed to be diluted with water several times before drinking.

One thing I appreciated was that you could pack your own leftovers using boxes and bags provided by the restaurant. It was convenient and meant we didn’t have to wait for a server to prepare everything for us.

Overall, a fun breakfast spot with personality, generous portions, and a memorable diner-style atmosphere.

Been wanting to come here with a friend for a while, and we are SO glad we did. We went on a Friday at 2:00 pm-ish and there was a good amount of seating open!

Food: 5/5. Genuinely ALL of the menu sounded and looked absolutely amazing. We got the red velvet tiramisu pancakes and shakshuka, and both were absolutely delicious. I feel as though shakshuka is something that is pretty much standardized all across restaurants, but here, it tasted even better than normal. The pancakes were also SO delicious, and while I am not typically a breakfast food person, the pancakes were just the right level of sweet, not being overly sweet. Loved.

Service: 5/5. The service was very attentive, prompt, and friendly. Our waiters were all very nice and helpful!

Atmosphere: 4/5. Only because I felt as though it was cramped and hectic (as expected, I know, but just personal preference for a brunch place, and nothing wrong with that!). I think if you want a relaxing, peaceful sit-down brunch, this might not be ideal, but that does not take away from their restaurant.

Overall, I have to say that this might take the spot as my favorite brunch spot in all of Philly, and I hope to come back soon. Highly recommend!

text.text:
After what felt like a long wait (the kind where expectations start creeping up), we finally made it inside—and honestly, it was worth every minute. From the moment you walk in, the ambiance grabs you. The atmosphere is lively but comfortable, with a really cool mix of people of all ages. The walls are covered with unique art that gives the place personality and makes you want to look around instead of staring at your phone while waiting for food. It felt welcoming, relaxed, and full of good energy.

Our waitress deserves a shoutout right away—super friendly, always smiling, and genuinely happy to be there. That alone sets the tone for a great meal.

Now let’s talk food. We started with the 1 lb Thai chili wings and… OOOOMMMGGG. These were next-level. Perfectly crispy skin, juicy meat, and that sweet-and-tangy chili sauce hit all the right notes. Easy 9/10. The buffalo cauliflower came next—nice crunch on the outside, decent flavor, but a bit mild for my taste buds. Solid 6/10.

Then came the potato and Vermont cheddar pierogies. Soft, delicate dough stuffed with creamy potatoes and cheese, topped with caramelized onions that absolutely made the dish. Comfort food at its finest—9/10.

The undisputed champion of the night was the Bee’s Backyard Burger. One bite and it was game over. Juicy beef, Cooper sharp cheese, caramelized onions—pure mouth euphoria. A flawless 10/10. And just when we thought it couldn’t get better, the chocolate bread pudding with vanilla ice cream sealed the deal. Warm, rich, indulgent—another 10/10 knockout.

Parking can be a little tricky, so plan ahead—but I’ll gladly deal with that to come back and work my way through the rest of the menu. This place is absolutely worth a return visit.

Very quaint neighborhood corner restaurant. I've been back a number of times since moving to the neighborhood and I always have a great time.

Food/Drinks: The menu is not extremely long and they rotate it with different specials menu on the daily. This restaurant is definitely great for brunch and dinner. I particularly think their brunch is better. Full bar (x2) and can make pretty much any drink you want. Their espresso martini is quite good. Neither expensive or cheap but right in the middle.

Environment/Ambience: The interior is larger than it seems with a larger dining area with the bar and a smaller side room with more tables and another bar. The vibe is rustic and moody, especially in the side room, during night but quite festive during the day. They have approximately 4-6 outdoor tables that are slightly covered and heated. Staff is nice and knowledgeable of the menu. Parking can be potentially tough but it's a great spot to walk to if you live nearby! You can also reserve a table!

Rating: 7/10
Recommendations: Wings, Buffalo Cauliflower, Espresso Martini

text.text:
A Must-Visit for Brunch in Fishtown (With a Heads-Up on Parking!)
I’ve been to Front Street Cafe at least half a dozen times, and it is easily one of my favorite spots in Philadelphia. If you are looking for a reliable, high-quality meal, this is it.
The Food & Brunch
The brunch menu is really where this place shines! Their commitment to farm-to-table ingredients is obvious. While they are known for great vegan and vegetarian options, their traditional breakfast fare is excellent, too. The pancakes and sausage are fantastic—perfectly prepared and very satisfying. I’ve never had a dish here I didn’t enjoy, with the exception of one "miss" a while back, but that was a total outlier.
The Atmosphere
The layout is great, featuring both a cozy indoor space and a beautiful outdoor garden. They also have a solid bar area with great cocktails. It’s a versatile spot that works just as well for a morning coffee as it does for an evening drink.
The Parking Situation (Important!)
Being in Fishtown, parking is definitely the biggest challenge. It’s not ideal—street parking is rare and requires a lot of luck, and the nearby lots can get very expensive. If you’re driving, definitely give yourself extra time to circle the block or be prepared to pay for a lot.
Final Verdict: The brunch and the atmosphere are well worth the trip! Just plan your transportation ahead of time so you can enjoy the fresh food and great vibes stress-free.

text.text:
Yards Brewing Company was one of the highlights of our trip. We tried the cheesesteak egg rolls, Philly Wing Phlight, fish and chips, sirloin beef chili, fries, the spring beer flight, and a Yard-a-Rita, and there honestly wasn’t a single thing we didn’t enjoy.

The cheesesteak egg rolls were delicious and disappeared way too quickly. I genuinely wish we had ordered more. The Philly Wing Phlight is a must-order because it lets you try several different sauces you might not normally choose. The Long Hot sauce was probably the most unique and hardest to describe, but it was excellent. The Caesar sauce was a surprise favorite. It tasted like a creamy Caesar dressing on wings and somehow worked incredibly well.

The fish and chips were also fantastic. The fish tasted very fresh, and the batter was light, crispy, and airy without feeling greasy or heavy. The fries and sirloin beef chili were both great as well.

As someone who normally doesn’t enjoy beer, I was pleasantly surprised by the spring flight. There were several options that I genuinely enjoyed, which is saying a lot. The Yard-a-Rita was also delicious, and they definitely weren’t stingy with the alcohol.

The atmosphere was excellent. A baseball game was on, and it was fun seeing everyone get excited and engaged with the game. It created a lively, welcoming environment that made the experience even better.

My only suggestion would be clearer parking information for first-time visitors. If there is dedicated parking, it wasn’t obvious to us, so we ended up parking on a nearby street.

Overall, the food, drinks, atmosphere, and value were all outstanding. If I find myself back in Pennsylvania, I’ll absolutely be returning, and I’d happily recommend Yards Brewing Company to anyone visiting the area.

As someone who normally doesn’t enjoy beer, I was pleasantly surprised by the spring flight. There were several options that I genuinely enjoyed, which is saying a lot. The Yard-a-Rita was also delicious, and they definitely weren’t stingy with the alcohol.

The atmosphere was excellent. A baseball game was on, and it was fun seeing everyone get excited and engaged with the game. It created a lively, welcoming environment that made the experience even better.

My only suggestion would be clearer parking information for first-time visitors. If there is dedicated parking, it wasn’t obvious to us, so we ended up parking on a nearby street.

Overall, the food, drinks, atmosphere, and value were all outstanding. If I find myself back in Pennsylvania, I’ll absolutely be returning, and I’d happily recommend Yards Brewing Company to anyone visiting the area.

text.text:
Yards is a nice brewery with plentiful space and seating and good service, but beers are nothing special and food was hit or miss.

The beer is alright, some are good but most are meh. A flight for $11 is not a bad deal but considering the majority of their beers are below average, it becomes less enticing. Their extra special ale is the only beer I would recommend, especially if you enjoy ales. The Schuykill Shandy is good, though it's low abv makes it less appealing to many, especially when you compare it to Leinenkugel Summer Shandy, which has a similar focus on a lemon flavor and a cleaner and more consistent taste.

It is also important to note that I am not an IPA fan and many of their beers were quite bitter, which is not the style I prefer. I ended up not finishing most of the beers I got, though my buddy finished them for me (he does not care about taste, he just wanted to drink). I do understand how subjective beer can be and I'm not sure of how they are brewed here, but there was a certain quality all their beers had, almost a heaviness that made it difficult to be mixing which kinds I drank in the flights. It is a quality that is difficult to describe in words, but usually if a beer is a good, you can have a lot of it without feeling sick, which unfortunately most of the beers here did not make me feel great. Most of the beers placed in the bottom half of my beer list, which has over 400 unique beers  I have tried on it.

As for the food, we ordered their smash burgers, which looked really good, though must have been accidentally cooked with too much salt because it was unbelievably over salted. My friend mentioned it and I called him crazy, but when I took a bite of the burger, I was slammed with nothing but the persistent flavor of salt bouncing around in my mouth. It was fine in one bite but after a second bite, it became oppressive. We mentioned something to the waiter to see if this was how they made their burger, but it must have been an error from the chef because he said he has never heard any such complaints, which is unfortunate for us, so take this review of the burgers with a grain of salt (pun intended).

I will say the side salads we got with our burgers were phenomenal, though a small portion. They were perfectly and lightly dressed to add just enough flavor to the already clean and delicious veggies. It also served as a buffer to the salty burger, which made it even more enjoyable than it probably would have been otherwise, but a great salad regardless.

Overall, I would recommend coming here if you have not been to see for yourself, especially given their large selection, though maybe ask to try a beer before you order a pint, and possibly even avoid the burgers.

The seating is plentiful and service was solid. Prices were very reasonable.

El Camino has both the indoor and outdoor dining. I asked if I could dine inside and the young woman at their front door seemed as if she didn’t understand my request. After a second attempt, it seemed like she was persuading me to take a table outside. The music was good. As a matter of fact, after I was done my drink I wanted to stay just to listen to more tunes. The atmosphere was ok, however the staff seemed to buzz around, as if they thought I’d run off without paying… Which made it awkward. I also don’t prefer to eat with animals nearby and there was a dog hanging out with customers at the table next to me.

text.text:
Bar1010 in Philadelphia is an absolute gem that exceeded all our expectations. From the moment we arrived on a bustling evening, we were met with impeccable service. Our server was incredibly attentive, making us feel welcomed and ensuring every detail of our dining experience was perfect. The restaurant’s flexibility in accommodating my vegetarian needs was remarkable, showing a genuine dedication to guest satisfaction.

The cocktail menu is nothing short of exceptional. The espresso martinis are to die for: rich, perfectly balanced, and executed flawlessly and the variety they offer ensures there’s a flavor to match every preference. The food at Bar1010 is equally impressive. As an Indian, my standards for flavor are high, and the Tikka Masala pizza absolutely blew me away. It was perfectly spiced, rich, and indulgent, yet balanced beautifully on a crisp crust. The Indian-style pizza is a unique and unforgettable twist, highlighting the creativity of the kitchen.

The bruschetta was light, refreshing, and simply delicious, a perfect start to our meal. The outdoor seating adds a charming touch, offering a pleasant atmosphere to enjoy both food and drinks while taking in the vibrant Philly energy.

Overall, Bar1010 is a perfect blend of innovative cuisine, exceptional cocktails, and unmatched hospitality. Whether you’re seeking inventive dishes, outstanding drinks, or attentive service in a welcoming environment, this spot delivers on all fronts. Highly recommend for both casual nights out and special occasions, Bar1010 will leave you coming back for more.

I started coming here just after moving to Philly and the staff here is the reason why I know I'm home.

This is a place that cares about their people, their customers, and is the kind of business I love to support.

text.text:
This wasn’t just food: it was a full culinary experience.

Everything was fresh, healthy, and generously portioned. The sashimi was the best I’ve ever had: silky, clean, and incredibly fresh, with none of that “rough sea” taste. The shumai actually had shrimp inside, and the chicken katsu was delicious with sauces that tasted genuinely homemade.

The atmosphere was calm. With two appetizers and two entrées, the bill came to only $50 for two people. This place is truly underrated, a real gem.

text.text: We were a party of five intent on sharing the bounty. We had the sampler of dips (mezes) and pita for our appetizer. We savored our favorites (babagannoush and hummus) and found some new loves (Ezme and Atom). For our main dishes we had the pan-fried liver and onions--which converted all the liver haters at the table. (ME!). So good. We also had the Manti (dumplings), Iskender (Sautéed bread layered with gyro, yogurt & special tomato sauce), chicken kebap,  and on the recommendation of the waitress, we got slow cooked lamb shank over smoked eggplant which was a standout. All her recommendations were spot on. Full from dinner, we didn't have dessert, but I will save room next time. The dining room was a cool vibe. We especially liked the plates. No reserverations at this place. It wasn't crowded when we went which was early on a Tuesday evening

I visited Pera Turkish Cuisine for my birthday and the food was absolutely delicious and well-prepared. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and seasoned perfectly. The meats were tender, and the portions were generous without feeling heavy. You can tell care and tradition go into the cooking.

Additionally the service was excellent—friendly, attentive, and professional without being intrusive. Staff were knowledgeable about the menu, made helpful recommendations, and ensured we were well taken care of throughout the meal.

Overall, a great dining experience and a place I would gladly return to and recommend.

I planned a surprise birthday party for 27 people at UV, and the entire experience was amazing! We come here once or twice a week, so I knew it would be the perfect place because he loves it there. From the very start, the staff was incredibly helpful and even made sure to keep everything a secret. They answered all of my questions, walked me through every step, and made the planning process completely stress-free.

A week before the party, I preselected all of the food to be buffet style. On the day of the event, we brought in the birthday boy, and he was completely surprised! The team did a fantastic job rearranging the space and setting everything up perfectly.

Our server, Emma, was outstanding. She stayed on top of everything throughout the party, making sure our large group had everything we needed. Between the exceptional service, delicious food, and great prices, this was easily a 5-star experience. I'll absolutely be hosting another party here, and I highly recommend it to anyone planning a special event!

This is one of the rare restaurants that both my husband and I absolutely love—which is saying a lot because our palates are worlds apart! It started as his favorite, but it has officially become mine as well.
​The interior is consistently spotless, and the staff is incredibly kind and attentive. Every dish is high quality, but the mains are truly exceptional. We visited today for my husband’s birthday and started with the Crab Rangoon (his all-time favorite appetizer), Som Tom, and Chicken Massaman Curry with Roti. While the Som Tom was standard, the other two were outstanding as always. For our mains, he had the Pineapple Curry and I had the General Thai Chicken—both were phenomenal.
​What made the evening truly special was our server. They must have overheard us celebrating, because they surprised us with a complimentary dessert that was the perfect ending to our meal. We left feeling so well taken care of. Highly recommended for any occasion!

Took a chance at this storefront location and was immensely rewarded. Got a General Tso lunch special, and, a Curry Chicken with Onions (and other vegetables) lunch special for $7.25 each. (Then, now looking at $8.95 plus tax for all Lunch Special items except for three that are higher priced.)

The containers were PACKED. No skimping on the chicken. The containers had half of each along with the pork fried rice I ordered. The rice had white onions and beans sprouts in it too. The pork was nice and fresh, and in chunks.

The General Tso's chicken was nice and moist, and came with three broccoli crowns. I'd prefer more spicy heat though. (The Sesame Chicken is similar but without the heat. See 5/2025 photo.)

The Curry Chicken was great and also came with julienned carrots, green bell peppers, zucchini, mushrooms, snow peas, and, celery. The Curry was very flavorful and had a nice mild kick. (P.S.: The Szechuan Chicken  at this place is also basically the same ingredients but comes in a brown sauce. This is how they do things with most veggies. See photo.)

The Curry Chicken also held up well as a next morning bite to eat.

*NEW!!!* Got the Boneless Pork Ribs. It's  candied pork butt with the pork fried rice (as usual, see rice description).  Be sure to ask for a side of hot chili oil. (Then every dish can become truly HOT AND SPICY.) New pics added below.

The dining area was basic but there was a steady stream of customers as I ate in during the 2 p.m. hour.

I would eat here again! This is a good storefront place!

P.S., This review still holds, I visited today, 3/3/2026.
