text.text:
Suya Suya West African Grill in Philadelphia is truly a gem for anyone craving authentic West African cuisine. From the moment you walk in, the inviting aroma of grilled meats greets you, setting the stage for an incredible dining experience.

The menu is a delightful array of options, showcasing traditional dishes with bold flavors that transport you straight to West Africa. The standout item is, of course, the suya chicken, which is perfectly spiced and grilled to perfection. Each bite offers a wonderful balance of heat and richness that keeps you coming back for more. The jollof rice is another must-try; it’s fluffy, flavorful, and pairs beautifully with the grilled meats.

The service is exceptional—friendly staff who are knowledgeable about the menu and eager to help you choose the best dishes to suit your palate. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, making it a great spot for a casual dinner or a celebration with friends and family.

Overall, Suya Suya is not just a restaurant; it’s an experience filled with flavors, warmth, and hospitality. I highly recommend paying a visit whether you’re a long-time fan of West African cuisine or a newcomer looking to explore. You won’t be disappointed!

text.text:
I’ve been to a couple Michelin Starred restauraunts, yet I wondered what a Michelin Bib Gourmand was; and I learned later, it's an indication of high quality at an affordable price (I agree).  And so my journey to Del Rossi’s was set in motion to dive in and discover the buzz.

We ordered the simplest cheesesteak & pizza.   The ingredients were basic, assembled with care and the highest quality IMHO.  To me the cheesteak was straightforward, but the richness of the bread & meat quality forces you to pause.  The bread reminded me of something you’d find from a German bakery, which in my opinion is the best in the world, edging out France.  With their pizza I found the crust thin, echos their bread without an oversaturation of oils.  Above all the tasty rich cheese stands out.

Arrive early because seating is limited, first come, and then it gets packed quickly.  The environment isn’t anything to write home about, however it was comfortable.  If you’re in Philly I certainly think this place is worth a try.  We loved it.

Probably the best cheesesteak I ever had. I ordered with fried onions. It’s big, overflowing with meat, and has plenty of sharp cheese and onions throughout. The bread is thick with a hard crust, a perfect vehicle to hold its heavy, messy contents. I am not from Philly so cannot compare this to other cheesesteaks from the city, but as someone who loves food it was excellent.

I thought my husband’s brick oven margarita pizza was good even though he didn’t like it. The crust had a good finish to it, and unlike other pizzas I get these days, there was plenty of sauce. The underside of the thin crust was perfectly crisped while the softness was maintained between the very bottom layer and the sauce and cheese. This made for a pleasant eating experience.

text.text:
Woke up with a serious hankering for soft-shell crab curry. After running a few errands, my husband and I decided to drive down to NoLibs to check this place out, since it was one of the few restaurants with this item on the menu that didn’t require a reservation 2+ weeks in advance.

We were very impressed by the food and the general atmosphere; it felt like eating at your friend’s home, with a very relaxed vibe. There were about 4 other parties in the restaurant with us, and people spoke freely among themselves.

The owner was serving and apologized profusely for not having wait staff that day, and warned us it would be a longer wait for our food. However, I didn’t feel like I was waiting long at all - 15 minutes, which feels fair for the quality of the food. She was also a great conversationalist and host to us all.

Don’t pass this place up if you’re in the area; just keep in mind it's BYOB (and they will happily supply a cold glass for your beer).

Try the duck tamarind!

*Just a note: we went in May 2026 but forgot to leave a review until now.

Location/parking: on a two way street with some parking spaces in front (3 hours allowed)

Service: They had a full house when we were there so it was a little on the slower end but it doesn’t matter since every server was super friendly and kind.

Price: see my menu photo. I think it’s good value!

Overall: will be back if I’m in the area! Would love to try there drinks next time

text.text:
Edit: The owner called me apologizing for the issue and gave me a credit. I ordered again and they were very kind to not only give me free pizzas, but also to show how the boxes were properly sealed in their delivery bag. The order was perfect and the pizzas were delicious.

I ordered 2 pizzas a couple weeks ago and had no issues. This past Sunday I ordered a large one and the box was not properly folded, making the pizza a bit exposed. Since it was delivery, I got concerned because I didn’t know how the driver handled the pizza. The issue was that the box wasn’t properly assembled, so it didn’t close on the sides (see pictures). I called Rustica and they said that they do that on purpose because they don’t want to fold the pizza. When I said I got concerned about the way the box was cared or stored in the vehicle (was it a bike, even?), they said they are transported in a bag. I didn’t see it, but decided to trust it. They said they would keep an eye on my address for the next time I order, but honestly, we know that’s a tough one. The call didn’t take long, but when I opened the box to eat, the pizza was super cold - so one more reason to properly close the box. This was not a delivery issue, so I don’t regret tipping the driver 30% because of the snow, but it was definitely a restaurant issue. Given their insistente in saying what they did was right, I might not order from them again.

Edit: Me, my husband, and child all got food poisoning. 6 hours later and we were all throwing up with diarrhea.
Came here because it looked like a fun spot for our 5 year old to run around in the playground while we ate and had a drink. For starters, Sundays are not the day to go if they’re having a party for someone. The tables near the playground were all taken and there had to be 20 kids running around, no parent was watching their kid either. We were able to get a table relatively close to the playground to watch our kid though. We got pulled pork sandwiches and fries and the food was SO SALTY. The food and the drinks were so expensive. We ended up paying $90 for 2 adults and a kid. The atmosphere was too hectic, it gave me anxiety just sitting there. And to top it off, a little boy bit my kid on the arm while on the playground. I wouldn’t recommend this place, especially on a busy weekend. The only positive was that the server was nice to us.

I recommend the wings, and the loaded fries! Also bring change or $1 bills, kids have games/ claw machine to play! Weekends parking is sometimes hard with an event, but not impossible. Just pick the best time, and you’ll enjoy yourself ! 10/10 always

This time I was thoroughly disappointed because for the price that I had paid for two large pizzas with pepperoni and sausage $50 plus the pizza was dry with barely any sauce on it usually that’s the first thing that you see when you open the box but the first thing I saw was cheese and they were very skimpy with the sausage and pepperoni ! I gave them a 4 because the female barmaid who was on that day was super nice and very attentive, sorry I forgot her name but I believe it starts with a L!

text.text:
Walked in on a random Monday evening and were able to enjoy the happy hour prices.

We were recommended the Santucci’s classic personal pizza which is a square pizza with cheese on the bottom and smothered with red sauce. I thought it was great and for happy hour with the $3 off personal pizzas, it was with the $9 price point.

The red sauce was bland, not too acidic but also not so flavorful. The crust was interesting — fluffy but a little flavourless. My fiance likened it to a larger version of a Lunchable. We did get a pretty cheese pull!

Was it the best pizza I’ve ever had? No, but it did fill me up cause I was hungry.

5 stars for service! Our server was sweet, helpful and patient with us 🫶

text.text:
I had been in Juno Mexican Grill several times. I always enjoyed dining in there. Recently I was there maybe one and half years later and I surprised because it was different menu and there was less options than before. They used to have really good menu options. I hope they change the menu and put some of the old menu items soon.

This time I ordered Guacamole Juno as a starter and it was absolutely delicious. It was very fresh and the portion was good. For my main course I ordered Quesadilla with chicken. It came with 3 sides and it was good. Btw they made quesadilla much better before. Still it wasn’t bad but it could be much better.

The service was good and my waitress Sarah was very nice girl. The atmosphere was just amazing. You feel really comfortable in there. Especially the music and their playlist was awesome. They always have really good music in there and thank god they didn’t change it for years.

If you like Mexican food and looking for casual and comfortable place, Juno Mexican Grill is a good choice. Their food and drinks prices are very reasonable.

text.text:
Me and my partner went to Juno’s on Tuesday, October 28th, 2025 around 7 PM, and honestly, it was a pretty dull experience this time around 😕. I’ve been here before, and even though there were only two people inside the first time, I still enjoyed it. I just expected a little more this visit since they have a dance floor in the back 💃🏽, $5 drinks 🍹, and $25 pitchers 🍾.

The food though? 10/10 for me! 🔥 I usually get something plain, but this time I tried their version of street corn and it did not disappoint 🌽. I actually liked the corn and the chips (which I took from my partner’s guacamole and chips plate 😅) more than the guac itself. My steak tacos were absolute fire and needed no changes at all 😋. My partner got the fish tacos and added cheese, but said the mango on top clashed with it and probably would’ve been better without the cheese 🧀✨.

My margarita was a basic classic, not strong, kind of calm and smooth 🍸. Our server seemed shy and a little nervous, maybe new, but was still super polite and kind 💛. The place itself is cute, cozy, and intimate, with a really pretty vibe. The purple flowers kept falling on our table which was sweet, even if unplanned 💐. It can get a little chilly by the door in the fall and winter though, so bundle up 🧥.

Overall, I still love the food and the aesthetic, but I think Juno’s could use a little more energy and fun! Maybe themed nights, influencer collabs, or events to bring people in and make use of that dance floor 🎶. There’s so much potential here, it just needs that extra spark to match how good the food is ✨💫(btw the food came out in less than 10-15 min, was still hot! Scorching!!! 🥵)

text.text:
I am new to the plant-based game. Since I started, I’ve been mostly cooking at home, which is sad because I miss eating out. I’m making it my life’s mission to try all the vegan spots in Philadelphia. This place was top of my list. The place has a really great energy the second that you walk in and all the staff are extremely nice.

I got the fried chicken platter with mac & cheese and kale. I got the Philly cheesesteak empanadas. I got a chocolate peach cake. I got a pumpkin cake. I got two fresh pressed juices.

I’ve always loved fresh pressed juice and theirs is very good. I would just recommend if you’re not used to drinking lots of ginger ask for them to go lighter on it. My daily green drink was burning me up. Both the cakes were phenomenal. I had to stop myself from finishing them. They were moist and full of flavor. The fried chicken platter was great. I like my food extra salty and spicy so I had to season it up a little when I got home, but other than that it’s exactly what advertised. A warm crunchy hearty platter. The empanadas were delicious as well. Didn’t taste like Philly cheesesteak to me, but still made super well.

I will definitely be making my way through the whole menu.

Atmosphere: I stumbled upon Street Side and decided to give it a try. It’s a small, cozy Vietnamese spot with a vibe that captures the lively spirit of street food culture. The interior is simple and casual, with bench-style seating.

Food: I ordered the chicken spinach dumplings and the classic hand-cut beef pho. The dumplings were flavorful and well-seasoned, while the pho came in a generous portion with tender beef and rich broth. It’s a solid choice if you're craving a comforting bowl of pho. I’d definitely recommend Street Side for a casual, satisfying Vietnamese meal.

I only ordered because I had a discount code, and thank goodness I didn't pay full price. Now I know why they lure you in with coupons. This place is basically serving Blue Apron meal kits that you reheat at home, except somehow worse.

The burger was pale, sad, and flavorless. I have had better from a McDonald's dollar menu. The fries were soggy and tasted like nothing. For a restaurant, I expected freshly cooked food, not a prepackaged box that someone microwaved and slapped on a plate. If I wanted a meal kit, I would order it myself and cook it better in my own kitchen.

Wonder Fishtown is a massive letdown. Save your money and your taste buds. Go literally anywhere else.

text.text: I live a few blocks from the original Honeysuckle Provisions and loved both the delicious breakfast and lunch options, plus had one of the best meals of my lifetime with their “Untitled” tasting experience back in 2024. It was bittersweet when they left West Philly, because we could use more elevated dining choices out West, but also felt happy for them to move on up. Fast forward to our first time at Honeysuckle restaurant in February 2026: it was a lovely meal. The vibe/atmosphere is welcoming, energetic, artsy, and very well composed. The servers are friendly and know the menu/mission very well. And the food was delicious! Notable items: Salad russe was one of the best things I’ve eaten in a long time, and the catfish was delightful! However, we got the prix-fixe menu and unfortunately left hungry, even though it was pricey. And there were a fair amount of missteps in the timing of our drinks/courses, leading to a somewhat bumpy, even if yummy night. I know this place has a ton of potential and could prob get a Michelin star someday. But it’s just not there yet. Can’t wait to come back and try again soon (and get the fancy burger!).

text.text:
My wife and I celebrated our 8-year wedding anniversary at Honeysuckle, and the experience was absolutely worth it. The food was so flavorful, bold, and masterfully prepared that each bite felt euphoric—every dish was an experience within itself.

This wasn’t simply dinner; it was a culinary journey. You could taste the creativity, passion, and intention behind every bite. The flavors were powerful, memorable, and unlike anything we’ve experienced at an ordinary restaurant.

What made the evening even more special was having the opportunity to meet and take pictures with Chef Cybille St. Aude-Tate. Celebrating eight years of marriage with my wife deserved something memorable, and Honeysuckle delivered an experience we will continue talking about long after our anniversary.

Amazing food, an unforgettable atmosphere, and a truly special evening. Honeysuckle was worth every moment, and we will absolutely be back.

text.text:
Honeysuckle has a beautiful atmosphere and an exceptional staff. From the moment we arrived, the service was warm, attentive, and truly one of the highlights of the evening.

Unfortunately, the tasting menu didn’t live up to the experience or the $135 per person price point, especially before tax and gratuity. At that cost, expectations aren’t just high, they’re set. You anticipate a memorable culinary experience where creativity, flavor, pacing, and satisfaction all come together.

Instead, we were served beautifully presented dishes on oversized plates with portions so small they felt almost symbolic. I understand that fine dining is about quality over quantity, but the portions were so minimal that they became distracting. The long gaps between courses only amplified that feeling, turning what should have been an exciting progression into an evening that dragged on.

The food was good and certainly different from anything I’ve had before, but it wasn’t memorable. Nothing left me thinking, “I can’t wait to have that again.” For this price point, guests expect more than novelty. They expect to be impressed.

One more frustration was the payment process. Requiring guests to prepay the full cost of the tasting menu, including tax and gratuity, sets the expectation of a seamless luxury experience. Instead, the final receipt didn’t clearly reflect what had already been paid, creating unnecessary confusion at the end of the evening. At this level, transparency should be effortless, not another question mark.

Honeysuckle absolutely excels in hospitality and ambiance, but the disconnect between the premium price, the pacing, the portion sizes, and the overall dining experience made the evening feel underwhelming. I left appreciating the staff and the beautiful setting, but thinking more about the bill than the meal.

text.text: My son and I stopped in unexpectedly after a bike ride. We were window shopping food options and the ambiance on the inside is what drew us in! He is a teen so we had to sit in the lounge section and order from the Ala cart menu but it did not disappoint. He got a mocktail that resembles an elevated Shirley temple that even he could not stop talking about. I got the espresso rumtini which was also incredible. We wanted the McDonald’s money burger and fries but were sadly told they were out so we opted for catfish. In the time we were waiting the GM approached our server to let her know they figured out a solution! We were so pumped. The burger and fries were great. Even the presentation! The ramekin looked like a paper sauce cup but it was actually a real ramekin plus the fry box the beef tallow fries came in definitely gave it that fast food feel. My teenager loved the unique take on the McDonald’s Big Mac. Our server Thalia was very kind and attentive. The Philly food scene has been great to us!

text.text:
I’d heard great things about Jerry’s chicken Caesar wrap, so I was excited to try it. Since I don’t eat meat, I asked if I could substitute shrimp for the chicken. I expected an upcharge, but I was shocked when the $18 wrap became $30 because the shrimp substitution alone was an additional $12.

What doesn’t make sense is that I’m not getting the chicken, so it feels like I’m paying for both the chicken and the shrimp. On top of that, the Caesar salad menu lists shrimp as a $10 add-on and chicken as a $6 add-on, a difference of only $4. A $12 charge to substitute shrimp on the wrap seems excessive.

My first interaction also wasn’t the best. I ordered a Bloody Mary and was told they had already put away everything needed to make one. I understand if that’s their policy, but I’ve ordered Bloody Marys later in the day at plenty of other bars, so it was a little surprising to be turned away.

Overall, the wrap was good, but it definitely wasn’t worth $30.

text.text: We usually have a great experience at Jerry’s, but tonight not so much. We went tonight for happy hour, we were a party of four sat at the inside, by the big window( facing Laurel Street) on the first level. The reason I name the area is because I don’t remember the name of our waitress unfortunately. The drinks were good and the food we ordered seemed like it was going to be great, but unfortunately we never got it. We had a reservation at 6:15, we wanted to enjoy a bit of what was left of happy hour( ends at 7pm) and then planned to get dinner as well. We were sat and she came around about 5 minutes after to take our order. We got our first round of drinks and then also put in two appetizers. After a while I noticed that other tables were getting their food and thought we would be next soon. Then some time continued to go on and we still hadn’t gotten the two appetizers, at this point it was going on about 6:50. She had also not come around to see if we were doing okay or needed another round of drinks. At around 6:55 we finally had to flag her down as she was walking away after tending to another two person table. We put in another round of drinks off the happy hour menu and she still didn’t say anything about the food we ordered. After that much time had passed we just didn’t feel like asking about the appetizers, in which case we also then closed out and went to get dinner somewhere else. Again, all other times have been great, but tonight we did not get good service. We honestly would have said something but we also felt at that time it was kind of a moot point.

text.text:
La Chinesca is an absolute crowned jewel. We were on our way to Union Transfer to see Electric Guest and stumbled upon this gem while walking to the venue. Neither of us had ever been there before, and I’m so glad we found it.

The atmosphere is cozy and eclectic with a perfectly chill vibe. Even without a reservation, we were greeted immediately by a warm, pleasant hostess and seated right away—thoughtfully placed as far from the door as possible since it was literally the coldest February evening imaginable.

We started with drinks. I ordered the On Empty, which was divine, and my partner had a spiked pomegranate lemonade. Both were creative cocktails, well-balanced, and incredibly delicious.

For food, we ordered the chilled cucumbers, spare ribs, chicken tacos, and wonton chips. Every single dish was fantastic, but the salsa roja deserves its own moment—I loved it so much I wanted to bathe in it.We didn’t get many pictures of the food because we devoured it as soon as it arrived.

Service was impeccable from start to finish. One of the staff even sent us home with a container of salsa roja after I asked if they sold it, which was such a thoughtful touch.

I dishes with a black limousine which is like a tequila espresso martini. The perfect ending to a delicious and creative meal. Everything was executed perfectly at La Chinesca!

My god, this place is amazing. We’ll absolutely be back.

text.text:
This is a properly hyped restaurant! The atmosphere is fun, but relaxed. The menu is curated and intentional. The service was attentive, not rushed. Every bite of food was delicious - not one bad bite. I was blown away.
I went with a pescatarian friend, so I did not eat a meat dish. We ordered the wonton chips and three dips (red salsa, salsa verde and duck sauce) the chips were crispy and salty, and the dips were so well done. We ordered the tuna tostada which was a great mix of texture and flavor. The macha crisp had great spice and the tuna was delicious. We ordered the fish tacos and the avocado tacos - both different and delicious. The orders had three tacle each of small corn tortillas, the fish was lightly spicy, and the avocado was fried but refreshingly light. For drink I had their take on a dirty martini which was an elevated and interesting experience for a simple cocktail. Finally we ended with 3 church's and chocolate sauce, the churros were light and airy on the inside, crispy and sugar coated on the outside and the chocolate sauce was great quality. Altogether our meal was $55 per person and the portions were filling. I was pleasantly surprised by the restaurant meeting it's very highly hyped expectation. I'll go again and you should feel compelled to try it out!

text.text:
A triumph!

Top three best restaurant experiences I’ve had in life. This restaurant has all the elements to achieve a standard-bearer of the best restaurant in the city and, potentially, qualify for the national league standing. The service is at the elite private club level; ambience is rightly detailed; music level and style meets you at the right notes.

One dish specifically,  Black Pearl Mushrooms, moved and touched me where I could not bring myself to drink a glass of water because I didn’t want the flavor to disappear from my taste buds.

Focaccia bread set you on the right  to have a great meal.

The meal finished with the peanut butter dessert. The chocolate is very well done. It is strong enough to hold its form yet it is delicate enough to melt in your mouth in such a way that coats the light peanut butter mousse creating an amplifying  effect.

Biggest tip: get the tasting menu - yes, it is worth and yes, you will regraded if you dont go for it.

text.text:
One of the best meals I’ve had in Philly, which is a bold statement for a city with a phenomenal food scene. A server at a restaurant in another part of town recommended Pietramala. “Even if you’re not vegan, go,” she advised.

Making a day-of reservation for 9:15pm on a Saturday in June, I walked in and was seated right away by a kind staff member. Within minutes, my glass of water was full and my equally kind server was walking me through the menu.

The menu elevates vegetables and they source their ingredients from 16 farms nearby. (Most are in Pennsylvania.) Not overly hungry, I ordered two mid dishes and a dessert. (The menu is organized by small, mid, large, and dessert.)

Each dish was masterfully executed and full of flavor. Suzuki Farm Kyuri Cucumbers were perfect. They come out as four large cucumber halves with all the fixings. Don’t be shy. It’s easier to eat them with your fingers per recommended by my server.

The next dish was the Urban Roots Farm Sugar Snap Peas. The crunch of the peas with the wasabina oil complimented each other well.

For desert, I ordered the Bomboloni with pistachio cream. The warm texture of the dough and creaminess of the pistachio cream was divine. I ordered another. It may be my favorite dessert I’ve ever had at any restaurant anywhere.

If you love creative and quality food, go here. You won’t regret it!

text.text:
This was the weirdest and worst experience I’ve had at a restaurant in Philly…

I came in to try a smashburger as someone recommended it to me. Sat at the bar, bartender took my order and it came out quickly. When I cut it in half, I noticed that it didn’t look smashed, but I wasn’t going to judge it off that.

I took a bite and was highly confused. It was rubbery and did NOT taste like beef. If you see in the pictures, it does not have the texture of a burger. It looks like two thick sausage patties that you would get at a diner or in a Mcdonalds breakfast sandwich.

I called the bartender over and he said oh I’m sorry you don’t like it, if you were drinking I’d get you a free drink… weird way to handle that. I then asked for the check and when I got it, I told him I would pay for the fries I ate but not the burger because I don’t believe it was a burger. He then looked at me and said “Yeah, I just had our burger last week and it was nothing like that. Our burgers don’t even look like that so I’m not sure what happened, its weird. I’ll talk to the chef later. Don’t worry about paying”

I am not a confrontational person, so I just got up and left without getting an answer on what I ate. Charging me for something that they know is not a burger, not offering to remake it when I initially said this doesn’t look right and then only comping me once I double down is the worst customer service ever. I don’t know what is going on in that kitchen but I will never go back.

Cicala is the perfect place to celebrate a special occasion! My husband and I went there to celebrate our anniversary last week, and it was truly a wonderful experience.
Peter and his team made our evening truly special. Their attention to detail and genuine hospitality made us feel so welcomed and well taken care of throughout the entire dinner.
The food was absolutely delicious. The fresh handmade pasta was incredible, the meat melted in the mouth, every dish was beautifully presented, and you could really taste the quality of the ingredients!
Thank you to everyone at Cicala for making our anniversary so memorable. We can’t wait to come back!

If feeding your guests an incredible meal is a priority for you like it was for us, you won’t regret hosting your event here. Our friends and family have been raving about the food and gorgeous atmosphere, and the friendly, hard working staff made our wedding a dream come true. Cicala is able to work with you to make your event uniquely yours, but at the same time, we’re delighted that our event was uniquely Cicala. Memorable is a guarantee. Their event coordinator, Dawn, was fabulous throughout the planning process and I was impressed with how she and the rest of the team at Cicala executed the plans day-off. They did everything they could to make sure that we could simply sit back and enjoy the occasion. Our only regret is forgetting to grab our doggy bag on the way out! Thank you, Cicala, and we’ll see you for dinner the next time we’re in town.

text.text:
We just left Cicala, and it was a wonderful experience. The atmosphere was incredible.

Honestly one of the best interior designs I’ve seen in an Italian restaurant, and probably the best in Philadelphia.

There was a gentleman named Peter at the front who took great care of us. Since we had our baby with us, he was especially attentive and thoughtful throughout the night, which we really appreciated.

We started with the arugula salad, and it was one of the best arugula salads I’ve had. Then we ordered a crab and tomato pasta — I can’t remember the exact name — and it was very good, although slightly under-seasoned for my taste.

After that, we had the slow-cooked short rib. The presentation and overall dish were beautiful, but for me personally, the meat was a little too cooked. If you don’t prefer very well-cooked meat, I’d recommend mentioning that beforehand.

Overall, I felt the salt levels in some dishes were a bit low, but it was still an excellent dining experience.

Special thanks again to Peter for his hospitality. I definitely recommend Cicala.

From the time I entered the restaurant I knew my night would be perfect. I made reservations for two with my best friend who was attending a concert with me at The Met. Peter greeted us at the door with a warm welcome and escorted us personally to our table. WE were able to enjoy the street view which is optimal for me to people watch while I enjoy wine and dinner. Our waiter Josh greeted us promptly after sitting and started us of with drinks and the list of the daily special. Note their menu is seasonal so the items we had may not be available during your season of dining.  Our food was delicious and served promptly. A pear gorgonzola salad, pappardelle pasta, branzino main course, and to top it off the carrot cake dessert.

I cannot to return to an atmosphere that was so welcoming. Thank you thank you thank you to the staff for being one of the best parts of our night.

text.text:
If you're looking for a stunning and affordable event space to host your birthday celebration, engagement party, or any gathering with friends and loved ones, I highly recommend the Winston Social Club! My fiancé and I faced an almost disastrous situation when our former venue ghosted us just a week before our event. Desperate to find a new space that could accommodate us and our 50+ guests on such short notice, we contacted numerous venues. By fate, we connected with Tiffany, an event manager at Winston, who truly saved our event!

Tiffany reserved one of their prime event rooms, The Emerald Room, which came complete with door security, a fully stocked bar, cocktail tables, and music and AV equipment ready to go. She ensured we had everything we needed and even went the extra mile by putting in a good word with the manager of the dance club next door, Mr. Ivy, so we could continue the celebration with our friends and family who were already having an amazing time.

I cannot express how unforgettable our engagement party was, thanks to Tiffany, the Winston Social Club, & Mr. Ivy. We will definitely be reaching out to host our upcoming wedding festivities and other events with Winston!

text.text: Came to The Winston for brunch with friends. They normally have a DJ on the weekends providing the vibes but he was not present when we went Sunday. The ambiance & vibes were still on point. The Winston was able to make up for that by playing a great music playlist from their phone. Whoever’s playlist they were playing was pretty good and a few of my friends mentioned they wish there was a dance floor. We settled to some chair dancing instead. Our waitress was attentive and took care of us. We all came with our appetites and ordered a wide variety of items. I took advantage of their $5 mimosas. A few girlfriends tried the brunch shots and they said they were good. For brunch, I had their Chicken and waffles. The Chicken and Waffle was served with a nicely seasoned chicken breast and the waffles were thick and fluffy in texture. My only gripe about my dish is that I wish my chicken was a bit bigger. I also sampled the avocado toast and the home fries from what my girlfriends ordered and they were both delicious. Overall we had a great time and there were no complaints about the food. I’d definitely come back! Great vibes, great food and reasonable prices 🙌🏾

text.text:
I genuinely rock with Darling’s Tavern. I’ve dined in multiple times and grabbed takeout too, and every experience been solid. Their flatbread pizza is easily one of the best pizzas you’ll ever have — especially the regular cheese. That joint is a must-try first before you even start exploring the rest of the menu. The other pizzas are good too, but the cheese flatbread is the one you have to lock in with.

The mozzarella sticks? Straight one-of-one. I’m telling you, they don’t make them like that anywhere else I’ve had.

Pro tip combo: get the French onion soup with the veggie pizza. That pairing hits crazy and lowkey feels like a cheat code meal.

Shoutout to the bartenders too — I don’t drink alcohol, and they still hooked me up with a fire mocktail. Everybody behind the bar is friendly, welcoming, and knows what they doing.

If you’re in the Rittenhouse/downtown Philly area, it’s definitely a spot worth pulling up to. Full menu is strong across the board, and the desserts? Super fire.

text.text:
If you’re looking for a cozy, homey Italian spot in Philly, Little Nonna’s absolutely delivers 🍝✨

From the moment you walk in, it feels like you’re being welcomed into someone’s home. The decor is warm and charming, making it the kind of place you want to linger a little longer and just enjoy the vibe.

For food, everything hit. The rigatoni vodka was rich, creamy, and so satisfying. The garlic bread was a standout too, especially because they give you extra garlic to spread on top which made it even better 🧄🔥

The Sunday gravy was another favorite. It’s perfect if you want to try a little bit of everything, with pasta, meatball, sausage, and veggies all packed into one dish. Super flavorful and comforting.

Portion sizes are generous and the prices feel very reasonable for the quality and experience. Overall, such a solid spot for a cozy dinner. Would definitely come back 🤍

Highly recommended.

text.text:
Let me tell y’all something…

I came to Sampan tonight as a party of one, and from the moment I said “table for one,” it felt like I had announced I was there to inspect the fire extinguishers.

Now, let me be fair. I’m a huge fan of the owner, which is exactly why this review hurts my feelings more than it should.

They sat me at the prep station bar, which was fine. I actually enjoy dining alone. What I don’t enjoy is sitting there so long waiting for service that I started learning the employees’ schedules through observation.

When service finally arrived, my table wasn’t fully set, I had no napkin, and nobody seemed particularly interested in making sure I was having a good experience.

I ordered the chef’s tasting menu thinking I was about to go on a culinary journey.

Turns out it was more of a culinary Uber ride. Fast, confusing, and over before I knew what happened.

No questions about whether I’d been there before.

No recommendations.

No explanation.

My server was moving so fast I felt like I was trying to catch instructions during a fire drill.

The ceviche was okay.

The cheesesteak bao had less flavor than a corporate training video.

And somehow it was greasy enough to leave my hands looking like I’d just finished helping at Jiffy Lube. The problem? No napkin. I had to ask the host for one.

At that point, I started feeling like I was participating in a social experiment.

Most of the tasting menu was forgettable.

Then came the bronzino.

Listen…

That bronzino walked out of the kitchen like Martin showing up at the last minute to save the episode.

The fish was outstanding.

The string beans were excellent.

For a brief moment, I thought we were back in business.

The pork chop was pretty good too.

Then the kimchi fried rice showed up and immediately reminded me why we were in trouble.

I’ve had that dish before and loved it.

Tonight it tasted like the recipe and the seasoning had gotten into an argument and stopped speaking to each other.

I sent it back.

By dessert, I was emotionally detached from the relationship.

I respectfully declined and asked for the check.

Maybe they were having an off night.

Maybe they were understaffed.

Maybe solo diners aren’t their target audience.

I don’t know.

What I do know is that bronzino fought for its life tonight.

That fish was in there working overtime, covering shifts, training new employees, and trying to save the entire restaurant by itself.

Unfortunately, even MVPs can’t win every game.

Sadly, this will be my last visit.

Went here for breakfast two mornings in a row since we were staying at the hotel.
We ordered their Eggs Benedict both days — the poached eggs were perfectly runny, the Hollandaise sauce was rich but not too heavy, and the potatoes on the side were amazing! Super crisp potato skin with fluffy potato inside — loved it.

The next day we wanted to try the Local Eggs Benedict, but surprisingly they were out of pork roll… on a Saturday morning! That part was a bit odd, so we just stuck with the classic again. Still delicious though!

Special shout-out to our server — it was the same lady both mornings, and she was incredibly kind and attentive. Right before we finished, she even asked if we wanted two coffees to-go. Such a thoughtful gesture, really made our mornings feel extra nice!

We also visited the bar the second night for a couple of drinks.
✨ Mojito — refreshing, minty, super easy to enjoy
🥃 Bourbon Sour — great balance of citrus and whiskey, very smooth

Friendly bartender and a cozy vibe to wind down the night.

Overall, great breakfast, lovely service, and a nice hotel bar experience — just wish they had the pork roll available on weekends!

🛒 Bonus: Don’t miss the little Market next door!

Right beside the restaurant, there’s a small market selling bagels, snacks, and baked goods.

We grabbed a couple of things — and their Cranberry Muffin might be one of the best I’ve ever had.
Super moist, tart berries, not overly sweet… such a pleasant surprise! 🥰🫐

text.text:
IF YOU’RE GOING TO MANDATE GRATUITY, CAN WE GET GOOD SERVICE???

Listen, I am a server as well and have worked in the service industry for years. I totally understand that some people will stiff you regardless of the quality of service, and servers need this money to live. However, I suggest our server NINA find a new job.

We came in 40 minutes before happy hour ended, but were left waiting for a few minutes before being greeted. Fine. Maybe she is just busy? It wasn’t that full in the restaurant but as a customer, I wouldn’t know if there more were duties beyond the naked eye.

However, we were not given any waters at all while we waited. When she finally came to greet us, we immediately noted her unfriendly attitude and inappropriate attire. She was wearing a sports bra, tight biker shorts, and had her long dyed hair out, and not tied back) Besides the obvious health hazard (not just to us, because it seems like an occupational hazard to not wear pants and a shirt), there were children dining. And not to be mean but I didn’t come to Bonchon for these kind of flats.

We were barely checked on throughout service ergo we were unable to get more than two rounds of drinks for happy hour. Somehow the food arrived slightly cold. Our fries were soggy.

By the time we paid, we still did not receive waters. No waters and no other drinks in a heatwave. And yet, mandated gratuity imposed on us.

Bonchon already suffers from major inconsistency. A lot of these mistakes could have been forgiven if there weren’t a lot.

I’ve been here a few times and only noted an issue with her. I hope she does herself and this franchise a favor by resigning and picking a career that would suit her clothing choices better.

P.S. There are more egregious things throughout service that we noticed, but I chose to not reveal any details about our table because she seems like the kind of person who would stick her fingers in our food as revenge. And Bonchon does have a convenient location and good food, sometimes.

text.text:
Last night in Philly, walking distance from the hotel, last-minute reservation -- and it ended up being the perfect way to close out the trip.

Nom Wah is tiny. Don't let that fool you. This place is a straight-up dim sum and dumpling situation, and it delivers hard. We ordered way too much food, which I maintain was the correct decision.

The spread: house special roast pork bun (pillowy, porky, perfect), pan-fried dumplings (crispy bottoms, juicy inside -- the way it should be), soup dumplings (golden, delicate, dangerous if you're impatient), scallion pancakes (flaky, savory, we did not share these equally), spring rolls (classic, crispy, no notes), and honestly some other stuff I've already forgotten because by that point we were deep in a dim sum fugue state.

We finished almost all of it. Almost. We tried.

And the price? An absolute steal. The kind of meal where you check the bill twice because you're sure something's missing.

If you're in Philly and you want dumplings done right in a no-fuss spot that punches way above its weight, Nom Wah is the answer.

text.text:
It's been so long since I last had sizzling spicy pork kidney – I've really missed that taste. So today I made a special trip back to my go‑to place, EMei Restaurant. One bite, and that familiar spicy, crispy, tender flavor exploded on my tongue. The kidneys were perfectly cleaned – no off‑putting smell at all – and cooked with just the right heat. Tender and springy, infused with the rich aroma of pickled chili and Sichuan peppercorns, it's the ultimate rice companion.

This restaurant is a true gem in my heart. From the taste of the dishes – which speaks volumes about the chef's skill – to the thoughtfully chosen tableware that complements each dish, everything shows care and attention to detail. Looking around, the decor is understated yet tasteful: wooden furniture, soft lighting – every corner feels warm and thoughtfully designed. It's rare to find a place that brings together great food, visual pleasure, and a cozy atmosphere all at once.

A restaurant this dedicated to cooking and hospitality deserves a five‑star rating. I'll definitely be coming back often, and I hope more friends get to enjoy this authentic, delicious experience.

I am writing this as I am finishing up an AMAZING breakfast! Now I have to preface that I am currently dieting and it SUCKS, because there are some VERY yummy things on this menu that are so enticing. I can see some of them being savored by neighboring diners and I am trying not to drool!

I ordered the Creme Brulee Latte. It was my only sinful pleasure and very worth it! For my meal I went for the Eggs Your Way, scrambled well. There was 2 options for bacon; thin or thick sliced. I went for the thick and asked if they can try to crisp it up. They did and it was awesome! I also got a side of small cubed potatoes and a both of very fresh fruit topped with a mint leaf!

The menu has something for just about anyone...sweet, savory, both, vegan, boozy, etc.

All the the staff were so very welcoming and attentive, which is always a great part of the experience.

While sitting here, I can see there is plenty of seating, an eat-at bar, Food Network on the TV and a beautiful mural on a building across the street that almost feels like a part of this place!

Pricing is appropriate and affordable. Come with a group or on your own, as I did. You can thank me after!

We tried the tasting menu and overall it was a really nice experience.

For appetizers, the Muhammara was excellent—rich, flavorful, and definitely a highlight. The cheese rolls were okay, nothing special, and the kibbeh was a bit underwhelming. The seared halloumi, however, stood out—it was very flavorful, and the addition of apricot and dates was a really nice, well-balanced flavor.

For mains, we got the ribeye cap (served as beef cubes with pilav rixe), which was really good—well-cooked and flavorful. We also tried the levrek (fish), which was just okay in comparison and didn’t stand out much.

For dessert, the kunafeh was really good and a great way to end the meal. The baklava, on the other hand, was disappointing, honestly one to stay away from.

Overall, a solid tasting menu with some standout dishes, especially on the appetizer and dessert side.

text.text:
Dark, sexy, moody atmosphere in the downstairs dining room. Very dimly lit and intimate, although it was so dark we had to use our phone flashlight to read the menu.

Our waiter was excellent throughout the evening: patient, cordial, informative, and helpful with suggestions.

Tuna Tartare: Creamy avocado provided a nice contrast to the tuna, while the rice pearls added texture. The chili oil wasn’t particularly spicy, but overall a solid dish.

Spicy Baked Scallop & Crab: Excellent dish, UNFORTUNATELY accompanied by a very unpleasant experience. After taking a bite, I felt something stringy in my mouth and pulled out a very long hair. Even after alerting our waiter, I was still pulling hair out of my mouth. The dish was remade, and our waiter handled it politely, but the restaurant’s response was nonexistent.

Wagyu Bavette: Another standout. The rare/medium-rare steak with Japanese sweet potato and miso butter was fantastic.

Black Cod Fried Rice: My least favorite. Very mild and not particularly memorable.

Toro + Soy + Caviar Nigiri: A classic combination. Fatty, buttery toro paired beautifully with the salty, creamy caviar. The nigiri are on the petite side.

Overall, great atmosphere, excellent service, and several standout dishes. Unfortunately, finding a very long hair in my mouth and continuing to pull it out after notifying the restaurant was difficult to overlook, especially at a restaurant of this caliber.

text.text:
I recently stopped by Tom's Dim Sum during lunchtime, and overall, my experience was a mix of pros and cons.
The location itself is in a convenient area, and when I walked in, the environment was calm, quiet, and nicely set up. It wasn’t too crowded around 12 PM, which I appreciated. However, the customer service could definitely use some improvement. Both visits, I felt a bit rushed while ordering, like I needed to make a quick decision instead of being able to comfortably look over the menu.
On my first visit, my coworker and I ordered the chicken wings. They were decent—lightly seasoned, not overly salty, and gave “quick grab-and-go” vibes. Nothing too special, but not bad either.
I decided to give them another try on a second visit, hoping for the same or better experience. Unfortunately, this time the wings didn’t hit the same. They had a powdery texture and lacked flavor, with very minimal seasoning. After biting into them, I also questioned the cleanliness/prep of the chicken, which made the experience less enjoyable overall.
One thing to note: there is a $10 minimum for card payments, and the wings were around $8, so keep that in mind if you’re stopping in for a quick bite.
At this point, I’m not sure I’d return specifically for the wings. I might give other items on the menu a try, but I’d likely order ahead instead of dining in, just to avoid that rushed feeling.
Overall: decent spot with potential, but consistency and customer experience need work.

text.text:
Paprica Grill – A Hidden Mediterranean Gem
If you find yourself wandering near Jewelers' Row, do your taste buds a favor and step into Paprica Grill at 811 Sansom St. This spot proves that the best flavors often come from the most unassuming places.

The Vibe
The restaurant is small, warm, and cozy, offering a truly "charming" atmosphere that makes you feel instantly at home. Whether it's the brick accents or the soft lighting, the space feels intimate and inviting—perfect for a quiet dinner.

The Hospitality
A huge part of the experience is the service. The owner, Ahmed, is a total sweetheart and ensures every guest feels like family. That level of personal care is hard to find and makes the meal even more memorable.

The Food
The kitchen is turning out authentic, homemade dishes that are deliciously seasoned, expertly wetting your taste buds from the first bite.
* Lentil Soup: Absolutely award-winning; it’s the ultimate comfort food with amazing flavors and vegetarian.
* Mixed Platter: A vibrant, must-order spread. From the creamy hummus to the perfectly seasoned dips, every element on the plate is a winner.
* Fresh Extras: The meal is served with warm, fluffy bread that’s perfect for scooping up every last bit of those Mediterranean flavors.
Verdict: For authentic Mediterranean soul food in Philly, this is it.

text.text:
Authentic Taste, but the Lack of Cleanliness is a Dealbreaker

After a Chinese friend recommended this Lanzhou hand-pulled noodle spot in Philly, I was excited to try their lamb noodles. I arrived shortly after 7:30 PM on a Thursday evening and was surprised to find only one other customer there.

The Food: I ordered the Noodles with Lamb, and I have to say, it felt very authentic and genuinely tasty. The vegetables added a nice freshness to the broth. While there wasn't much lamb in the bowl, that is understandable given the very reasonable price point of $12–$13. The hand-pulled noodles themselves were excellent.

The Issue: Unfortunately, the experience was overshadowed by the lack of cleanliness. I am aware that some small, authentic spots aren't always known for being spotless, but the level of grime here was hard to ignore. The red chili oilwas delicious, but the serving cup it came in was quite dirty. Even the bottle of hand sanitizer on the table looked so filthy that I didn't want to touch it.

Final Word: I’m really not asking for a high-end, sleekly designed, or "shiny" place. Customers come here specifically for the authentic food, not the decor. However, all we are asking is for the staff to maintain a minimum level of cleanliness—like simply wiping down the condiment bottles on the table more often. It is a shame, because I would love to return for the flavor every time I'm in town, but the unsanitary environment means I won't be going back.

text.text:
Incredible and Worth the Hype

Terakawa Ramen is an incredibly popular, small cozy restaurant that delivers excellent, quick service and a truly outstanding menu. I got the miso ramen and it was divine. Everything was served hot and fresh, and the flavors were absolutely delicious. The meat literally melted in your mouth, and the signature egg, the noodles, and the rich broth were all perfection.

They offer appetizers, multiple ramen bowls, and several other menu items, and you can also get drinks to go with your meal. The customer service was wonderful, the prices were very fair, and the food was fantastic.

There was a line of people when we arrived and another line when we left, and I can see exactly why. This place is absolutely worth it.

text.text:
Yamitsuki is such a great spot right in the center of Chinatown. Parking around the area can be a little risky or difficult sometimes, but honestly it’s worth it — you might just need to park a little farther and walk a bit.
The food here is absolutely flavorful and satisfying. I highly recommend the spicy ramen if you enjoy a little heat — rich broth, great flavor, and very comforting. The Mango Salmon Roll was also surprisingly amazing, fresh and perfectly balanced with sweetness and savory flavors. The takoyaki was delicious too, crispy outside and soft inside with great sauce. I also tried one of their rice bowls before and it was honestly excellent.
What makes this place stand out even more is the atmosphere. It feels like a mix between a Japanese-style bar and restaurant with good music, dim lighting, and beautiful Japanese-inspired decorations that make the whole place feel cozy and stylish at the same time.
Overall, this is a really nice spot for ramen, sushi, drinks, and late-night vibes in Chinatown. Definitely worth trying if you’re in Philly.

text.text:
Just wanted to share our experience so others are aware.

My friends and I came here as a party of four. The menu says an 18% service charge is only added for parties of six or more, so we weren’t expecting any automatic gratuity. After we left, we realized a 20% gratuity had already been added to our bill. Since no one told us it was included, we also left an extra tip without realizing we were tipping twice.

We reached out afterward, and they told us it was because of a “World Cup all-you-can-eat event.” The problem is that this was never mentioned to us at any point during our visit. We also got different explanations about whether the 20% charge was mandatory or just recommended, which was pretty confusing.

This also wasn’t our first uncomfortable experience. On a previous visit, we felt pressured about tipping and were told that the staff rely on tips, which didn’t sit right with us.

Not trying to bash the restaurant—we just think service charges like this should be clearly communicated before customers order or pay. Just double-check your bill so you don’t end up accidentally tipping twice like we did.

text.text:
I’ve been going to Yamitsuki for 4+ years. The food is amazing, the store is beautifully decorated, and the drinks are awesome. As of recently, however, the customer service has been horrible.

I used to be a regular and the attitudes I’ve been getting for the past 6+ months in comparison to times prior has completely turned me off of the restaurant.

There has been a couple of times I walked into the nearly empty store and been sat DIRECTLY next to another party. I’m walking couples being placed side by side with 5 empty seats following them. I find it to be very inconsiderate.

If you come in during the lunch special the servers often deliberately ignore you in order to charge the full price. I know this is the case because I’ve been here plenty of times during their regular hours w/o any sort of issues being serviced. There was even one a time they tried to charge me full price even though I was well within the discounted time frame… I would’ve never noticed if my friend didn’t say anything.

The gratuity on parties as small as 3 is also true. It is fairly recent thing they started doing and uncommon in Philadelphia as it typically starts on parties of 6. I have no problem paying it and I tip every-time, I was caught off guard when they just started to be adding w/o prior warning.

I will lastly add that this establishment is cash only Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays which has been creating issues for people with this new gratuity.

I’m writing this in hopes that you guys improve, the owner seems to only reply to positive comments on here while completely ignoring valid critiques which is not a good look.

There are plenty of ramen places and this used to be my favorite :( If my experiences improve maybe I’ll change my mind but I would suggest researching other options as well.

text.text:
If you’re in Chinatown and craving authentic Korean food, Dae Bak Korean Restaurant is a hidden gem you don’t want to miss.

Tucked away on the second floor, it already feels like one of those “you have to know about it” spots and it delivers. I tried the bulgogi bibimbap and it was everything: perfectly seasoned, super flavorful, and served hot with that comforting, home-style feel.

But let’s talk about the banchan… SO good. Everything tasted incredibly fresh, well-balanced, and thoughtfully prepared. Honestly, those little side dishes alone elevate the entire experience.

The vibe is cozy and authentic, and the food speaks for itself. If you’re into real Korean flavors (not watered down), this place hits.

Definitely a spot I’ll keep coming back to.

text.text: My boyfriend and I decided to try the $53-per-person dinner, which came with 2 appetizers, 2 salads, 4 entrees, and 3 desserts. All the food was incredible, and the desserts were amazing too. We had the margaritas and loved them too, they were definitely different to the usual. The portions were huge so be mindful if you’re not too hungry, and we had plenty of leftovers for the next day. This place has that cozy, old-school Italian atmosphere with classic decor and an upscale feel for a chain restaurant. Our server, Matteo, was amazing - attentive, super lovely, and really made the experience feel special. The staff overall were professional and welcoming, and it’s definitely a spot we’ll come back to for another great dinner together.

text.text:
Visited with the family while in search of some good ramen in the Philadelphia area.

Lovely and well-maintained space. It was practically empty during our early afternoon weekday visit...presumably after the lunch rush and before the dinner rush.

Lots of delicious options in the menu...including sushi and ramen as the establishment name implies. Prices were very fair with lots of appetizers under $10, specialty sushi rolls around $12ish and ramen around $15-18.

We ordered a few items including two ramen bowls. Both were very sizeable and delicious. Some of the best ramen I've had. Food took about 20-25 minutes...not very long.

Staff was friendly, helpful and accommodating.

Clean bathroom.

Metered street parking wasn't difficult to find during our early afternoon weekday visit. We utilized the Park Mobile app...but there are others you can use as well.

text.text:
I should have listened to Tim when he warned my fiancée and me back in March of 2024 when we visited this restaurant about the reality of the size of the Peking Duck Dinner for Two we ordered. Because prior to ordering that sequence of delicacies, we ordered Fried Wontons and Two Peking Duck Rolls to share. We should have not done that. Because the Peking Duck Dinner for Two was huge enough that we could not finish it. Despite our inability to finish it, we truly enjoyed each of its components.

The Half Peking Duck was truly delicious. To be our first time eating duck in our respective lives, we were truly blown out of our minds. The Chow family really know how to roast their ducks like back in their old country. The Wonton Noodle Soup with Green Vegetables was hot enough like to help us deal with the cold weather outside the restaurant. We could not have asked for more. The Shredded Duck and String Bean Stirfry was also delicious and enjoyable. The Spicy Duck and Pineapple Fried Rice was a little more spicy to suit our taste, but we still ate it enjoyably. There was not a single thing we did not enjoy at the restaurant when we dined there during our stay in Philly two years ago.

Like we mentioned before, Tim was an attentive server who puts guests above profit. That was surprising to us despite his language barrier. Because knowing we were not from the area, let alone the city, he would have not bothered in warning us about the bigness of the banquet we were about to order. But he still did showing us we were his priority and not the money he was going to make the restaurant at our expense. He truly has character and integrity.

People like Tim give the restaurant a better atmosphere than it already has. We unfortunately did not focus much on the atmosphere of the restaurant because we were truly tired and sleepy after having arrived in the city by place early that morning. But we focused enough in it like to know we were eating not only Philly’s oldest, continuously operating Chinese restaurant. We knew that perhaps we were eating at the city’s BEST Chinese restaurant and that we would NOT eat at any other than Sang Kee Peking Duck House. We will definitely be right back the next time we go back to Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

text.text: Sang Kee is literally my favorite restaurant in all of Chinatown, or Center City for that matter. The duck is fantastic, but so is their incredible BBQ pork. I'd highly recommend the pork and duck with veg and rice dish, it's always been my go to. The appetizers are also fantastic, so feel free to try anything that catches your eye on the menu, I've never had a bad meal at Sang Kee in the 9 years I've been dining here. It was very busy when we arrived around 6pm on a Saturday night,  but table turn around was very fast and our wait was short. Service was tremendous, we never felt rushed despite how many people were waiting to get inside, and we left satisfied and very full. Sang Kee is the best!

We stopped by after visiting Big Bounce America on a rainy weekend and chose this restaurant based on its great Google reviews.

We ordered the sautéed pea shoots with garlic, roast duck wonton noodle soup, and the roast duck & BBQ pork over rice. The roast duck was definitely the highlight—juicy, flavorful, and with just the right amount of rich fat. I would recommend the duck.

Unfortunately, the BBQ pork was extremely salty. Every bite needed a big mouthful of rice to balance it out, and it was honestly disappointing.

Overall, I’d come back for the roast duck, but I would probably skip the BBQ pork next time.

The bread was crusty on the outside and warm and soft on the inside. So so good! Ate every bite. Try it!!

text.text:
Finally made it to the Georgian boat place! I swapped my dumpling cravings for a mushroom cheeseboat (plus beef sausage), and it was a flavor explosion. The crust has that perfect Turkish pide-style pull—crispy yet chewy. The cheese is so bold and rich that it honestly stands on its own; I could have skipped the meat and still been in heaven.

Is $25 a bit much for a single-serving "boat" with extra beef topping? Probably. But you’re paying for quality and, more importantly, kindness. The staff here are actually smiling and attentive—a stark contrast to the legendary rudeness at places like DiNic’s, Uncle Gus, or Hershel’s. It seems those guys think they’re sandwich-making angels descending from the heavens to do us a favor! I’ll take the "overpriced" boat and a friendly smile over a grumpy "angel" any day.

One final note: these 'boats' deserve better than plastic. The bread is so beautifully resilient that a plastic knife simply can't handle it. I mentioned this to the staff and want to reiterate it here: this food needs metal utensils. I understand the logistical headache—more washing and the risk of 'lost' cutlery—but to truly enjoy the texture of that crust, you need a real knife. Let’s be fair to these boats; they’ve earned a proper grip!

Sat at the bar on a recent Saturday. Was phenomenal food and atmosphere. Decent music. The bartender was also really nice and knowledgeable. He happed to be from Towson Maryland, same area i went to college. The food bites were incredible. Absolutely LOVED the crabcake sliders, and the eggplant bao.

We had some clever cocktails and some other drinks. I thought the cocktails were well priced for the labor and ingredients.

My only gripe is sort of dumb one. I don’t usually get cocktails because of too much sugar and love a bonded whiskey on the rocks. I had some old granddad bonded from the well on the the rocks. text.text:
Wayward is a good name for this restaurant. As in the service went wayward. Or the food order went wayward.

I ate here at least five times since I was staying at the Canopy Hilton.  One of the hostesses is very nice and over the week she knew instinctively which tables I preferred. I’ve eaten here mid afternoon, breakfast, brunch, dinner, and lunch.  I had free meal vouchers as a Hilton member.

The first time I ate here there was a food item missing from the burger. The staff was very accommodating and retrieved the missing ingredient.

I received an entrée and a salad at the same time even though I specifically asked for the salad first. I was told that since I had ordered from the bar menu, my instructions were ignored because all dishes are supposed to come out on the table at the same time.

The last time I visited, I ordered the smoked  salmon Benedict, but the server brought out the ham Benedict, then claimed that she had entered the correct salmon order into the system and that the kitchen had erred. There was a 45 minute wait for the correct order to arrive. The restaurant the way of accommodating me was to charge me for only the price of the ham Benedict, which was a whopping two dollars savings.  It was that that point that I found out from a different lady that my server had entered the order incorrectly.

The two people at the table next to me smirked when I had gotten the wrong order. However, they asked their server how they could use their meal vouchers and a server said she didn’t know anything about that, that she just worked at the restaurant. I know that you’re supposed to charge to the room to be able to have the hotel apply the meal credits to the meals, but I decided to say nothing.  The two people ended up charging their breakfast individually on their respective credit cards.

The Wayward is a beautiful restaurant. The furniture is comfortable and the decoration is meticulous.

The stuffed French toast was inedible.  The mixed green salad was fantastic. The meatballs were very good.

text.text:
I stopped by Down Home Diner while walking around Reading Terminal Market, mostly because I wanted something filling and familiar. The place has a laid-back, no-frills vibe—nothing fancy, just a straightforward diner feel that fits right in with the busy market around it.

I ordered a classic breakfast, and it came out pretty quickly even though it was a bit crowded. The portions were generous, definitely enough to keep you full for a while. The food itself was solid—nothing overly special, but comforting and satisfying in that “home-cooked” kind of way. The pancakes were fluffy, and the eggs were done just how I asked.

Service was friendly but a little rushed, which makes sense given how busy it gets. It didn’t feel like a place to linger too long, but more like somewhere to grab a good, hearty meal before heading back out to explore.

Overall, it’s a reliable spot if you’re in the market and craving something simple and filling. Not a standout dining experience, but it does exactly what you’d expect from a diner.

text.text:
After much anticipation, Mr. Edison has finally opened! Nothing about the concept feels like it was neglected in development. The vibe and aesthetic is consistent across the visuals, menu themes, and live music. The interior feels like you are stepping onto a set in the best way.

The service was lovely and attentive to the event you are celebrating. We witnessed a slight spill by a server at a nearby table and the response by management was apologetic and beyond accommodating for their mistake. That’s all you can ask for from service. Things happen and they take their customer’s experience very seriously.

Because the menu can be ordered in modest shareables, sides, up to large entrees, you can ensure you get exactly amount of food for your appetite. I love that aspect of customization within menus so they stuck the landing with that. Also - so many aspects of dishes are made in-house and the quality is elevated because of this.

The drink menu was diverse, but remained on theme. Each drink came out like a tiny work of care and creativity. They were a bit pricier than other comparable restaurants, but I believe it was justified in the steps taken to make each drink and the presentation. The non-alcoholic menu was very flavorful without falling into the extra sweet or fruity trap that many mocktails menus fall into. It’s considerate and it’s appreciated. It was thought about with equal care to the alcohol menu. Lastly, the range of luxury spirits and liquor they offer is not something you see in casual dining if you aren’t keen on mixed beverages. If you are looking to try something without the commitment of investing in a full bottle personally, this would be a good place to try a high end item.

The live jazz can be heard throughout the restaurant via discreet speakers if you aren’t near the musicians. The music between pieces by the act aren’t distracting or take you out of mood being set. You can easily hear others in your party to converse which I love. Food brings people together and yelling over music is horrendous if that isn’t called for by an upscale experience.

Lovely all around! We are excited to celebrate many life events here in the future. I hope that eventually a lunch service is considered as dinner is only available at this time. It would be an amazing place to bring valuable clients during the day and raise awareness of the restaurant with those visiting the city for business during the workday.

The restaurant is absolutely beautiful, and the atmosphere is just as impressive. Unfortunately, that was the highlight of our experience. The live music was not something we particularly enjoyed, and once the band finished, we actually found the background music that followed to be much more fitting for the dining atmosphere.

We were celebrating my loved one’s birthday, but it felt as though the staff completely overlooked the occasion. That was especially disappointing since we chose this restaurant to celebrate such a special moment.

I was also very disappointed with my meal. The lobster Thermidor was undercooked, and the Sea Bass had a terrible smell—it was simply awful. The selection of sides that accompanied our 18 oz Bone in New York steak strip was also very limited and not particularly appetizing. The drinks were also disappointing and did not meet the expectations I had for a restaurant of this caliber. After hearing so many wonderful things about this restaurant, I expected a much better dining experience.

Paying premium prices has never been an issue for us—we’re happy to do so when the food, service, and overall experience reflect that level of quality. Unfortunately, on this visit, they did not. The restaurant itself is stunning and has so much potential, which makes the experience even more disappointing.

I always choose valet parking when dining out, and unfortunately, even that part of the experience was disappointing. I won’t even get started on the details, but it was another area that fell short of expectations.

I truly hope this was simply an off night,
So disappointing overall.

Went there with party of 4 on Sat evening. Good thing we had reservation. They were pretty full and people without reservations were turned away. We did have to wait before they sat us but it wasn’t too long. It’s a byod place so bring your own 🍷 🍻.
Parking was difficult - but that’s typical in downtown Chinatown. Recommend the calamari appetizer that was made just right. Lightly battered and flavored. Really enjoyed the sauté mushroom - flavored very well. I had the egg pancake with scallion on rice… which reminds me of my childhood. Others in our party had interesting options too. I tried the salmon over sticky rice - that was hands down the best dish on the table that night! Cooked perfectly - when the salmon flakes but not overcooked and rice was delicious! The chicken dish was also good.
We tried two of the dessert that turned out perfectly - not too sweet. Mango sago had something like grapefruit in there adding a twist to the dish. I would go back !

text.text:
Bai Wei used to be the pride of Philly's Chinese food scene — the restaurant everyone recommended. Tonight, the dining experience was a disaster from start to finish, and it really feels like the quality has fallen off a cliff.

Food: We ordered dishes that used to be excellent. One bite in, it was obvious something was off — over-salted, unevenly seasoned, nowhere near the level it used to be.

Service: Plates were set down carelessly at the edge of the table and left there, with no help arranging anything — we had to do it ourselves. The attitude felt cold and indifferent throughout.

Takeout experience: This was the most frustrating part. We asked a server to box up our leftovers. He took the dish to the back and never came back. We waited a full 30 minutes. When we tried to find help, almost every server seemed to have vanished. We finally caught one who said he'd "check," then disappeared for another 10 minutes with no update. In total, we waited half an hour just to get a box of leftovers.

Honestly, both the front and back of house felt like they were failing — it seems like there are serious issues with management and staff attitudes. The one exception was the older woman clearing dishes — she was the only staff member all night who was hardworking, attentive, and polite.

I really hope the owner takes management and staff hiring seriously, because this used to be a beloved spot, and it's clearly slipping.

text.text:
First time visiting after seeing it on XHS. Tried to pre-order roast goose but called too late the day before—they explained honestly it couldn’t defrost in time (appreciate the transparency). Also missed the Taishan rice roll since it’s only available before 3pm—next time!

Biggest surprise was the lai fun—super smooth and perfect with roast duck/goose legs. Roast duck and char siu were excellent; roast pork still crispy though a bit heavy on five-spice. Better than most in DC, though I’ve had slightly better in NYC/Canada.

Service really stood out. When I praised their BBQ, the server said, “Chinatown Philly has many good BBQ spots”—very classy. Even helped buy live fish from next door before closing with no extra charge. Prices were very fair ($37.95 fish incl. prep, $39.95 eel).

Minor downsides: salt & pepper ribs lacked flavor; sizzling intestines had a strong odor. Wonton noodles and congee were average.

Overall: great value, standout service, and I’ll definitely be back (next time pre-ordering goose).

However, based on the quality of the duck and the pork, I’ll be skipping those dishes next time.

name: Chubby Cattle Wagyu Shabu House | Philadelphia

text.text:
We arrived right at opening and were the first ones there on Saturday morning. We were then greeted by our server who adequately taught us how everything works.

Pretty simple, there are different tiers and each tier offers something different. Of course, we went for the top diamond tier which includes all-you-can-eat Japanese and Australian wagyu, unlimited appetizers and pretty much everything on the menu was unlimited at that tier.

Starting off with all 4 of the appetizers offered, the bone marrow was quite amazing. Rich, buttery and tasted great, fresh off the grill. The wagyu nigiri was a favourite of ours. The rice was nicely seasoned and we couldn't get enough. The wagyu tartare was nice, and we wished we were served the toasted bread from the bone marrow rather than the chips. Unfortunately, the sweet shrimp wasn't too fresh. The heads showed signs of blackening, and it tasted close to the end of its shelf life.

The thinly sliced wagyu was exquisite. We tried not only the Japanese wagyu, but the Australian wagyu as well, and we kept ordering tray after tray of it. The seafood bowl that came with our tier was a nice touch. I can't say I was a huge fan of the king crab that was offered. These were the end and knuckle pieces that didn't have much meat in them. These could have been skipped as amazing as king crab sounds. As for the vegetables and sides, they were fresh and really added to our hot pot experience.

Overall, coming in at $90/per person, I feel this is a steal. An amazing price point to eat unlimited rich, buttery, marbled beef. We also found our server to be very attentive which was greatly appreciated. We did not wait long in between ordering more items and when they arrived which is a huge plus.

I went to Chubby Cattle in November 2025, as I liked the idea of being able to eat good-quality meat at a relatively affordable price. Unfortunately, my experience took a turn when I was served raw fried chicken. I had already eaten about half of it before realizing it was undercooked, which is obviously a serious food safety issue.

I told the server right away, to which he took the dish back and gave me a 20% discount. I felt slightly nauseous afterward and completely lost my appetite, so I wasn’t able to enjoy the rest of the meal I had paid a lot of money for. Given the situation, the 20% discount did not feel adequate. The server also barely apologized, which added to my frustration.

The AYCE wagyu concept is appealing, but this experience made me very concerned about how food is being handled. I asked to speak with a manager at the restaurant, but none were available. I also called a few days later to request a callback from a manager and never heard back.

I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with my recent experience at your establishment, which occurred during a birthday celebration for a friend. This was my third visit, and unfortunately, it was the most disappointing.

To start, the service provided by our server, George K., was subpar. He took a considerable amount of time to take our order, and when our appetizer arrived, it was cold. Upon expressing my concern, George informed us that the chips were indeed cold, but he did not apologize or attempt to rectify the situation. His dismissive attitude was alarming and unprofessional.

Additionally, one of my friends ordered a steak cooked medium, but it arrived well done and extremely dry. She chose not to take it home due to its unsatisfactory condition, and we left half of it untouched.

Moreover, the chicken Alfredo we ordered had an unpleasant tangy flavor, which further added to our negative experience.

Throughout our visit, we were disheartened to witness a lack of attentiveness not only from our server but also from the kitchen. Given that management fees and gratuity were automatically added to our bill, we expected a much higher standard of service and food quality.

It appears that George may have been having an off day, but I urge you to address these issues with your staff and your kitchen team. Proper training in customer service and culinary standards is essential to maintaining a satisfied clientele.

This experience has left me feeling that it may be my last visit.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.
