text.text:
After enjoying the biggest snowstorm we've had in a decade, the roads were pretty rough. But not wanting to stay cooped up inside, I called a friend and asked if she wanted to go out for a bite to eat. We searched Google to find any places that might be open and luckily, the Reading Terminal – my favorite spot – was open. While only a few vendors were able to make it in, I'd say the market was running at about half capacity. Parking was easy to find and the inside wasn't crowded, so we took our time browsing our options. We decided to try Molly Malloy's, which had a few vegan choices on the menu. It has a nice pub-style vibe and our server was friendly and attentive.

I usually like to do a bit of research before trying a new place, but I didn't in this case. It's possible they were understaffed due to the storm, but regardless, the food was a bit of a letdown. We ordered a vegan tahini Caesar salad and a vegan mushroom french dip with fries. The vegan Caesar salad is something I'm passionate about because it's so easy to make and can taste just as good as a non-vegan version, sometimes even better. This particular salad had kale, romaine, radicchio, crispy chickpeas, croutons, and a lemon tahini dressing. Unfortunately, we both found it to be very bitter and overly dressed with lemon, lacking the tahini flavor. We tried to balance it out with some maple syrup, but it didn't quite work.

As for the mushroom French dip, I had high hopes, but it fell short. The dip – or au jus – was cold and gelatinous, with decent flavor but not the best presentation in a plastic cup. The ciabatta bread was good, the mushrooms were cooked well, but overall it lacked depth in flavor. I think garlic, rosemary maybe a little onion powder would take this to the next level.  While we appreciated the vegan options on the menu, we believe that if you're going to offer something, make sure it's the best it can be.

For Center City Philly, this is a unique AM place that will give you local neighborhood vibes, differentiated food, and for an hour and a half, maybe take you away to a place far far away.

Food Ordered:  Shakshuka, Croque Madame, and Berry w Chocolate & Nutella Crepe.  This was all great.  Adult and kid approved.  Also iced matcha and mint tea.  Didn’t blow us away but thank you for the differentiation relative to the community!

Service & Atmosphere:  it’s a small intimate operation. We went on Memorial Day Monday, were the 2nd or 3rd party into this small place.  Order at counter, seat yourself, and have your food taken to you when complete.  My partner wished it was full service, but I liked how it played out.  Felt different and more raw.  If you ever watched Spy Game w Robert Redford and Brad Pitt, feels like a toned down version of the cafe where they in Beirut where they conjur up the idea of Operation Dinner Out.  It’s just cool.  Okay maybe not that raw (it was maybe half cool like, but also half cozy euro country cafe)

Would we go back?   Yes we would.  Not every week.  But we’d be back.  Esp if in center City again.   There’s so much plain jain / diner vibe around there…. This is a nice twist.

Pearl & Mary on 13th St — A Happy Hour That Actually Delivers

Let me tell you, Pearl & Mary came through in a big way.
We stopped in for happy hour and honestly, the prices alone would've been enough to win us over — $2 oysters, $1 clams, $5 beers, $6 house wine, and $7 cocktails. The kids' smash burger rang in at $7. In this economy? Yes, please. But what sealed the deal was that the food actually matched the price. The oysters and clams were fresh, clean, and exactly what you want when you're sitting down with the family after a long day. No shortcuts, no "well, what did you expect for $2?" moments.

We also ordered off the regular menu — fish and chips and a clam chowder — and both were a hit with mom and the kids, which, if you know anything about feeding a family, is the real victory lap.

The service was the cherry on top. Joe was attentive without being overbearing, checked in on us just the right amount, and made the whole experience feel easy. And shoutout to Francesca, the manager, at the front — she got us seated right away and was incredibly accommodating from the jump.

Pearl & Mary is the kind of spot that makes you feel like you found something. Whether you're visiting Philly or you already live here and somehow haven't been — fix that. It's a must-try, full stop.

We stopped in for happy hour and honestly, the prices alone would've been enough to win us over — $2 oysters, $1 clams, $5 beers, $6 house wine, and $7 cocktails. The kids' smash burger rang in at $7. In this economy? Yes, please. But what sealed the deal was that the food actually matched the price. The oysters and clams were fresh, clean, and exactly what you want when you're sitting down with the family after a long day. No shortcuts, no "well, what did you expect for $2?" moments.

We also ordered off the regular menu — fish and chips and a clam chowder — and both were a hit with mom and the kids, which, if you know anything about feeding a family, is the real victory lap.

The service was the cherry on top. Joe was attentive without being overbearing, checked in on us just the right amount, and made the whole experience feel easy. And shoutout to Francesca, the manager, at the front — she got us seated right away and was incredibly accommodating from the jump.

Pearl & Mary is the kind of spot that makes you feel like you found something. Whether you're visiting Philly or you already live here and somehow haven't been — fix that. It's a must-try, full stop.

text.text: Visited Knock for the first time this evening with a large group of colleagues and it was a fair experience. Located in a historic district, Knock is one of several local businesses and shops. My party consisted of fifteen (15) professionals, all with eclectic palettes. The menu has several different options ranging from seafood, burgers, and pastas. Overall, I wasn’t impressed with the quality of the food. You’ll notice several different food options via the pictures I upload.  Personally, I ordered the jumbo crab cake, as an appetizer and seafood alfredo. The jumbo crab cake, came on a bed of warm spinach and a tomato based sauce. The crab cake was not jumbo and was okay. The consistency of the crab cake was not to my liking, nor was its firmness and taste. Overall, for the cost, it wasn’t worth the value. The seafood Alfredo consists of scallops, cod fish, and shrimp. I asked could the pasta only be shrimp and the restaurant was able to accommodate that. I was very impressed with my waitperson’s follow-up to ensure that I got what I wanted. Unfortunately, the Alfredo sauce was watery and the shrimp seemed boiled. Overall, it was eatable, but not on my list of favorite dishes. Several of my colleagues ordered the NY Strip, medium well, and some of their orders can me back rare. Rare to the point that we had to send it back. Overall, the staff was friendly, the food was average, but I enjoyed the company of my colleagues in their large dining area. I don’t plan on coming back!

Pistola’s Del Sur might officially be one of my favorite spots in Passyunk. Easily one of the best happy hours around, and honestly just a great place overall.
I tried all five tacos: tuna, carne asada, roasted chicken, cheesesteak, and buffalo cauliflower, and every single one was amazing.

Overall, I’ll 100% be back multiple times. Highly recommend, not just for happy hour, but for the food, service, and atmosphere too. 🌮🍹🔥

text.text:
Review for Cantina Los Caballitos

I had high hopes for Cantina Los Caballitos based on the appealing menu, but my experience quickly turned sour. Upon arrival, I ordered a Gingerale, but what I received was something that tasted off—eventually identified as club soda, which the waitress later confirmed was due to a tank issue.

When it came time to place my food order, I made my allergy to scallions clear, and the waitress assured me they didn't serve them. Despite this, my chipotle barbecue wings arrived drenched in scallions and were frankly unappetizing. The shrimp tacos were somewhat better but still left me feeling unwell hours later.

I also attempted to order a strawberry daiquiri, only to be told they didn't have it, and the alternative margarita was unavailable due to a broken machine.

While the ambiance was pleasant, with a nice outdoor setting and friendly patrons, the overall service and food quality were major letdowns. Given my experience, I cannot recommend this restaurant and certainly wouldn't return.

text.text:
Stopped into Stogie Joe’s in Passyunk Philly for happy hour and this place continues to be one of my go-to neighborhood spots.
I’ve been here multiple times already and will definitely keep coming back and recommending it. Stogie Joe’s has been a South Philly staple for years and really captures that classic neighborhood bar-and-grill feel- laid back, welcoming, always packed with people, and the kind of place where everyone seems to know each other.
The spot has even gotten national attention after being featured on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives with Guy Fieri, which honestly makes sense once you try the food. It’s one of those places that stays true to its roots while still becoming well-known outside the neighborhood.
One thing to know before you go: it’s cash only, which honestly adds to the old-school South Philly vibe. The happy hour deals are tough to beat too. I believe they do the $10 buckets of Rolling Rock or PBR all day, every day, which is one of the better beer specials you’ll find around the city.
The place has plenty of indoor and outdoor seating, so it works whether you’re stopping by for a quick drink or hanging out for a while with friends. Service is consistently great every time I’ve been there- the staff is always friendly, attentive, and checking in without overdoing it.
The food has always been solid too. I’d definitely recommend the pizza- pictured was the small size, and it was more than enough for two of us. There are honestly a ton of good menu options, and I don’t think I’ve ever left disappointed after eating there.
Overall, Stogie Joe’s is just a reliable South Philly staple with great vibes, strong happy hour specials, good food, and a fun crowd. If you’re in the Passyunk area, it’s absolutely worth stopping into.

text.text:
This place was popular; I was nearby at various times throughout this past Saturday and it was teeming with customers every time. But based on my experience you want to either good with food or other drinks. I stopped by around 1:30pm on Saturday, needing to burn some time before meeting up with my cousin chums at my Airbnb down the street. I'm not very familiar with Philly (much more of a NY person) and I'm sure this was my first time walking around this particular neighborhood in South Philly - very cool area, reminiscent of downtown Jersey City. I didn't do any research and just popped in here because they had a bar. Lesson learned.

I was wearing a Mets jersey in anticipation of the game that night (which was a horrendous experience and doesn't need more of a reference than that), so I appreciated that everyone in this establishment was pleasant and accommodating. That honestly wasn't the case everywhere I went - the bartender was nice, and a customer actually walked up to me on his way out to pay his respects (though mostly for the recently anointed NBA champs, the Knicks). Very classy.

At the end of the day, I had a drink here and it wasn't very good. I ordered an Old Fashioned, which is a risk at a place that isn't a bougie mixology-type bar (and this isn't that), but they WERE explicitly advertising this cocktail on their board above the bar. It was a massive overpour, which you can probably tell from the accompanying picture. I barely detected any bitters, and maybe he thought it was an appropriate amount because he loaded the glass down with ice, but there was easily six or seven ounces instead of the standard two or so. Result? Basically gasoline. I strategically waited for some of the ice to melt to assist here, which helped a little. Also, he basically mulled an orange slice into the bottom of the drink so I accidentally sucked up some pulp/seeds once or twice. Honestly mystifying on a couple of different levels.

Given that I was in a hipster Philly neighborhood, the price point was a little high. I think it was about $15, and should have been closer to $12 or $13, especially given the quality and time of day, but it is what it is. As several others mentioned, it's a cash only bar (a rare breed these days). The bartender seemed a little surprised I had the cash to begin with in my wallet, which makes me think they really rely on the processing fees for the on-site ATM, but I'd stock up on the bills beforehand if this is a pre-planned trip.

I really have to stop ordering Old Fashioneds at regular bars.

text.text:
**CASH ONLY** – Just a heads-up, this wasn’t clearly posted anywhere that I saw, so I want to make sure it’s the first thing you notice.
I visited this spot because I’m a big fan of *Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives* with Guy Fieri, and I was excited to try it out. The restaurant has a cool, laid-back vibe with both indoor and outdoor seating, and the outdoor area is dog-friendly, which is a nice bonus.
We started with the honey hot baked wings. They had a great flavor and were fall-off-the-bone tender. That said, I wouldn’t call them “jumbo” as described on the menu—they seemed more average in size.
I ordered the Chicken Parmesan, which was a bit disappointing. It resembled more of a chicken patty topped with sauce and cheese, rather than a traditional cutlet that fills the plate. The sauce was runny and on the sweeter side—not really my thing, though that’s on me for not reading the menu more closely. The entrée only comes with *either* linguine marinara *or* a vegetable side, not both, which feels a bit stingy for the price.
My girlfriend ordered the Eggplant Rigatoni, which was advertised as spicy but really wasn’t. The portion size was also smaller than expected. I guess we went in with high hopes—I was expecting more of a “Nonna’s kitchen in South Philly” kind of experience.
Overall, the ambiance was nice, but the food didn’t quite live up to the hype.

text.text:
Bomb Bomb Grill absolutely lived up to the name - food, service, and vibe were all 10/10. We celebrated my sister’s bachelorette dinner here and couldn’t have picked a better spot.

The food was unreal. We did the Dungeness Crab upgrade and it was so worth it. Our table ordered the shrimp cocktail, crab cake, clams casino, stuffed calamari, and lobster & shells. I’m not exaggerating when I say the lobster & shells was everyone’s favorite. Total show-stopper.

For pasta sides we had the carbonara and the black ink pasta, plus broccoli rabe (which was shockingly delicious even for someone who normally skips it) and fries with Bomb spice .. AMAZING. The only mistake we made was not asking for the fries to come out earlier so we could dip them into all the leftover sauces from the table 😭.

To finish, we shared the sundae with the works and wow… we all immediately wished we’d ordered our own. The fried/caramelized banana alone deserves its own fan club.

Service was fantastic, the energy was perfect for a celebration, and every single person left happy and full. Highly recommend for a special night out. Especially if you’re celebrating something big. We’ll absolutely be back. 💣🔥🍝🍤🍨

text.text:
wanted something that opens late that isn't fast food or diner. came across this establishment which opens til 2am. when arrived, I can see why it opens to 2 because it'll probably take you a couple hours to find parking - holy. but once you do, it's worth it.

this place offers both indoor & outdoor seatings along w @ the bar. great selections of beer & cocktails, including seasonal and taps. inside seating from where we were were limited to about 3 tables of 4, while outdoor offers both sides of the building on the sidewalks.

the staff were all very pleasant and friendly. we had K/Crystal, who was prompt, professional, and a delight. she made sure we were ok but also didn't hover around us.

as for the menu. it offered your typical gastropub type of food from apps like wings, nachos, calamari, sliders, etc. entrees has steak, pasta, salmon, and chicken. also included salads & soup, burgers, and a kids menu!

we started off w buffalo wings. not your fried type - seems baked. fell off the bone. nice, unique buffalo flavor. very enjoyable.

had their blackberry lemonade (alcoholic) and a fruit drink w pineapple & cranberry (non-alcoholic, courtesy of our terrific waitress). very refreshing. definitely didn't skimmed out on the liquor.

for entrees, we had the pennsport burger: burger w arugula, vinaigrette tomatoes, basil aioli, and caramelized onions. chose tater tots for the side...& braised short rib w asparagus and bow-tie pasta mac & cheese. both meal were absolutely delicious! burger was cooked perfectly and paired well w all the trimmings. short rib was super tender while swirling around the pastas in the meat sauce.

too full for dessert. would love to come back to try their other dishes. highly recommended!

text.text:
I am impressed and I shall return! They have something that is hard to find these days - a classic burger! If a person wants one with cheese, they just need to order the The Pennsport Burger. This makes it fair for us lactose intolerant people, because we are not having to pay $16 for a burger that has cheese we cannot eat. Instead, we order a classic burger for $13 and it is quite good!
Most places in philly have tried to get me to pay for the burger with cheese price and they become angry when I say "No thank you, I will not pay for cheese that I'm not going to eat, so I will refrain from ordering". Then I walk out.

Some of them offer to refrain from adding the cheese, but they still want me to pay then for the cheese. outrageous.
Anyhow, Moonshine has a new fan because they are not unethical.
Oh, and their drinks selection is good, and the service is fantastic.

text.text:
Went here last night to take out burritos with my queen. Lemme tell yall. These were the worst, driest bloodclat burritos I’ve ever had. I got the chicken one and the chicken was so dry. And it’s not because I don’t do dairy so much, the burritos aren’t dry at the spots I normally go to. Shout out to Taco-Taco Mexican. My lady said the meat in her burrito just wasn’t good. I ended up pulling off so much of the tortilla that seemed so excessive, huge. Then I just abandoned the wrap all together and decided to have it from a bowl at home. I couldn’t even do it. I ended up eating the rice and threw out the bomboclat dry chicken.

It was just a little before 11pm, there was no one in there, no one picking up food, and it took us 30 minutes to get our food.

And lastly, the prices for this food is at gouging standards at best. Especially when there’re so many other similar places south Philly who offer the same thing. $15 for a chicken burrito with no cheese. While the spot across the street offers the same thing for $9.  I wouldn’t have minded the high price if the food was good. Very disappointing. And they shouldn’t be using Frieda’s name, image, artistic anything to push this terrible food. Use dark chicken meat if that’s how dry your food is going to be bro.

I should’ve known something was off when I saw more people coming out of the spot across the street with food. We tried them first but they said they were closed and we settled for this terrible, over priced food instead. I don’t recommend, and I hope they see this and go try their own food again to see what I’m talking about. The ingredients they use just don’t seem to be good. I want every business to do well, and I want every business to provide good service and products. I hope they do better than what we experienced. Call me, the quality connoisseur, if yall need to conduct an overhaul of yall food operation. They have to make most of their money from liquor sales here🤷🏾‍♂️. Because the food we had was 👎🏾👎🏾.

text.text:
I have always had wonderful experiences at Miller's Ale House, and Roger, our server, truly enhanced this visit. He was exceptional, demonstrating great attentiveness by continuously refilling our drinks, checking in on us, and promptly removing empty plates. We had come to the restaurant to watch the Eagles game, and I was pleasantly surprised by the lively crowd and the multitude of TVs that allowed us to catch all the action from any part of the restaurant or bar.

As a vegan, I was on the lookout for suitable menu options. Unfortunately, there was only one item available, the vegetable burger, which needed some adjustments to fit my dietary preferences. While I have enjoyed the vegetable burger before, I decided I wanted something heartier for the game. The Tex-Mex nachos with chicken caught my eye, but I had to make some modifications. I opted to remove the chicken and cheese, and instead had guacamole, pico de gallo, black bean and corn salsa on the side, topped with jalapeños, and it was absolutely delicious.

In contrast, my friend, who wasn't as hungry, decided to order a simple soup. She chose the classic French onion soup, along with a cup of hot tea, and found it to be delightful. Hopefully, in the future, Miller's Ale House will consider adding more vegetarian or vegan options to their menu. With the array of ingredients they have available, it shouldn't be too difficult to introduce a few new dishes.

Barcelona always seems to be the place to be, no matter what day of the week it is. The atmosphere is lively, and there's a fun energy even on a Tuesday night when the rest of Philly is closed. The spacious patio is also a great bonus when the weather cooperates.
The food is solid, the service is consistently on point, and it's a great spot for a group. With so many tapas to choose from, it's easy to order a little bit of everything and share. The warm bread with olive oil is the perfect way to kick off the meal and sets the tone for everything that follows.
One thing I really appreciated was how seriously they took my food allergy. As soon as I mentioned it, the staff went above and beyond to explain what was safe for me to eat, which made the experience much more enjoyable.
I will say my first visit about a year ago wasn't the best, and it kept me away for a while. I'll spare you the details. Let's just say someone in our party found an unexpected "extra" in their food. Thankfully, this was my first visit back since then, and everything went much more smoothly. I'm glad I decided to give them another chance, and I'll definitely be back.

text.text:
From the moment I arrived, I had an exceptional dining experience. Since it was my first time dining here—and my first time enjoying a meal out on my own—I immediately felt welcomed and comfortable.

My server, Nate, was incredibly welcoming, attentive, and accommodating throughout the entire evening. He recommended several excellent menu items and also let me know about the half-off wine bottle special, which made the experience even better. He was professional, friendly, and consistently checked in to make sure I had everything I needed without ever being intrusive. His positive attitude and attention to detail truly made my visit memorable.

I also want to recognize Mike, the manager, who came over to introduce himself and took the time to answer my questions and offer thoughtful recommendations about the menu. His genuine hospitality and willingness to ensure I had a great experience spoke volumes about the restaurant’s commitment to outstanding customer service.

The food was absolutely delicious, and I thoroughly enjoyed experiencing the restaurant’s cultural cuisine. Combined with the warm hospitality from both Nate and Mike, the entire evening exceeded my expectations.

I highly recommend dining here and, if you have the opportunity, requesting Nate as your server. You won’t be disappointed. Both Nate and Mike provided exceptional service that made my first solo dining experience feel welcoming, enjoyable, and memorable. I look forward to returning and will definitely be requesting Nate again on my next visit!

text.text:
We have been to Noir numerous times over the years, with large parties of up eleven and smaller parties of four.  Overall, our experiences have been good, with good service and food and atmosphere, and we enjoyed the place  Our last visit for dinner, a party of five to celebrate a birthday, was not one of those times.
The service was horrible, with it seeming that the server was more interested in chatting it up with a group at the bar than ensuring that our food and drinks were moving.  It took a long time for food to be brought out.  Someone from our table literally had to get up from the table on more than one occasion to get the server to refresh our drinks.  One of the meals we ordered was very substandard; the food, a pasta dish, seemed overcooked and was not edible by one of our party-only about 4 or 5 pieces were even attempted to be consumed.  In such circumstances, it is not unusual, and has been my experience, that the restaurant offers to take the item off the bill or offers to bring something else...that did not happen here.  When we were finished dinner and had birthday cake, the check was finally brought over (after what seemed like a while and after we again had to find the server to bring it). The item was still on the bill.  When the issue about the returned food was raised, and after another delay, the server came back and said they would only credit a portion of the cost for the item.  Needless to say, after many visits to Noir over the last four to five years, this will most likely be our last.

Luk Fu at Live Casino Hotel offers a cozy dining spot with a nice, dimly lit atmosphere that's perfect for a relaxed meal. The beef bulgogi stands out as the highlight, flavorful, and especially delicious with the onions, while the Chinese pepper steak is solid but doesn't top it.
They also serve the best hot and sour soup with perfectly balanced taste, and though the kimchi was a bit too sour for my liking, servers were quick and attentive throughout. Overall, it's a great choice for Korean flavors in a casino setting, earning 4.5 stars for the bulgogi and soup alone.

Chicken tasted like fish oil.

When was the last time the fryers cleaned? We don’t know.

My husband and I ordered the 5 piece chicken fingers, but the moment we bit into them, they tasted overwhelmingly like fish. Not slightly fishy…completely fishy. It was obvious that something was wrong, whether it was filthy fryer oil, poor food handling practices, or cross-contamination from cooking fish and chicken together. The taste was absolutely disgusting.

To make sure it wasn’t just one bad piece, we each tried a single chicken finger. After realizing the entire order tasted the same, we brought it back to the counter and explained the problem. Instead of addressing the issue, the manager refused to issue a refund because we had already tasted some of it.

Apparently customers are expected to discover food quality problems through telepathy rather than by taking a bite.

The food was inedible, the customer service was terrible, and the manager showed no interest in making things right. He then sent an elderly employee to the window to give us a phone number handwritten on paper of the real manager or franchise owner, we don’t know who it was- it wasn’t even a business card.

We spent $30 on a food and he acted like we only bought one item.

If you’re from out of town, do not waste your time here. Lots of other places to be a patron. Go across the street to the cheesesteak place instead.

This is a favorite spot - hopefully, next time will be better.

We dined at the Oregon Diner last night after the Savannah Bananas baseball game, and I have to say, the service was impressive. The staff was not only friendly but also attentive. The portion sizes? Enormous! They certainly know how to serve up generous helpings at the Oregon Diner.

I ordered the Pepper Jake burger, and it delivered; it was quite good. My wife, on the other hand, chose the chicken croquettes, which fell short of expectations due to an off-putting floral taste. These were far from the traditional chicken croquettes one would anticipate.

My oldest daughter opted for "dippy" eggs, specifically requesting them over light. Unfortunately, when they arrived, they were fried hard—definitely not what she expected. The rest of her meal was acceptable, though. My youngest daughter ordered spaghetti and meatballs and had a great experience with that dish.

Overall, I would classify it as a typical diner experience—three stars. The staff was commendable, the portions were generous, and the food was adequate. While it wasn't anything extraordinary, I would not hesitate to return.

Jackie delivered great service to our family last night. We arrived about 9p and were greeted and seated immediately. The booth was comfortable and the seating firm. We ordered the Tuna Salad Platter and Ravioli with Meatballs to share. We also ordered the Lima Bean and Italian Chicken soups- both were hot and tasty.

The portions were hefty and the prices were reasonable. Our daughter could not resist visiting the dessert counter and Jackie gladly packed us a slice of Strawberry Cream Cake to-go. The cake was light and had nice fresh strawberries throughout.

Altogether our experience was great and we will definitely consider returning to Oregon Diner in the future! Thank you!!

text.text: Ventured into Stargazy on a rainy Saturday afternoon for a cozy takeout experience. Opting not to dine in due to the quaint size of the space, we were nonetheless charmed by its inviting ambiance and the unique selection of pantry items available for purchase. Our order included a hearty Shepherd’s Pie, a flavorsome Cheese and Onion Pasty, a rich Lamb Lancashire Hotpot, and a savory Beef & Onion Pie accompanied by Mash & Parsley Liquor. Each dish was a testament to traditional flavors, with the pastries particularly standing out - a true highlight for anyone with a penchant for baked delights. Despite the limited space, Stargazy offers a heartwarming glimpse into classic cuisine, making every bite worth the visit. Perfect for those seeking authentic, delicious meals on the go. Highly recommend for a taste of comfort, especially on a chilly day!

text.text:
Underwhelming experience overall. The bread service started things off with a focaccia that had nice flavor from black pepper and sesame, but the texture was off and there was too much crust for the amount of crumb. The second bread was dense and kind of wet.

Corn souffle had good corn flavor but came out dense, more like a crustless quiche than a souffle. The salad alongside it was fresh.

The sausage was good; flavorful and cooked well, though the lentils under it were pretty boring.

Spaghetti with lamb ragu was a touch undercooked, probably needed another 5-10 seconds in the water. The sauce didn't leave much of an impression.

The pork ragu was a real letdown. The pasta itself was done well, but the dish had no pork flavor at all and was underseasoned. The pork tasted like it had been boiled plain and then added at the end.

We opted to skip dessert after all that.

text.text:
A Michelin recommended restaurant that lived up to its name! So happy we took the chance to walk in Monday night to River Twice! It was the best dinner I've had in Philly in awhile!
Started off sooo strong with the oysters! I could've eaten dozens of them by myself! Never would've though green strawberry on oyster would be a bit but here we are.

The soft shelled crab came highly recommended and though we were a bit worried about the size, it was phenomenal!  The char and sauce really came together so well.

Before our next dish came out, we were concerned we'd need to order more food.

Then the halibut collar came out and squashed that thought. It was such a great meaty white fish that paired so nicely with the sauce.

Last came The Mother Rucker: this meaty burger was named as one of America's Top 10 Burgers by Infatuation and rightly so! What a great way to end our meal, and for the record, we were quite full!
(Only served on
Monday nights.)

Be careful though bc they add 20% service fee already into your bill and if you’re not paying attention, you’ll double tip them like I did 🥴 My fault for not looking over the bill more carefully.

text.text:
it’s a small, cozy open-kitchen restaurant with a warm atmosphere — but unfortunately the food and service fell far short of expectations. Overall, the seasoning was overwhelmingly salty, which made it hard to appreciate the actual flavors or character of the ingredients. Each course felt unbalanced, and even the rice grits were inconsistently cooked, with some parts almost like raw rice.

The halibut dish was especially surprising: the cabbage served with it tasted like pure salt, while the halibut itself had almost no seasoning at all. Half of it was warm and the other half was completely cold, which was really unexpected.

Only chopsticks were set on the table, and no one explained that other utensils were stored in a drawer — we only realized after watching another table take theirs out. For a restaurant with so many positive reviews, the service felt unprofessional and careless. Even though I had stated the reason for our reservation, the staff randomly asked whose birthday it was, which felt awkward and out of place.

The highlight of the night was actually the bill — a receipt that already included a 20% service charge, yet still had the extra tip line marked and emphasized as if we were expected to add more. I couldn’t help but wonder when it became normal for restaurants to openly push for additional tipping on top of an already-included charge. It just felt unnecessary and uncomfortable, especially after such a disappointing meal and experience.

To top it all off, both of us experienced stomach discomfort and diarrhea later that night after the meal. Overall, it was a disappointing experience on what was supposed to be a special occasion.

text.text:

The fries were a bit overwhelming with the over seasoned taste, felt like my mouth was being burnt alive. The cheese dip was the only thing keeping me from giving up on the fries, and it made the fries actually taste really good. I know some people who might like the overwhelming taste, but I am not one of those people.

Service:

The line was longer than Godzilla’s tail but the service was so good, we didn’t even have to wait 10 minutes!(probably because there are only 2 food items on the menu) and the sheer amount of smells in the air makes it impossible to resist buying a bucket.

Atmosphere:

It’s in a Phillies stadium. If that’s not enough, what is?

I chose this restaurant to celebrate my birthday with my husband. We ordered six dishes from the menu, along with a bottle of wine and two additional glasses of a different wine, and our total came to $250+ plus tip.

We truly enjoyed the food — everything was delicious and beautifully presented, and the service was excellent. However, the restaurant did not offer any small birthday gesture or complimentary treat. Of course, this is not an obligation, but it would have been a thoughtful touch for a place of this level.

Out of everything we ordered, the fish stood out as the best dish, in both my opinion and my husband’s. We also really loved the mushrooms and would definitely recommend trying them.

One small note: the music felt slightly louder than we would have preferred, which made the overall atmosphere a bit noisy. As a result, we sometimes found it a little difficult to hear each other, even though we were seated at a table for two.

Overall, I would definitely recommend this place to my friends.

There were mixed reviews about this place but we still wanted to give it a try as reviews are always so subjective.

The “small plates” are not small for fine dining standards. I feel like the reviews that said the portions were small for the price they are paying are expecting Olive Garden portions knowing they are at a tapas fine dining establishment.

The dishes are supposed to be shared tapas style, so don’t expect to just order one dish as an entree. Order several dishes for the table and try a bit of everything. My favorite are the fried cheese, crispy potatoes, and steak. I think the eggplant was done really well too.

We dined indoor and there was a nice breeze from the large open windows. Loved that they noticed I was pregnant and offered pregnant friendly drink options and they even popped a candle on our dessert. It was a lovely last dinner date before the baby arrived.

I visited Prime Rib at the casino to celebrate my birthday, and this visit was especially meaningful because I had been invited back after my first experience didn’t go so well.  I’m happy to say this time was completely different in the best way.

Larry, the manager, was incredibly kind and attentive from the moment we arrived.  Our waitress, Bre, was just as accommodating. We were initially seated at a four-top table in the middle, but it was a bit hard to hear each other.  When we asked to move closer to the wall, she didn’t hesitate at all and made the switch quickly, which made a big difference in our comfort.

We started with a Caesar salad, and Bre suggested splitting it since it’s large something I’ve honestly never had a restaurant offer before.  It worked out perfectly, especially since I don’t eat much, and it was a thoughtful touch.

I went in for brunch on a Saturday. Whilst enjoying my meal, a Hispanic family of 6ppl walked in, stood around for about 2 mins; was not approached by any staff. The hostess was not at the stand. When they did return she IGNORED THEM. It was so blatant. She then pulled out her phone  and was scrolling God knows what.

The family walked out. I was fuming inside. This is gentrification to the nth degree. You’re serving Mexican food at a high level that is transmitted in a way that screams it only matters to get the accolades of those have held the privelege to give out them out, ahem, Bib Gourmand.

It really colored my experience for the worse.

My waiter was very sweet and pleasant. Get the choripapas, que rico! The ceviche was tasty, but the cut of salmon was very cheap and looked to have been frozen/defrosted 2x as the flesh was not plump, nor firm. Not worth $26.

As a brown person, I’m really embarrassed for the subvert culture of exclusion that El Chingon allows. After the family left, I looked around and only myself and the staff had all the melanin, iykwim.

text.text:
This spot strikes you right away with its modern vibe, and cool art  which lines the walls, blending Asian and Italian influences in a way that feels both unique and intentional.

We kicked things off with the fried pork pot stickers, and they were outstanding. Crispy on the outside, flavorful and juicy inside, and a perfect start to the meal.

I went with the Wagyu burger, which was next-level. It featured two perfectly cooked smash patties topped with fontina, all brought together by a rich, truffled mushroom gravy with a long hot on iop . The togarashi fries on the side—reminiscent of sweet potato fries added a great balance of sweetness and spice.

My wife ordered the Italian curry, and it was truly something special. Made with Italian sofrito, blood orange, coconut milk, and tomato chutney over rice, it perfectly captured the Asian-Italian fusion concept and absolutely delivered on flavor.

My brother had the Korean BBQ brisket, and it looked incredible. He said it was some of the most tender brisket he’s ever had, coated in crushed garlic and packed with bold, savory flavor.

All around, a creative and delicious experience that really stands out.

A very nice fusion restaurant between Asian (Korean) and Italian.

The combination of the food worked really well.

The drinks were also pretty good. Would recommend the Hentai Punch.

Unfortunately there was only one waitress serving the entire place, but she was very lovely and accommodating. Due to that the service was a bit slow, but nothing too bad.

I had the Korean BBQ briskets. They were very juicy and tender and went well with the rice. And the quantity was also pretty good for the price. Just wish there some picked onions or something similar to cut the sweetness so that I could enjoy it a bit more.

They offered free homemade limencello shots along with the check which was a nice surprise.

The ambience and music was also pretty good (they switched between Italian and Asian inspired music).

All in all it was a great experience. Would definitely recommend for a visit.

Overall I think coming here for a date, birthday or nice dinner is a wonderful experience and I hope that the staff get the appreciation they deserve.

The Bok building is a magical place, but go to the roof and eat at Irwins. The food, drink, and service was outstanding. The outdoor rooftop seating has a beautiful view of south Philly. Our reservation was outside. During our experience it did rain a bit, but it was worth staying. Our server was a trooper for keeping the patio goin. At night during a Phils/Eagles game you can hear the crowd roar. Electric.

The food and drink was great. There are Mezze, Pasta, Main Entree and Dessert options. I assume the menu is seasonal based on the ingredients, but I am unsure. There is a cocktail menu, wine offerings and full bar. I didnt have time to even take pictures of all the food and cocktails we were enjoying it soo much. We ordered about half the menu and will be returning to order the remaining items.

Dessert is worth it's own mention. At a lot of places, dessert is kinda a throwaway/pass. Not at Irwins. I told my wife we will also be coming back to Irwins solely for drinks and desserts next time we are eating somewhere else close by. We got the Milk and Honey Pistachio Gelato and an Almond Torta Cake that should be nominated for some kind of award.

I would recommend making a reservation. If the weather is nice, eat outside. Tell your spouse you are taking them to a Sicily Roof Jawn for dinner.

FYI, this was the original Tony Luke’s and it’s still owned by the same family.  They just changed the name because of family drama.

We arrived around 8:00 PM and ordered three dishes: Bánh Bèo Chén, Bún Đậu Mắm Tôm, and Lẩu Gà Lá Giang. The hostess was very friendly and welcoming, and we just had to wait a few minutes for a table to be cleaned.
The food itself was decent, but the service really affected our experience. The first dish arrived about 15 minutes after ordering, but the second didn't come until around 45 minutes later. We honestly don't mind waiting when the restaurant was busy, but no one ever informed us there would be a delay. A simple update would have made a big difference.
The last dish arrived only after we had finished the second one. Since the restaurant closes at 10 PM, we had only about 15 minutes left to eat our hot pot, so we rushed to finish. After that, we waited for a to-go box and our check, but it felt like we were being ignored. No one checked on us or acknowledged that we were ready to leave.
So, don't expect to have a dedicated server taking care of your table. The food was fine, but the lack of communication and attention made the overall dining experience disappointing.

text.text:
We had such amazing authentic Vietnamese food from Gabriella’s Vietnam. Starting with the location, it is a considerably spacious restaurant on Passyunk that can accommodate for up to groups of 7-8, but mostly people come here as couples. I would recommend coming in a bigger group setting as a lot of dishes are meant to be shared. These are what we ordered:
1. Appetizer - calamari, 4/5. Amazing with the chilis and shallots, giving it a sense of Vietnamese street flare and flavor bomb. I’d like the calamari to be more crispier.
2. Appetizer - banh xeo, 4.5/5. These are made to be smaller than the typical ones you find elsewhere, but great for sharing. Its crispy exterior was a nice contrast with its gooey pork, shrimp and bean sprouts filling. Only thing I’d wish for is for its coconut flavor to stand out more.
3. Appetizer - coconut cake, 3/5. Compared to banh xeo, this wasn’t much of a surprise factor.
4. Appetizer - prawn and mango salad, 5/5. This was the favorite of the table. The shrimps were grilled to perfection, not overcooked and very flavorful. They are such a good match with slightly unripe mangoes, chili and shallots!
5. Main - Grilled catfish 5/5 - very well cooked, not fishy. Eaten perfectly in a combined bite with rice crackers, fermented shrimp sauce, vermicelli noodles, lettuce, cucumbers.
6. Main - Shaken beef, 5/5. Another popular dish on the table. Very juicy and tender beef that absorbs all the umami flavor of the sauce.
7. Main - chicken hotpot, 5/5. Definitely an acquired taste for those who are not used to a sour spicy soup. Which I ended up really enjoying!
8. Main - egg fried rice, 5/5. Very flavorful fried rice cooked with Chinese sausages.
9. Side - sweet and sour Brussels sprouts, 5/5. Decently cooked Brussels sprouts that turned my husband into liking the dish for the first time.

We would definitely return and try more dishes!

I want to provide an honest and transparent review of my experience at Asian Fusion. I was initially drawn to this place due to another reviewer's praise for the General Tso's chicken. After two visits and three meals, I must say that the General Tso's chicken was a 6/10 (not pictured), and my overall rating for Asian Fusion is a 3/10. It might have been even lower if it weren't for the surprisingly delightful sauce accompanying the beef and broccoli. Despite the commendable sauce, my experience left much to be desired.

To begin, the food was severely undercooked. The chicken wings had an overly soft exterior, the French fries were disappointingly soggy, and the rice was mushy and watery. This level of undercooking was unprecedented for me. I had to use an air fryer for an additional 3 minutes to ensure the chicken wings were properly cooked (as pictured). Furthermore, the staff's practice of keeping the door open led to an influx of flies, which, while not uncommon in Chinese restaurants, was noticeable.

Even after using the air fryer to salvage the undercooked items and mixing the beef and broccoli with the rice, the meal still only reached an average standard at best. Given the numerous dining options available in the neighborhood, I find it hard to recommend this restaurant.

text.text: I drove almost 3000 miles last month for work. I go all throughout New England, New York and New Jersey. I typically try to find pho for dinner because it is healthier than fast food when I’m on the road. Let me tell you, Pho Duyên is the best Vietnamese restaurant I’ve been to in a long time. The authenticity is off the charts. At other places, you get wilting produce, brown mung beans and sad jalapeños. Here, the produce was fresh, the ingredients authentic, and they served a Birds Eye chili instead of jalapeños. The hot chili oil was insanely good. In addition to pho, I got the #8 special rice. It had an interesting accoutrement I had never had before… Tàu Hũ Ky, or meat paste in tofu skin, pan fried. It sounds weird, for sure, but it was AMAZING. I would have gotten an appetizer just of that if it was an option. The glaze and sear on the pork chop were perfect. The pho broth was clear and flavorful. I highly recommend Pho Duyên. I don’t live anywhere close, but I will definitely be back!

text.text:
Ristorante Pesto is truly one of Philadelphia’s hidden gems. This family-owned Italian restaurant has been operating for over 30 years, and you can absolutely feel the pride and tradition the moment you walk in. The atmosphere is warm, welcoming, and authentic — exactly what you hope for in a classic Italian spot.

The lobster ravioli was incredible — perfectly cooked, rich, and full of flavor. It was easily one of the best pasta dishes I’ve had in Philly. My friends loved their meals as well, and everything that came out of the kitchen looked amazing.

They’re BYOB, which is always a plus, but they also offer reasonably priced bottles of wine if you prefer to purchase there — such a nice option to have.

A special shoutout to Gianna, who was super attentive and took the time to explain everything on the menu. Her recommendations and knowledge made the whole experience even better.

If you’re looking for authentic Italian food with outstanding service, Ristorante Pesto is a must-visit. Can’t wait to go back! 🇮🇹

text.text:
Went to Mr. Martino's Trattoria in East Passyunk and came away really impressed. This is one of those hidden gems that feels like you've stumbled upon a family restaurant somewhere in Italy rather than a busy Philadelphia neighborhood. It's BYOB, reservations are pretty much a must, and if you're looking for a relaxed meal with homemade food, this place delivers.
One thing to know going in: service is intentionally slower than your average restaurant. We were told right away that much of the cooking is handled by a single chef (Maria), and honestly, once the food starts coming out, it makes complete sense. Everything feels homemade and prepared with care rather than rushed out of a kitchen.
Mr. Martino's has built a loyal following over the years because of that old-school approach. The restaurant has become somewhat of a neighborhood secret among locals who appreciate traditional Italian cooking, generous portions, and prices that are hard to find anymore, especially in one of Philly's most popular dining neighborhoods.
For appetizers, we ordered the White Bean Soup, Red Peppers, and the Baked Ricotta with dried Italian sausage and olives. Everything was excellent and had that homemade European-style comfort food feel. Nothing felt overly complicated- just quality ingredients prepared well.
For dinner, I got the Polenta with sausage, which was outstanding. We also ordered the Spinach Ravioli with tomato sauce, and that was equally good. The portions were generous, and every dish felt like something you'd get at a family dinner rather than a restaurant trying to be trendy.
The staff deserves a shoutout as well. Everyone was incredibly friendly, welcoming, and knowledgeable about the menu. You could tell they genuinely cared about making sure guests enjoyed their experience.
And whatever you do, save room for dessert. We ordered the Tiramisu and the Rice Custard Cake, and both were phenomenal. Honestly, they were far better than "good"- they were some of the best desserts I've had in a long time and ended up being one of the highlights of the meal.
Overall, Mr. Martino's is one of those sleeper spots that deserves more attention. Great homemade food, friendly staff, unbeatable value, and a cozy BYOB atmosphere make it a place I'd absolutely return to. Just remember to make a reservation, bring your favorite bottle of wine, and don't rush the experience. It's worth slowing down and enjoying it.

text.text:
I must say that we are fortunate to have a remarkable diversity of restaurants in our City. Recently, a friend of mine extended an invitation to explore a particular establishment that I have passed by numerous times, under the impression that it was just another generic spot. You know how it goes—sometimes you drive past a place and think it holds no allure, only to discover later that it is, in fact, a hidden gem. Well, I was entirely wrong in my previous assumptions.

It turned out to be an absolutely delightful little eatery, managed by a family, which instantly added to its charm. Having indulged in more than 20 Vietnamese restaurants over the past year, I can assert with confidence that this establishment serves the best pho I have ever tasted. I opted for a vegan pho, which featured tofu and gently fried mushrooms. This dish was accompanied by a fantastic variety of mixed vegetables, including broccoli, cauliflower, zucchini, carrots, and naturally, the aromatic mushrooms, all swimming in a delicious vegetable broth and served with noodles. The photographs I took will clearly illustrate the vibrancy of the meal.

My partner chose to order the pork pho, which, while similar to mine, included meat and vegetables, and she also could not resist trying a shrimp toast. She was absolutely thrilled with it, declaring it to be phenomenal. This restaurant is one that I could easily frequent, primarily due to its charm and the soothing ambiance that echoes the essence of Saigon.

Additionally, there is outdoor seating, which I am eagerly looking forward to experiencing once the weather warms up a bit. The family that operates this establishment is genuinely wonderful; their service is impeccable, and they are all truly kind-hearted individuals. Without hesitation, I would rate this place five stars for its food, service, and atmosphere.

As for parking, it was incredibly convenient—we managed to find a spot directly out front without any cost. What a delightful perk that was! I am already excited about my next visit here. I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant to anyone seeking exceptional food, whether traditional or nontraditional. The menu was so extensive that I consolidated it into a couple little videos. It was just too big to list.

The food, Irish pub atmosphere, and music selection were on point and the bartenders were very accommodating. We did have a slight hick up that I wouldn't hold against the business but as a business owner myself I'll share as I know I'd like to know when and where to fix things. But keep up the business, your bartenders spoke very highly of you as a boss and even told us an amazing story of your friends who frequent the establishment! If I ever come to Philly again or anyone I know, I'll definitely recommend or stop in again!

text.text:
Had an amazing meal at Virasat Haveli on Market Street and this place is seriously a gem in West Philly. The vibe is super cozy with colorful umbrellas hanging from the ceiling and rainbow-striped walls that make you feel like you're at the world's best-smelling party. Their menu is packed with everything from crispy dosas to chicken biryani, plus tons of Indo-Chinese options like chili paneer and hakka noodles.

The portions are huge and the prices won't break the bank, which is always a win. I loved how flavorful everything was – the spices hit just right without being overwhelming. The staff was really attentive and even asked about our spice preferences before we ordered. Whether you're vegetarian or craving some meat dishes, they've got you covered with their extensive menu. Definitely my new go-to spot for Indian food in Philly!

text.text: My husband and I were in the mood to try out a new place so we called this place up to order something to eat. The person who took our order asked for my Credit/ Debit card information which included the number of the card; The CVT number on the back of the card and the Zip Code of where the card was issued. I gave my bank card information. Exactly two days later my bank's Fraud Detection Center notified me of someone using my bank card information. The representative informed me someone made an small purchase to see if the card was activated when they knew the card was activated they attempted to make another purchase for $26.85 at an Polvens online store for animal accessories based in Texas! Never been.They flagged the purchase as suspicious and temporary deactivated my bank card. I called Evans to speak to an manager or possibly the owner. An employee named Tanya answered and was really professional, polite and understanding. She informed me to call back at 7pm the manager will be in by then. I called back at 7:00pm and an guy with a very thick and heavy accent answered the phone. I had no idea he would be so icy cold and unsympathetic. I informed him of how I gave my bank card information to an employee over the phone when I ordered there just a couple days prior. I also informed him of the order and date and time of my order. He  cut me off in mid sentence and never stated he would due his due diligence to investigate. He just kept repeating "Call your bank-Call your bank" He had a very cynicism attitude toward me and refused to let me speak with the manager. He also, threatened to hang up on me. All I wanted to accomplish by informing him is that this was a very unfortunate thing that happened to me and maybe he can try to get to the bottom of it. Instead, he was extremely condescending and rude toward me and could really care less. I did call the police and took a report. I'm disappointed because I really had high hopes for this place. The driver was really nice.  It's reasonable to say they lost a customer.

I will only recommend the Mexican Fries here, but even now I’m hesitant to do so. The food is solid, but their prices are hard to justify. Especially because they keep shrinking the portions too.

They have been continuing to shrink their portions, while increasing their prices (look at this burrito I paid nearly $18 for). They’re also taking away ingredients that used to be free, like the pickled jalapeños on the Mexican Fries

The icing on the cake is their rehaul of the rewards system. After spending an already high threshold (I can’t remember exactly), they used to reward you with a free meal. Now, they took that away and only give a $3 discount, without moving the threshold at all. I have no idea how you can treat a $3 discount the same as a free meal.

Update: they did remove the free meal reward and replaced it with a discount. I remember it being $3, definitely no more than $5

None of the food came out together and some of it never came out. We were there for over an hour. We had to ask numerous times for things we ordered that never came and she couldn’t keep track of anything. Multiple guests orders were wrong when they finally came out, including mine. Even our bills were messed up and nothing was rectified. We just paid and left once we were finally able to get our checks. Yikes.

The ceiling next to the bar is leaking and the women’s bathroom was very unclean. The soap dispenser was empty and there was a broken soap pump on the sink. The paper towels were also empty. I get it’s the end of the day but YUCK! People eat here. We need to wash hands. What about your staff??!!

As a retired kitchen manager and chef this place gave me anxiety. It definitely needs some work.

text.text:
I was very disappointed with the chicken at this place.

I ordered wings and drumsticks, as well as the chicken sandwich.

The chicken tasted as if it was boiled rather than fried. And the meat was tough because it was overcooked. I have never had fried chicken that tasted like boiled chicken, whether it be Korean fried chicken or regular American fried chicken. The wings were a little better. I genuinely am curious how they cook the chicken. I felt like they boiled the meat first and then covered it with bread crumbs and then fried it. So very disappointing.

The only redeeming feature about their chicken was the breading. It was very crispy, and the sauce was okay. But again, the meat was bad.

I don't know if all Bonchon chicken is like this, but I cannot recommend this place.

I came across Royal Pizza while visiting a friend and crazing something simple. There are a few pizza options in the area, but something drew me into wanting to give them a try.

I ordered through the Slice app for convenience and got 3 items.
My order was made correctly to order.

The first item I chose was a small meat lovers pizza w/ extra cheese. This was made perfectly. The pizza was flavorful and filling. It even kept it's flavor after upon reheating it for leftovers, which shows using more quality ingredients.

My second item was a plain cheesesteak with american cheese. This did not stand out too much and left me desiring more out of it. It could've used more meat and cheese, but I know that there is an extra meat option through the app that I didn't choose.

Lastly, I got the cheese fries with whiz. This is a classic and exactly what I was looking for.

This is a go to over all the other local shops when I'm in the area.

Best service I’ve seen in a restaurant in years. There weren’t any virgin cocktails on the menu so the bar tender (owner?) whipped something up that suited my taste perfectly. Honestly made my day. There was a bit of a wait for the table but the bar window seating was worth it for the impeccable ambiance. The music wasn’t too loud either.

Got the pumpkin Mac. Super cheesy and creamy. The ideal comfort food. The community pie had the perfect crust - chewy but not too crunchy. The toppings were fun and flavorful.

Staff is just genuinely happy. Just comfortable and cozy and everything you want in a local spot. A lot of love has been put into this place and you can tell. Can’t wait to come back.

Food
We sampled Sal’s Famous pie, Clarkville Hot Chicken, a vegetarian pasta, and a charcuterie appetizer. Each dish was bursting with flavor and a true delight. These are all items we would eagerly reorder on our next visit. We also enjoyed a selection of drinks, including a specialty draft beer, a bottled beer, and a few cocktails. The restaurant offered some outstanding low-sugar cocktail options, which we greatly appreciated.

Service
Our waitress was attentive and accommodating during our meal. She ensured our drinks were always filled and provided extra napkins, condiments, and take-out boxes without us having to ask.

Atmosphere
The dining area was small yet cozy and thoughtfully designed. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit and look forward to returning.

text.text:
This was our first visit to this establishment. The pizza selection is quite extensive, with many options available for vegans. The atmosphere is spacious and inviting. Although the space is not very large, it is well utilized. Our server, Haley, promptly greeted us upon arrival and provided linen napkins and silverware. She offered us drinks, including water with slices of lemon and lime. The drink menu includes a variety of options, from cocktails to wines.

After much deliberation, we decided to order the vegan white pie, which was topped with kale, shiitake mushrooms, onions, housemade tofu, ricotta cheese, and vegan mozzarella. The pie arrived within 12 to 15 minutes of placing our order. The thin, crusty crust was generously topped with cheese, mushrooms, and kale. While we found the pizza to be delicious, we felt that it could benefit from a touch more seasoning. We also ordered a side of hot honey, buffalo sauce, and garlic for added flavor.

The medium-sized pie proved to be quite satisfying for the two of us, with a diameter of approximately 12 inches. Despite feeling full, we couldn't resist ordering a dessert. To our surprise, they offered vegan options, including freshly made donut holes made from pizza dough and sprinkled with cinnamon sugar. These treats were served with a delightful caramel dipping sauce.

The ambience of the restaurant was delightful, with light and relaxing music playing in the background. The service provided by Haley was very good, and we look forward to returning to sample more of their menu offerings.

text.text: Best pizza spot in west philly! We LOVE the pizza here and also the trivia night on Monday is so fun. Their quizzo format is great with a variety of categories, a music round, and a great host.  I die for the Honey Pie and the Moussaka - we usually go back and forth between those and they're both so good. We switched it up last time and got the Peppe le Bleu and that was great too.   The pizza is good because it's got an amazing crust, and they do an amazing job of cheese to sauce to ingredients ratio. It always comes out melt in your mouth hot with the best texture.   If you're not feeling pizza, the meatballs are good, too.  The service both at the bar and at the tables is always prompt and friendly. Definitely my choice pizza spot in this part of town.

This is such a unique, wonderful restaurant, especially this location of their's set in converted Victorian brownstones. The food is so fresh and high quality. I LOVE the burger, its always cooked perfectly, juicy and comes with a great house-made aioli. Their fries are also fantastic.

You can't go wrong with most menu items though. At this and various other locations of theirs, I have had wonderful southern style brunch, roasted chicken, and great desserts. The single, only item I didn't care for was the salmon.

text.text:
We visited Sang Kee Noodle House for a birthday dinner and left feeling underwhelmed. It doesn’t measure up to Sang Kee Peking Duck House in Chinatown. The food here is just average, portions are smaller, and the prices are slightly higher. Service was lackluster. The only real advantage is that the location offers easier parking.

Overall Ratings:

Restaurant: 3/5
Service: 2/5
Food: 3/5
Parking: Street Parking (more convenient than Chinatown)

Atmosphere:

I liked the decor—clean, open, and modern—but the menu is quite limited. Unlike the Chinatown location, there’s no Peking duck on display, and the variety just isn't there.

Service:

Nothing notable. We ordered, they brought the food. The staff didn’t seem particularly attentive or engaged. Overall, the experience felt pretty forgettable.

What We Ordered:

-House Special Noodle: Just okay. The flavor was weak and didn’t stand out.
-Braised Beef Flank Noodle: Also just okay. The broth lacked depth and had a strange aftertaste.

Neither noodle dish came with wontons—you have to pay extra for those, along with other typical add-ons. It felt like everything that would normally be included came with an extra charge.

Final Thoughts:

I probably wouldn’t come back. If I’m craving Sang Kee, I’ll stick to the Peking Duck House in Chinatown. Sure, parking there can be a hassle, but the food makes it absolutely worth it.

I've been wanting to go here for many years, so finally took the opportunity to do so last weekend for brunch with a friend. Because people are typically away at the shore for summer weekends, it was easy for us to book a quick reservation that morning.

The decor is cute, modern and clean with bright lighting throughout the space. Once I came in, I was immediately checked in and seated. All of the staff were  very friendly and polite. Our waiter (think his name was Logan) was also super personable, gave good energy when interacting with us and had a good balance of attentiveness & letting us enjoy our food/time.

We decided to order a few dishes to split and sample. Salmon Cake Eggs Benedict was unfortunately a let down for me - the salmon Cake seemed over cooked and tasted a bit plain/not seasoned. The Brioche French Toast with the peach bourbon cheesecake topping was amazing! That topping really added a good touch to the already well made french toast slices. And the side Biscuit and Gravy was shockingly good. We also had Rum Punch as our cocktail drink which was made very well.

Overall, we had a good dining experience. There are a few other brunch items I want to try out, so definitely hope to come back again soon.

text.text:
We booked a table for 10 to celebrate my son's graduation, and the experience was wonderful from start to finish. Graduation day is notoriously tough when it comes to getting reservations—most restaurants are fully booked—but this place was incredibly accommodating and made room for our group.

The staff was kind and welcoming, which made our celebration even more special. My personal favorites were the beet salad and the spinach and goat cheese salad—both were fresh and delicious. Everyone loved their entrees, and the pasta was cooked perfectly. The seafood fra diavolo usually comes with a spicy tomato sauce, but since my husband doesn’t eat spicy food, they were happy to adjust it for him.

My daughter couldn’t stop talking about the LaScala fries—they were a big hit!

We only wish we had discovered this gem sooner. My son has already graduated, but we’ll definitely be coming back for future celebrations!

The matcha pancakes also didn’t really work for me, although I’ve had other pancakes here that were much better.

text.text:
My wife and I visited CO-OP Restaurant & Bar at 20 S 33rd St in Philadelphia for Valentine’s Day, and the experience was excellent from start to finish.

The food was outstanding. The cast-iron skillet dish with roasted potatoes, fried eggs and fresh peppers was flavorful and  short ribs perfectly prepared. The scrambled eggs were light, fluffy, and seasoned just right. The turkey sausage was wonderful. We also ordered the pancakes, which were thick, soft, and served with a generous butter and syrup a perfect balance of sweetness without being overwhelming.

Beyond the food, the atmosphere made the experience even better. The setting felt warm, relaxed, and welcoming ideal for a date. It had an upscale feel without being pretentious. Service was attentive and professional.

CO-OP delivered on quality, presentation, and overall dining experience. If you’re looking for a great brunch spot in University City, this is definitely worth a visit. We’ll absolutely be returning.

Greek Lady is located just couple blocks away the main campus of the University of Pennsylvania in university city. They have absolutely great location and it’s very convenient for everyone.

Greek Lady is a hidden gem. I was there for dinner and surprisingly it wasn’t very busy, maybe lunch time or early evening time they are more busy. The place was very clean and they have open kitchen. Their dining area is very big and very comfortable. Also their playlist was just great.

I ordered stuffed grape leaves which came with good amount of tzatziki sauce and pita bread. The stuffed grape leaves were just average but the tzatziki sauce was phenomenal. I just loved it. I ordered their famous spinach pie (spanakopita) which was crispy and huge. It was very good. My main course I had their plate option. I ordered grilled chicken with rice, mashed potatoes and baked veggies. They serve the plates one protein with 3 sides, sauce and bread. This is just a great deal because it’s a lot food. I liked everything so much especially baked veggies was very very tasty. They cooked chicken very well.

The service was great and all the service team members were very helpful people. Their prices are very reasonable and they serve the food with really huge portion. I strongly recommend this nice place for everyone.

name: Chengdu Famous Food 成都名吃

text.text:
Writing this as I’m eating their food in my dorm haha.
If you’re looking for authentic Sichuan food then this is THE place to go. I can only think of maybe two or three restaurants that are on par with this place spice-wise that are all located in Chinatown. I’m really happy that I can find this type of cuisine here in University City because I don’t have to take the train to Chinatown just to get Chinese food. As a Chinese person that grew up in both China and America, the amount of spice they have in their dishes is more than enough to satisfy your cravings for Sichuan cuisine.
I came here first with my friends to dine-in but I couldn’t resist ordering take-out one week later because I was CRAVING their spicy edamame! Their dry pots are also very delicious and flavorful. Their non-spicy foods such as the pancake and potatoes are also well-made and crafted and tastes as authentic as it gets. Even the atmosphere itself reminds me of every other Chinese restaurant that my family and I used to go to back in China.
I even kept a menu to myself when I first came because I knew that this was the spot for me to order from if I want familiar food. Definitely will be coming back to order regularly!

If you're craving real Sichuan food near Penn or Drexel, this is the spot. Highly recommended!

text.text:
Incredibly disappointed. Got the dry pot spicy pork, cooked wonderfully, spice was wonderful. Very well done. The only problem was the MSG and salt were completely out of control. I love spice, I love salt, I love MSG, but there was so much that I couldn’t even taste the food. Tried to clear my pallet with rice, rice tasted like MSG. I drank some water, water tasted like soap. I tasted the water before I ate, and there was nothing wrong with the water. My taste buds were just shot out. I had some Coca-Cola to wash the taste of MSG out of my mouth, tried the process again to see if it was just me. Nope very disappointed, considering how good the food could have been. I asked a young lady at the front what was up, she said, yeah the chef cooks like that. Didn’t offer to remake, didn’t offer me a refund, just gave me a 15% discount. So basically spent $20 on a side of rice and a Coke. Unbelievable.

***update:
I’ve been eating “bold flavors” for the last couple of decades. I’ve also messed up dinner by adding too much salt. There is, in fact, a difference.

text.text: The atmosphere hits that sweet spot—there’s an easy, social hum that makes it perfect for a big table of friends, yet the lighting is gently dim and warm enough that a two-person dinner still feels intimate. Conversations don’t get swallowed by noise; you can hear each other without shouting. Menus can sprawl, but this one has range without chaos: plenty to explore, clearly laid out, and a mocktail section that feels thoughtful rather than sugary. Prices are kind to the wallet given the portion sizes. My must-order lineup starts with the scallion pancakes—the clear headliner. The shrimp lo mein is comfort done right: soft, chewy noodles, well-seared shrimp, and a sauce that coats rather than drowns. And a new favorite is the egg custard—silky and softly set, lightly sweet.

text.text:
Review – Dim Sum House (Philadelphia)

Dim Sum House in Philadelphia is a great Chinese restaurant with a fun and efficient way of ordering: you get a paper menu and a pencil, and simply check off what you want. It’s quick, easy, and perfect for trying multiple dishes without any fuss.

The food comes out fast and everything we tried was fresh and flavorful. The eggplant with sauce was delicious, perfectly cooked and full of flavor. The chow fan (fried rice) was solid, and the pork dumplings were excellent —juicy, well-seasoned, and definitely the highlight of the meal.

Prices are very affordable, especially for the quality and portions, making it a great spot for a casual meal with friends or family.

📍 Conclusion:
Dim Sum House is a must-visit in Philly if you’re craving authentic Chinese comfort food in a relaxed setting. Great flavors, fast service, and excellent value for money.

⭐ Overall rating: 9/10
🥟 Best: the pork dumplings and eggplant dish.
🍚 Worst: nothing major to point out.
💸 Price: cheap and absolutely worth it.

text.text:
It's been a while since I've been here. But with it being nice out and them having Saturday movie matinees for kids, we decided to check them out a couple of weeks ago with our little one.

We went on that Saturday with our own blankets (make sure to bring that with you), extra sunscreen (it was 90 something degrees that day) and the extras for a comfy movie watch on this rooftop park. We drove and parked in the Cira lot for convenience, took the elevator to the top and walked up a flight of stairs to get to the spot - all very seamless and easy. There were a good amount of people there, but we still lucked out with a good spot on the lawn.

Of course we were hungry, so we got food there. Decent portions and prices were ok. They had a special price for a kids burger, which really looked like the same size as a regular burger (we don't know what the difference was). My chicken sandwich was decent size and appetizing - nothing extraordinary but also not bad either. Chicken tenders were also decent, and the drink I had (Mango Daiquiri) was refreshing but I wish it was a larger size.

Hope to come here more over the summer season for other things they have going on.

text.text:
I finally tried Asad's Hot Chicken at 40th Street in Philadelphia, and it definitely lived up to the hype. I ordered the chicken sliders with fries, and everything came out hot, fresh, and packed with flavor.
The chicken was crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside, and seasoned perfectly. The sauce added the perfect kick without overpowering the chicken. The fries were easily one of the best parts of the meal—crispy, well-seasoned, and paired perfectly with the chicken. The portions were generous and worth the price.
The staff was friendly, and my order was ready quickly. The location is small, so it's better for takeout, but the food quality makes up for it. If you're a fan of hot chicken, loaded fries, or flavorful comfort food, this spot is definitely worth checking out.
My rating: 9/10. I'll definitely be back to try the loaded fries and milkshakes next time.

text.text: I would like to start off with saying the food we ordered was very good. We have been to the old location but this was our first time visiting since they have moved. There was miscommunication when ordering though that was quite annoying. We ordered the chapli kebab meal, side of tandoori chicken, and 3 sides of resham beef. The confusion occurred because we asked the man taking our order multiple times if the resham beef was beef cubed chunks or minced kebab. He kept telling us one side order came with 3 individual beef chunks. We thought wow that's awesome so we ordered 3 since it was affordable and were expecting 9 pieces of cubed beef chunks in total. We also asked how many pieces of chicken came with the tandoori chicken and he told us 2 pieces. When our food came out, we received 3 long minced kebabs and 1 piece of tandoori chicken sitting on top. We were confused and asked what it was. He said "this is the resham beef and tandoori chicken". We said "you told us it was beef chunks and not minced kebabs. You also told us it was 2 pieces of chicken and not 1 piece." He apologized and brought it back to the kitchen and then moments later brought it back along with our chapli kebab meal and another staff member. The other staff member asked us what was going on and we explained what we were told vs what actually came out. He apologized and just said the guy was new but I didn't think that was great. Thats a totally different outcome of what we expected when ordering. We didn't feel like arguing though so we just let it go. The food itself was really good and I don't have any complaints about that. We really enjoyed everything even though it wasn't exactly what we were expecting. The resham kebab was really good and actually was my favorite thing even though again, it wasn't what we were told we were getting when we ordered. My only other complaint was the music was extremely loud. That made the dining experience kind of uncomfortable because we could barely hear each other talk. I think if we came back we would probably just get it to go because of the music aspect, it makes the dining experience not so enjoyable even though the food is good.
