text.text:
Arrived around 4:30!pm on a weekday finding only one waiter and two occupied tables. We still had to wait for a recently occupied table to be picked up and cleaned before being seated, even though there were plenty of other tables available.
Menu does not offer full descriptions of listed items named in Hindu, so unless one is familiar with South Indian cuisine one feels at a loss as to what to order.
Our waiter tried to help but we were unable to understand his English and embarrassed to have him repeat what he had just said.
Even though we were the only diners waiting to be served the dishes took a LONG time to arrive. The samosas did not come with the dosa as we had requested, but in separate courses with at least 10’ in between.
The samosas were lukewarm and the two dipping sauces scant in quantity.
The dosa was good but the meager potato filling should have been spread out inside instead of being just lumped in the middle. A knife was needed so we could cut it in half and share it.
The bone in chicken biryani took a long time to arrive, with chicken bone and skin but with hardly any meat. The rice was served cold so we asked for it to be warmed up and that took another 15’ 😠
The papadom was greasy and it did not have any cumin seeds which is what makes them so tasty.
Our waiter disappeared mid service and a new young girl replaced him but she had to be summoned each time we needed something. Same speech difficulties as her previous coworker.
That is why I suggest add a good description in writing to compensate for unintelligible spoken English.
The warm rice dessert with cooked cashews and some kind of fruit, was just too sweet.
Overall a big let down.

This is a very nice, intimate place and the new home of the Laugh House. While the food and cocktails are a bit on the pricey side, both are absolutely delicious and worth it. It’s definitely a great spot for a date—very intimate and romantic.
I went for the first time with a female friend of mine, but honestly, it’s not really a “friend hangout” type of place. Most of the seating is arranged for two people, the dining area is quite dark, and the atmosphere is cozy and moody. Each table has a flameless candle, which really adds to the vibe.
The staff—waitresses, waiters, and everyone else—are extremely helpful, polite, and accommodating. The shows themselves were very enjoyable. One thing a lot of people don’t know is that many of the shows are part of the Access Philly program (if you’re not familiar with it, definitely look it up).
Overall, I highly recommend this place.
Overall rating: 9/10
Food & location: 10/10
Staff: 10/10
Comedy shows: Solid 8–9/10 — funny and entertaining, though not every show had me crying from laughter.
Still, a great experience and a spot I’d absolutely return to.

I had the opportunity to eat at the Bistro Perrier on a few occasions. Booking a reservation online is quick and easy. Upon arriving I was greeted by a host who took us to our seats. I have been able to sit in different parts of the bistro to enjoy different scenery.

The students are really able to showcase their skills whether greeting, managing tables, taking orders and the students making the food.

text.text:
This precious student run dining features specials developed solely by them as well as other favorites. Keep this in mind as aside from your host (also their professor) 100% of the staff are students. Think of it like Culinary Institute but in University City

I started with a glass of wine and a salad based on arugula with a spring pea purée. I followed that with a lamb dish that had probably the best roasted carrot I ever tasted, perfectly cooked lamb and a parsnip purée that had deep umami. I splurged on a side of the  mushroom fricassee which had a great variety of mushrooms in a light cream sauce. I wish I had room for the in house desserts but I may have accidentally eaten one of the baked breads with sea salt encrusted butter which filled me up!

A few things - the students are also servers so they are learning different parts (front bs back of the house). So I had to ask for a wine list and a little more detail than she was able to provide in some entrees. Also the plating is a place they could improve so keep that in mind - the food tastes great even if it’s not decked out in microgreens etc.

The atmosphere in the back is like a French bistro and the bar area is a throwback charmer. Perfect for friends or a date night. Any tips go back to the program enjoy!

text.text:
The food is tasty, and the prices are very reasonable. For a little over $8, I got a platter of scrambled eggs, pork bacon, and cheese grits. Toast comes with it - they have both white and wheat bread - If it was extra, it was only by a dollar or so.
They used to have multiple tables that you could sit and eat at, but not anymore. The back of the restaurant looks like they're renovating, so those tables are not there. That is the only reason I didn't give the atmosphere 5 stars. However, there is one long table up front. There are no chairs, but on it are the various condiments: ketchup, maple syrup, salt and pepper, hot sauce, etc. My fiancé and I didn't want to eat on the train we were waiting to catch, so we ate at that same long table. Standing up and eating was the better option than trying to eat on a fast-moving train and/or bus.
Staff is very friendly and accommodating.

text.text: I'm biased, Idc ! I've lived in the neighborhood over 30 years and can say that Let's Grub is the BEST breakfast spot this side of West Philly!! They're literally the most consistent with the flavor. All of your favorite breakfast staples are bussin at this spot no kizzy. Don't take my word for it though, just go by there and grab you a shrimp & grits platter with cheese eggs and bacon on the side and crumble that bacon on top 😘🤌🏽 chefs kiss!! Also, try that French  toast sprinkled with powdered sugar, with the most deliciously buttery, melt in ya mouth, better than yo mama savoriness in every bite 🤤!! Now, Idk about y'all, but I like a lil pork on my fork no shade 😎. If you just want a sammich, I recommend the pork sausage egg and cheese on croissant 💯. Hands down, my favorite breakfast sandwich 👌🏽. Finally, I'd wash all of this down with the biggest size half & half ice tea they got🥤!! Babyyy!! idk who back there blendin that up, but that stuff is fye🔥!! The prices are on point (🤫, I don't want them hiking them up cause baby they're affordable right now in this recession), they're friendly, and, they've had the same owners since I was a kid, nothin like a familiar face making you feel right at home.  They've also had some upgrades since back in the day iykyk lol 😂. My only gripe is that they don't have any type of delivery service cause they'd have my money every day! (Although,I guess that's actually a good thing 🤔). All i'ma say is TREAT YASELF ‼️

I travel to Philadelphia often, and found this place since it was close to one of the hotels that we stay. To me, it's the epitome of the dive bar atmosphere; not too much noise and cheap prices.

text.text:
Wow, I stumbled across this place by accident heading to the CVS across the street.

This has now become my favorite sandwich shop. The staff are super friendly and treat you like family as soon as you walk in the door. You get friendly hellos, an actual name from the employee and let me know when your ready.

I ordered the spicy beef hoagie with black pepper cooper sharp. The beef is amazingly tender and flavorful and I've never seen that cheese anywhere else. But the same could be said for a lot of thier meats and cheeses. Where else do you find a beef tounge sandwich or roasted garlic and horseradish cheddar.

Once you order your food and move to the back to wait for it you are presented with a non stop buffet of meat and cheese slices from the sandwich chefs. They hand out generous samples of every meat and cheese that hits the cutting machine for other orders while your waiting.
I was already stuffed by the time I got my sandwich.

For great customer service, amazing samples and a variety that you would usually have to hit multiple shops for Koch's is the place to go. Bring your appetite and they'll handle the rest.

text.text:
Food
During our stay, we dined here multiple times. For an evening meal, we ordered Beef Cheese Steak Manakeesh and Chicken Shawarma without rice. We also sampled various types of Baklava, including the Pistachio Square and Walnut Square. We truly appreciated the crisp layers and lightly sweet flavor. The Pistachio Maamoul was delightful and fresh, without being overly sweet. The Power Bar, the sweetest dessert we tried, was deliciously nutty and crunchy. Throughout our visits, we enjoyed bottles of water, the Turkish Coffee Pot, and the Manakeesh Tea Pot. The refreshing mint tea option was a highlight for us.

Service
The staff members are genuinely delightful and make an effort to bridge cultural barriers, ensuring you have a wonderful experience.

Atmosphere
The restaurant features a spacious dining area, while the coffee shop section offers a cozy, smaller seating area—perfect for enjoying a hot tea and a treat in the evenings.

text.text:
Despite my own awkwardness of entering a 'neighborhood regular' fueled bar, Bad Brother is a cozy, friendly, scootch-on-through spot that I'm excited to be right around the corner from.

I've not yet made reservations and have been turned away a couple of times on busy nights with a long wait, but every time I take the chance to catch an open bar seat and get one, I have such a wonderful experience. I'm always eager to read through the food menu to discover a new combination or fusion of flavors. Every dish I've tried has been exceptional, and the portion sizes are certainly shareable when paired with a pint or two. My fiancé and I have found the sweet spot of sharing a small dish and a main dish.

The game is always on, and the conversations are always flowing. I would say that's everything you could ask for from a neighborhood bar, but the food is far too exceptional to stop there.

While I hope to one day be a regular, I'm happy to keep taking my chances on an impromptu bar seat in the meantime.

text.text: I dined here last night--it's in my neighborhood--with my husband, brother, and mother. We had a nice time and some good food. This is now the 3rd restaurant in the space in the 30 years we have lived here, and very glad to have it open! This is just the very beginning of the restaurant's time, here, so I am granting them some leeway, and looking forward to improvements. My #1 issue was that when we entered the restaurant, the only aroma was Fabuloso. No restaurant or any food preparation business, should smell of cleaner. There are specific disinfectants/cleaners designed for food preparation and service spaces that do not have any lingering odor, and that is what any restaurant should be using. It was strong enough that after dinner when we were preparing for going to sleep, I smelled the Fabuloso on my husband's hair. Uncool. The other comments are minor: the bread in the basket was wet on one side of the loaf/each piece, as in sodden. The butter in little plastic cases is for diners or take out, not a dining room. Crostini were a little on the high side and because the loaf was small diameter, very hard to subdivide: either use bread with a larger circumference, or give more, with less topping on each one. While I hope we all appreciate that credit card companies are making too much on service, it would have been nice to let us know there was a 3% service charge for paying with a credit card. Last thing: yesterday was a little muggy, but not particularly hot, and the AC was not up to the task of cooling the room, so either crank it up earlier or having it serviced. I am looking forward to future meals here!

This place was absolutely wonderful. The food was exquisite, but what really made this place stand out was the hospitality and level of service. If you’re able to walk in and sit at the bar, I couldn’t recommend that more. If you’re by yourself or just with one other person, I recommend going in to look at the bar top seating for availability. Masha was my waitress on Saturday and it was such an amazing time that I went back the next day with my friend. Asia was our waitress on Sunday and she was really great too!! The entire weight staff was super friendly all the way to the emotional support worker who is working to go orders (she knows who she is). We made such great conversation that we ended up getting the honor of trying the 25th anniversary specialty French toast and it was 100/10 an absolute must have. Huge shout out to the chef and especially to Dave for all of his hospitality and making such great conversation.

Their food is like art, and so beautifully made, and prepared. If you’re in Philadelphia, this is a place you must go to!!!! on Saturday I had the breakfast tacos, and there are raspberry and lemon poppy pancakes. On Sunday I had the eggs Benedict Florentine with Canadian bacon and my friend got the shrimp and grits. Additionally, we had the banana French toast that is going to be served for their anniversary menu on April 25th.

Parking is hard anywhere so don’t let this be a deterrence. We walked from our hotel.

He was there until the very end and was constantly reading the room and making adjustments as needed. He made my family so comfortable and checked in all night.

Osteria is the best of the best!!

text.text:
I am a wedding photographer and Osteria truly is THAT GIRL. A true broad street gem. I’ve photographed several events here and every single one has been such a smooth and thoughtful experience from start to finish.

The attention to detail from the staff is incredible. The team, including Kyle (and his iconic dessert table), is consistently kind, organized, and genuinely invested in making the day flow seamlessly. It makes such a difference not only for couples, but for vendors working behind the scenes as well.

The ambiance here is unmatched. The space feels warm, elevated, and intimate in a way that photographs beautifully in every season. From candlelit dinners to the natural movement between cocktail hour and reception spaces, everything transitions effortlessly and keeps the evening feeling relaxed but refined. So many photos locations woven throughout the space. The venue is SO aesthetic, inside and out.

The flow of dinner service is also one of the literal best I’ve seen at any venue. Courses are timed beautifully, guests stay engaged, and the overall pacing helps the night feel intentional rather than rushed. It creates such a lovely experience for everyone in the room.

Every event I’ve photographed here has been a joy. Osteria is truly a gem in Philadelphia and such a special place to celebrate.

text.text:
Have been seeing this place for a few years now and, instead of us going to our normal choice of Urban, we decided to finally give this place a try. We went on a Tuesday night and it was overcrowded but wasn't empty either - there were a good number of people there for dinner. We initially sat outside since it was a nice night, but moved in since it started drizzling and we didn't want to get caught in any more rain if it came down.

We expected inside to be bigger than it was, but it did have a good number of tables and bar seating. The lighting and decor were nice - have like modern, chic nautical feels. For you meal we shared the Mozzarella Sticks as an app, he got the Fish and Chips while I went with the Chicken Sandwich with the Pier sauce. The waitress said the sauce was like Chick-fil-A sauce and I thought she was making a loose comparison but, honestly, it really did taste like Chick-fil-A sauce but slightly more rich in flavor. And as someone who doesn't prefer fries, these were delicious! My boyfriend said he really enjoyed his meal as well. Truly enjoyed the drinks and appreciate the nice pours of tequila shots.

Glad we finally have this place a try. Recommend checking em out and, because it's close to us, sure we will come here again.

text.text:
Went to Bar Hygge in the Fairmount area of Philadelphia for breakfast/brunch and would definitely recommend it.
The place has a really cool atmosphere- modern but still cozy, which fits the whole “hygge” concept they’re going for. For anyone who doesn’t know, “hygge” is a Danish term centered around comfort, warmth, and enjoying the moment, and the restaurant honestly captures that vibe really well.
One of the biggest reasons I want to come back is because they brew their own beer in-house through Brewery Techne.
Philly has a strong craft beer scene, and Bar Hygge has become a pretty well-known local spot for both food and beer lovers because of that. I didn’t get to try the beers this time since we came for brunch, but it definitely gave me a reason to come back for dinner or drinks.
For the table, we ordered the Cinnamon and Sugar French Toast, and it was really good- came out warm, soft, and loaded with cinnamon flavor.
For my meal, I got the Eggs Benedict with poached eggs, pork roll, braised collard greens, hollandaise, buttermilk biscuit, and hygge home fries. Everything worked really well together and felt like a quality brunch dish rather than something basic thrown on a menu.
The restaurant also has plenty of seating both indoors and outdoors, which is nice since the area can get busy on weekends. Service was great too-the waitresses were super friendly and attentive throughout the meal.
Overall, it’s a really solid brunch spot with good food, good vibes, and a unique brewery aspect that helps it stand out from other places in the city. Definitely recommend checking it out if you’re in the Fairmount area.

I checked out Bar Hygge in Fairmount, PA, and it completely lived up to the hype. From the moment you walk in, the place just feels right. The space is beautifully put together with a mix of furniture from all over that somehow fits perfectly, creating a warm, cozy, and stylish atmosphere. The decor is incredible, and the whole place has an effortless vibe that makes you want to settle in and hang out for a while with friends.

The staff was excellent and the service was fast and on point without ever feeling rushed. Everyone was friendly, attentive, and clearly knew what they were doing, which added to how relaxed the experience felt.

As for the food, I had their burger, and it was outstanding. Easily one of the best burgers I’ve ever had. It was packed with flavor, had a great smoky element, and was cooked perfectly. This is absolutely a burger worth going out of your way to try, especially paired with the atmosphere that comes with it.

Overall, Bar Hygge is more than just a restaurant. It is a full on vibe. A perfect spot to grab great food, enjoy excellent service, and spend a few hours catching up with friends in a space that feels both unique and welcoming.

Service throughout the evening was attentive without ever feeling intrusive.

The restaurant itself was very comfortable—welcoming, relaxed, and refreshingly free of loud, distracting music, which made it perfect for conversation and celebration.

Overall, it was a wonderful setting for a post-wedding celebration, and we would gladly return!

When I found out about this restaurant in the art museum, I immediately assumed that it was going to be overpriced and mediocre. A tourist trap, right? But I went for Sunday brunch anyway.

I was completely wrong and their food and service blew me away. Their biscuits are crispy but not dry, with delicious herbal flavors that make them special. The crab cakes were entirely made of crab meat—not filled with bunch of other things. The texture was wonderful as well. The pancakes were so soft and perfectly cooked as well.

With big marble tables, comfortable chairs, and fantastic architecture, my Sunday brunch was a wonderful experience. The plates and cups, the plating, presentation, were all really great and fitting for the museum.

While not the cheapest place, this place is a great bang for your buck. And just delicious.

Will definitely try again.

text.text:
Welcome is how you will feel at Angelino's restaurant. This restaurant is larger inside than it looks from the outside and I had it all to myself before the lunch rush.

Staff were very attentive. I only had to glance towards the waitress and she came rushing over to see if I wanted anything. The manager came to my table just to ask if the music was too loud or if I wanted it turned down when he saw that I was working through lunch.

The food was traditional Italian, pizza place, and Greek. And it was excellent.

Everything, including the bathrooms, was spotlessly clean.

This is located a couple of blocks away from Philadelphia’s Museum Row and a few blocks from the Eastern State Penitentiary tourist attraction. But it is definitely well worth a few minutes of travel. Parking, however, is tight on street parking.

text.text:
Local sushi spot that has been rebranded and revitalized into a more modern trendy restaurant.

Prices have gone up and there is a bar that serves fairly good cocktails. The matcha cocktail is great without being overly sweet.

The miso soup is suprisingly great here without being overly salty. The sushi rolls were decent, dragon roll tasted mediocre  for the price. Sushi rice tasted a bit bland. The calamari was not over battered which is good but the portion size is small, compared to similar restaurants. The lowest point was the Miso black cod. Very small portion, majority just vegetables and rice with barely any flavor on the cod, which was dry. The sashimi platter saved the dinner.

The lunch special is not a terrible deal but nothing to run over for. The sushi rolls for lunch were heavy on the rice.

All in all, an easy local spot to come for some Sushi but not the best value or taste.

text.text:
Javelin is a new sushi restaurant in Fairmount serving up some fantastic food at fair prices!

The interior is quaint and casual. We came on a very cold day and it was pretty cold in there too. Just a fair warning you may want to bring layers!

We started with the berry blossom drink and miso soup. The drink was sweet and tart, the taste was on point. However, there was so much ice in the cup. It was filled to the top. I only took about 4 to 5 sips before it was completely done. The miso soup was a bit of a letdown, the rich umami flavor was missing. It almost seemed like the stock was watered down.

On to the showstoppers - s*x on a beach roll, pan seared black cod and rock shrimp. All three dishes left us saying wow. The sushi roll had a flavor of textures that worked so perfectly together. The creamy sesame sauce was so unique and delicious. My favorite roll I’ve had in philly. The black cod was a huge portion for only $30. It was cooked well, the veggies were seasoned and everything about it felt hearty. The rock shrimp were huge and a large portion. The sauce was sweet and creamy.

The only feedback I have would be to add some type of fresh herb to the rock shrimp and plate it on a darker dish to present it a bit better.

Overall, we had a great experience and are so happy to have a go-to sushi place in Fairmount! I can’t wait to come back.

text.text: Pizzeria Vetri has the best pizza not just in Philly, but in the country. My family and I have been coming here for over 10 years. The authentic brick-oven Neapolitan pizza tastes exactly like the pizza I had when I traveled to Italy, and it is as good as it gets! The dough is fermented 4 days in advance, making it so much more delicious (and so much healthier, too!). The seasonal pizzas are always changing, so there's always something new on the menu, and the classics are always there for you. My wife absolutely loves the rotolo, a unique appetizer that can only be found at Pizzeria Vetri. The Limoncello Spritz is my absolute favorite drink anywhere, made with homemade Limoncello based off of the manager's personal family recipe from his Grandmother (how authentically Italian is that?!). Speaking of which, for anyone who loves to experience Italian culture - Pizzeria Vetri is as authentic as it gets! We feel like we're stepping back into Italy every time we walk through the door. The staff is as friendly as can be, and they are very welcoming to families with kids. We can't say enough good things about Pizzeria Vetri and can't wait for our next visit soon!!! Best restaurant in all of Philly!

The interior of the restaurant was noticibly dirty. When offering to pay with a debit card, we were informed that a 3.5% credit surcharge would still apply, while their menu clearly states the fee only applies to credit card transactions. This fee was actually labeled as a "service charge" on the final receipt, which is shady and misleading.

All the proteins were overcooked, to the point that it made the meal difficult to eat without constantly drinking water. The pasta dishes were underwhelming and unbalanced, with sauces that were not properly emulsified. The tiramisu was dry and was made with whipped cream rather than marscapone.

text.text:
My friends and I selected the 3 course experience, and were pretty satisfied with everything. I would say that everything that I have tried were in between great and excellent, and even if nothing was exceedingly spectacular, I would recommend this place to anyone who wants to have a pleasant Italian food experience!

The peach panzanella and the roasted beets were both pretty good, with the beets having enough whipped ricotta and vinaigrette to remove the beets' earthy flavor. I had the rigatoni bolognese for primi, and the pasta was very al dente, which was a plus! The sauce was a bit soupy, and sometimes it was a bit difficult to get the sauce on the rigatoni, but in terms of taste, it definitely had a good amount of flavor. Out of all the primi we have had, mine had the largest portion, and I was a bit surprised at the portion size for the potato gnocchi and the squid ink lumache. The roasted beets also had a very small size, which surprised me as well.

In terms of dessert, my friend thought the honey rosemary panna cotta was too sweet, while I thought the tiramisu had a very strong espresso flavor and the ladyfinger at the bottom was a bit too wet. But the mascarpone ratio was good and it still tasted good enough.

Service and atmosphere were both great! Our waiter was very attentive to our needs, and made a conscious effort to ensure our orders were correct. The place also had good decor and a good vibe for dates for those that are interested!

text.text:
High expectations for this restaurant, but only the food missed the mark.

Everything was heavily salty and seasoned. The chips were homemade and complementary, which we appreciated, but they were very salty. The hamburger had a nice runny egg yolk, it was on the smaller end for patty size, the brioche bun was nicely toasted. Fingerling potatoes were heavily seasoned as well.

Forest mushroom bucatini had a great pasta, but the sauce was so salty. The cashew truffle oil did not balance the dish at all. This dish was so disappointing.

The atmosphere of the restaurant was beautiful. The garden outside was incredibly blooming in June. Though the weather is hot, the outdoor patio has umbrellas and shade. The indoors have very open window concepts. Service was really good.

Not very many seats. Reservation highly recommended on weekends. Reservations are made through resy.

If you like salt, this is your place. Every dish is so overloaded with salt that it’s all you can really taste.

The vibe is fine except the several large screen TVs. Service is ok but clearly they need more staff on hand.

We ordered 2 beef & lamb gyros. They came out in a broom pan. Odd presentation… the meat is salty and fatty, so tasted like cheap gyro. The fries were good.

The platters are massive and can be split between two people.

Besides the over salted food, the biggest disappointment was the spanakopita. It’s 4 small pieces, mostly feta with very little spinach, and is fried instead of a flaky phyllo dough.

Greek food is about simplicity of flavors, but the only thing we could taste was the salt.

Overall, won’t be coming back so will try the competitor down the street.

text.text:
McCrossen's Tavern in the Fairmount area is a really great spot to grab food with family or meet up with friends for a relaxed meal and drinks. The atmosphere is one of the first things you notice when you walk in—it’s cozy, welcoming, and has that classic neighborhood tavern feel. It’s not overly large, but it comfortably holds around 50 to 100 people, making it feel lively without being overwhelming. It’s the kind of place where you can settle in and enjoy your time without feeling rushed.
The service was quick and friendly from the moment we sat down. The staff was attentive and made sure everything came out in a timely manner. One unique feature is their wine selection, as McCrossen’s is the official tasting room in the United States for Decibel Wines, which is a really cool touch if you’re into wine or looking to try something different beyond the typical bar offerings.
For food, I ordered the roasted pork sandwich with long hots along with a Guinness. The Guinness was fresh, cold, and poured perfectly. The sandwich itself was massive and packed with flavor. It was a bit messy and greasy, but that’s honestly part of what makes it so good and authentic. The fries were a standout—crispy, well-seasoned, and easily some of the better bar fries I’ve had. We also ordered the crispy chicken sandwich and a wrap, and both were very large portions, filling, and flavorful.
Overall, the prices are very reasonable for the amount and quality of food you receive. McCrossen’s is a great place for solid bar food, drinks, and a comfortable atmosphere. I would definitely recommend it and would come back again to grab food or just hang out at the bar for a few drinks.

So fun!! HOT and SPICY is on the menu today on International Hot and Spicy Food Day 🌶️🌶️🌶️🌶️
It’s not just spicy, it’s Philly spicy as we find ourselves at McCrossen’s Tavern in Philadelphia, PA where “every day is spicy and hot!” According to David the Bartender.
Indeed, McCrossen’s is known for their famous Tavern Wings, and the XXX Carolina Reaper version which are wings with “some of the world's hottest peppers like Carolina Reapers, ghost peppers, and scorpion peppers, mixed with smoky habaneros and citrus for intense heat, requiring gloves and caution, with a bell to ring if you can't handle the burn.”
🌶️
We did not have those 😬
We did have the Habanero Tavern Wings, the Bang Bang Shrimp and the Bang Bang Deviled Eggs.
🔥
It can get crowded and you may have to wait for a table.  We snagged seats at the bar. Everything was delicious.  The drinks were generous, the beer cold.  What more can one ask for?

text.text:
I’ve always enjoyed the food at Gyu-Kaku, which is why this experience was so disappointing.

I spent nearly $80 on my order and arrived to pick it up. I briefly stepped away to grab a few items, came back, let the employee who took my order know I had returned, paid, and was told, “You can sit down and I’ll come get you.”

I then waited on the bench for about 25 to 30 minutes. Eventually, I became frustrated and went  to ask what was going on. As soon as the employee saw me, the first thing he said was, “I forgot about you.”

To be honest, I found that insulting. I understand the restaurant was busy, and mistakes happen. I’ve worked in customer service and know that things can get hectic. But I was also a paying customer, and hearing that I had simply been forgotten made me feel like my patronage didn’t matter.

The issue wasn’t even the wait itself. It was the way it was handled. A more appropriate response would have been something like, “I sincerely apologise for the wait. Thank you for your patience.” Even if you did forget a customer, saying “I forgot about you” directly to them isn’t the best way to handle the situation.

The food here is still great, and I’ve generally had good experiences with the service in the past. However, this experience left a bad taste in my mouth and showed that there is room for improvement when it comes to customer service and communication.

I hope the owners see this as constructive feedback and remind their staff that how you address a mistake can make all the difference to a customer’s experience.

text.text:
The staff were friendly and welcoming, which we appreciated. Unfortunately, the food did not meet the standard we’ve come to expect from Green Eggs Cafe. We’ve visited other locations many times, but this was our first experience at the Girard location and it was disappointing.

I ordered the Surf and Turf ($35). When it arrived, the steak was cooked medium rare instead of medium. After asking for it to be cooked longer, it appeared to be reheated in the microwave. When it came back, we finally tasted the steak and it tasted old, as if it had been sitting in the fridge for a while, and the flavor was very off-putting. The crab cake also tasted freezer-burnt and was inedible. The sautéed spinach was overly salty, the diced potatoes were underwhelming, and the sourdough bread was tough. Overall, the dish did not taste fresh and was not worth the price.

My fiancé ordered the buffalo chicken mac and cheese, which lacked flavor. There was very little cheese, and the sauce was bland. Even after adding hot sauce, it still didn’t improve much.

My mother-in-law ordered the egg white omelette with diced potatoes. She said the omelette was okay, but the potatoes again had an off taste.

One of my biggest pet peeves is wasting food, but the steak and crab cake were truly inedible, so I had no choice but to leave them. I even felt unwell shortly after leaving. For over $100 spent on just three plates—with no drinks or extras—this experience was extremely disappointing. I hope management takes a closer look at food quality and freshness, because this did not reflect the standard we’ve experienced at other locations.

text.text:
Buena Onda punches far above its weight and is better than it has any right to be. It's an extremely affordable fast food/fast casual taco spot but I'll be honest, they are serving the best tacos I've had in the city. Yes, they aren't fancy or crazy unique but they are consistently high quality with fresh ingredients and delicious and varied flavors at a price point that I don't fully understand.

The happy hour has recently changed, but previously it was $4 fish tacos which were absolutely delicious. Now, it's $3 tacos for al pastor, as well as few different chicken options. Drinks are also crazy cheap, but still strong and taste pretty good. $5 margaritas and sangrias during happy hour and beers are even cheaper. So for excellent tacos and drinks for two people you can have a tasty meal under $30, which I don't think I can say about anywhere else.

While the interior is pretty basic, I will mention that the service is very friendly and helpful. It's fast food style but they'll bring out your food to your table and take away your trash as well, and like the food the service is better than it has any right to be. I highly recommend stopping by!

text.text:
Delicious food, friendly service, quick turnaround time, and very fair prices.

The dine-in setup is very casual — there is table service but you order/pay at the counter & self-serve water. There is a lot of natural light inside, a good view of the sidewalk to people-watch, and the two folks running the restaurant while I was there (possibly the owners) were phenomenally gracious hosts. There is a cold case of to-go snacks and drinks. The rice balls are a must try!

Having tried the chicken galbi lunch box and the squid dolsot, I can enthusiastically recommend both, but the dolsot was truly the star of the show in my opinion. The combination of buttery squid, jammy egg, umami & spicy sauce, veggie mix, and that crispy caramelized rice at the bottom is just absolutely magical.

This is an absolute gem of a restaurant.

I was excited to see there was a good amount of veg options (beyond just the typical avo roll) but was disheartened when the vegetable burrito arrived with kani in it. There was no mention of this on the menu. Under the veg burrito it states: “ Sweet potato tempura, pumpkin tempura, cucumber. avocado.w.chef sauce” and when I called I was informed that all burritos have kani in them.

Again I can’t fully knock them bc I’m not the ideal demo. The avo/ginger/tofu roll and seaweed salad were good. The miso soup was meh. I hope they’ll add the hidden kani to the menu for those with allergies, which thankfully is not me, as it could cause a much worse situation for someone.

My ranking would be 2.5 but rounding up to 3.

**see close up burrito picture to CLEARLY see that there is kani (the red stripey piece that’s white in the center)**

Overall, the experience was far below expectations.

text.text: ABSOLUTELY LOVE THIS PLACE so much i had to go back twice. Now, the staff is super sweet and fun. Always helpful always fast even when they are busy things come out fairly quickly. My ONLY caveat with this place is the food is not that great. Online everything looks amazing but I think flavor profile wise it’s just not a strong fusion menu. Some things taste better than others. The nachos could be good if they used pita chips or fresh pita but the toppings don’t go with the regular tortilla chip they use and together just make for a confusing mouth experience that doesn’t taste all that great. The onion rings even have potential, but the seasoning they are throwing on them to make them taste more “Asian inspired” is way too heavy. And maybe just not the seasoning for onions rings, a food that AT MOST requires salt and pepper. Street tacos were ok but again another situation where i desperately wanted all this on some form of Pita or Naan. The hot dog? Just not good. It’s a hot dog with queso, the essence of bacon, and peanuts 🫠 very strange and doesn’t taste authentic to the cuisine they’re trying to create just tastes like somebody in there throwing paint at the wall. The WINGS?! Best thing on the menu. Haven’t had the buffalo. But all in all I’ll say they should get someone who is that culture in the kitchen and let them come up with a menu bc right now it just tastes like Americans doing it the way they think they should and it could be better. BUT this is how you know the place is good because I would still go back even if the food leaves a lot to be desired.

text.text:
Hot, confusing, crammed, chaotic!!

Entering this eatery felt a lot like stepping into an unfamiliar high school cafeteria.

In contrast to the relative peace and order in the regular Museum, this cafeteria is a zone of excessive heat, zero assistance re: figuring out food ordering system, and BONUS! Herds of loud-talking, slow-walking tweens/teenagers with no spatial awareness (and no visible adult supervision).

The teens/kids loiter around the food stations and make it impossible for presbyopic adults to get close enough to even squint-interpret the posted menu.

And just like I did in my high school cafeteria, I went to the station with shortest line, grabbed random items, and retreated to a table as far, far away from other people as I could get.

To summarize:
Hot, loud, not user-friendly, taken over by tweens/teens.

text.text: What an awesome experience! Hiring Chef Aaron Griffin was a huge win for Kansai. My family and I ordered hundreds of dollars worth of sushi at his bar and he put on a magnificent show for us. The restaurant looks brand new and sharply decorated. We had miso, shumai, gyoza, edamame, lots of sushi, coctails, mochi and everything was very good. The sushi was top notch. We had to remind our server about some things we ordered he had forgotten about, but we ordered a lot and he was preoccupied flirting with some server girls lol forgiveable we tipped him 20% and also tipped the kitchen staff over 20% for the excellent fair. It's a hidden gem, they are looking to expand with some upstairs entertainment space in the future. You should definately go sit at Chef Aaron's bar and let him treat you to a wonderful night of fine dining!

text.text: Cosmic Cafe, located on the end of Lloyd Hall just before boathouse row, is a pleasant spot to grab a drink or coffee, sandwich, burger and more. They are largely farm to table with much ingredients locally sourced. There is a small interior with seats overlooking the large patio area with lots of seating and upstairs seating as well. They have an assortment of homemade lemon and lime ade and cold tea drinks. I don't usually have a meal - as this is more of a stop off spot after a ride before heading home - but I had a shrimp summer salad today that was fresh and very good. My experience has been that the prepared food is a bit uneven, but was usually addressed if I brought it to the attention of the staff. All in all, a good place to stop if you're taking a stroll on Kelly drive.

text.text:
I don't understand why this place only got a 4.2. The hubby and I stumbled in here while we were walking along Kelly Drive. We were pretty hungry and we saw that they had vegan options for us.

When we walked in, the line was out the door. After the wait, we ordered with the really friendly woman at the register (pink and purple braids).

We split the tofu burrito and the vegan burger. I also got a strawberry banana smoothie with peanut butter.

Everything tasted so good! The burrito has sweet potatoes which was excellent!  The smoothie legit tasted like a peanut butter and jelly sandwich.

We dined outside and the wait for the food was minimal. We also fed some of the ducks who were hanging around!

It was a beautiful Sunday afternoon to eat wonderful food along the drive.

What a beautiful day we had on our bicycling journey from Center City Philadelphia. We rode north on a bike/walking path to Boathouse Row.
The weather was gorgeous. As we explored the area north of the City.
Then we came upon a lovely place to buy lunch and some mint tea. It is called The Cosmic Cafe and Cider House. Where we ordered a tuna on marble rye and a turkey bacon BLT wrap, with two glasses of delicious mint tea.
The service was extremely good. The food was absolutely perfect. And the mint tea was so refreshing.
I am so glad that we discovered this hidden gem, just off of the Schuylkill River.  As it's nestled underneath the trees and a cool soft breeze is felt.
We had such a relaxing time eating lunch outside of The Cosmic Cafe and Cider House.

Picked up a to go order, place seemed super lovely. Only down side was that the report said that it would be ready and I was still kept waiting for another 10-12mins. So if you are ordering delivery be mindful that carriers may be told it’s ready when it isn’t. HOWEVER, the food was amazing and they have lots of vegetarian options. They also have some of my favorite chopsticks (the rounded ones that you don’t have to break).

A couple weeks later I came back for delivery service. Placed the order (on Dim Sum’s website) before opening and I will say, delivered to perfection. Previously I’d posted 4/5 Service stars for the delay in the pickup time, corrected today for 5/5. Not to mention that the food is wonderful, I didn’t quite care for the Dan Dan noodles w Chili Peanut Sauce. These were dry and powdery rather than saucy. But everything else was great.

The lunch specials are gold for anyone looking to order ahead and have your lunch delivered just before lunchtime at the office. My favorite dish is the Eggplant in spicy garlic sauce. Perfect portion (for me I like a little extra rice to take some heat off).

Would like to see Thai iced tea on the menu but I went for the Vietnamese iced coffee and it is strong to keep you going through the afternoon!

I recently had the pleasure of dining at "Dim sum & Noodle" and I must say, it exceeded all my expectations. From the moment I walked in, the friendly and attentive staff made me feel welcomed and appreciated. The ambiance of the restaurant was warm and inviting, creating a cozy atmosphere that was perfect for a relaxing meal.

Now, let's talk about the food. The menu offered a wide variety of dim sum and noodle dishes, each bursting with delicious flavors. I couldn't resist trying a little bit of everything, and I was not disappointed. The dim sum was steamed to perfection, with delicate wrappers and flavorful fillings that left me craving for more. The noodles were cooked al dente and paired perfectly with the savory sauces and toppings.

What really stood out to me was the quality of the ingredients used in every dish. It was evident that the chefs took great care in sourcing fresh and high-quality ingredients, resulting in dishes that were not only delicious but also nutritious.

Lastly, I have to commend the service at "Dim sum & Noodle." The staff was knowledgeable about the menu and provided great recommendations based on my preferences. They were attentive without being intrusive, ensuring that my dining experience was enjoyable from start to finish.

Overall, I would highly recommend "Dim sum & Noodle" to anyone looking for an incredible dining experience. The combination of delectable dishes, friendly service, and inviting ambiance make it a standout restaurant in the area. Whether you're a fan of dim sum or noodles, or simply looking for a new culinary adventure, this is definitely a place worth checking out. Trust me, you won't be disappointed!

text.text:
To Fairmount's pizza place,
I'm writing this because I care, and because nobody else in the neighborhood is going to say it to your face.

You are the pizza place here. Not a pizza place — the pizza place. When someone moves to Fairmount and asks where to grab a slice, your name is what comes out of our mouths. That's a real thing. That's a kind of trust the neighborhood hands over to you without asking for much in return.

And I think you've stopped noticing.

The last few pies I've had were swimming in grease, with a crust that gave up halfway through the first slice. It's not that it was bad in some dramatic way — it's that it felt like nobody in the kitchen was paying attention. Like the pizza was just something getting made, not something getting made for someone. And that's the part that actually stings, because we are someone. We're your neighbors, and we keep showing up.

Here's the thing I want you to hear: I am not rooting against you. I am so deeply rooting for you. There's no version of this where I want a new place to open up and put you out of business. I want you to be the place. I want to walk in on a Friday and have the guy behind the counter nod at me, and I want to bring out-of-town friends and say "wait until you try this." That's the dream. That's what a neighborhood pizza place is supposed to be.

You have something most restaurants would kill for — a built-in community that wants to love you. All you have to do is meet us halfway. Drain the grease. Respect the crust. Care about what's going out the window. Take a little pride in being ours.
We'll keep coming. Just give us something to brag about.

With love from a hungry neighbor who really, really wants this to work.

In all honesty, as convenient as this location is for me as a fairmount local, this place's food is really lacking in certain key areas. I feel strongly that if there was some extra effort put into sprucing up the menu and using more quality ingredients as well as perhaps changing the pizza oven to one that can operate at a better temperature, the food quality would quickly improve. It is one of the only options in the area with quick to access food and it is a bummer that it is lacking in quality. Additionally, as it is one of three fast casual pizza places in the area, perhaps some more originality would make a difference.

I'm hoping that this review helps to encourage the owners to put effort into their product.

Sincerely,

A loyal but disheartened customer

As a customer, it was disappointing to see the dining area being closed three hours before the restaurant's/pizza store posted closing time. If a restaurant advertises that it is open until midnight, customers reasonably expect to be able to sit down and enjoy their meal until then.

Removing chairs and shutting down seating at 9:00 PM creates a confusing and unwelcoming experience. It gives the impression that customers are being discouraged from dining in, despite the restaurant still being open. Situations like this can leave guests feeling rushed, dissatisfied, and less likely to return or recommend the establishment to others.

If there is a specific reason for closing the dining area early, it should be clearly communicated to customers. Otherwise, guests should be able to enjoy the full dining experience during the restaurant's advertised hours.

text.text:
My partner and I recently visited a local breakfast spot, and while we spent around $30, the experience was a bit of a mixed bag. The standout of the meal? The hot chocolates. They were absolutely delicious—rich, creamy, and the perfect balance of sweetness. If you’re a fan of a good hot chocolate, this is definitely the place to get it.

For the food, my partner opted for a breakfast sandwich on a croissant. He found that the sandwich was mostly carried by the butter. For me, the eggs were over-peppered and lacked enough salt for seasoning. Unfortunately, the rest of the sandwich didn’t have much going for it flavor-wise.

The gluten-free options were a bit underwhelming, as the only option they seemed to offer was gluten-free bread, with little variety for those with dietary restrictions.

On a positive note, the café is clean, and the service was friendly and attentive. The staff made us feel welcome, which added a nice touch to the visit. However, unless we’re coming back just for the hot chocolate, we’re not sure we’d return.

The banana bread chocolate chip one is a bit heavier but I think by design--It's super rich and delicious. I also love trying the flavors I'm not normally as draw to because I know they'll knock it out of the park. Today I tried the coconut pound cake, and it is top notch.

I don't often buy breakfast out, but the couple times I've gotten food, it's been great. The coffee is from Reanimator, which is great. The one time I got a double shot, I'm not sure it was dialed in exactly right, but the drip is always good, and I love an occasional mocha and theirs is on the sweeter side but is a nice rich treat.

Overall, I think this is place is a gem. I don't think you can go wrong ordering anything, but no matter what, you'd better try the baked goods!

text.text: Good evening Google Family. I arrived in a Lyft to visit the Eastern State Penitentiary. I walked here to the Golden Lake Chinese Restaurant after the prison tour. My first time eating here. I wanted an egg roll and so I glanced around at the available options. I spotted this place when I left the CVS across the street. I was hoping that they had a dining area since I wanted to sit down and eat my food. Thank God and thank goodness there is a dining area here. I sat down when I arrived and I scanned the menu. I decided to get the Triple Delight Specialty which consisted of chicken, imitation crabmeat, crawfish, shrimp and mixed vegetables. I wanted brown rice instead of white rice and thank goodness they had brown rice which was $1.50 more. The dish was $15.99 with the $1.50 made it $17.49, which was the subtotal and the tax was $1.40 and the total was $18.89. I paid by cash. I informed the young lady that I was dining in. They thought that I was taking out. Then I went to sit down. They brought me water and I did not drink any of it since I do not want to constantly have to go to the bathroom. I will drink my water when I arrive home. My meal arrived quickly. I did not wait long. It looked so good. I am realizing more and more that presentation of the meal is just as important as the taste of the meal. The meal did not disappoint. It tasted as good as it looked on the plate. I surprised myself since I did not realize how hungry I was. I ate all of the food on the plate. It was so delicious!!! And I ate all of the brown rice. I usually do not eat the brown rice, since I am not a rice eater, but I devoured every morsel today. I laughed at myself!!! I definitely do not like white rice. When I finished I visited the rest room and it was clean. They have one rest room and it is unisex. The rest room was equipped with soap, soap dispenser and paper towels. Then I left the restaurant and called a Lyft. I walked back to Eastern State Penitentiary. I had a good eating experience here today at the chinese restaurant. Have a good night, workout, be active and mobile, fit and fabulous especially for people over 50 years of age.

text.text: If you’re looking for a cute restaurant to just grab drinks and not really eat, this is perfect for that! Our server Liz was great and made sure we had everything we needed. The restaurant itself was pretty and nicely decorated but the food was disappointing. The smoked salmon flatbread was soft/undercooked, the grits had more of a mash potato consistency and the beignets were just fried dough balls. My favorite thing i had was the cinnamon pecan butter that came with the beignets. The outdoor heated patio was comfortably warm for the majority of our time there, at one point they did turn the heat off and we had to request it to be put back on. If i were to return i would sit indoors and do drinks only.

text.text: This was my second visit and likely won’t be my last. I recommend starting with the braised meatballs. All of our entrées were flavorful and generously portioned. The chocolate cake wasn’t as moist as it looked, but the olive oil cake and pistachio gelato were much better and worth ordering. None of the cocktails particularly stood out, though an espresso martini is always a safe choice. Service could have been more attentive, as we often had to flag someone down or wait for our server to check in, but it was a busy Friday night. I’d recommend requesting seating away from entryways to avoid winter drafts. Overall, I enjoy this place and would return.

text.text:
Absolutely loved brunch at The Dandelion! I would definitely recommend making reservations if you can. We didn’t have one and showed up around 11:45 on a Saturday for brunch, so I was honestly expecting a wait. To my surprise, they were able to seat our party of two immediately! They did let us know they’d need the table back by 12:45 for an incoming reservation, which was totally fine because we are quick eaters anyway lol.

The staff was so sweet and accommodating the entire time, and every single room in this place has its own charm and personality. I was especially excited that we got seated in the dog room. It has such cozy, classic vintage vibes and just feels incredibly unique.

Brunch itself was phenomenal. The French toast with the chantilly cream was absolutely decadent, and my husband thoroughly enjoyed his salad as well. Even little details stood out here. If you order tea, it comes served properly in a teacup and everything, which just added to the whole experience.

Cannot recommend this place enough!

text.text:
This was a great restaurant for both large and medium-sized groups. During my business trip, I ended up dining here two nights in a row, and I was actually excited to come back the second night.

They offered a prix fixe menu with a choice of appetizer, entrée, and an assorted cake platter for dessert. The appetizer options included carrot soup and Caesar salad, while the entrées included the Dandy Beef Burger, artichoke risotto, and chicken curry.

I got to try a little bit of everything from both my own dishes and my colleagues’ plates.

The carrot soup was good - if you really love ginger, you’d probably enjoy it even more than I did. The Caesar salad came with an enormous pile of romaine lettuce covered in grated Parmesan cheese. It was a lot, but my colleagues clearly loved it because they all finished theirs.

I really enjoyed my burger, and the fries were interesting in a good way: thick-cut and hearty. The artichoke risotto became the mysterious dish everyone at the table was curious about. It arrived buried under a mountain of grated Parmesan cheese and had a slightly lemony flavor. The chicken curry was also good, though the portion was huge and the yogurt flavor was a bit too strong for me personally.

On the second night, I tried the scallops: three perfectly cooked scallops served with a creamy sauce and bacon. I absolutely loved that dish. I was advised to order a side since the scallop portion was small, so I chose the tri-color carrots, which turned out to be generous enough to share and were excellent. I also tried the green beans, and they were amazing. My colleagues who ordered steaks practically licked their plates clean - honestly, the kitchen probably didn’t even need to wash them afterward.

The assorted cake platter was a really nice way to end the meal.

What truly made the second night memorable was our server, who went above and beyond. As soon as I walked in, I asked if he could help us celebrate a special occasion. He immediately suggested a few options, including champagne and cake, and I chose a cake with a candle. We also needed to split the bill across seven people, and somehow he handled everything smoothly without any confusion. I unfortunately forgot his name, but the receipt listed him as “Dining Room P.” He did an outstanding job.

Overall, this was a memorable dining experience with great food, excellent service, and a welcoming atmosphere for groups.

Fantastic experience at Wilder in Philly this May 2026 UPenn Wharton Reunion weekend!

Wilder came highly recommended by friends, several of whom told me they regularly host their board meeting dinners in the beautiful upstairs dining room — and now I can see why.

Huge shoutout to Prior, the event manager, who went above and beyond trying to expand our reservation from 11 to 14 people before the weekend even started — and then our group somehow grew again from 14 to 20. Carolyn, our server, handled it all with incredible grace, professionalism, and warmth throughout the night.

The entire team was accommodating at every step, the food was excellent, and the vibe was outstanding. Really impressed by the hospitality and execution from the Wilder team.

Thanks for making our Wharton MBA 25th reunion even more memorable!

text.text: I loved visiting Patchwork for a little date night! We were invited by them and a PR company (just for transparency!) but my review here is total honesty. We started off with apps. The arancini was just okay, I anticipated a bit more flavor but they were filling. Would skip those and head straight to the shrimp cocktail (refreshing!) and their onion dip. The onion dip is otherworldly! We would have eaten the bowl haha. There’s a perfect crunch of onions and the lattice chips are a great accompaniment. For entrees we did the steak frites, cooked medium, it was melt-in-your-mouth delicious.. and the patchwork burger! A burger’s a burger but they definitely made it well. Lastly, we finished with desserts. I chose a basque cheesecake but for my partner, our server recommended the new spring dessert, a phyllo pastry with pineapple custard inside?! 10/10 needs to stay on the menu. After having a heavy meal, it’s so easy to finish and it really sparks your tastebuds with the tropical flavors. Very lightweight and it was really what sealed the deal. As far as ambience, it’s in the Hyatt centric, so it seemed to be used as a place of work but toward the end of the night, more families and couples came in to sit and drink/eat. Lighting is nice, music is pretty radio friendly and overall, we had a really good time. It seemed as though the service was round as well, like we weren’t treated any differently for creating content. So if you go, expect a pretty good time and GET THE TROPICAL DESSERT!

text.text:
Butcher Bar — Fallon for the Plot Review

Good service deserves applause. Bad service deserves notes.

Let me just start here: Johnny, our server, is an actual angel.

Yes, he took incredible care of us at the table—attentive, intuitive, immediately adjusting the patio temperature when we mentioned it was too warm. But that’s not even the headline.

I left my credit card behind.

This man remembered—from casual conversation—that we were heading to Helium Comedy Club. He left work, walked in the rain from Butcher Bar to the club, came inside, found me at my table, and handed me my card.

If my boyfriend wasn’t there, I would have kissed him on the lips.
That’s the level of service we’re talking about.

Johnny, if you ever see this—round of applause. Standing ovation. Lifetime achievement award.

Now—the food.

We leaned into appetizers and shared plates:

- Pretzel bread: warm, soft, delicious
- Short rib toast: rich, well-executed
- Korean short ribs (special): standout, flavorful, absolutely worth ordering
- Bone marrow luge: fun, aesthetic, very “for the plot”—but the whiskey and marrow didn’t really enhance each other
- Burger: solid, satisfying
- Filet: cooked well, flavorful

And then… the onion rings.

I don’t know what happened there, but they tasted like manure.
A full outlier in an otherwise strong lineup.

Cocktails

Several specialty cocktails were ordered across the table, and not a single complaint. Everything was well executed—clearly not from a mix. The bartender knows what they’re doing. Each drink felt thoughtfully crafted, properly garnished, and served in glassware that matched the aesthetic.

The Scene & Experience

We sat on the covered patio during a rainy night. There were a few drips hitting two people in our party throughout the meal, which wasn’t ideal. That said, the space itself is comfortable, and the ability to adjust temperature quickly is a plus (shoutout again to Johnny for handling that immediately).

Observation

Great food will bring you in.
Service like that will have you talking about it for weeks.

Notes

- Remove or revisit the onion rings recipe immediately
- Address rain leakage on the covered patio seating

Verdict: No Notes (because Johnny tipped the scale into legend status)

Round of applause. No notes.

text.text: The service was worth noting. I think Brandon was the name of our waiter - friendly, knowledgeable and very proactive and anticipating our needs. Exactly what service should be! The food was ok. We had a business dinner and everyone finished their plates but nobody noted any outstanding dish or flavors. What stood out from the appetizers - the bone marrow - very well prepared but lacked salt. The octopus was another "different" dish we tried - half of it was really good, the other half was chewy. So I have mixed feelings. Our table was on the second floor and thankfully the music could be controlled to the extent that we could hear each other. The windows were open and the weather was good as the breeze was very pleasant (and also dissipated the kitchen flavors and fumes coming upward to the second floor). Overall a good experience which our server had a heavy influence on.

I had a great experience at Bar Bombón in Philadelphia. The atmosphere is welcoming and stylish, with a lively yet comfortable vibe that makes it a great spot for a casual meal, date night, or catching up with friends.

The food was impressive, especially considering the menu is entirely plant-based. The dishes were creative, flavorful, and thoughtfully prepared, proving that vegan dining can be exciting and satisfying. The flavors were well balanced, the presentation was beautiful, and every dish felt like it was made with attention to detail.

The staff was friendly, knowledgeable, and attentive throughout the visit, adding to the overall experience. The drinks were also a highlight, with a great selection that paired well with the food and the atmosphere of the restaurant.

Bar Bombón is a standout vegan restaurant in Philly that offers much more than just plant-based options — it delivers a full dining experience with great food, a fun environment, and excellent service. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a unique and memorable meal, whether they follow a vegan lifestyle or simply enjoy good food.

The bartender Bryce was exceptionally friendly and knowledgeable and made our experience so much better!

Their menu is incredible and their staff seem very nice!  But my husband and I found the food to be extremely mediocre — it lacked a lot of flavor. IWe love Puerto Rican food and is a country we go to often, so we were expecting many WOW factors, especially with it being Vegan.  What we ordered:

1. Chips and Queso - the chips are great and I like the healthy ingredients used to make the queso, BUT it lacked flavor. It needed some salt or something - 6.5/10
2. Grande Breakfast - avocado didn’t look fresh so I didn’t even bother eating that, cuban black beans were completely tasteless, breakfast sausage patty has a strange taste, pico was good + the tofu scramble was really ehh tasting and I love tofu scramble - 3/10
3. Empanadas - had absolutely no taste but the sauce that came with it, semi helped - 4/10
4. Breakfast taco - also mediocre - 3.5/10
5. Lemonade - good and not too sweet which I liked - 8.5/10
6. Cardamom mint tea - different! I usually just drink plain mint tea, so it was cool to try something different - 7/10

Bar Bombón’s food was AMAZING truly made me forget that we were on a animal product fast for 21 days. By this day we were on about day 15 with no meat and it was our wedding anniversary so we had to find something to celebrate. Bar Bombón was definitely the best option for us as far as food goes.

By far our favorite item was the heart of palm fish taco and my husband loved the burger and tres leche cake. The yuca was delicious with the sauce that came on the plate with the Maduros (fried plantains) I would definitely go back for those hearts of palm tacos !

I took one star off atmosphere because the place is VERY cramped and over booked for the amount of space they have. When I got up to use the bathroom I felt like my body may touch the people next to me eating on the way there. It was like we were at dinner with the two tables to the left and right of us. The tables are VERY VERY close to each other.

Our waiter was very professional, kind and gave great recommendations. I would recommend to anyone interested in trying vegan food but I will say they set the bar pretty high for us. Not all vegan foods are created equal.

text.text: I’ve been to Cleavers several times over the last two years for work. It’s my go-to spot in Philly for cheesesteak. I’m a creature of habit. I stopped by again on 4/11/26 around 2pm. There was zero wait time. Even when there is a line, it moves fast. I ordered a Ribeye cheesesteak with provolone, grilled onions and peppers with a side of regular plain fries. No drink. At first glance at the menu you think you’re paying $15 for a basic sammy. But they up charge for the standard toppings, like cheese, that should be included. After all, how is it a Cheesesteak without cheese? I ended up paying $28.08 after tax plus a tip on top of that. And if you pay with a debit/cc they charge an additional 0.78 cents on top. Quantity wise, it’s a lot of food! One cheesesteak feeds two. Every time I’ve been here I’ve never been able to finish my fries and a half of the sammy. I always bag the second half for leftovers. I wish you could order just a half sammy, and if you can I clearly have missed it on the menu. If there’s more than one of you in your group, I recommend one cheesesteak for two. Trust me, you’ll need Shaq sized hands to finish the entire sammy. The meat is good however it’s sliced so thin that at times it tastes like ground beef. Not a big fan of that. They put the cheese on top of the bread and the hot meat on top. By the time you get that first bite in, there’s zero taste of cheese because it basically turned into liquid seeped into the bread. I recommend asking for extra cheese or cheese on top of the meat. The seating area up stairs is clean including bathrooms.

text.text:
I was able to score a same day rez at this tiny Italian BYOB we discovered well over 20 years ago & that we liked very much at the time, yet somehow had never gone back —perhaps we’d been too eager to explore new places.

Every table in the small room was occupied, which we took for a good sign. We shouldn’t have.

The bread basket was accompanied by a little dipping jar with ricotta marinated in olive oil with garlic and herbs, which was a nice touch. We split the garlicky, buttery mussels — probz the highlight of the meal, as well as a highly unremarkable Caesar with ‘homemade’ dressing that was barely there.

As for the pasta, I ordered the fresh linguine with imported porcini jus (sic!) and cream*, figuring it had to be the star of the menu, being the namesake of the place and all, and my dining companion got the rigatoni with sweet sausage and rustic tomato sauce.

Perhaps the phrasing / description of my pasta dish should’ve already given me pause, bc what arrived was a tangle of about ½ pound of linguine drowning in a watery ‘sauce’ with barely detectable porcini flavor. Adding insult to injury, there wasn’t a SINGLE porcini mushroom — just regular ole button mushrooms (about 4-5 pieces), yet the place has the audacity to charge a whopping $30 for the plate 😱

My partner's rigatoni were just alright. He was hungry. The best part of the meal was the Josh rosé we brought. Meh.

I wish I’d read all the negative reviews here on the place, most of which are countered by the owner in a highly unprofessional manner. Looking forward to his comments on mine 😂

*On their takeout/delivery page, the same dish is described as “fresh pasta, imported porcini mushrooms, and jus cream sauce.”

Lies. 1/10. Best to skip this one.

We split the garlicky, buttery mussels — probz the highlight of the meal, as well as a highly unremarkable Caesar with ‘homemade’ dressing that was barely there.

As for the pasta, I ordered the fresh linguine with imported porcini jus (sic!) and cream*, figuring it had to be the star of the menu, being the namesake of the place and all, and my dining companion got the rigatoni with sweet sausage and rustic tomato sauce.

Perhaps the phrasing / description of my pasta dish should’ve already given me pause, bc what arrived was a tangle of about ½ pound of linguine drowning in a watery ‘sauce’ with barely detectable porcini flavor. Adding insult to injury, there wasn’t a SINGLE porcini mushroom — just regular ole button mushrooms (about 4-5 pieces), yet the place has the audacity to charge a whopping $30 for the plate 😱

My partner's rigatoni were just alright. He was hungry. The best part of the meal was the Josh rosé we brought. Meh.

I wish I’d read all the negative reviews here on the place, most of which are countered by the owner in a highly unprofessional manner. Looking forward to his comments on mine 😂

*On their takeout/delivery page, the same dish is described as “fresh pasta, imported porcini mushrooms, and jus cream sauce.”

Lies. 1/10. Best to skip this one.

text.text:
We had a great dining experience at Veda Restaurant. The Mango Lassi was excellent (5/5), and the vegetable soup was full of flavor with a pleasant, aromatic spice rather than just heat.

The dahi kebab came as a serving of 3 pieces. While I wish the portion was a bit larger, the taste was outstanding, with subtle cardamom and black pepper notes wrapped in a crispy, savory crust.

For the mains, we ordered Palak Paneer and Chicken Lababdar, both served with rice. The portions were generous and more than enough for the three of us. We also tried the garlic naan and chili cilantro naan, which were the only items that didn't quite meet the same standard as the rest of the meal.

Overall, the food was flavorful, the portions were generous, and we'd definitely come back. Just hope to see the naan improve next time!

text.text:
I really wanted to enjoy this place, but unfortunately our experience was very disappointing and concerning. There were four of us dining together last night. We started with the chicken murmuri appetizer, which was actually quite good and gave us high hopes.

For entrées, we ordered goat cheese naan, chicken chettinad, Bombay goat curry, and palak paneer. Almost immediately after taking our first bites, all four of us commented that something felt “off” about the food. The chicken chettinad was clearly undercooked — the chicken was chewy and had a raw texture that made it difficult to eat. The Bombay goat curry also did not taste right and felt questionable.

At the time, we didn’t want to create an issue and decided not to say anything to the manager, which in hindsight we regret. Later that night, all four of us experienced stomach issues, and two people ended up vomiting.

This was not just a matter of taste or preference — undercooked meat is a serious food safety concern. I truly wish we had spoken up in the moment, and I hope the management takes food preparation and quality control more seriously to prevent this from happening to other guests.

text.text:
The food here was excellent. The braised short rib pappardelle was the highlight of the meal—the beef was incredibly tender, full of flavor, and clearly slow-braised with care. The homemade pasta paired perfectly with the rich sauce. The truffle fries were also very good. I especially appreciated the Parmesan and flaky sea salt, which elevated what could have been an ordinary side dish.

Unfortunately, the service was a completely different story.

I understand that every server has their own style, but there are a few basic parts of the dining experience that I expect from a full-service restaurant. During my visit, it was around 3:45 PM, well outside the lunch and dinner rush, and there were only about three occupied tables in the entire restaurant. Because of that, it didn’t seem like the staff was overwhelmed.

Normally, the experience would be something like this:

* Welcome guests and bring the complimentary bread.
* Let guests take their time with the menu instead of making them feel rushed.
* Check back after the food arrives to ask if everything is okay.
* Refill water or ask whether another drink is needed.

Unfortunately, none of those things happened during our meal.

Our server came to the table several times before we ordered, but each visit felt more like she was checking whether we were finally ready rather than making us feel welcome. We were never offered the complimentary bread. I eventually had to ask another server, who immediately took care of it, and someone from the kitchen even brought the bread to our table. After our food was served, our server never returned once—not to ask how everything was, not to refill water, and not to see if we needed anything else.

I do want to emphasize that this review reflects the service provided by our server, not necessarily the restaurant as a whole. The other staff member I spoke with was prompt and helpful, and the kitchen responded immediately once the issue was brought to their attention. The kitchen clearly knows what they’re doing, and the food easily deserves five stars. I would happily return for the food and hope to have a better service experience next time.

From the moment we walked in, the experience set the tone for a great night. The ambiance was warm and inviting, with that perfect candlelit vibe that makes you slow down and actually enjoy the moment.
We started with a shrimp scampi that was cooked to perfection—tender, buttery, and full of flavor without being overpowering. For the main course, the lobster fri diovlo that delivered in every way: perfectly cooked, rich tomato sauce, and balanced seasoning that tied everything together.
What really elevated the night was the service. Joe was excellent—attentive, professional, and made sure we were taken care of without ever being intrusive. Basil, the manager, was just as impressive, checking in and making sure everything met a high standard. That level of hospitality doesn’t go unnoticed.
Overall, this wasn’t just a meal—it was a full experience. Great food, great service, and a vibe that makes you want to come back again.

text.text:
A Delightful Morning at K'Far Cafe Philly

I recently stopped by K'Far Cafe in Rittenhouse for a morning bite, and it was absolutely delightful. From the moment I walked in, I was struck by how inviting the space is. The pastel interior, with its bright, airy feel, creates such a warm and cheerful atmosphere.

I ordered the famous Egg and Cheese Jerusalem Bagel, and it did not disappoint. The egg was unbelievably fluffy, like a pillow, and combined with the melty cheese, it created the most perfect, soft texture in every bite. But the real star was the delightful, peppery aftertaste left by the schug. It added an incredible layer of flavor that lingered just long enough to make each bite exciting.

To wash it down, I tried one of their signature coffee drinks, which was perfectly rich and well-balanced. If you're looking for a gorgeous cafe with food that has complex and memorable flavors, K'Far is an absolute must-visit in Philly.
