text.text:
K’Far shows how much atmosphere CookNSolo can create within a relatively compact footprint. It has the ease of a neighborhood café, yet the confidence, visual sophistication, and social energy of a much larger restaurant. We have eaten at the high tops, in the main dining room, and at the tables extending into The Harper lobby, and each area feels like part of the same unified experience. The colors and lighting inside are especially warm and inviting, giving the room a glow that feels cozy and uplifting, especially during a Philadelphia winter.

Food remains at the center of the experience, and my order is always the Jerusalem bagel with egg and cheese. On the rare occasions when turkey bacon appears, I add it as a welcome delicacy and a little extra sustenance, though the bagel is already delicious on its own. The cinnamon sugar kubaneh, the chocolate chip cookie, and the Bloody Mary are excellent. K’Far has also expanded its selection of bowls and salads since we ate here most regularly, and they look consistent with the quality of everything else.

These days, a full breakfast here does not always fit within our budget, but I still make a point of stopping in for OX Coffee, which is delicious and, happily, roasted in Philadelphia. The Yemenite latte is another distinctive pleasure, aromatic and satisfying without feeling like a novelty created merely for attention. The staff is consistently charming, welcoming, and composed, and the team's continuity and energy suggest that people genuinely enjoy working here. When our budget allows, I will absolutely return to eat.

Perhaps the clearest expression of K’Far’s brilliance arrives in one memory from a cold, radiantly sunny Saturday, when “Inspector Norse” by the Norwegian producer Todd Terje comes through the speakers as the restaurant buzzes around us. The track, the worldly crowd, and the aroma from the kitchen create the elusive feeling Steve Cook and Mike Solomonov understand so well: people go out to eat because they want to feel seen and be briefly transported into a more vivid version of life. I already love K’Far and The Hoxton as separate brands, so seeing them come together at The Hoxton in Williamsburg feels like an unusually natural and exciting partnership. Creating this kind of social magnetism inside a bakery and café is a subtle achievement, and Philadelphia is richer for having a place with this much flavor, warmth, and personality.

text.text:
This has got to be one of the best prime rib restaurants I’ve come across. I usually book restaurants like this only during the AMEX quarterly promotion through Resy, which makes the experience even better. We went during Valentine’s Day week on a weekday, and the atmosphere was perfect, quiet, relaxed, and unhurried. There was no wait and no rush, which made the evening feel even more enjoyable. The live piano music added a romantic touch, and our server was very attentive throughout the night.

For appetizers, we ordered the seafood tower and calamari, both of which were excellent. If you’re going for the prime rib, I highly recommend ordering the Rittenhouse cut. The double-cut prime rib is massive and could easily feed three people and I barely made a dent in mine. Overall, it was a great dining experience for our group of three couples, and gratuity was already included for a party of six. It is definitely on the expensive side as we spent about $1,300 for the evening but the quality and atmosphere made it worthwhile.

The only downside was the valet parking confusion. We called ahead to confirm valet parking since it was listed on the restaurant’s website, but when we arrived, the hostess told us there was no valet available. Fortunately, since it was a weekday, we were able to find street parking using the ParkMobile app. Better communication on that detail would have helped.

Overall, a fantastic experience and a great spot for a special occasion or date night.

text.text:
I do want to start this post off with that I am a Lebanese person myself who LIVES for a good Shawarma wrap. Chicken Shawarma is the best part of every trip back home and trust me, I am a harsh critic when it comes to this because I have tasted heaven in a wrap. I was told to try this locations Chicken Shawarma because it was extremely good and similar to Lebanon, so I did. I went into the location and ordered a Chicken Shawarma with extra Thoum and Spicy Jalapeño Sauce/Green sauce. I was baffled that there was no vertical skewer in sight and the portioning of the Thoum when told for extra was so scarce. On the other hand, the chicken portion was very generous so no complaints there. The staff were rude themselves when requested to add extra of any topping and they simply will not give you extra. Hospitality should NOT be expected when coming here. It was so unprofessional, but it is in no way shape or form to be connected to the Lebanese/Middle Eastern culture as that is the complete opposite of what defines us. The wait time was little to none and your food comes out in less than 5-7 minutes. The taste of the Shawarma is probably the closest to genuine Lebanese food you will get in the US. It is indeed Lebanese but it is not elevated as they claim to be delivering. If you are looking for genuine, and this goes for every Middle Eastern place in the US, you’re better off tasting the real deal in the country it comes from. Shawarma in Lebanon will always be far more superior than it is here, but hats off for making such a close comparison to it here.

In conclusion, the food was close enough to Shawarma in Lebanon but has way more evolution to do. The staff were terrible. Atmosphere and colors gave off a very welcoming vibe, and the seating was great. I do hope to see this company succeed 🇱🇧❤️.

3/5 Stars for food, 1/5 stars for service, 5/5 stars for atmosphere.

Amanda provided excellent service. She answered our questions and provided spot-on suggestions on menu items. The food was well prepared. We had the Branzino, which was delicious. Our other entree was Tartufate (pappardelle pasta, truffle oil, walnuts, pecorino cheese) It is a heavy dish, but it is unique and tasty.

At the end of the meal, we ordered tiramisu and coffee. Amanda overheard us talking about my birthday, and when she brought the tiramisu to the table, there was a lit candle on top. Nice touch! And she prepared a cup of coffee that tasted great.

The atmosphere is nice and not stuffy. We enjoyed the experience and will return.

text.text:
Melograno was a very pleasant and enjoyable Italian BYOB that I can best summarize as "nothing wrong with it but not impressive enough to return". While I liked the rustic Roman-inspired interior and the friendly staff, most of the food was simply fine and not especially remarkable.

For a starter we ordered the gnocchi croquettes that embodied my feelings mentioned above; they were fluffy and pleasant but didn't leave too much of an impression, and they did feel a bit pricey for how small they were. The highlight of all the food was my pasta dish the "granchio", with crab, cherry tomatoes, bread crumbs, and a lemon cream sauce. It's probably the one thing we had that I would go out of my way to recommend as the flavors and textures were great, even if the cream sauce was a little thick bordering on coagulated. My wife's duck ragu on the other hand was much less compelling. The pasta was too soft leading to a mushy feeling dish, and the flavors were fine but didn't impress.

Finally, desserts were par for the course. I ordered the daily special which was a caramel panna cotta (I think?) with whipped cream and blueberries which was ok, but tasted quite eggy which was unexpected. My wife had the tiramisu which was a generous portion and enjoyable enough, but also nothing special.

I would certainly not dissuade anyone from trying Melograno, as it provided a very acceptably nice evening and it's a BYO which you can't complain about. Maybe some of the other dishes are more impressive that will have people coming back. For me however, it didn't do enough to justify a return when there are many similar restaurants in the area.

text.text:
Devil's Alley Bar & Grill was one of my favorite hangout spots in Philadelphia for years, from December 2013 all the way through January 2020. It became my go-to place for after-hours drinks, and I brought so many friends and coworkers here over that stretch — it never disappointed.
The drinks were always solid, but honestly, the baby back ribs are what kept bringing me back. Consistently good, fall-off-the-bone quality, and the perfect pairing after a long work day or a night out.
I haven't been back since the pandemic started, but this place holds a special spot in my Philly memories. Really hoping to make it back soon to see if the magic is still there. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a solid bar and grill with great food and an easy, welcoming vibe.

text.text: Huda is an absolute revelation in the Philadelphia food scene, serving up a masterclass smashburger defined by its lacy-edged patties and pillowy, house-made Japanese milk buns. It is a chef-driven, high-end culinary destination that comfortably claims the title for the best burger-and-fries duo in the city

I’ve been wanting to try Huda for a long time and finally got takeout! I got the spicy chicken sandwich and a side of small fries.

Price for the chicken sandwich is high (almost $17 without fries) and while it is on the larger side, the chicken was thin. I expected it to be juicier and thicker. I enjoyed the sauce and the bun. Fries were crispy, but a little over fried. They were hard, but I’m glad they weren’t soggy.

For the high price tag, I was a bit let down in the sandwich. I hear they have good smash burgers so maybe I’ll try that next!

We went to Huda for lunch. We ordered the smash burger with an extra patty and sauce on the side. We also ordered the fries with the house made ranch.

The burger was insanely good. It was juicy, cooked perfectly, cheesy and gooey. They give you wet naps for a reason. The bun was so soft but the toast on it gave it a perfect crunch. The onions and cheese were just right. This is one of the better burgers I’ve ever had.

The fries were salty and crispy and seasoned well. I used the ranch to dip them. The buttermilk and dill just worked so perfectly to offset the saltiness of the fries. It was just perfect.

Do not miss this spot!

text.text:
Overall loved the atmosphere and meat dishes and desserts!

For appetizers, we ordered skewers (pinchas de pork, chicken, and shrimp). Sauce for the skewers was interesting the brown sauce was fruity/jammy and paired well especially with the pork and chicken (rating it a 8/10). The mussel ceviche tasted overpoweringly of just antipasto peppers + fishiness (rating it a 6/10). The bacalaitos were DELICIOUS and the crab salad was alright (rating it a 7/10).

For the main course, we ordered vaca frita (9/10), seafood asapao (7/10), imperial chicken rice (6/10, chicken was tender and well done but not as noteworthy especially after the pinchas, and the rice was also a bit too salty and oily, it felt like I had to chug water), and short rib carne guisada with a side of extra rice (7/10, ribs were delicious but the dish was also too salty).

For dessert, flan con queso (9/10, so delicious loved water the tomato looking topping was), tembleque (7/10 for me because I love coconut and coconut smoothies but 2/10 for my family who compared the taste to the smell of dirty socks), and Buñuelos (7/10 anything fried is delicious and the chocolatey sauce was wonderful)

text.text:
I went here with a friend for dinner for restaurant week in the beginning of February!

Food: 5/5. It was SO absolutely divine and delicious. The flavors and food were unlike any I’ve tried before. The meat was so tender and soft. Every single one of the dishes was unique and left an amazing impression. I loved everything we had.

Service: 4/5. Our waiter was sweet and friendly. The only thing I have to say is that the service felt rushed, despite there being a good amount of empty tables when we went on a Monday night. The dessert came out just 15-20 minutes into our main entree and the check shortly after, despite us not asking for it yet. Thankfully the desserts weren’t meant to be had warm otherwise they would’ve been cold by the time we had them. But overall, it was still very good!

Atmosphere: 5/5 I loved it. The interior was so aesthetic, with the first floor having more of a moody, darkly lit bar vibe and the second floor semi-brighter with lots of plants and colorful paintings. The interior was absolutely gorgeous, and definitely one of the best in Philly.

Highly recommend checking this spot out for a date night and/or nice dinner night out.

text.text:
The food and drinks were amazing. Definitely try the Bolo beer. I’ve been to so many restaurants around Rittenhouse, and somehow this one was still on my list to try. I’m so glad we finally did because the food truly lived up to the hype.

The standout for us was the ceviche sampler. Every ingredient complemented the others perfectly, and every bite was bursting with flavor. It was like a party in your mouth (exactly what I told my husband). the one that have jalapeños was surprisingly not very spicy and I enjoyed it very much. Wish the portions are a bit bigger but they are called sampler for a reason. 🤷‍♀️ Everything we ordered was delicious.🤤

The service was also excellent. Our server was attentive throughout the meal, and we never had to wait for our water glasses to be refilled. We were so happy with his service that instead of adding the tip to our credit card, we gave him cash so he could receive the full amount.

The restaurant wasn’t particularly baby-friendly since they didn’t have a high chair, but honestly, that didn’t bother us. We made it work because the food and service were so good.

Unfortunately, one thing completely ruined the experience once we got home. We asked to have the rest of our short rib entrée and the leftover chicharrones appetizer packed to go because our baby was getting fussy and we needed to leave. The chicharrones, which we had barely touched because they were still too hot to eat, were packed in the same paper container as the short rib. Because it was a paper container, the sauce from the short rib soaked into the chicharrones, making them soggy and completely changing the flavor and texture. By the time we got home, they tasted awful and were no longer enjoyable.

It was disappointing because this could have easily been avoided by using one extra container to separate the two dishes. ☹️Considering the quality of the restaurant and the price of the meal, sparing one additional container would have preserved the food instead of ruining it.

Overall wonderful dining experience with just a little hiccup.

Overall: Great experience, very cool cuban/latin ambiance, excellent food!

Not sure how this place is not 4.9*  - it surely feels and tastes like it! Not surprised one bit this was already a James Beard nominee within its first 3 years of existence.

One of the best places we've been to this year.

Unbelievable atmosphere.
Food is absolutely killer - not sure there is anything that is not mind blowing good on the menu
Drinks were bang on.

AND they accommodated all allergies like it was nothing.

Tostones are not your usual tostones. More like garlic bread but way better (with a little zing), pinchos de panza melts in your mouth, short rib oh-so-good, etc. all accompanying sauces were delicious. we ordered so much food. Left full and happy.

text.text: My partner and I had a lovely breakfast here on Saturday morning. We made reservations for 9am, it wasn’t too busy at that time when we arrived. The host and waitstaff were very kind and informative! I got a cappuccino (with oatmilk) an omelette with a side of breakfast potatoes, my partner got two espressos and the farmhouse breakfast. The food was excellent and came out in a timely manner. The coffee, which is Rival Bros, was exceptional. The atmosphere was great, the space is tastefully decorated. Just staring up at the ceiling has great views. It was on the expensive side for breakfast, about $70 for two. But this was a special treat and it was money well spent! It would be a great place to go for a pre-show drink before heading to the Kimmel center. The space itself is smaller, there were about 10 tables and seems best suited for parties of 1-4 people.

text.text:
I recently dined at Condesa in Rittenhouse Square to celebrate my wife's birthday, and it was one of the best restaurant experiences I've had in Philly. From the moment we walked in, the vibe was vibrant yet sophisticated—beautiful decor inspired by Mexico City, with that perfect mix of energy and comfort in the heart of the city.
The food was outstanding. We started with the fresh guacamole and house-made salsas, which were bursting with flavor, then moved on to tacos featuring their incredible heirloom corn tortillas (they mill it themselves—such attention to detail!). The carnitas were tender and perfectly seasoned, and the cocktails (especially the mezcal-based ones) were creative and spot-on. Everything felt elevated without being pretentious—true modern Mexican done right.
But what really made the night unforgettable was the service. The entire staff was warm, knowledgeable, and genuinely attentive. They checked in at just the right moments, offered great recommendations, and made us feel welcome from start to finish. The team clearly takes pride in what they do, and it shows in every interaction.
A huge shoutout to Emily who went above and beyond to ensure we had an amazing experience. She personally made sure every dish came out perfectly timed, suggested pairings that were spot-on, and even swung by multiple times to check if everything was to our liking, with such genuine warmth and enthusiasm. Her care turned a great meal into something memorable and special. Servers like Emily are rare, and she made us feel like VIPs.
If you're looking for delicious food in a lively atmosphere with top-tier hospitality, Condesa is a must-visit. We'll definitely be back—thank you to Emily and the whole team for making our evening so wonderful!
Highly recommend! 🌮✨

text.text:
I had an amazing dining experience at this Mexican restaurant!
From start to finish, everything was exceptional.

We ordered Papas a la Mexicana, Brisket Tacos, Pescado Frito Tacos, and Pollo Asado, and every single dish was full of authentic flavor and perfectly cooked. The highlight at the end was the chocolate meringue dessert, which was the perfect sweet finish to our meal.

The service was outstanding — our server knew the menu very well and answered all of our questions with confidence and kindness. We truly felt welcomed and taken care of.

The pricing was very fair considering the quality and portion sizes. The atmosphere was warm, clean, and inviting, making it a perfect place to relax and enjoy a great meal.

I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for delicious Mexican food, excellent service, and a wonderful dining environment.
We will definitely be back!

text.text:
I was originally planning to grab something quick before heading back to the hotel, but I walked past this place and changed my mind almost immediately. The room had a nice buzz without feeling chaotic, and the smell coming from the kitchen made ordering harder than I expected. I finally settled on the oysters on the half shell, lobster roll, New England clam chowder, and crab fries.

The oysters were the first thing I reached for, and they tasted clean and fresh with just a squeeze of lemon. The clam chowder came next and had a creamy texture without feeling too heavy, which made it easy to keep eating. I usually order a lobster roll whenever I see one on the menu, and this one didn't disappoint. There was plenty of lobster, the roll was lightly toasted, and nothing overwhelmed the seafood itself. I thought the crab fries would just be something to share, but I kept grabbing another handful until they were gone.

Walking back outside, I realized it had turned into one of those meals where everything just clicked. Nothing was overcomplicated. Good seafood, friendly service, and a place I'd happily return to the next time I'm in Philadelphia.

text.text: If you are visiting Philly, you have no choice, you must try this place. It’s the first place I visited when I moved here and it’s still a place I want to bring my friends and family back to time and time again. Well rotated menu. Excellent vibe. The hustle and bustle, the drinks being made, the oysters being shucked, the kitchen busting their asses, pan after pan, and oysters decorated all around you. Maybe I wish I could hear the person I’m with, even when it’s a crowded night. It’s a bummer to be eating peek bliss food and drink, but I can’t hear my partners joke from across the table. For this reason, I believe most of the time the oyster bar seating is best when only with one other person. Service is always excellent, and you’ll always get the sense people know how to execute their job responsibilities. Every server here does their job well. They read their tables well.  The food never disappoints. You can only expect a really high standard of excellence out of their kitchen.

text.text:
A Must-Visit Lunch Spot in Philadelphia!
Visited Cava on Chestnut Street for a family lunch with 4 and ordered the Greens and Grains Bowls — and we were thoroughly impressed! The best part about Cava is how customisable the bowls are. From choosing your greens and grains to loading up on toppings like falafel, roasted veggies, hummus, fire roasted corn, Persian cucumber, fiery broccoli, and an amazing selection of dressings and dips — every bowl felt personal and packed with flavour.
The portions were generous, the quality was excellent, and the pricing felt very reasonable for what you get. The ambience was pleasant and the location on Chestnut Street is super convenient.
All four of us thoroughly enjoyed our meals — not a single complaint at the table! If you’re in Philadelphia and anywhere near Chestnut Street, this place is an absolute must. Highly recommend! 🥙🌿

Absolutely love CAVA!

Cava is hands-down one of the best fast-casual restaurants I’ve been to. The food is always fresh, flavorful, and high-quality, and you can really taste the care that goes into every ingredient. I love how customizable the bowls and pitas are — whether you want something healthy, filling, or indulgent, there’s always a perfect option.

The ingredients are vibrant and delicious, from the tender proteins to the bold dips, spreads, and toppings. Everything tastes clean, well-seasoned, and satisfying without feeling heavy. Plus, the portions are generous and worth the price.

The staff is consistently friendly, patient, and efficient, and the restaurant is usually clean, modern, and welcoming. Even during busy times, the service stays quick and organized.

If you’re looking for a spot that’s healthy, tasty, filling, and reliable, Cava is a top-tier choice. I always leave happy and looking forward to my next visit!

Where do I even begin? If you are considering a reservation here, don't think twice—just book it.
The ambience is a solid five stars. We were lucky enough to be seated in the upstairs chef’s pasta room, which provided such a unique and intimate backdrop for the evening.
We were a group of five and opted for the **Chef’s Tasting**, which was the best decision we could have made. Every single dish was unique, layered in flavor, and incredibly well-executed. We started with the focaccia, which is so good it honestly can’t be put into words—it’s a mandatory order.
As for the mains, the pasta courses were the stars of the show:
* **Rigatoni with Beef Cheeks:** Rich, tender, and perfectly seasoned.
* **Lamb Cavatelli:** Deeply savory and unique.
* **Shrimp & Crab Spaghetti:** Fresh, bright, and packed with seafood.
We also rounded out the meal with the asparagus a perfectly prepared branzino, and finished with the chocolate hazelnut dessert, which was the perfect end to the night. Even the cocktails were next level—creative and expertly balanced.

My fiancé and I went out for our anniversary dinner last night. The service was great—very friendly and attentive. The appetizers were a strong start: the guacamole and ceviche were both delicious and well prepared.

Unfortunately, the experience fell short when it came to the entrées. I paid $44 for a plate of small, barely any meat, langostines that were extremely overcooked and completely lacking in flavor. I was hoping the sauces would help, but they tasted more like cocktail sauces and didn’t elevate the dish at all. The rice served alongside was lukewarm, as were the langostines themselves, which was disappointing.

Thankfully, my fiancé had a more pleasant experience with the molcajete, which he enjoyed.

After the entrée experience, dessert felt like a safer choice. I ordered the tres leches, but it was very basic to my taste—honestly less flavorful than versions I’ve had from a local Latin supermarket.

text.text:
Tequilas has always been one of Center City’s gems and one of my my favorite Mexican restaurants in the city. After being closed for a while due to the fire, it’s safe to say they’ve come back better than ever. The food is outstanding; each dish beautifully presented and layered with authentic flavors that feel both refined and comforting... From the tender barbacoa bathed in rich consommé to the fresh guacamole con atún and the indulgent queso fundido, every bite feels like a celebration of Mexican tradition elevated to fine dining.

The service deserves its own praise. You can tell the entire staff, like the servers, busboys, food runners, they all work seamlessly together as a true team. Everyone is attentive, warm, and genuinely passionate about creating a great experience.

Tequilas is not just a meal, it’s an experience- one that reminds you why this restaurant has such a loyal following in Philadelphia. I’m so glad they’re back, and even more impressed by how they’ve elevated every detail. Highly, highly recommend!

The texture was very smooth and it was a very interesting interpretation of the traditional crab cake. I love to see what a chef will create if left to his/her own devices so I loved it personally. It felt like it was cooked in a sous vide or possibly a baño María… me likey.

I do recommend this place it’s lovely.

I understand the hype around Parc; I just came back from France and yes, it has all the styling of a bistro but... meets Cheesecake Factory in terms of the scale/size of the restaurant, ha. It's a bustling and noisy inside but very charming.

The food is pretty outstanding as well:
*Pastry Basket ($17 - lemon poppy seed cake, blueberry lemon tart, pistachio raspberry danish, pain au chocolate, croissant, chouquettes) - all the pastries were so perfectly baked!
*Onion Soup Gratinée - for $20, French Onion soup better be outstanding and it was! It was lovely - savory with the little bit of funk from the gruyere on the nose and a slightly sweet broth from the onions. Lovely.
*French Toast ($18 - blueberries, chantilly crème, lime zest, maple syrup) - this STOLE the show. I am not a french toast girlie but Parc has made me a french toast girlie. It was soaked lightly and soft and pillow-y. The fresh blueberries and lime zest with the luscious yet light chantilly - CHEF'S KISS!

We first visited Parc back in 2018, and we've been talking about coming back ever since. This week we finally had the chance when we met a client for dinner.

We arrived about 45 minutes before our reservation, so we grabbed seats at the bar and enjoyed a glass of wine while people-watching. The sidewalk tables were packed, and inside the restaurant every table seemed full. Even with how busy they were, everything moved smoothly.

When our client arrived, we were seated right on time.

We shared the tomato salad and the beet salad to start. Both were excellent. I had the New York strip, Trish ordered the trout, and both meals were cooked exactly as ordered. One thing we really appreciated was the portion size. Sometimes higher-end restaurants serve beautiful food but leave you wishing for more. That definitely wasn't the case here.

The service was friendly, attentive, and never rushed. We enjoyed another glass of wine, caught up with our client, and before we knew it, it was after 11:00 PM. What surprised us was that the dining room was still about three-quarters full on a Wednesday night.

Parc reminded us exactly why we'd wanted to come back. Great food, a fun atmosphere, excellent service, and an enjoyable evening with good company. It won't take us another eight years before our next visit.

text.text: Came here for dinner for the first time today. Our server was amazing really friendly and attentive. During the entire meal we had multiple servers serving us but the main one came by to check on us quite often to make sure everything was fine. All the food was really flavourful and we enjoyed every dishes. Since during my reservation I indicated it was my birthday so they brought out a lit candle on a plate. I’m Chinese so based on our culture it’s not lucky to put a lit candle on a plate because that’s when we pay our respects to our deceased ancestors we would light candles and place them on a small plate and incense. So just a thought perhaps put the lit candle on the dessert or throw a couple pieces of fruits onto the plate with a lit candle. Overall it was a great meal and I would definitely come back.

A. Kitchen stands out for what matters most: exceptional food and a thoughtfully curated wine program.
Every dish we tried was beautifully executed, with high-quality ingredients and great balance.
The wine program deserves special mention. The selection was exceptional, with a thoughtfully curated list that offered everything from classic producers to more unique and lesser-known bottles.
Exploring the list felt both educational and enjoyable rather than overwhelming.
Whether you’re a serious wine enthusiast looking to discover something new or simply hoping to enjoy a great bottle with dinner, you’re in very capable hands.
Thank you to the team for helping us celebrate my boyfriend’s birthday and making the evening feel memorable!

text.text:
We went here for lunch and dined on the rooftop patio around 1:30 PM. It wasn’t too busy which made for a really relaxing experience. The atmosphere was nice and the interior downstairs is beautiful with plenty of seating areas.

One thing that was a little confusing was the hours online, it showed the kitchen was closed and reopening at 5 PM even though lunch hours were listed until 3 PM. Thankfully, we called ahead to confirm and they were open.

We started with the edamame which was delicious. For my main plate, I ordered the seared tuna with mushroom risotto. The tuna itself was good, but the sauce was a bit overpowering for my taste. I also tried the blackberry mango marteani which was a little too sweet for me personally.

Overall, it was still a nice lunch spot with a great rooftop atmosphere and beautiful ambiance.

(My only suggestion would be to wipe down the walls at the end of meal service, especially the white ones along the downstairs windows.)

text.text: This was our first visit to The Continental Mid-town and we were excited when we walked in because it had such a great vibe. We went to celebrate a birthday and had a wonderful time. Our waiter was great, attentive, and so kind and patient with all the menu questions I asked because of some dietary limitations I have. We had two starters - the crispy brussel sprouts (pictured) and bbq chicken quesadilla - fabulous - and four entrees - the seared tuna (pictured), killer shrimp (pictured), the chicken tikka masala, and the strip steak. One was better than the next. It was one of the best steaks I've had, cooked perfectly medium, and the coconut thai curry with the killer shrimp was phenomenal. The seared tuna with mushroom risotto was outstanding. I didn't taste the chicken tikka masala but was told it was very good. When they brought it to the table, I immediately caught the scent of authentic masala, which was amazing. You can't go wrong with any of these dishes. If you're looking for a fun restaurant with a great vibe and unique layout (the second floor had tables for two with swinging chairs), look no further. We cannot recommend this more highly.

text.text: Jean-George rooftop bar/restaurant atop the Four Seasons in Philly. Lots of windows and mirrors making it look very spacious. There was a live band playing that day which made it a little extra special. Credit card deposit to make the reservation for a prix fixe brunch. Service is kind of slow. The food was delicious. Avocado toast, the warm Brie with pita, the lobster risotto were all highly recommendable.  Desert is included and when you go down the stairs to the lower level, the bar is setup with a massive spread of dessert bites. Delicious. Great place to go for special occasions or to impress a date! Day time views of Philly aren’t that amazing but it must be gorgeous at night.

We celebrated our wedding anniversary at Jean-Georges Philadelphia, and it was such a wonderful experience from beginning to end.

The service was absolutely phenomenal, attentive, warm, and incredibly thoughtful without ever feeling intrusive. Every course was introduced to us with such care, from the ingredients and flavors to the details behind the presentation. You could really tell how much attention goes into every part of the dining experience. Whenever we needed anything, the team was always there and happy to help.

The food was just as impressive. Every dish was beautifully presented, creative, and full of flavor. The attention to detail, both in the food and the service, made the entire evening feel truly special.

It was the perfect place to celebrate our anniversary, and they made the occasion even more memorable. Exceptional food, outstanding service, and a beautiful atmosphere.

Pleased to see they open at 4:30, I chose this place because of a train schedule. Also, the menu is just what I like.
I could tell that I surprised/confused the staff by entering at 4:45. They recovered quickly and seated me courteously. I was seated in a greenhouse room (glass wall and roof) which was cold. Later, someone turned on a ceiling-mounted heater. The temperature went from 66 to 70F in about 20 minutes. (Thermometer on the wall.)
There were dried-out Christmas decorations all around me; on March 2nd.  (See pic)
The Brussels sprouts were as good as everyone says: their appearance, their flavor, and their texture.
The server, Emi, and the cooks accommodated my special request. I was very happy to try the crispy gnocchi. Their texture, inside and out, was perfection. I could tell they were made in house.
The restrooms (down stairs) were spotlessly clean, but the (non-slip?) rugs on the stairs could use a good cleaning.

text.text: WOW it’s been a while since I had this kind of feeling of awe at a restaurant especially all my usual favorite places had gotten downhill after COVID or closed. This place restored my faith in Philly dining. Through the complementary bread with the most delectable special sun dried tomato oil dip and then the crispy Brussels sprouts and beets… I found myself thinking if vegetables always tasted like this I’d eat them all the time. The goat cheese that came with the dish was literally perfect and whipped and light without that heavy pungent kick that usually makes me not like goat cheese. Each bite of the beet salad was both beautiful (it had two kinds of beets in it) and so refreshing to taste. Both of these dishes brought my soul back to life as the freshness invigorated me. I got the branzino and the skin was so delightfully crispy while the fish was perfectly cooked tender over a bed of grilled corn. Finished off with tiramisu for dessert. Definitely need to come back the next time I’m in town to try other dishes!!

Ambrosia absolutely delivered from start to finish. Every dish felt thoughtful, vibrant, and dialed in.

The hamachi crudo was incredibly fresh—clean, bright, and the perfect way to open. The Brussels sprouts with labneh and pomegranate seeds were a standout—rich, tangy, and lifted with just the right pop of sweetness and texture.

From there, things only got better. The octopus was beautifully grilled, tender with a perfect char, paired with a bright, herbaceous salsa verde that brought everything to life. The squid ink pasta was deep and briny in the best way, loaded with crab and calamari—comforting yet refined.

The branzino was expertly crisped, flaking perfectly, complemented by a corn salsa that was fresh, balanced, and full of flavor.

Finished with an excellent espresso martini and a black raspberry gelato that was light, vivant, and the perfect sweet note to close.

A truly standout meal—thoughtful execution, bold flavors, and a kitchen that clearly cares.

The one saving grace was the dessert at the end, which was genuinely the highlight of the entire meal and felt like it belonged to a completely different level of quality compared to everything else.

Overall, it felt inconsistent and not worth the visit, aside from the dessert at the end.

text.text:
My Loup is the sister restaurant to Her Place Supper Club, and was absolutely incredible. Went here with a friend for an end of sem/year celebration in mid December.

Taste: 5/5. Absolutely divine. Presentation, quality, and flavor combinations were done incredibly well. Everything we tried was so distinct and delicious. We didn’t do the tasting menu, hence why the price pp was lower than what Google rates it as, but it could easily become $100+ with it and/or more dishes.

Service: 5/5. Fast, attentive, and patient. We asked our waitress for suggestions and her preferences and she patiently guided us through the menu, and continuously checked in throughout our dining experience.

Atmosphere: 5/5. Absolutely loved it. It was dark, cozy, and extremely well decorated. It was beautiful and easily one of the best interiors of any restaurant I’ve seen in Philly.

If you are looking for a higher-end date night and/or friends night out, highly recommend checking out My Loup!

text.text:
I haven't seen my Cuzn since we dined at Louis Vuitton Cafe in NYC. Called her up and asked her to join me for a late dinner. She obliged me. I made reservations (day of) for 8:30 pm. We were a little late due to traffic, but our reservation was still honored.

Our seating was inside and upstairs (which we appreciated b|c it rained while we were dining)

Ambiance was lovely, dimly lit and romantic if you're on a date. Restaurant is family friendly!!

We were quickly sat, our waiter introduced himself to us -- lovely gentleman by the name of Vincenzo?!? He was effortlessly efficient and friendly. Made our night exceptional.

My cousin said it was late and she didn't want to really order anything. I talked her into ordering and then at least she could eat the leftovers for "midnight snacking" or lunch the next day.

We ordered:

-- Bellini: Prosecco infused peach purée

-- Bread

-- Scamorza -- Fire-roasted aged mozzarella, prosciutto

-- Torta Granchio -- Italian crab cake infused with crab, shrimp, and mascarpone served with cucumber fresco and gastronomic roasted red pepper gelato

-- Cesarina -- Kale, romaine, creamy Parmigiano dressing

-- Agnolotti -- Torino-style Ravioli filled with veal, pork, and vegetables. Butter sage sauce topped with gastronomic black and white truttle gelato

-- Pappardelle al Ragu -- Ribbon pasta, slow cooked pork, veal, lamb and chicken ragu (my cuzn's meal)

-- Tiramisu Classico -- Lady fingers, espresso, mascarpone

Everything was delicious, especially the Torta Granchio. Gran Caffè L'Aquila needs to lead with this appetizer. It was delicious. My cousin and I ordered two more to go!!

Our pasta meals were decadent and delicious. We shared the tiramisu and we both agreed it was fantastic. Classic is the way to go. We left with full bellies after having wonderful conversation.

We both agreed we'd be back!!

BTW: I booked our reservation OpenTable and got 1000 points for it!!!

Gran Caffe L’Aquila has a beautiful atmosphere and some genuinely excellent products. The latte was expertly made with gorgeous latte art, and both the coffee and gelato were absolutely delicious. You can tell they take pride in the quality of what they serve.
Unfortunately, the service did not match the quality of the food and drinks. Most of the staff came across as dismissive and unfriendly, which took away from what could have been a wonderful experience.
The only one exception to this was Luca, who was welcoming, professional, genuinely kind, and knowledgeable. He made us feel appreciated as guests and stood out in the best way possible.
At the end of the day, hospitality is about making people feel welcome.
The rest of the team could certainly take note. If the level of service matched the quality of the coffee and gelato, this would easily be a five-star experience.

text.text:
Vernick Food & Drink became one of my top restaurants in Philly after my first visit! The experience from beginning to end was delightful.

We were immediately greeted by a host who opened the front door for us. We arrived a few minutes early for our resy, so they sat us at a table downstairs. We had water and menus at our temporary table in less than a minute. I’ve never had a restaurant be so accommodating, usually we just stand until the table is ready.

The upstairs was intimate and cozy, with probably about 15 tables or so. Our servers, Brandon and Elijah, were SO helpful and informative about the menu and allergy information. They made a lot of great suggestions, and coursed out the whole meal perfectly.

We started with the king salmon. It was an interesting dish because of the texture - buttery salmon, crunchy asian pear in a yuzu kosho sauce that provided some more sweetness and the slightest kick. Delicious!

We then had the tuna tartare. My favorite dish of the night and top 3 bite in Philly. The toast had crispy edges but the softest center, and the tuna was high quality. It was on a bed of bonito mayo, which provided a perfect smoky/umami aftertaste.

For our entree, we got the grilled sea bass. It was flaky and cooked perfectly, but just a bit unmemorable. The veggies were slightly bland, in no way was it bad though. We would get the 1/2 roasted chicken next time.

I’m so glad we saved room for dessert, the chocolate tart blew us away. The rich dark chocolate combined with the creamy vanilla ice cream was a perfect bite. We couldn’t get enough of it.

Vernick is a perfect fancy date night spot, birthday/celebrations, etc. as it is on the pricier side but the service and ambiance is immaculate. I am so looking forward to coming back in the future!

We started with the king salmon. It was an interesting dish because of the texture - buttery salmon, crunchy asian pear in a yuzu kosho sauce that provided some more sweetness and the slightest kick. Delicious!

We then had the tuna tartare. My favorite dish of the night and top 3 bite in Philly. The toast had crispy edges but the softest center, and the tuna was high quality. It was on a bed of bonito mayo, which provided a perfect smoky/umami aftertaste.

For our entree, we got the grilled sea bass. It was flaky and cooked perfectly, but just a bit unmemorable. The veggies were slightly bland, in no way was it bad though. We would get the 1/2 roasted chicken next time.

I’m so glad we saved room for dessert, the chocolate tart blew us away. The rich dark chocolate combined with the creamy vanilla ice cream was a perfect bite. We couldn’t get enough of it.

Vernick is a perfect fancy date night spot, birthday/celebrations, etc. as it is on the pricier side but the service and ambiance is immaculate. I am so looking forward to coming back in the future!

text.text: As I learned last night, service is not dead at Vernick F&D — not in the slightest. Terrific service, nice lighting and decor. Menu is well edited, and so is the wine list. Standout cocktail was a nightcap — a “Skeleton Key,” apparently a local creation by a member of their talented bar staff, our server noted. Had broc & bean toast, radd salad, the sea bass, and half a chicken (not to be missed). Dessert did not disappoint either. I’d come back again, again after that, then a third time to be sure. A full-on jam.

text.text:
Beautiful Patio and Great Dips, but Let Down by Service and Food

We visited Dear Daphni to celebrate a special occasion—my younger brother finishing his sophomore year—but unfortunately, the experience ended up being quite a mediocre mixed bag, especially considering the price point.

There were definitely a few bright spots. We sat outside on their heated patio, which was comfortable and beautifully set up. Additionally, the dips platter was absolutely delicious and easily the best part of our meal.

However, the rest of the food really struggled to live up to the high price tag:

The Sides: The fries were entirely underwhelming and lacked any real character.

The Halloumi: This dish was heavily fried and overly sweet, completely lacking the balanced flavor profile you'd expect from a higher-end Mediterranean spot.

The Feta Salad: This was incredibly unbalanced, loaded with far too much heavy feta that completely overpowered the fresh greens.

What really dragged the evening down, though, was the service. While the host stand was happy to accommodate our request to sit outside, our server clearly was not. They seemed actively annoyed to have us on the patio and spent the entire night being incredibly short, cold, and impatient with us.

When you are paying premium prices for a celebratory dinner, you expect both the food and the hospitality to match. Unfortunately, Dear Daphni fell well short of that mark. We left feeling like we paid a premium price for a very underwhelming experience.

Went here with a friend last week and just WOW--it truly exceeded my expectations!

Food: 5/5. Everything was absolutely delicious and the plating/presentation was phenomenal. We got the mezze and the kebab sampler. The mezze was so cute and colorful, and every different dip/spread unique in its own way! The bottomless pita had my friend and I grinning, and it was SO worth! The meat was also absolutely delicious--the salmon, chicken, lamb--it was all SO divine. I have to note though that I definitely agree with reviews about how the meat is definitely on the pricier side and it really is up to you to decide if you find it worth it, but I definitely appreciated it for a one-time experience!

Service: 5/5. Our waitress was super friendly, attentive, and prompt, and I love how they give a rundown of the various dips on the mezze platter! She was very helpful in guiding us through the menu.

Atmosphere: 5/5. It is absolutely stunning in this restaurant. The exterior with the black and blue is already aesthetic, but the interior's decor, ambiance, and atmosphere is just perfect. I absolutely loved every detail and it truly complemented the experience perfectly.

Overall, highly recommend this spot for anyone in the Rittenhouse Square area wanting a nice, sit-down meal in a nice, but unique restaurant! Love it and cannot wait to be back!

text.text:
Finally scored a seat at Her Place Supper Club — one of the most coveted tasting menus and one of the hardest reservations to land. With just 26 seats, it’s no surprise that booking a table feels like winning the lottery. After earning its first Michelin star last year, the hype is absolutely real.

Every course was thoughtful, beautifully executed, and served to perfection — the kind of dinner where you slow down and savor every bite. Chef Amanda, Lauren, and Danielle were all incredibly sweet and lovely, taking the time to introduce every single plate and chat with guests, which made the experience feel even more special and personal. The entire staff was warm, attentive, and welcoming from start to finish.

And that Rabbit Pie… hands down my perfect bite of the night. Rich, comforting, and packed with flavor. One of those unforgettable meals you keep thinking about long after the last course. ✨🍽️

text.text: To start with let’s say this is a very unique approach, and I appreciate both their seasonal choices and connection with the local providers of ingredients.  I was super excited to eat here and it all started wonderfully during the cocktail gathering part of the evening with some really delicious hors d'oeuvres (especially the little fish bites and also the lobster ones).  However, upon being seated for the meal, I was unfortunately quite disappointed during the first half of the evening as none of the first few courses were pleasant at all. I’m not a fan of socca, preferring the panisse from the Marseille region to this Niçoise approach of preparing chickpea batter and the brandade topping lacked flavor.  The worst of the first few courses was the asparagus niçoise which ended up just being a vinegary mess.  Speaking with some others afterwards they also agreed that that was the low point of the meal. The bone marrow with fava beans was rather oily as was the lovage leek sausage dish.  Luckily, it improved for the second half with the ravioli, the pork chops, as well as the dessert being quite delicious.  But that was a couple of untasty dishes too much for me to have been satisfied with the overall experience.

text.text:
It was an unforgettable dinner. The moment I stepped inside, I felt as if I had been invited to a close friend’s or family member’s home for a warm, intimate meal. The space is small, cozy, and wonderfully personal. The two chefs prepared and served each course with perfect timing, offering fresh, beautifully crafted dishes one after another without a single moment of dullness.

It was a joy not only to taste the food but also to watch the careful, thoughtful preparation behind every plate. The flavors were excellent, the progression of courses felt seamless, and I left with that perfect feeling of satisfied fullness.

There is no doubt that this restaurant fully deserves its Michelin one-star rating. A truly memorable dining experience.

The only thing I found disappointing was that, although I mentioned it was our wedding anniversary when making the reservation, nothing was acknowledged at all. The staff’s prepared guests’ birthday cakes, special party hats, cards and even a moment where the lights were turned off so everyone in the room could celebrate together. In contrast, our table didn’t receive even a simple mention of our anniversary.

text.text:
Atmosphere:
Urban Farmer is conveniently located inside The Logan Philadelphia, Curio Collection by Hilton, making it an easy and comfortable spot for breakfast if you’re staying at the hotel. The space feels rustic yet warm.

Service:
We arrived right when they opened in the morning, and we got personalized 1:1 service. The staff was welcoming, happy to answer our questions, and offer recommendations.

Food:
Over a few days, I sampled both their sweet and savory options:

1. The strawberry French toast is topped with roasted strawberries, cream cheese icing, and sliced almonds. It was super filling with generous portions and just the right balance of sweetness.

2. The crab omelet with grilled onions, local mushrooms, and béarnaise sauce. A unique combination that oddly worked really well together.

3. The classic two-egg breakfast with crispy potatoes and a biscuit. Simple and a great traditional option.

Overall, Urban Farmer is a great place to grab breakfast in Philly, whether you’re visiting or local.

text.text:
My friend and I went here for restaurant week for their lunch special, and it was amazing!

Food: 4/5. I thought the food was delicious and flavorful, and the flavors themselves unique and complementing each other in ways I’ve never tried before! We got the pierogis which were absolutely delicious, and the toppings were surprisingly a perfect combination. The chicken schnitzel flavor was incredible and the potatoes great. The only thing is that I definitely agree on some reviews about the place being relatively overpriced; I think we paid over ten dollars for the apricot dumpling dessert but it was small and I found the price abysmal for the size. I think the lunch restaurant week $20 menu made it worth it, but I don’t think I would’ve come otherwise! But still, everything was impressionable, unique, flavorful, and the presentation was so pretty!

Service: 2/5. I think our waiter was definitely friendly, but she was not attentive. She did not come around to refill our waters, etc. and even though I wanted to call her over and request some things, she was nowhere to be seen for me to even call her. In addition, the food took noticeably long to come out, despite us being one of three parties there (and none of the parties were big). So that was a bit disappointing.

Atmosphere: 5/5. The ambiance and interior is so pretty and aesthetic! There is a range of rooms with a range of seating from countertops to tables to booths. It is so beautifully decorated and definitely feels like a perfect spot for a date night / hangout with friends!

Overall, I would definitely recommend this spot if you want a unique, European food experience, as it is very tasty, and a perfect place for a date night/time with friends. Just be aware it is on the pricier side and food does take quite a bit to come out.

text.text:
Trying to score a seat at Friday Saturday Sunday on a whim is notoriously difficult, but my recent experience as a solo walk-in proved that their hospitality is just as world-class as their kitchen. Despite the house being packed, the staff was incredibly accommodating from the second I walked through the door.

While waiting for a spot to open up, they immediately ushered me into the bar area and took my drink order. The bar manager went out of her way to look after me, constantly checking in and reassuring me that a seat would turn over soon. True to her word, I was comfortably seated at the bar within 15 minutes.

I opted for the full tasting menu with the wine pairing. Even though I was dining alone, the warmth of the staff meant I never felt isolated. The bartender looking after me was phenomenal—attentive, kind, accommodating, and just straight cool. The pacing was perfect, and the energy at the bar made the night.

As for the meal itself, everything—and I mean everything—was excellent. Here is how the menu delivered:

The Standouts:

- Eggs and Caviar: A luxurious, flawless combination of potato, leek, and truffle that set an incredibly high bar right out of the gate.

- Fusilli: Perfectly cooked pasta tossed with clams, a striking allium ash, and a deeply savory lobster sauce that had incredible depth.

- Sweetbreads: Beautifully executed with mushroom, plantain, and a precise vin blanc. The touch of sweetness from the plantain was a brilliant contrast to the richness of the dish.

- Fish Course: Flawlessly cooked fish paired with a sharp salsa verde, a complex sauce vin jaune, and served with a side of coco bread that was perfect for wiping the plate clean.

- Koshihikari Rice: An absolute knockout. The texture of the premium rice combined with the subtle heat of aji dulce and the crunch of crispy mangalitsa pork was spectacular.

- Grilled Short Rib: Meltingly tender, glazed in a rich oxtail jus with a hint of peanut that brought a unique, savory complexity to the finish.

- Duck Egg Semifreddo: A vibrant, forward-thinking dessert utilizing mango, passion fruit, fig leaf, and tepache. It was exceptionally bright, balanced, and the perfect note to end on.

The Verdict: Friday Saturday Sunday is easily one of the best dining experiences in Philadelphia. The food and wine pairings are operating at an elite level, but it is the elite, unpretentious hospitality that truly sets this place apart. Whether you are with a group or dining solo at the bar, it is a mandatory stop.

text.text: It is almost impossible to reserve a table for the dinner.   They have a lover’s bar that you can order limited items, you may get lucky that you sometimes can try one of the items from the prefix menu from the dinning room.  The bar opens at 4:45pm, so you need to be there at 4:30pm in order to get a seat because the bar has very limited seats.  You need to try the Carousel spin, it is a conceptual cocktail menu from the head bartender Paul MacDonald.  This menu is the culmination of his decade-long Fibonacci cocktail project, and presents a truly novel approach to cocktails, see the restaurant web site for more detail about the Carousel.   We loved all the mix drinks we ordered, especially the one that we told the bartender to make something that is old fashion like, the drink was awesome.  The espresso martini was very very good as well.  The chicken liver mouse was very very good, beef tartar was excellent, the octopus was exceptional, NY strip was yummy, and the smoke herring was delicious.  Bartenders are very friendly and Service was very good even sitting in the bar.  The experience was wonderful, we will come back again.

name: Dim Sum House By Jane G's - Rittenhouse

text.text: We were treated to takeout dinner from Jane G's. Our order was ready on time and included a free container of white rice. We sampled 2 of their dim sum appetizers, shrimp dumplings (har gow) and bbq pork buns (char sio bao). Both appetizers were delicious and the portion was a good size for the price. Their scallion pancakes were light, cripy and flavorful. Our group picked Jane G's because they offer a good selection of vegan and vegetarian dishes. The tofu with sauce was excellent. We would also recommend their lo mein, which can be ordered with a variety of meat or seafood mixed in. We got the shrimp lo mein. The classic beef and broccoli dish was also well done. Since the portions are generous, we had enough leftovers for another dinner.

I spent 24 hours in Philadelphia for a Queen of Neo Soul concert and wanted to support a local cheesesteak spot without venturing too far from our hotel in Center City. The hostess at our hotel highly recommended this place, and I’m so glad she did!

When we arrived, the restaurant was buzzing with energy. The bar was packed, and they were busy filling a steady stream of orders, which is always a good sign.

I decided to step outside the box and order the Jerk Salmon Cheesesteak. I know—it sounds unexpected! I questioned it too, but it absolutely did not disappoint. It was bursting with flavor, had just the right amount of spice, and the salmon was cooked perfectly. Every bite was delicious. I almost forgot to take a picture..lol

If you’re a foodie looking for a unique twist on the classic Philly cheesesteak, this is a must-try. I’ll definitely be back the next time I’m in Philadelphia!

A special thank-you to Norma, our server, for taking great care of us. She was friendly, welcoming, and made the visit feel comfortable from start to finish. Good service always makes good food even better, and Norma definitely added to the experience.

— JM

I wanted to enjoy it more fully and, considering the many other mostly positive reviews,  I expect that I'll try it one more time to give them another chance.

text.text:
I’ve been keeping this place as my best kept secret in Center City, but it’s time to come clean. Mission Taqueria is one of the best restaurants in the city, and you’d never know it was there if you weren’t looking for it.

Hidden behind a small “TACOS” sign is an upstairs safe haven from the fast paced city life. Great food, amazing atmosphere, and my favorite happy hour menu (4pm-6pm) in the whole city!

I can always garuntee a pleasant and comfortable dining experience from the moment I walk upstairs. This restaurant is bright, welcoming, and everyone is so kind! These are not descriptions you’ll commonly find in a city like Philly (no shade, this is my favorite city in the country!)

I found this place 2 years ago on accident and now I’ve brought every person I know to eat and drink here. Mission Taqueria is my shining gold north star of restaurants in center city.

I’ve now moved out of the city but Mission is a place that brings me back atleast once a month. I still haven’t found any place that has as flavorful food + refreshing margaritas that are anywhere as good as Mission.

If you have the chance to dine here I legit couldn’t reccomend any other restaurant more than Mission Taqueria!!

((Oh yeah, and you gotta try the Beef Barbacoa and Carnitas tacos cuz oh my GOD I can’t live without them..))

I’ve now moved out of the city but Mission is a place that brings me back atleast once a month. I still haven’t found any place that has as flavorful food + refreshing margaritas that are anywhere as good as Mission.

100% RECOMMEND

text.text:
Went here for a date night out with a friend.

Food: 3/5. We ordered the mozzarella ball, burrata salad, truffle pasta, chicken parm, and tiramisu. I think all the food was solid! However, I felt as though the chicken parm was not that remarkable. The truffle pasta was good but the amount of truffle was "stingy", if you could even call it that, only just dotting the pasta. Understand it is an expensive ingredient but it didn't feel like a truffle pasta to me. The tiramisu was a bit too bready for us (it was not soaked, the cake did not feel spongy like how it should), but it was still good. I think the food was solid, but nothing out of this world.

Service: 5/5. They definitely know how to do their service here! Our waiter was so attentive, friendly, and just overall very good! In addition, the food delivery is incredibly unique. When we ordered the mozzarella ball, they showed us the curdles before kneading and stretching it into a ball in front of us. For the pasta, they made it in a cheese wheel in front of us and added the truffle shavings on top. It was overall a very unique and fun experience!

Atmosphere: 5/5. The vibes in here are stellar. The stairs leading to their location and the hallway of aesthetic photographs before entering the restaurant officially are so aesthetic. The ambiance and decor is incredibly photo-esque and the perfect spot for a fancier night out. There is a variety of seating ranging from tables to booths. It has a dark, dimmer lit ambiance with shades of gold, tan, and greens contrasted with dark brown and everywhere you turn it feels special!

Overall, recommend this plate for a fancier night out with friends or a date night. Just had some personal preferences regarding some of the food, but it was still fairly solid!

text.text:
The spouse had a great meal here in the past, so it was one less place I had to research for dinner.

ATMOSPHERE:
Intimate spot with a small loft, soft music and big windows for people watching.  Takeout and deliveries seemed to be the majority of the business.

RESERVATIONS:
Not needed on this particular Monday night.

PARKING:
Street or garage.

MENU:
Sichuan & Taiwanese dishes.  No dim sum.

BEVERAGE:
Lychee Martini
Perfectly chilled and balanced, complete with a whole lychee garnish.

FOOD:
Dan Dan Noodles
We got it plain but proteins were available.  Thicker noodles coated in a thick peanut-flavored sauce with a little kick of heat.  Very good but I’d definitely add either chicken or tofu to break up the carbs.

Dry Pot Dish
Served in a steel wok, we opted for chicken which was super tender.  Very flavorful dish but it wasn’t presented sizzling as the menu stated.

Taiwanese Beef Noodle Soup
If you’re a ramen fan and want something different, I think you’ll love this as much as I did.  A generous amount of thick noodles (available hand-ripped flat noodles are a $1 option), chunky slices of tender and fatty beef swimming in a savory and slightly sour dark-hued broth.  Forgot to nix the cilantro but it wasn’t overly loaded.  Total yum.

SERVICE:
Greeting was immediate and friendly.  Male server was knowledgeable but there was no follow up.

OVERALL:
A very enjoyable alternative to traditional Asian cuisine.

My wife and I have been coming to Dan Dan Noodle since 2017, and it’s remained one of our most reliable go-to spots in the city. The food is consistently strong, and the signature dan dan noodles are a must-order. We also tend to get the chicken potstickers, scallion pancake, kung pao chicken, and dry pot beef, along with white rice for the table. It’s a menu that rewards repeat visits.

We’ve had both takeout and dine-in here, and we definitely prefer dining in. The food is at its best when it comes straight out of the kitchen. The staff is always friendly, helpful, and kind without being overbearing. For seating, we prefer the cozy but small upstairs dining area, so making a reservation on OpenTable is usually a good idea. There are a few high-top tables downstairs near the kitchen and windows, which are also great, but if you prefer a quieter or cozier spot, we think the upstairs is best.

They also offer a happy hour with good prices, and overall, the value for the food quality is excellent. We often bring out-of-town guests, and it’s always a hit. Sichuan cuisine remains distinct from typical American Chinese, which helps Dan Dan stand out. We’ve also noticed their Ardmore location, which appears to be a strong alternative.

Consistently good, well-run, unique, and worth visiting, especially for the dan dan noodles. Highly recommended and hope to be back soon!

I don't normally bother writing restaurant reviews, but I have to share my experience with Ninja Bao. I've been wanting to visit this place since I moved back to Jersey over a year ago and I finally got the chance yesterday while cat sitting for my mom and I was NOT disappointed!!

I already knew trying to find the place might be difficult from other reviews and I don't ride the train much so I was super nervous about the trip, but once I got into Suburban Station the guards helped direct me and I found it no problem!

The restaurant was clean and surprisingly quiet! There were so many things I wanted to try and share with my boyfriend that I definitely ended up splurging a bit, but it was so worth it!

Everything we tried was absolute 🔥! Even reheated once I got home later that night, though I'm definitely looking forward to bringing family and friends back so we can eat it hot and fresh!

The service was excellent and the staff very sweet, allowing me to sub out a different drink with the meal I purchased. If you get the chance to stop by this little dive, do not hesitate!! This place is an absolute gem!

**Pro-Tip:** If you're in the area, do not bother trying to get a cheesesteak delivered from somewhere else just to have it arrive cold and soggy. You are much better off coming straight here to get it fresh. It blows the local competition out of the water.

Overall, this was an amazing experience. **10/10 would recommend to anyone!**

text.text:
Brought my daughter here for a Valentine's Day dinner on a last-minute reservation, and I'm really glad we pulled it off. The space alone is worth the visit -- beautiful interior, the kind of place that feels special without trying too hard.

We went full small plates mode and shared four dishes: burrata with leek, walnut, and sourdough (a classic done right), chicken dumplings with basil, jalapeño, and lemon (bright, a little heat, very good), grilled octopus with tomatillo, chili, and lime (tender, well-balanced, my personal favorite of the night), and a margherita pizza that was simple and exactly what it needed to be. The whole spread worked really well together.

I had a Maker's Mark Manhattan that was, frankly, fabulous. No notes.

Service was a bit slow -- we sat with empty water glasses more than once -- but it was Valentine's Day and the place was packed. I'm not going to pile on servers for having a brutal night. They were warm and clearly doing their best under the circumstances.

Would absolutely come back. Harp & Crown is the kind of dinner spot that makes you want to plan a return trip to the city just to eat there again.

This is a nice place for a date or a girls night. It’s more of a vibe focused place where you will spend more, so just keep that in mind versus a sit down date night kind of place.

You will probably order two meals due to sizes. The only dish large enough was the chicken. For me personally the variety wasn’t enough, and not a lot of healthy options. However everyone at my table enjoyed it. We did a bday plate and it was a little lack luster but if you are focused on the surprise and not the actual sweet treat it’s fine. The drinks were good!

This is on a VERY busy street so you will either park a bit away and walk or Uber. It’s located near a lot of bars and other spots too.

Inside is super cute but bustly (again not a dinner sit done vibe). You will need reservations. The staff was VERY accommodating to us being late due to traffic, just call the and they will try to work with you.

If you have a larger party they will try to make it one check, so you need to tell them immediately that you will split it (they seen a little frustrated we didn’t tell them).

Honeygrow is a regular takeout spot for my family, especially for stir-fried noodles. The food is consistently delicious, portions are solid, and I think the price-to-quality ratio is very fair. I can usually feed myself, my wife, and my daughter for around $40.

The standard noodle options are all strong, and I’ll sometimes add double protein if I’m extra hungry. The seasonal specials are worth trying, too; the Chesapeake crab is a standout. They also have salads, yogurt options, and the brownie is delicious.

A big plus is the app, which is intuitive and helpful. The loyalty program actually pays off regularly, which I appreciate.

Just as important, the staff here has always been friendly and welcoming. Overall, this is a well-run chain with good ingredients, healthy options, fair pricing, and consistently good food. HG is a solid balance of convenience, value, and quality. Definitely recommend.

text.text:
Fantastic Meal with Thoughtful Service at Marathon Grill

Our recent visit to Marathon Grill was an absolute pleasure. From start to finish, everything about the experience was seamless and enjoyable. We had a reservation but arrived a bit early, and the staff kindly seated us right away, a nice start to what turned out to be a standout meal.

Our server, Greg, was exceptional, attentive, courteous, and well-informed. With my gluten sensitivity, dining out can be tricky, but Greg navigated it gracefully. He was knowledgeable about the menu and, when unsure, double-checked with the kitchen to ensure everything was safe for me. His care and professionalism were deeply appreciated.

The food? Excellent across the board. I opted for the special of the day, an ahi tuna salad, and it was absolutely delicious—fresh, flavorful, and perfectly prepared. I was impressed by how many gluten-free options were available, which made ordering feel relaxed rather than limiting.

Everyone at the table found something to love. My boys were thrilled with their choices, the Marathon Burger and the cheesesteak, both hearty portions served with crispy fries. My husband also selected a daily special, broiled mahi mahi tacos, and raved about the flavor and texture.

The entire meal was served quickly and arrived at just the right temperature, a testament to the kitchen's timing and quality. Beyond just being a great restaurant for those with dietary needs, Marathon Grill proved to be a versatile spot for the whole family.

Highly recommend this gem for anyone looking for a delicious, welcoming, and well-run dining experience. We’ll definitely be returning!

text.text:
Alice Pizza should be studied, not just eaten.
Jen and I got invited to an AI event—where, ironically, Jen felt like she needed a software update. But the real upgrade of the night? The pizza.
They served three pies: plain, potato, and a “Philly special.” I went in expecting cheesesteak on that one… nope. Curveball. But the pesto? Absolutely carried it—fresh, bold, and the star of the slice.
Now let’s talk about the surprise hit: the potato pie. Yes, potato. And yes, it might’ve been my favorite. The potatoes were soft—perfectly mushy in the best possible way—paired with this spicy, cheesy, Alfredo-style sauce that just worked. Way better than it sounds, trust me.
The plain slice held its own too—simple, solid, no complaints.
Alice Pizza isn’t just different—they’re doing something right

text.text: Strolling around Philly I slowed my roll at the intersection of Locust St. and good smells.  Looking into the window I saw a case of gelato and desserts.  Ok, I have to go in now.  It was busy but the Hostess was welcoming and found a spot for me at the bar.  Bustling time but you didn’t know it because the staff was attentive the whole time.  Let’s start with a cocktail and Italian Sushi — it was savory, creamy, and a nice starter to pair with a cocktail, beer or wine.  But, I came for the smell good pizza so I ordered the Pork BBQ pizza.  This is where sitting at the bar goes wrong — in a good way LOL!!  The dessert case had me drooling.  I’ll just try one small cannoli — it had a nice crunchy shell filled with creamy goodness.  The cannoli was so good I had to try cheesecake — it was sooo creamy with a fluffy texture on tongue and the strawberry added a hint of sweetness.  Now the pizza arrives.  Hmmm, it was over-crunchy and thin on meat so I ended up taking the toppings off of two slices and putting them onto the other two slices — I like meat over dough so I had to do this.  The pizza was overcooked but edible — it smelled better than it tasted.  Oh well that means room for another desert.  I ordered Tiramisu but it was sold out.  That was my cue to push away from the bar.

text.text: This is my second time coming to this restaurant, and I cannot say enough good things about it. From the food, to the service, it is worth every penny and minute taking the trip to Philly. We had reservations at 4:00 because I wanted to eat early knowing it gets crowded and we also didn't want to get home late. We were seated right away and immediately staff was already tending to our table. Our server Jaime was great- very friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable about the menu. The owner himself frequently goes around stopping by tables to chat and make sure the customers are satisfied. The reason I originally came across this restaurant last year was because of their expansive gluten-free menu and the ability for me to enjoy pasta at a restaurant knowing that it’s safe. I got the GF braised beef spaghetti and the burrata appetizer and they were both incredibly flavorful and fresh. My other guests had the sweet potato gnocchi and lobster ravioli and a few other dishes that they said were delicious as well.  I finished off my meal with the Crème brûlée (picture of it is from last year also from my birthday and my guests chocolate tartufo is last year as well). Before I left, I told Jamie I will be back for my birthday again next year but I didn’t tell her it was my birthday this time around. After we left the restaurant, she ran out down the stairs with a little slice of GF flourless chocolate cake with a candle telling us nobody gets away on their birthday without a candle. It was so sweet and thoughtful, and it’s those little touches of customer service like that that really add the extra touch to an establishment, especially a mom and pop shop. Other restaurants wouldn’t go above and beyond like that after the customers have already left. I highly recommend this restaurant for great Italian food and ambiance. Can’t wait to go back again.  11/10 rating

text.text:
I came in looking homeless, because currently, I am; for it is fleeing from domestic abuse to a place that fills me with love. I felt a energy that was home like. They don't just work there, they are there, as **people**.

The food was excellent, I have a refined pallet, for what I would expect of this place, with the reviews, it met that exceptionally well! 9.8/10 Food (only critique is to have the chicken even easier to slide on through with a fork and knife), 9.8.8/10 Service (only because I wished for a refill for a small while), 8/10 Atmosphere (Felt a bit anxious in the environment with the smaller space for everyone to fit through, and wish the music filled the space better for walk ins; being given higher on the scale, as for the people, made up for it extraordinarily so).

A personal preference for the bread, serve warm, I think the flavors from it being fresh, alone with the oil, would of been greatly enhanced, melting on the tongue.

The understanding shown when I hadn't known my food contained ham, it felt human, they were quick to take it back and prepare me it again!

I am familiar with all sorts of environments, even ones like this, despite my current circumstances.

It was felt, a much needed patience in order for me to access pay, manual card input, as for most of my finances and cards are currently inaccessible for having to leave my place of residence so quickly.

Glandness takes, I had gotten to eat so incredibly well, honestly, it was good enough to push through fullness, and to end up signing off on my trip to Philly if needed, the satisfaction that it gave me, if I had to go back to my residence, I was okay going back with that being my last experience in the big city.

text.text:
If you're searching for everything a local bar should be, Locust Rendezvous in Center City Philadelphia delivers in spades. Since 1989, this beloved dive has been gathering the neighborhood with its no-frills charm, affordable drinks, and a cast of lively regulars that make every visit memorable.
Atmosphere: The vibe is pure Philly, warm, nostalgic, and buzzing with energy. Think wood-paneled walls, 2000s bangers on the jukebox, and TVs tuned to the latest Eagles or Phillies game. Whether it’s a playoff night or a casual weekday, the bar is alive with conversation, laughter, and the occasional friendly debate about sports or city politics.

This is where locals come to unwind, and visitors (like me, a lone Sailor) quickly feel like part of the family. It’s the kind of place where you come for a drink and stay for the people.

Reuben sandwich gets rave reviews from me! Phenomenal!

Locust Rendezvous isn’t trying to be trendy, it’s just real. It’s the kind of bar where you can watch the game, complain about work, celebrate a win, or just enjoy a cold beer with good company. It’s everything a local bar should offer: incredible atmosphere, lively characters, and a sense of belonging.
