text.text:
GOOD DOG BAR — PHILADELPHIA
224 S 15th St | Opened in 2003 | 3 Floors | Dog-Friendly

We finally hit up Good Dog Bar in Philly after hearing their cheeseburgers were legendary, and let me tell you right now: this place did not disappoint.

We started with the buffalo chicken wings, because I always say if the wings are good, the rest of the food is probably going to be good too. These wings were crispy, juicy, fiery, and absolutely drenched in homemade blue cheese dressing. The flavor was bold, the texture was perfect, and the heat came through just right. Trust test? Passed.

Then we asked about the specials, and when they mentioned there were Latinos in the kitchen, we knew we had to try the chorizo empanadas. And wow. These might be the best empanadas I’ve ever had. They were packed with chorizo, potatoes, onions, poblano peppers, and Chihuahua cheese, then served with a chipotle crema sauce that brought everything together. Hot, juicy, savory, smoky, a little sweet, and loaded with flavor. I’m not even the biggest empanada person, but I would order these again and again. No exaggeration — these were incredible.

Now let’s talk about the cheese sticks. Philly has its own food identity, and these cheese sticks were on another level. The cheese pull was absolutely ridiculous — I’m talking strings stretching across the table like they were building a bridge in mid-air. Pecorino-dusted, basil-kissed, marinara-dunked, and completely photogenic. I’ve never seen cheese sticks like this before. These are the kind of appetizers people stop and stare at.

Then came the burgers.

text.text:
As a Nigerian myself, I am always eager to try Nigerian restaurants. The reviews weren’t great, but I try to form my own opinion. That being said, the reviews were spot on. Before I review the food I want to say that the owner was very kind and welcoming. The restaurant located underground of JFK was clean and inviting. I wish I could say positive things about the food. I ordered jollof rice with peppered goat, and the seasoned spinach , 2 meat pies and a bag of chinchin. My total was $61. Never have I paid that much for African food, and I have frequented many African restaurants in Philadelphia. I was literally flabbergasted when I reviewed my receipt. There was a 15% gratuity automatically included. How do you as a business owner do that, for a take-out order no less? The food took about 20 mins to come out after we ordered. We didn’t dine in. When we got home to eat, the portion was crazy… as in crazy small. I had to laugh because  surely this was a joke.

The jollof rice Smokey and tasty, but it was so salty.
The peppered goat: by far the worst item, was also salty and SO OILY. Literally baptized in grease and tough to chew.
The spinach was really tasty, good flavor but unfortunately also oily.
The meat pie, has no taste. The dough was nice and flaky. We welcomed the meat pie, it was a much needed palate cleanser.
The chinchin was crunchy and delicious with the right amount of sweetness.
All in all, I would not recommend this restaurant. It is overpriced and the food quality and quantity does not justify the price.

Dolce is a gorgeous restaurant and the food presentation is amazing, but our experience was very up and down. Service was extremely slow our server had tables on both sides of the restaurant and got overwhelmed fast. He was genuinely trying, and the supervisors eventually stepped in to help him, so I don’t blame him at all.

The mussels were the best part of the night super flavorful. The lentils under the branzino were actually good. The fish itself was okay, but the broccolini and bok choy had a strange, almost spicy-bitter taste that wasn’t enjoyable.

The pasta came out way too al dente for my liking, but the carpaccio was the biggest issue. It was cut way too thick, and the raw taste was really strong. I took one bite and couldn’t finish it. My partner also had a single bite and we didn’t eat anything else after dinner and the next day he was extremely sick. Non-stop cramps, throwing up, couldn’t keep anything down... it’s concerning enough that they should definitely look into it. 🫤

text.text:
First: a big shoutout to Andre, our server, who went above and beyond to help us celebrate our anniversary with Ocean Prime. Thank you, Andre. Don’t ever stop doing what you do, man. It’s working.

Okay: This place is badass. Lights out. I love an upscale steak and seafood place and since we moved to the City of Brotherly Shove my wife and I have been looking for a Truluck’s Austin replacement and we found it. It’s got the ambiance, the setup, looks old school modern and it’s a real joint.

We celebrated our twentieth year together with this warm and wonderful staff and they were kind enough to give us a big booth, put out a little sign, give my wife some champagne and comp us a wonderful crème brulee dessert. The experience would have been stellar without those thoughtful add-ons.

The new menu is almost over the top; I only say that because looking at it hungry you want to try a little of everything but that’s just not possible. You’d pop. Your wallet, too.  It’s not Cheesecake Factory pages, but it’s a lot and everything sounds delicious so choosing can be hard.

The sushi is great. Spicy and tasty. The drinks are just exotic enough so you don’t feel like you’re having Joe’s margarita at the corner bar. The sides are plentiful and well thought out. The mains, we had wagyu filet and lobster, were delicious. 1200 degree sear on the steak and the lobster tail was a quarter pound.

The service, again, was just fantastic. You’re gonna go out to a place like this and you know you’re gonna drop some cash. The right joint strikes the right tone between briskly taking care of business and being attentive and treating you like you’re someone special. Ocean Prime does not appear to take your business for granted, they want to earn it.

Oh: and happy hour Sundays. New menu, the food is fantastic, Andre is a great server and whoever is running this place has their act together. Keep it up. Thank you!

text.text:
The Perfect Pre-Theater Greek Gem
If you are heading to a show at the Kimmel Center, Estia is one of the most convenient and pleasant spots in the Theater District. I believe I visited during Restaurant Week and had a great experience with their prefix menu before a performance.
The Vibe & Decor
The restaurant has a very interesting and "neat" look. The decor is rustic Greek with a beautiful, airy feel—it’s pleasant and unique, making it feel a bit more special than your average dinner spot. It’s large enough to accommodate crowds but didn't feel overly packed when I was there.
The Food
Since it’s an authentic Greek Mediterranean spot, the food is fresh and well-prepared.
• The Main: I had the fish, which was delicious, along with some great traditional side dishes.
• Must-Try: We had a "quiche-type" Greek dish (likely Spanakopita) that was very tasty.
• Dessert: You can’t go wrong with their Baklava, and the sorbet was a refreshing way to end the meal.
Service & Location
The service was efficient and professional, which is exactly what you need when you have a curtain time to catch! It’s just a short walk to the Kimmel Center, making it a stress-free choice for dinner and a show.
Final Verdict: While it might not be my #1 favorite in the entire city, it is a very solid, high-quality choice with great decor. I would definitely go back, especially before another show!

Palm Vintage has quickly become one of my favorite weekday brunch spots in Philadelphia. Despite being right on Rittenhouse Square with one of the best views in the city, it’s remarkably peaceful. Somehow, you feel completely detached from the hustle and bustle, making it the perfect place to slow down and enjoy your morning.

The coffee selection is incredibly creative, with unique drinks that make every visit feel a little different. I’m a creature of habit and always order the chicken Caesar salad—it’s consistently fresh, flavorful, and one of my favorite lunches in the city. My boyfriend is much more adventurous and loves working his way through the breakfast sandwiches, and every one he’s tried has been a hit.

Between the beautiful atmosphere, outstanding food, inventive coffee menu, and relaxing setting, Palm Vintage has become a place we look forward to visiting again and again. Whether you’re meeting a friend, enjoying a quiet solo brunch, or just looking for a peaceful spot overlooking Rittenhouse Square, I can’t recommend it highly enough.

text.text:
Kissho House on Locust Street is an excellent addition to Philadelphia’s dining scene and a great choice if you’re looking for high-quality Japanese food in a stylish, upscale setting. From the moment you walk in, the restaurant has a cozy welcoming atmosphere that feels refined without being overly formal. It works equally well for a date night, dinner with friends, or a special occasion.

The presentation of the food is beautiful and you can tell there is a lot of attention given to the details. The menu offers a great variety, with everything feeling thoughtfully prepared rather than just being another typical sushi restaurant. The omakase experience is especially appealing for anyone who enjoys trying different flavors and letting the chef guide the meal.

The atmosphere is one of the things that really makes Kissho House stand out. It feels modern and intimate while still having enough energy to make the restaurant feel lively. The staff is attentive, friendly, and helps make the entire experience feel comfortable and enjoyable. Cocktails are next level...

Overall, Kissho House is definitely worth checking out if you’re in Center City Philadelphia and enjoy Japanese cuisine. Between the atmosphere, presentation, variety, and overall dining experience, it feels like a restaurant that puts real effort into creating something memorable. I would absolutely recommend it and would gladly come back again.

The yellowtail with Serrano pepper was incredible and the spicy salmon with nori chips was also very good, except there were only like 3 nori chips which wasn't nearly enough for all of the salmon. Also the presentation of that needs work, but most importantly it was not spicy at all which was the only disappointment (still delicious).

Our server, Anastasia, was knowledgeable and friendly and attentive. She really went above and beyond for us. We got a roll as well that I can't remember the name of, and it was tasty although too sweet. There was just a little too much sauce on it.

The quality of fish was outstanding. Fresh, flavorful, melt-in-your-mouth, beautifully prepared and came out very quickly. I WILL be back. I actually can't wait.

For the two of us it was about $100 including tip. We had 2 sashimi appetizers and 1 sushi roll, a beer, a glass of white whine, and a bottled water.

Overall I was very happy. If I had any recs, it would be to offer a spicy condiment/ sauce / pepper flakes with the dishes advertised as spicy because they really aren't spicy.

text.text: Loved Samurai!  We dined privately in our very own 360-degree video room. We were given a private room.  Our table was surrounded by beautiful reef fish and sharks. It was something you might experience at Disney World. It was a very cool concept.  Watch out! The Sushi chef will overfeed you with amazing sushi roll after amazing sushi roll. The sashimi was super fresh. We tried the steak too, and it was delicious. The owner is a sushi distributor who hand-picks whatever is served, which is the equivalent to Charlie from the Chocolate factory handing you just the right candy bar! This restaurant will end up being one of the next great places to eat in Center city, Philadelphia. Go before everybody finds out about it, or you won’t get in, and you will be waiting outside. Trust me, it’s that good!

text.text:
The venue itself is attractive, well-designed, and creates a strong first impression. The host and bouncers were equally commendable—welcoming, professional, and set a positive tone upon arrival.

Unfortunately, the experience at the bar did not match that standard. The bartender’s demeanor came across as unfriendly and disengaged, which made the interaction feel unwelcoming. As someone with prior experience bartending in a fast-paced environment, I understand the pressures of the role, but professionalism and basic courtesy should remain consistent regardless of volume or stress.

After one drink, my party and I chose to leave and continue our evening elsewhere due to the lack of service quality. In hospitality, attitude and attentiveness are not optional—they directly influence customer satisfaction, repeat business, and ultimately tips. A well-designed space can draw people in, but it is the quality of service that determines whether they stay or return. (Usually best to not upset your customer / client base regardless of industry :))

text.text:
The Lesieur is a total hidden gem.
The atmosphere here is unmatched—stepping inside feels like finding a secret, upscale underground spot. The dark bowling alley with the tin ceiling gives off such a cool, vintage industrial vibe that makes for an incredible night out with friends.
The attention to detail is everywhere, from the candlelit stairways to the top-tier service and food. Whether you’re here for the lanes or just the aesthetic, it’s easily one of the best spots in the city. 10/10 experience, definitely coming back.

Dined here on Valentine’s Day weekend and snagged a super late reservation (10:30pm). Felt super guilty about it but tried to go in with low expectations and as prepared as possible to make this smooth for everyone.

We arrived and our host informed us there would be a small wait (understandably) but offered for us water and to checkout the bar downstairs. (We already had reservations for a later date there)

We were seated shortly after and I cannot tell you how AWESOME our server Casey was. (I hope that’s how his name is spelled if not I’m SO sorry 😢). As mentioned we were pretty certain about what we wanted and intended on making this a very cut and dry experience for the sake of everyone getting home safe and enjoying their night as much as us, but he was such a warm and welcoming spirit.

I was concerned about the Mac and cheese being too heavy but he encouraged I get it to accompany the Pork Tomahawk we got. Everything came promptly and again, everyone was so sweet in a very compromising and normally chaotic circumstance.

text.text:
I’ve been downstairs to Giuseppe & Sons so many times and wanted to give Bar Lesieur a try!

The ambiance is great for a date night, filled with warm moody lighting. Unfortunately, the food didn’t match the atmosphere.

We started with an espresso martini, which was fine. I much preferred my second drink, Queen Bee. We then got a caesar salad, we did not like it. It tasted watery like the lettuce was washed but not fully dried before putting the dressing on. Also, no croutons.

We got the crab cake which we did enjoy. Had a nice crisp on the outside. $25 for one crab cake with no sides was pretty outrageous though. The mac & cheese was delicious!

Lastly, we got the burger. I found it to be overcooked and didn’t have great flavor, my friend thought it was good. The fries were very crispy and tasty.

Overall, for the prices and portion size, I was not impressed and unfortunately will not be coming back.

We ordered the burrata & tomato small plate,  the tuna wonton cup small plate, and the shrimp and grits. The burrata dish was mostly tomatoes and just didn’t taste as great as we had hoped. The wonton cups were pretty good but not excellent. The guacamole at the bottom was a little too spicy for some of us. The shrimp and grits dish was excellent - the grits were creamy and perfectly cooked and the flavor of the bacon and shrimp was excellent. Our waiter also kindly concocted a fun juice drink for one of my kids. Overall, a super fun dinner experience!

text.text: Every meal was so divine. I went with my parents and each of our meals was so good, it turned into a family style affair. The braised short rib was unbelievably tender and flavorful, and with a side of the chips it was perfect. The buttermilk chicken was my favorite, and it wasn’t even my dish! The chicken was so beautifully sweet with crispy skin that accompanied the sweet potato amazingly. My dish was the fish and chips, and it was just as spectacular as the others! It was a massive fish to start, and indescribably fluffy and light battered cod, and the tartar sauce was perfect for it. The rosemary and parmesan chips were delicious, as was every other part of this meal. Finally, the cornbread was fluffy and melted in my mouth. Our server was also so sweet, and gave great opinions and made sure all was well at the table (it definitely was!!). Accompanied with the lovely live blues music, the atmosphere and food made for a wonderfully casual night out. I will be back for brunch next time for sure!

We stopped here based on the good reviews, and we are sorry we did. The food was flavorless. We paid $73 for two pasta dishes, one salad and a water. The final total was $4 more than presented on the bill as the server never mentioned the card upcharge of 4%. All total, we were in for $77 for some of the worst Italian food we have ever had.

The service was no better. The server had no personality what so ever. He did not check on diners or ask if anything was needed. We had to ask for everything, including the bill.  We did not have even a slight conversation with him. For a customer facing food service worker, he did not seem interested.

We ordered the Tacconelli ai Porcini. The pasta was ok, but the sauce and mushrooms were not good. My boyfriend said the mushrooms had the texture of wood and were difficult to chew.

I ordered the spinach gnocchi. This was unlike any gnocchi I have ever seen. They were big pieces of pasta, heavy on dough with an overpowering taste of overcooked spinach. I didnt finish it and really should have asked to order something else.

The salad was OK but not worth $15. It was basically similar to a bag of arugala blend greens mixed with their house dressing and topped with cheese. Nothing special.

I hate to leave a bad review because this is someone's business and livelihood. We work hard for what we have though, and this meal was money wasted.

South Philly Barbacoa is a place with incredibly delicious food and very friendly staff who make you feel welcome from the moment you arrive. 🌟The food really stands out, everything is flavorful, authentic, and clearly made with care. 👌🌮🤤

That said, the restaurant can sometimes get very busy, which can slow down service or make things feel a bit chaotic. Even so, it’s absolutely worth the wait and/or being patient, because the experience and the food more than make up for it. 🙌🏼

On certain days, there’s also music or some variety in the atmosphere, which adds to the overall charm. Overall, it’s highly recommended: amazing food, great energy, and a spot definitely worth coming back to. 😃

text.text: South Philly Barbacoa was such a gift to have at our wedding. Not only was it so special to have our guests try the best of the best barbacoa philly has to offer, but having Chef Cristina at the event was such a cherry on top. The food was incredible and they were willing to accommodate a menu change for my dad who has a seafood allergy. We never felt pressure from them food-wise and it was super easy to make adjustments to the order up until the week of the wedding. For my side of the family especially, I know it was a nostalgic experience to order from the cart set up for tacos and it was comforting to get to chat with Cristina. She was truly the best–fixing us a plate and making sure my husband and I ate at cocktail hour and at dinner. (photos by Lilith & Eve)

Had one of the best American meals I’ve had in Philly at Alice. Honestly, everything from the apps to dessert was great.

We started with the green salad and the octopus. The salad was simple but really fresh, but the octopus was incredible, very tender. Definitely one of the standouts of the night.

For mains we got the dry-aged burger, ribeye for two, and tagliatelle. The burger was ridiculously juicy- like one of the juiciest burgers I’ve had, and the onions on it were so good. The ribeye was probably the best dish overall though. Perfectly cooked and the sauce that came with it might be the best steak sauce I’ve ever had. The tagliatelle was also really solid and rounded out the table nicely.

Finished with the absinthe chocolate chunk ice cream,which was a great way to end the meal, very creamy with a really nice subtle absinthe flavor.

Hard to pick favorites because everything was good, but if I had to: octopus, burger, and the ribeye were the standouts. Would absolutely go back.

text.text:
Alice is the kind of restaurant that reminds you why dining out can be an art form. As a visitor to Philadelphia, the meal felt less like dinner and more like an invitation into a creative conversation between the kitchen, the ingredients, and the season itself.
What impressed me most was the restaurant's confidence. The menu is ambitious and inventive, yet never feels experimental for the sake of novelty. Each dish was thoughtful, balanced, and deeply satisfying, allowing exceptional ingredients to shine while still delivering moments of surprise. There is a clear point of view behind the food, but it is expressed with restraint and precision rather than excess.
In a city celebrated for its dining scene, it takes something special to stand out. Alice manages to do exactly that. Every course felt intentional, revealing a kitchen that is both imaginative and disciplined. There was always something unexpected to discover, which made the experience feel exciting from beginning to end.
The atmosphere complements the food perfectly—warm, welcoming, and intimate enough to encourage lingering over each course. It is rare to find a restaurant that feels both elevated and approachable, where serious culinary talent is matched by genuine hospitality.
Philadelphia is known for outstanding food, and Alice has distinguished itself as one of the most memorable and rewarding dining experiences I enjoyed during my visit. Long after returning home, I still find myself thinking about specific dishes, flavors, and moments from the evening—a testament to how thoughtfully every aspect of the experience is crafted.
For anyone visiting Philadelphia in search of a truly exceptional meal, Alice deserves a place at the very top of the list.

I had such a great experience at Bridget Foy’s!

The food here really surprised me as I went in with no expectations. The wings were great, the salads were delicious and fresh, and the pasta was also good. The standout for me was actually the garlic toast that comes with the pasta. I’m not a fan of garlic toast because it’s always too hard or oily. This bread was absolutely perfect and a great addition to the pasta. In addition to the food, the drinks were also good (love a lemon with my Diet Coke!)

We sat outside on the patio and the atmosphere was very enjoyable. Along with our wonderful server, there were other staff that made sure we had everything we needed multiple times throughout our visit.

The only issue we encountered is it did take a long time for our second unlimited pasta dish to come out. Additionally, my salad was supposed to come with bacon, but didn’t have any on it. None of this was at any fault of our server, I believe there must have been something going on in the kitchen that caused the mistakes.

The prices are a little a little steep for more casual dining, but the portion sizes make up for it a little bit.

text.text:
Whatever review I undertake, I make it a priority to approach each one with mindfulness, respect, and fairness. It’s never my aim to harm a business; my goal is to offer insights based on my extensive experience in the culinary world. Having spent nearly 40 years in the food industry, over 30 of which were in various restaurant capacities—from quaint mom-and-pop diners to upscale establishments and hotels—I understand the impact my reviews can have, especially as I reach 1.5 million views and reads weekly.

Having lived in Pennsylvania for most of my life and spending over 25 years in Philadelphia, I often regret not discovering this restaurant sooner. Its legendary reputation is something that nearly every Philadelphian, including myself, is aware of. With that said, this place truly shines.

I adore the layout. There’s a welcoming indoor dining area perfect for gatherings with family or friends, and the bar section features comfortable swivel barstools with backs. In addition, I believe there’s a delightful mix of high-top and low-top seating around the bar. I can easily envision bringing someone special here for an intimate experience. Moving from the bar to the outside, there’s charming outdoor patio seating and additional tables alongside the restaurant, as seen in the photos. This diversity in seating arrangements creates a unique experience at every turn.

Now, let’s talk about the food—I’m a fan of the menu. It’s refreshingly straightforward with fantastic options. As someone who often finds vegan choices a bit challenging, I appreciate this restaurant's veggie offerings that may not be fully vegan. I opted for the beet and mushroom burger, made in-house with a blend of chickpeas, black beans, beets, and mushrooms, topped with lettuce, tomato, onion, cheddar cheese, and chipotle mayo. While not entirely vegan due to the cheese and mayo, it was an easy fix for me; I simply left those off and added a bit of hot sauce and a drizzle of olive oil. The result was outstanding—rich in flavor and expertly crafted. My only suggestion would be to serve it on a crusty artisan roll, perhaps one topped with sesame seeds, to elevate the burger even more.

Typically, this comes with fries, but I opted for a fresh spring mix instead, featuring diced red onions, cucumbers, and tomatoes—extremely refreshing, especially with the delightful poppyseed dressing. My friend chose a lighter fare, ordering from the bar’s specials. She enjoyed a lovely tomato soup with the option of grilled cheese, which she declined, along with crispy green bean fries served with ranch dressing. She paired it with a non-alcoholic frozen dragon fruit lemonade, which I sampled and found excellent. The green bean fries and tomato soup were both tasty as well.

Overall, the menu is well-conceived, offering something for everyone without being complicated, which I appreciate. Notably, Bridget Foy endured a devastating fire in 2017 that forced them to decide between demolishing the building or renovating what they could salvage. They chose to rebuild from the ground up, and as far as I can tell, they’ve done an incredible job. This historic location is irreplaceable in Philadelphia, and the family that has owned and operated it for over half a century is truly remarkable.

I must also highlight our server, Stefan (forgive me if I misspell his name). He was outstanding—attentive, on point in every way—and we were even fortunate enough to meet Bridget Foy herself. She is genuinely wonderful, and we’re lucky to have her as a representative of the best that Philadelphia has to offer.

text.text:
La Nonna is a small family-owned BYOB on South Street overlooking historic Headhouse Square, serving Roman and regional Italian cuisine with a menu centered around housemade pasta and classic dishes. Cash or Venmo only, no heavy modifications, and honestly the restaurant is better for it.

The chicken parm was huge with bright, fresh-tasting marinara, the piccata had a rich lemon butter sauce loaded with capers, and the pasta actually tasted homemade instead of mass-produced. The fried calamari was light and crisp instead of greasy, and the portions felt generous without losing quality.

The space itself feels intimate and personal — stained glass lighting, vintage decor, layered textures, and eclectic details everywhere without feeling overly curated. One of those restaurants where the atmosphere clearly reflects the people running it instead of feeling designed by a restaurant group. A really solid South Street spot if you want comforting Italian food in a smaller, more authentic setting.

text.text:
There's something satisfying about sitting at a traditional bar watching pasta get cooked. Tight space, but they've somehow squeezed a full bar, a pasta station, and a cold prep station all in a row.

The apps were some of the best I've had in a bar setting. Simple but still creative, the Insalata Frutti di Mare especially. Usually it's just seafood tossed in olive oil and lemon, but here they set it over a cold corn bisque. I normally prefer a tangy seafood app like a ceviche, but the subtle sweetness of the corn and the little bit of texture from the skins added so much dimension to the dish.

For pastas I went with the staples (rigatoni, cacio e pepe, ricotta gnocchi), but they were a little plain, honestly. After apps like that I expected some refinement, but these were comfort-style, punchy, and heavy on the parm/ Pecorino Romano. A sprinkle on the cooktop, then another once it hit the plate. The first few bites, I didn't mind. But by the third pasta I realized they all carried the exact same salty-funky top note, which flattened the distinctions between them.

Still a great place to casually drop in for satisfying pasta and drinks. Even in that tight space the service was excellent, and I'd be back to try their seasonal pastas.

I also tried the crepe with fig jam, and unfortunately that one missed the mark for me. I don’t think it complements the rest of the menu.

text.text:
Angelo’s Pizzeria in South Philly is hands down one of the best spots in the city for both pizza and cheesesteaks, and it absolutely lived up to the hype when I brought a couple buddies there on a Saturday at peak time.
This place has built a serious reputation over the years- especially for their bread, which they make fresh in-house daily- and that alone puts them in a different league.
We pulled up to a long line, but don’t let that scare you- it moves pretty quickly and is 100% worth the wait.
We ordered the Diavlo pizza (Italian long hots, hot sausage, homemade arrabbiata, red pepper flakes, fresh garlic) along with a cheesesteak, and both were unreal. The pizza had a perfect balance of heat and flavor, and the crust was exactly what you want- crispy, airy, and fresh. The cheesesteak lived up to its reputation too, with that signature bread really making the difference.
After ordering at the counter, we got the text to pick up the food in about 10–15 minutes, which is impressive given how busy it was. The staff kept things moving and were all really friendly despite the rush.
One thing to keep in mind: there’s no seating inside or outside, so plan ahead. A lot of people grab their food and find a spot nearby or head to a park to eat, which honestly adds to the experience.
Overall, this is a must-visit Philly staple at this point. If you’re in the city, you’ve got to try both the pizza and the cheesesteak.
I’ll definitely be back and would recommend it to anyone!

This place has built a serious reputation over the years- especially for their bread, which they make fresh in-house daily- and that alone puts them in a different league.
We pulled up to a long line, but don’t let that scare you- it moves pretty quickly and is 100% worth the wait.
We ordered the Diavlo pizza (Italian long hots, hot sausage, homemade arrabbiata, red pepper flakes, fresh garlic) along with a cheesesteak, and both were unreal. The pizza had a perfect balance of heat and flavor, and the crust was exactly what you want- crispy, airy, and fresh. The cheesesteak lived up to its reputation too, with that signature bread really making the difference.
After ordering at the counter, we got the text to pick up the food in about 10–15 minutes, which is impressive given how busy it was. The staff kept things moving and were all really friendly despite the rush.
One thing to keep in mind: there’s no seating inside or outside, so plan ahead. A lot of people grab their food and find a spot nearby or head to a park to eat, which honestly adds to the experience.
Overall, this is a must-visit Philly staple at this point. If you’re in the city, you’ve got to try both the pizza and the cheesesteak.
I’ll definitely be back and would recommend it to anyone!

text.text: Me n my bros came from Commiefornia to Philly to see the All-Star game and eat cheesesteaks. Doing research, we all agreed Angelos was a necessary stop. To compare, we earlier in the day tried both Pat's and Geno's so we had something to compare it to. We got there 30 min before they opened, and there was already a line. We were the 7th to place an order and we didn't get our food til almost 11:20. And it was worth it. We got a pizza and cheesesteak. The pizza was decent. Nice crust. My bro who ordered, forgot to add pepperoni, which I think would have kicked it up a notch, leaving the cheese and basil pizza just OK. Not something I'd get again, but the cheesesteak, oh my.  After opening the wrapper, we knew this was going to be next level. The mix of meat and cheesy yumminess was off the chart. First bite was incredible, and of the 3, we all agreed on the champion. Will definitely come back if ever in Philly. Thx Angelo 😋

Now I know why the place is so hard to get in.

We had elected to have the puck-and-see, where the chef selected the dishes for us and each of of them was exquisite and delicious.

All the components of the dishes separately had great flavor flavor and combined together they were a symphony in the mouth.

I also got the Vietnamese spiced ice coffee and it was great.
It's a BYOB if you want some alcohol.

I believe each person (may differ according to amount of people) got 2 appetizers and main and a shared large dessert.

All of the appetizers were great, I especially liked the char on the skewer, the soft shell shrimp and the broth of the mussel dishes.

From the entree the chicken coconut Noodle dish (Ramen) was the best of the night. And the quantities they give are pretty good too.

I thought I might not be able to finish the funnel cake when brought out (as we were pretty full) but the moment I tasted it, i knew I would finish it up then and there.

The servers were great and very friendly.

The cons of I had any is the smaller place and how hard it is to get dinner reservations, but it is a known issue (or non-issue),but since this place has been open for some time, people should expect it. It doesn't take away from the great experience you will have visiting this place.

text.text:
Mawn absolutely lives up to the hype. Every dish we had was packed with flavor while still feeling incredibly balanced and thoughtfully prepared. The yellow curry noodle soup was comforting without being too heavy, with a rich coconut curry broth and perfectly cooked chicken. The Thai crab fried rice was outstanding. The crab was fresh, the rice had incredible wok flavor, and the crispy garlic tied everything together.

The head-on soft shell shrimp were another highlight. The fish sauce caramel delivered the perfect balance of sweet, savory, and heat, making them impossible to stop eating. The jasmine rice pudding was the perfect way to end the meal and is absolutely worth saving room for.

It’s easy to see why Mawn is one of the hardest reservations to get in Philadelphia. The food is creative without trying too hard, every ingredient tastes intentional, and the service matched the quality of the kitchen. If you’re lucky enough to get a reservation, don’t think twice.

Solid brunch spot. We ordered the sweet Dutch baby, uitsmijter, and marble rye club. The portions are large. It was our first time trying a Dutch baby pancake so we weren’t sure what to expect, but it was light and airy. The club sandwich and uitsmijter were both good as well.

The interior is small, which is pretty typical for Philly restaurants. My only complaint is that the tables are a bit cramped for two people. We ordered three entrees to share, and it was difficult to fit all the plates on the table comfortably.

The food took a little while to come out, but overall it was a good brunch spot and I would recommend to try.

text.text:
For all the good things we have heard about Blue Corn, we left fairly disappointed and generally unimpressed with the food especially for the price we paid. Everything was fine, nothing was bad, but it did not meet our expectations.

Although the dishes came out looking very nice and full of rustic charm, the flavors and quality felt lacking. I ordered the "Blue Tacos" as it seemed to be the signature taco dish on the menu. The al pastor meat was not flavorful and lacked any sort of char or smoky flavor. The salsa was lacking and did not add anything positively or negatively. The blue tortilla itself was nice, but I did not care for the melted Oaxaca cheese personally and probably would have enjoyed cotija more.There was nothing bad about these tacos, but I realized that the al pastor tacos at Buena Onda (a cheap fast casual taco spot) had more flavor than these and didn't cost nearly as much.

My wife's entree was the huarache with steak, which she was also disappointed in. She expected the huarache base itself to be much thicker but it was basically just a tortilla. There was almost more nopales in the dish than the tortilla or chicken itself. There was some decent flavor in the sauce but neither of us cared enough to finish it.

The only other thing we got was a Horchata, which was fine. But when our total before tip was over $50, we felt like it was not money well spent whatsoever.

text.text:
Marrakesh — A Total Escape to Morocco in Queen Village
If you want to feel like you’ve been transported straight to Morocco without leaving Philadelphia, Marrakesh is the place to go. From the decor to the traditional customs, it is a completely authentic experience that is just as much about the atmosphere as it is about the food.
The Experience & Decor
The restaurant is stunning, filled with authentic flair, rich colors, and traditional low seating on cushiony banquettes.
• The Rituals: One of my favorite parts was the traditional handwashing at the table with rose water—it’s such a beautiful and unique touch.
• Entertainment: On certain nights (usually weekends), they have belly dancers, which adds so much fun and energy to the evening.
The Food
The food is delicious and very traditional. We enjoyed everything from the kebabs and freshly prepared rice to a variety of vegetable dishes. For dessert, they serve a beautiful spread of fresh fruit that is the perfect light finish to a rich meal.
Group Dining & Value
We had a massive group of nearly 30 people, and the staff was incredibly accommodating. While the space is very unique and probably best suited for groups of about 6 to 15, they handled our large party well by giving us our own section.
• Price: I was shocked at how reasonable the price per person was for such a multi-course feast.
• Pro-Tip: It is BYOB, so definitely bring your own favorite wine or spirits to pair with the meal!
Final Verdict: 100% recommended for anyone wanting an authentic, colorful, and delicious night out. It really feels like you’re in the heart of Marrakesh!

I will focus on the food part first like I believe I am supposed to.

The food was definitely delicious. Its owners are NOT wrong whenever they claim its cuisine is authentically Italian-American. Since we were already tired of gravy sauce coming down from New York City, we chose seafood instead. We started our food journey here with some cheesy garlic bread and Shrimp Scampi. It was really to die for. We accompanied them with a Peroni beer to water these down. The entrees were so much better, of course.

My fiancee ordered Chicken Lorraine with Rigatoni pasta because she saw the lady next to us eating that dish. Again, we refused gravy because we already ate it back in NYC. She was enormously satisfied with her dish. I was with mine too. I ordered a Pasta Di Linguini, which is a House favorite. I did NOT regret it at all. Like I said in the paragraph above, they DO serve authentical Italian-American cuisine. The service Ronny provided us contributed to make it more authentic, but Carol diminished everything he was striving to build with us.

Ronny is an amazingly attentive gentleman who does his best to accommodate your needs. Carol, on the other hand, seemed like she was NOT comfortable serving a Hispanic couple like us and she did not hesitate to demonstrate it. Carol wanted to rush us to order despite we had NOT read the menu. She acted like she was TOO busy to take care of us because she was conversing with the other patrons seating in front of us. When she bought us our entrees, we asked her to please take a picture of us with our meal. She refused us TWICE claiming she was "too" busy.

We expressed Mr. Pippy DeLuca, the restaurant owner, our disatisfaction with Carol. We told him we wanted to leave a tip for Ronny but NONE for her because of the way she treated us. He understood our situation and told us we did NOT have to leave a tip for the service; which really pained us because Ronny came economically undone as a result. We had to withdraw money from their in-house ATM because one must pay them in cash. That specific part of their service is still back in the era when they started. Just like the atmosphere of the restaurant.

Besides the deliciousness of the food, the atmosphere of the restaurant makes you want to enjoy their delicious cuisine right there. It definitely takes you back to the times Mr. Pippy's parents founded the restaurant. The lightning at night is appropriate for patrons to immediately feel welcomed at their restaurant. The DeLuca family, as veterans of the neighborhood, truly show you the scenes of an Italian-American restaurant. You immediately feel inside a mafia movie like The Godfather Part I (1972), Goodfellas (1991) , or The Irishman (2019). We enjoyed the ambiance even more when we ordered a Tartuffo to share with our coffee.

Despite my disatisfaction with Carol's service, I would still give this amazingly classic restaurant another try on a future visit to Philadelphia. I would just refuse Carol serving me because I do not give my business to a prejudiced individual. However, I would only ask for Ronnie to serve me some of those delicious Italian-American dishes this place has earned its reputation for. Next time, I want to try their VIlla Salad, Ziti & Meatballs, Shrimp Scampi over Linguine, Sausage Genovese, Veal Bella Bucca, Chicken Neapolitan, or a Steak My Way. All these at their classic atmosphere.

text.text:
Lets first talk about parking. If you want a good parking without taking numerous rounds of the neighborhood, consider arriving considerably early. We spend about 30 mins rolling our car in the neighborhood which has stricter night time parking rules. I'd suggest to take a cab if you have impromptu plan. And also good to make a reservation since the place is locally quite popular and fills up really quickly. We'd called beforehand so we only had to wait for 5 short minutes.

It has modern, hip vibes and is a fun spot to dip your toes into vegan food in Philly. The dishes put a creative spin on everyday veggies and definitely lean more towards big flavor than low calories. The menu feels more like elevated bar food, with plenty of fried, shareable bites. We tried chorizo empanada, crispy broccoli, crispy tofu. Had Emerald Fox as a calorie-conscious drink to avoid sugar and alcohol and still feel the ambience.
Their sourdough bread came with a generous portion along with cashew-based dip - turned out to be a good choice to feel filled aat the end, better to have it ordered in the beginning though.

A place slightly higher on pricing side though, but worth trying..

We stopped by Geno’s Steaks while in Philadelphia expecting one of those “must try” cheesesteak moments. It was a solid experience overall, but honestly it landed right in the middle for us at a three star stop.

The sandwich was decent and definitely filling, with a good amount of meat and cheese, but it didn’t stand out compared to other cheesesteaks we have had in the area. The flavor was fine, just not memorable enough to make it a repeat craving.

The atmosphere feels very fast paced and tourist driven, which makes sense for the location. Service was quick and efficient, but it felt more like a grab and go spot than somewhere you settle in and enjoy the experience.

My wife and I both agreed it was just okay. Not bad by any means, but there are better sandwiches nearby that hit more on flavor and balance.

Overall, a solid three star visit. Worth trying once if you are in Philly, but not the one we would go out of our way to return to.

text.text: I went to Philly just to settle the Geno's vs. Pat's debate. I got both with whiz, peppers, and onions. What I liked about Geno's was they put the whiz on the bread so it stayed on the sandwich, unlike Pat's, where it ended up mostly on the paper. Both are tasty, but a little salt and pepper wouldn't hurt. Pat's onion and peppers were way better than Geno's. Geno's meat was thinly sliced whole pieces of steak, while Pat's was chopped. Both were good, but I leaned more towards Geno's because it was super tender. I walked around checking out other people's food before ordering, and Pat's fries looked a little too light for me, so I got fries and a drink from Geno's. Overall, both are great, and you won't be disappointed with either. Neither offers half sizes, so you have to get a whole sandwich. I guess they don't want taste testers. My overall winner would be Geno's. Slightly more bang for your buck. But if the wind blows east, I totally get why some would say Pat's.  Try both!!

text.text:
Overpriced and mediocre.

Came in late on a Sunday night. This was my second Philly cheesesteak, after Jim's South, and even though plenty of people warned me it's a tourist trap, I still wanted to try the iconic sub. They ran almost $20 each, and we got a Steak Milano and a plain cheesesteak.

The shop wasn't busy, so we had our subs in under 10 mins, but they didn't look great. Everything came out dry, and the roll and the toppings just weren't working together. The thing I noticed most was that they don't chop the shaved steak, they grill it whole. So with no sauce and barely a smear of cheese, it was about the driest meat filling I've had on a sub. The whole strands of steak also made it awkward to bite through.

Glad this wasn't the first cheesesteak I tried. If you're after the real Philly experience, go somewhere else.

text.text:
What an incredible dining experience!

Service: we were a little late to our reservation but we had no issues getting seated and served right away. Everybody was kind, helpful, and informative. Our server answered all of our questions and was happy to help us make food and drink choices.

Food: amuse bouche - delicious rutabega, apple, and tarragon soup. It was perfect and really elevated the experience for us. Such a nice gesture from the kitchen
Tuna crudo - perfectly fresh fish, tangy and crispy, and herby accompaniments. Well thought out
Goat cheese gnudi - soft and pillowy texture, melts in your mouth, great contrast with the crispy pancetta
Papardelle with smoked pheasant  - perfect pasta texture, smokiness really comes through in a pleasant way
Caramelized onion ravioli - the onions were great, came off a little bit more sweet than I would've liked, but otherwise well balanced with the marrow crema sauce
Citrus olive oil cake - so well done. The zinginess of the citrus fruits, the variety of preserved vs fresh fruits, and the lovely whipped labneh texture and crispy meringues all worked together in a perfect way. Will dream of more cake

Atmosphere: quiet where you can enjoy your conversation, but has fun backround music so it's not stuffy or high strung. Staff are busy but it never feels rushed or stressful.

Pricing: reasonably priced for the high end experience and dishes. They're not trying to be anything that they're not which I really appreciate. The food comes first, and pricing suits the high quality of food without being pretentious

Dining area is clean and tidy, with a palm tree backdrop and theres even a glass cabinet displaying kawaii style trinkets and treasures that bring a smile. Seating is sturdy and about 12-14 people total could dine in comfortably without crowding Casual calm atmosphere.
Will definitely be back.

We took home some more cannoli & a piece of limoncello mascarpone cake - also heavenly. In all the dishes we were given, the presentation was beautiful. It is obvious that this restaurant and the staff exceeded our expectations to the max. We will definitely be coming again with family and friends!!!

I’ve eaten a lot of sandwiches in my life, and somehow Paesano’s keeps making me question whether I’ve ever actually had a good sandwich before.

Five stars. My only complaint is that they’ve permanently raised my standards.

text.text: Regrettably, this establishment operates on a cash-only basis and does not provide an on-site ATM. Guests are directed to a nearby corner store, which is conveniently within walking distance, to access an ATM. It might be more practical for a cash-only business to offer an ATM on its premises. Freshly squeezed orange juice is available for $5, served in a small, child-sized glass.

text.text:
Sophie’s Kitchen is a family owned restaurant serving up some incredibly delicious and authentic Cambodian cuisine!

Lemongrass wings: the absolute star of the show. hot off the fryer, the chicken had the perfect crisp but so much *tenderism*. crispy, garlicky, slightly sweet… 10/10 from me

Papaya salad (nhoam la hong): a great starter and/or palette cleanser. the red pepper flakes added a nice heat that built up the more i ate it, it surprised me

Stir fried egg noodle (mee cha): i have never had a noodle dish this flavorful. i was expecting this to be a standard side of noodles and veg to eat with other items, but i found myself wanting to just eat the entire plate. very savory and garlicky, good comfort food

Yellow curry coconut sour soup (somlawe majou kteah): i found this curry to be overly sweet, but that is no fault to the restaurant. my friend really enjoys pineapple and coconut milk in their curry so she picked this one. she loved it, i am more of a savory person so i would pick something else next time. the meat and veggies were tender and cooked well

Tony was very helpful and attentive. The inside was casual and the front seating area was pretty tight. But the food was so delicious, the ambiance didn’t matter. I will absolutely be back in the future for more!

The stir fried noodles (lort cha) is okay, a little too oily, I have had better. The sngour jruok mohn is a sweet and sour soup with mushroom and your choice of meat. It is not spicy at all, kinda a nice solid soup. I think between this and the other soup, the other one's flavor is more complex and in a way better but too spicy for me :( I think good food overall and price is affordable.

text.text:
Best cheesesteak I've had on my Philly trip.

Never really understood the fuss around cheesesteaks, but Jim's got me there. It's always mentioned in the top 10, and since it was a couple blocks from where we were staying, I made it our first late-night snack of the trip.

The lad on the grill kindly walked me through the steps, and I ordered two subs. One regular "whiz wit" (Cheez Whiz with grilled onions) and one with peppers. $13, and I did a double take. For a sub this packed I assumed the number would start with a bigger digit. Both were fantastic.

The difference seemed to come down to the flattop. No pre-cooked steam-tray pile here. The shaved beef hit the griddle raw, to order, and then he hit it with a squirt of water. The water flashed to steam, kept the thin meat from drying out, and deglazed the browned bits back into the pile instead of letting them scorch. By the time it's scraped onto the roll, the beef's own juices have soaked in just enough to take the bread from sturdy to plush without getting too soggy. Meat, cheese, and roll synced perfectly.

Not the most technically ambitious thing I'll eat in this city, but out of the dozen-odd places I hit, this was one of the most memorable.

text.text:
When Kindness Meets Community

Some experiences transcend food and drink—they become memories you'll treasure forever. My evening at this gem of a establishment was exactly that: a beautiful reminder of why we go out, why we connect, and why certain places become more than just venues—they become the backdrop for life's loveliest moments.

I stopped in for happy hour with modest intentions—just a drink or two to unwind before catching my train. The atmosphere immediately embraced me: laid-back without being sleepy, comfortable without being generic, the kind of place where you can breathe and just be. I settled in with my first drink, soaking in the easy vibe.

As I was ordering my second round, a lively group arrived. Without thinking twice, I shifted down the bar to make room for them—just basic courtesy, the kind of small gesture we all should make but sometimes forget in our rush through life.

Then something magical happened.

A lovely woman from the group approached me with the warmest smile and insisted on buying me an Erdinger beer—as a thank you for making space for them without being asked. I was genuinely touched. In a world where rudeness often goes viral and kindness feels increasingly rare, this simple act of reciprocal generosity stopped me in my tracks. It wasn't about the beer (though, let's be honest, who turns down a free Erdinger?). It was about being seen, being appreciated for a tiny moment of consideration.

But the story gets better.

A gentleman from the same group struck up a conversation, asking how I was enjoying the Erdinger. I told him the truth: it was superb—rich, mellow, beautifully aromatic, with that distinctive character that sets German beers apart. I was genuinely impressed. I jokingly asked if he was the owner or perhaps a distributor.

He smiled and replied, "No, we're from the Erdinger region of Germany."

My mind raced. The timing, the generosity, the specific beer choice, the pride in his voice—I'm still convinced this man had some connection to the brewery. Perhaps family ties? A longtime resident with friends in the business? Whatever the case, his passion for his homeland's brewing tradition was palpable and infectious.

The venue itself deserves immense credit for cultivating this kind of environment. The setting is perfectly pitched: relaxed enough to encourage strangers to become friends, elevated enough to attract thoughtful, quality-minded patrons. The staff was attentive without hovering, the happy hour offerings were generous, and the overall atmosphere struck that rare balance between energetic and intimate.

When Kindness Meets Community

Some experiences transcend food and drink—they become memories you'll treasure forever. My evening at this gem of a establishment was exactly that: a beautiful reminder of why we go out, why we connect, and why certain places become more than just venues—they become the backdrop for life's loveliest moments.

I stopped in for happy hour with modest intentions—just a drink or two to unwind before catching my train. The atmosphere immediately embraced me: laid-back without being sleepy, comfortable without being generic, the kind of place where you can breathe and just be. I settled in with my first drink, soaking in the easy vibe.

As I was ordering my second round, a lively group arrived. Without thinking twice, I shifted down the bar to make room for them—just basic courtesy, the kind of small gesture we all should make but sometimes forget in our rush through life.

Then something magical happened.

A lovely woman from the group approached me with the warmest smile and insisted on buying me an Erdinger beer—as a thank you for making space for them without being asked. I was genuinely touched. In a world where rudeness often goes viral and kindness feels increasingly rare, this simple act of reciprocal generosity stopped me in my tracks. It wasn't about the beer (though, let's be honest, who turns down a free Erdinger?). It was about being seen, being appreciated for a tiny moment of consideration.

But the story gets better.

A gentleman from the same group struck up a conversation, asking how I was enjoying the Erdinger. I told him the truth: it was superb—rich, mellow, beautifully aromatic, with that distinctive character that sets German beers apart. I was genuinely impressed. I jokingly asked if he was the owner or perhaps a distributor.

He smiled and replied, "No, we're from the Erdinger region of Germany."

My mind raced. The timing, the generosity, the specific beer choice, the pride in his voice—I'm still convinced this man had some connection to the brewery. Perhaps family ties? A longtime resident with friends in the business? Whatever the case, his passion for his homeland's brewing tradition was palpable and infectious.

The venue itself deserves immense credit for cultivating this kind of environment. The setting is perfectly pitched: relaxed enough to encourage strangers to become friends, elevated enough to attract thoughtful, quality-minded patrons. The staff was attentive without hovering, the happy hour offerings were generous, and the overall atmosphere struck that rare balance between energetic and intimate.

I didn't try the food on this visit, but I'm absolutely planning a return trip specifically to explore their menu. If the kitchen operates with the same care and quality as the bar program—and if the clientele continues to be this exceptional—I have no doubt it'll be outstanding.

text.text:
Dining at Saloon Restaurant is always a special experience—but when you’re fortunate enough to be seated with Sam, it becomes something truly unforgettable.

Sam brings a level of elegance to service that perfectly mirrors the sophistication of the restaurant itself. From the moment we sat down, her presence elevated the evening—graceful without ever being intrusive, attentive without feeling overbearing. She has a remarkable ability to read the table, anticipating needs before they’re spoken and guiding the experience with effortless confidence.

Under her care, the meal itself became extraordinary. The seafood dishes were nothing short of spectacular—fresh, delicate, and perfectly prepared, with each bite highlighting the quality and precision that defines Saloon’s kitchen. From the richness of the sauces to the flawless execution, every seafood course felt luxurious and thoughtfully composed.

The steak was equally outstanding—cooked to perfection with a beautiful sear and melt-in-your-mouth tenderness that made it a true centerpiece of the evening. It was bold, flavorful, and deeply satisfying, standing shoulder-to-shoulder with the best in the city.

What truly set the night apart was how Sam magnified every moment. Her thoughtful recommendations, seamless pacing, and polished demeanor transformed an already exceptional dinner into a refined, memorable experience. She doesn’t just serve food—she elevates the entire evening.

In a city known for great dining, Sam represents hospitality at its highest level. Her unparalleled service is not just impressive—it’s the kind that keeps you coming back.

text.text:
We were so excited to finally try The Saloon after hearing so much about it. Everyone seems to rave about it so our expectations were high.

Unfortunately, we left feeling disappointed. The standout dish of the night were the diver scallops, which were excellent……. but at $85???  The Clams Pavarotti were also very good and one of the better items we tried.

For our entrées, we all ordered the lobster franchise. While the flavor was good, the portion was underwhelming…..just a small piece of lobster with no sides……For that price point we expected at least a side of pasta, potatoes, or vegetables. The lack of anything on the plate made it feel incomplete and not reflective of the premium pricing.

The service was mediocre at best.   For a restaurant charging these kinds of prices, exceptional service and attention to detail should be.  We repeatedly had to look for our waitress to ask for more water or bread. Also, our coffee came out 15 minutes after our dessert. We would not consider this the best Italian food in Philadelphia, and it did not live up to the hype.  Sorry not sorry.

The sandwiches are the real deal.  Got there around 2pm today (Sunday) just a few people ahead of me in line.  Ordered the spicy Augustine and the Damien.  Originally was told they were out of cutlets, but the woman taking orders found me outside while I was waiting and said they had enough cutlets to make me one (I guess the guy making sandwiches didn’t know if he had enough since he was doing phone orders and call ahead orders as well). And the Damien was out of this world delicious - the tang of the pepper cuts through the heaviness of the sandwich, which makes for a perfect bite.  I came to Philly on a sandwich tour and this by far was my favorite on this trip.  Unfortunately they’re closed on Monday or I’d make another visit before my flight home.  Very fair prices as well with both sandwiches at $8 plus tax.

Tip:  get there early so you don’t run the risk of them running out of cutlets

text.text:
I've been coming here since 2017 and I've honestly never had a bad meal. It's a real classic kind of place with display cases filled with baked goods, smoked fish, salads, and of course their famous cold cuts.

You really can't go wrong here, but I think their Ungashtupt sandwich menu is where the magic is. There's nothing like those huge layers of fresh deli meat mixed and matched in all kinds of satisfying ways.

Their platters are extremely generous, with the shrimp salad being my personal favorite. In fact, all their menu portions are generous. One of their overstuffed sandwiches can provide 3 solid meals. Last time I stopped in for a meal, they dropped a baggie of warm chocolate chip cookies on the table.

The only downside here is that the service, while friendly, can be on the slow side. If you're short on time, best call your order ahead and do take out. But it's always worth it.

I want to give a special thank you to Michele and her staff at Angelina's for hosting a beautiful 80th birthday dinner for my mother.

The family-style dishes kept coming from the kitchen, one after another, and each was more delicious than the last. The food was outstanding, the service was warm and attentive, and the entire evening exceeded our expectations.

Michele and her team made this milestone celebration truly special for our family. We have found our new go-to restaurant for family celebrations and special occasions.

Thank you again, Michele, for your kindness, hospitality, and an unforgettable evening!

text.text:
Philadelphia is lucky to have Roxanne.

This was, without question, the best meal I’ve eaten all year.

The sun gold tomatoes were so good they made me want to slap my mother. The pork chop had absolutely no business being that insanely delicious. Every course arrived with the kind of confidence that only comes from a chef operating at the height of their craft.

What makes Roxanne special isn’t just the food—it’s the way Chef Alex continues to blur the line between dining and art. The meal feels less like a restaurant experience and more like an invitation into someone’s creative process. Thoughtful without being precious, ambitious without being self-important, and executed with a level of care that is increasingly rare.

Philadelphia is fortunate to have a restaurant willing to push the boundaries of what a meal can be while remaining deeply hospitable and genuinely enjoyable. Roxanne isn’t following trends or chasing relevance. It’s creating something entirely its own.

A remarkable meal from a remarkable chef.

text.text:
You can look at my whole profile - I want to be fair and also honest, so people can make the best dining decisions.

I don't really need to rattle off all of the good things -- if you're even considering eating here, you know what they are. But to share in case...

- There’s both a seriousness and a lightheartedness to the tasting menu that happily coexist, making the whole experience stand out in a good way.
- I don't know much about the chef but I now know she makes some of the best crusts I've had (baby tuna melt, honey pie).
- The reductions were nearly phenomenal (I'll explain soon)

Even with all of that good though, the misses clouded the experience. I would never go into a meal like this with a frugal mindset -- I like to spend my money on food. But with so many incredible restaurants that exist in Philly and NY, there's a real opportunity cost at this price point...and if you're going to be a $140/pp tasting menu, there's very little margin for error.

One of the two errors was how salty numerous dishes were. The French onion agnolotti, prawn stuffed chicken, lamb loin, and spinach morel were all almost really, really good but just got crushed with salt to where we did a would-you-rather of would you rather have food that's over salted or under seasoned. Felt inedible at times.

Which leads me to the second error, which is how long we were sitting there. I think we were there for 3 hours and there was way too much time between courses. Once you're onto the 'f-marry-k' part of the night, you know you've been there too long. We felt a bit trapped.

Btw, I think they could either make the portions smaller or scale back the amount of dishes on the tasting. Not a negative - more a note, because we were absolutely stuffed (combo of amount + idle time).

We still enjoyed the experience and respectfully mentioned the saltiness aspect to our server. To be frank. her response felt like it was kind of throwing Alexandra under the bus as if she couldn't properly salt food because a group of 4 became a group of 7 unexpectedly. I know how difficult it is to open a restaurant, let alone thrive...so without knowing her personally, I know Alexandra is stupid talented.

Maybe it was just an off night - it's not robots doing the cooking (thank god). I'm glad we went, and I hope some of those issues can be ironed out bc tbh they're easy ones to fix. For now I won't be heading back any time soon but I wouldn't be opposed to trying again with some cautious optimism in the future.

Even with all of that good though, the misses clouded the experience. I would never go into a meal like this with a frugal mindset -- I like to spend my money on food. But with so many incredible restaurants that exist in Philly and NY, there's a real opportunity cost at this price point...and if you're going to be a $140/pp tasting menu, there's very little margin for error.

One of the two errors was how salty numerous dishes were. The French onion agnolotti, prawn stuffed chicken, lamb loin, and spinach morel were all almost really, really good but just got crushed with salt to where we did a would-you-rather of would you rather have food that's over salted or under seasoned. Felt inedible at times.

Which leads me to the second error, which is how long we were sitting there. I think we were there for 3 hours and there was way too much time between courses. Once you're onto the 'f-marry-k' part of the night, you know you've been there too long. We felt a bit trapped.

Btw, I think they could either make the portions smaller or scale back the amount of dishes on the tasting. Not a negative - more a note, because we were absolutely stuffed (combo of amount + idle time).

We still enjoyed the experience and respectfully mentioned the saltiness aspect to our server. To be frank. her response felt like it was kind of throwing Alexandra under the bus as if she couldn't properly salt food because a group of 4 became a group of 7 unexpectedly. I know how difficult it is to open a restaurant, let alone thrive...so without knowing her personally, I know Alexandra is stupid talented.

Maybe it was just an off night - it's not robots doing the cooking (thank god). I'm glad we went, and I hope some of those issues can be ironed out bc tbh they're easy ones to fix. For now I won't be heading back any time soon but I wouldn't be opposed to trying again with some cautious optimism in the future.

text.text:
Dante & Luigi’s is truly a piece of Philadelphia history, and you can feel that the moment you walk in. The service was a perfect 10/10. We called to change our reservation last minute, and they still managed to squeeze us in with zero attitude just kindness. Throughout the night, two staff members were always nearby, explaining the menu and making us feel taken care of. It really elevated the experience.
The dishes overall were great, but a couple really stood out. The Carbonara was one of the best I’ve had in my entire life rich, flavorful, perfectly done. The lasagna was also exceptional. We tried the seafood pasta, which was good, though I think it could’ve been executed just a bit better. We also ordered mussels, and those were fantastic fresh and packed with flavor.The vibe was lively but comfortable. It felt like an older crowd overall, but there were definitely younger diners as well. The atmosphere reflects the restaurant’s long history I believe it’s one of the city’s oldest Italian spots  and that classic charm is part of what makes the place special.

text.text:
Pho South Corner embodies everything great about about a local, low-key spot with kind owners and great service. We enjoyed a very pleasant meal that was reasonably priced, tasted like comfort food, and would be very easy to return to!

The interior is very casual but cute with lots of tables. We were also pleasantly surprised that they had the world cup game playing which was fun to watch. We started with the veggie spring rolls, which had great flavor and the slightly pickled veggies it came with were cooling and added nice contrast. The rolls were certainly a bit oily, but enjoyable nonetheless.

I thoroughly enjoyed the broken rice special, a big comforting platter of nicely grilled pork, rice, egg, noodles, and some veg. It also came with some sort of slice of meat/grain loaf which, I still don't really know what it is and I have never had something like it, but it was pretty tasty! I would have enjoyed a bit more of the sauce that the dish came with, but it was simple and delicious and seems like a reliable plate for when you're hungry. My wife ordered the pho which was solid as well. It had a nicely spiced broth with good portions, though it was just a touch sweet maybe.

The highlight honestly wasn't the food, though it was very good, but I just really appreciated the kindness and hospitality from the owners. The one that took care of us was attentive, helpful, brought us things when he noticed they were needed, and helped explain some of our questions. It makes me want to return. Overall I would recommend this as an easy choice for a solid Vietnamese meal with lots of choices and variety!

Flan doesnt look pretty but is delicious as it is served w coffee not just caramel.

This was my first time booking this place. I went there with my partner hoping to have a lovely romantic night together. The atmosphere was beautiful, very romantic, and honestly a great place for photos and spending a nice evening.

However, the food experience was very disappointing. The steak we ordered is something I seriously question in terms of freshness, because shortly after, my stomach became extremely upset. I spent almost the entire night vomiting and dealing with diarrhea. I normally don’t leave negative reviews, but this experience was bad enough that I feel people should know.

We also did not enjoy the appetizers or some of the other dishes. We mentioned it to the staff, and they kindly replaced them with something similar, but unfortunately we still did not like the food.

For two people, we spent around $200 in one night, and honestly we left very unhappy with the food quality. The only positive part of the experience was the romantic atmosphere and the overall vibe of the place.

I truly hope the restaurant pays more attention to the freshness and quality of the food, especially the steak.

text.text:
We celebrated our 36th anniversary dinner at Bistro Romano, a place that has been special to us since our dating days. Walking in always brings back memories, from the old murder mystery dinner theater nights to the days when they prepared Caesar salad tableside. The bar area with the piano player still creates such a wonderful, classic atmosphere.
Our table was ready right when we arrived, and there was even a thoughtful anniversary card waiting on the table, which was a lovely touch. Parking in the area can be a bit of a challenge, but on a Saturday night in the city, that’s to be expected and certainly not the restaurant’s fault.
Our server Kisher was outstanding throughout the evening, pleasant, attentive, helpful, and even kind enough to laugh at my bad dad jokes.
We started with 2 Old Fashioned cocktails and the Affettati Misto, a charcuterie board for two that immediately reminded us of the one we enjoyed in Bologna, Italy at La Prosciutteria. For dinner, my wife’s veal saltimbocca and my duck breast were both cooked perfectly and absolutely delicious. A great bottle of wine followed by espresso and cappuccino,  panna cotta and pistachio cannoli to finish the meal. Mamma mia.
The restaurant even surprised us with complimentary glasses of bubbles for our anniversary, which was a wonderful gesture.
Thank you and grazie mille, to the entire team at Bistro Romano for making our 36th anniversary so special. After all these years, when we find something we love, we stick with it.

Our server Kisher was outstanding throughout the evening, pleasant, attentive, helpful, and even kind enough to laugh at my bad dad jokes.
We started with 2 Old Fashioned cocktails and the Affettati Misto, a charcuterie board for two that immediately reminded us of the one we enjoyed in Bologna, Italy at La Prosciutteria. For dinner, my wife’s veal saltimbocca and my duck breast were both cooked perfectly and absolutely delicious. A great bottle of wine followed by espresso and cappuccino,  panna cotta and pistachio cannoli to finish the meal. Mamma mia.
The restaurant even surprised us with complimentary glasses of bubbles for our anniversary, which was a wonderful gesture.
Thank you and grazie mille, to the entire team at Bistro Romano for making our 36th anniversary so special. After all these years, when we find something we love, we stick with it.

text.text: I want to start by saying I do absolutely love the atmosphere of this restaurant, which is why I chose to come here. It’s very unique and intimate, perfect for a date night. Ambience is dimly lit but barely any music, you can hear very loud talking and laughing,  so most of the time I heard other people’s conversations; almost like a bar atmosphere and not fine dining. Our food however was a bit disappointing. My bf and I got the NY strip, and the steak tasted odd and was chewy despite getting medium rare. The sauce and mash potatoes were great, the veggies were so bland unfortunately. Portions were ok, barely any mash on the plate and a heaping load of veggies to cover for the lack of mash. The sauce was the best thing on the plate. I also got a side of Brussels sprouts and they were so soggy. I got the espresso martini and for the price it was SO small. I’m talking a miniature glass, and barely any alcohol. (Almost $20 for just that drink alone) For desert we got the crème brûlée with oranges. The oranges were phenomenal but the crème brûlée was also so flavorless. It was my birthday so I was disappointed especially with how much we spent here. I’m not sure if it was off day. Our server was nice but she barely checked on us. Had to refill our own waters, and call her over multiple times. The table was so small that things were getting knocked over, nothing fit and was very uncomfortable. To top it off I spent the rest of the night with really bad upset stomach, close to food poisoning which I believe was from the steak which tasted off. I’ve spent the same amount at Jean George’s and that experience was 10x better.

text.text:
**CASH ONLY**

I’ve been here many many times. As a viet, this is my favorite Bun bo hue (BBH) in all of Philly. It’s just sooo good. Their BBH broth is flavorful but balanced between sweet, sour, salty, it’s heavy with herbs and spices such as lemon grass (as this broth should be), while the meat is thick and plentiful. My go to tend to be BBH or banh cuon (also the best around). I’ve also tried their dry noodles and beef pho, both were phenomenal and would reorder again. The food is always fresh and hot, I could tell it was made with care.

The place is small and there may be a wait depending on party size and when you go but food gets served quickly. They serve tea at no charge instead of water (it’s rare to get free tea like this anymore). All the ladies there are very friendly. Highly recommend this place for great authentic Vietnamese food.

text.text: While I visit 9th St., Italian market quite often for my fresh produce it’s not often I get a chance to sit down and actually eat at a restaurant on ninth Street. It’s actually been a couple of years. It was beautiful out 60+ degrees and sunny and I was hungry and I was on my way back from the Asian farmers market in FDR Park in South Philadelphia and that made me very hungry so I found a spot on ninth Street was in a hunt for fresh tacos. There are many places on ninth Street that sell fresh tacos so this is a random pick and I’ll be damned if I didn’t pick the right place. A lot of these little places are considered hole in the wall, that being said you can find some real gems here. I didn’t plan to do a review on this place. It was just a quick bite that turned into a review when I walked in. I was greeted by a really nice man very helpful and the place was actually very nice looking kinda upscale, actually on the menu, there are a few vegetarian options that can quickly be made into a vegan option along with regular items so this would be a place that has vegan options. They have seating on the inside and the outside. I choose the outside such a pretty day in the gentleman provided me with tableside service immediately brought me a nice fresh glass of water, napkins, plates, and flatware, and not soon after my food was delivered within 10 minutes the pictures say it all just look how fresh the tacos had Fresh sautéed onions, peppers, mushrooms, fresh, shredded lettuce, fresh herbs, and cilantro with freshly whipped up sauce, Verde and spicy red sauce, served with fresh limes, cucumbers, and radishes on the side what a great combination reasonably priced at $13. I asked the gentleman for a takeout container because I thought I was gonna take at least half home…. that didn’t happen, these are up there with the best of the best when it comes to fresh tacos. These were seasoned perfectly. I’ll have to hit this place up again in the future. There are a few pictures.
