text.text: My wife is Indonesian and we eat Indo food all the time. We had high hopes for this restaurant but from the moment we walked in they seemed rushed but disinterested. I had Nasi Campur which is usually marinated and very tasty. This was bland and tasteless. My wife had Rendang and it was very hard. She let them know and they claimed that is how it is made. We have had Rendang many times and it is usually tender and full of flavor. They offered her another chicken dish which was just as bad. Despite a 4.6 rating it was not up to par. The rice was also poorly cooked. Rice is a staple of Indo food. You have to try hard to mess it up. The tofu and tempeh on my plate and the pickled vegetables on her plate were the only savory items. There was also a hair in my wife's food. Since this is her culture she politely told them we picked the wrong night to come. The waiter just said sorry but just didn't seem to care. I hope they will see this and make improvements so their business can flourish.

text.text:
Their variety of Indonesian dishes used to be consistently delicious and was the main reason I kept coming back over the past few years. Unfortunately, it feels like both the portion sizes and overall consistency across the menu have declined over time.

The beef rendang in particular used to be one of my favorite dishes here, but lately it has been very hit or miss. On some visits, the beef is flavorful and tender, but most of the time it comes out dry and tough. The portion also feels quite small now, with just two small pieces of beef. I’m hoping they can improve the consistency because the food here can still be really good when it’s done right.

One thing to keep in mind is that the parking lot can also be difficult. It’s usually very full and tight since the plaza is shared with the supermarket and several other restaurants.

I went with a friend around 5pm, right when they opened on a week day. We sat in the bar area, had a good chat. It started to get REALLY busy for some league night event, I think, but it was still easy to converse. I got the buffalo wings, kimchi burger, and roasted shishito peppers. Peppers were good, but could have been grilled longer overall for more crispy bits and the wings were a lil too crunchy from being cooked a touch too long, but the flavour on both was good. The burger was nothing super special, but a solid prepared Beyond patty and the fries were good. Dessert provided challenges, but so be it. The fact that nearly the whole menu was vegan was a huge selling point.

I am def looking to come back and explore more of the games that they have on offer, fun concept for the place and in a really cool building.

text.text:
On 01/07/2026, we decided to revisit the Queen & Rook for a quick bite. We were in the mood for pizza, and since I had tried every pie on the menu except for the fall veggie, we decided to give it a try. The fall veggie pizza comes with oyster mushrooms, roasted red peppers, red onion, spinach, and garlic housemade marinara with your choice of vegan or regular mozzarella. We opted to add vegan sausage crumbles to take it up a notch.

For drinks, we chose a pot of "Computer Eyes" hot tea, which had a cute name that aligned with the restaurant's theme. The tea was made with lavender, Elderberry, peppermint, and honey, and it was absolutely excellent. It was a very relaxing tea that we enjoyed together. We also shared a turmeric golden milk latte with oat milk and honey, which was perfectly done - smooth, silky, a little bit peppery, and creamy. It was the perfect choice to warm our souls on a chilly night.

The pizza itself was done perfectly, with a nice crispy crust on the underside and loaded with toppings. The vegan cheese was oozing and delicious. Not stopping there, we decided to indulge in a warm brookie with vegan vanilla cream for dessert. Our server, Riley, was excellent - very accommodating and ever present. It is safe to say that we love this place and can't get enough of it.

11/10/2025
Back at Queen and Rook, one of my favorite places, I find myself in love with this establishment all over again. The atmosphere exudes warmth and invitation, with the staff always ready to greet you with a smile. What I appreciate most about them is their imperfection - it adds to the charm and genuineness of the place. Their food consistently delights my taste buds, and their willingness to accommodate any dietary needs is a welcomed gesture.

Visitors to Queen and Rook come here to relax and enjoy good food, surrounded by friends and family. The extensive collection of over 2500 board games provides hours of entertainment, catering to a wide range of preferences. Additionally, the arcade in the basement takes patrons on a nostalgic trip back to the 80s and 90s with its selection of great games.

For me, Queen and Rook holds a special place in my heart. I've frequented this spot numerous times this summer, and the anticipation of my next visit already warms my heart.
